events.title: Wisdom Healing Qigong with Hiromi Vardy
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Experience the deep benefits of Zhineng (Wisdom Healing) Qigong. This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Through simple, time-honored movements, the nervous system unwinds, the mind becomes more spacious, and the heart opens. Over time, practitioners often feel more resilient, centered, and connected — both inwardly and outwardly.

Tickets are sliding scale $10-$25 - Please arrive at least 5-10 minutes early.

 Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back 

Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts.

While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga.

After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today.

Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

events.title: Live at inStudio
events.location: inStudio with Empowerment Avenue, 473 25th St., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time Program & Event Overview Currently on view at Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio in Oakland, The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time brings together stories told through the work of Black currently and formerly incarcerated artists. Their work traces histories of enslavement and confinement alongside the realities of incarceration today, while carrying memory, endurance, and imagination toward something beyond them. Together, these works invite us to explore the space between captivity and liberation, to see differently, and to imagine a world beyond systems of punishment. Friday, October 2 | 1:00–9:00 PM 1:00 PM | Gallery Opens Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio will open its doors at 1:00 PM, inviting visitors to experience The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time and spend time with the work throughout the afternoon. Live at inStudio 6:00 PM | Panel Discussion: Black Yearning for Freedom At 6:00 PM, we will gather for a conversation exploring a continuing Black yearning for freedom and the ways artists carry memory, history, our bodies, and our imaginations onto canvas and paper. Moving between histories of enslavement and confinement and the realities of incarceration today, the conversation will consider art as a place to hold these experiences while also imagining beyond them. What does it mean to create from within systems of confinement without allowing confinement to define the limits of the imagination? What can Black creative practice teach us about freedom, possibility, and the worlds we have yet to make? The conversation will feature exhibition artists Ray Williams Jr. and Alvin Smith, alongside exhibition co-curator De’jon Joy. The discussion will be moderated by Milan Drake, Community Design Lead at the Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford University (the d.school). 7:00 PM | Live Performance by Inertia the Artist Following the conversation, Inertia the Artist will offer a live performance in the gallery. Inertia the Artist is an Oakland-based vocalist, loop artist, facilitator, and somatic psychotherapist whose soulful music and sound work center healing, transformation, and social change. The performance extends the evening’s exploration beyond the visual, bringing voice, sound, body, and collective experience into the exhibition space.

events.title: ‘Selena Scott: Intimations of Ignition’ opening at Mighty Mighty Gallery
events.location: Mighty Mighty Studio, 480 23rd St, Oakland, CA 94612
events.description:
in conjunction with Nexus: SF/Bay Area Black Arts Week @NexusSFBay @MoADsf @mightymightystudios @selenarosescott

Join us for the opening reception of ‘Intimations of Ignition’, a solo exhibition of paintings and mixed media works by British artist Selena Scott.
This exhibition explores the endurance of the Black psyche. Drawing from William Wordsworth’s ‘Ode: Intimations of Immortality from Recollections of Early Childhood’ and James Baldwin’s ‘The Fire Next Time’, ‘intimations’ are reimagined through a racial lens and ‘ignition’ as a form of destruction and salvation. What happens to our rose-tinted view of the world as we age? How does optimism survive within systems designed to extinguish it?
Moving between the mourning of lost innocence and the forging of power from pain, these works consider what it means to remain hopeful in our society.

events.title: Eriq La Salle with Dave Clark - Laws of Solomon
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Propulsive and deeply human, Laws of Solomon is a story of redemption, found family, and the cost of choosing compassion in a brutal world. In saving Gaby, Solomon may finally discover whether peace is something a man like him can earn—or something he must sacrifice everything to protect. Eriq will be joined in conversation by Dave Clark, an Emmy Award-winning television journalist, professional announcer, emcee, speaker, interviewer, and community advocate with more than five decades of broadcasting experience. "Beautiful and heartbreaking." — Walter Mosley "An amazing read!" — S.A. Cosby "Lush and brutal, a poem hiding out as a novel." — Rachel Howzell Hall "La Salle writes with verve." — Dennis Lehane Redemption isn't given. It's fought for. After years of violence, Solomon leaves the brutal backdrop of New York and its underworld to find peace in California where he settles for the quiet life of a gardener defined by routine, restraint, and a fragile kind of peace that had alluded him. Having been a former child soldier, mercenary, and hit man, he is determined to put his past behind him. But as violence erupts on the grounds he tends, his hard-won tranquility shatters when he encounters a young boy named Gaby whose life is in danger. Protecting the child pulls Solomon back into a world he swore he'd buried. As they set out on an unexpected journey, hunted by men who will stop at nothing to get what they want, Solomon must confront not only the threat closing in but the darkness he carries within. Propulsive and deeply human, Laws of Solomon is a story of redemption, found family, and the cost of choosing compassion in a brutal world. In saving Gaby, Solomon may finally discover whether peace is something a man like him can earn—or something he must sacrifice everything to protect. Eriq La Salle brings readers into the world of his acclaimed Martyr Maker series with this standalone novel—the perfect entry point for readers new to La Salle's writing. Actor. Director. Producer. Author. ERIQ LA SALLE is best known to audiences for his portrayal of Dr. Peter Benton on the ground-breaking medical drama ER. Other notable acting appearances include Coming to America, One Hour Photo, and Logan. La Salle received his formal training from Juilliard and NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts. La Salle has built a prolific career behind the camera as well, directing and executive producing for Law & Order, On Call, FBI, Chicago PD, among others. After decades of success in the entertainment industry, La Salle launched his highly personal and award-winning Martyr Maker series. With these novels, he brings an unusual new depth and emotion to the traditional procedural thriller. Find Eriq online at iameriqlasalle.com, on Instagram @eriqlasalle and TikTok @eriqlsalleauthor Dave Clark is an Emmy Award-winning television journalist, professional announcer, emcee, speaker, interviewer, and community advocate with more than five decades of broadcasting experience. Since 2007, he has served as a morning news anchor for KTVU TV Channel 2 in the San Francisco Bay Area, where viewers know him for his credibility, warmth, and steady presence. His on-camera presence reflects journalistic authority and genuine human connection. Beyond the anchor desk, Dave hosts KTVU’s “Talk of the Town,” where he interviews newsmakers, artists, business leaders, and community voices. His commanding voice and engaging style have made him a sought-after master of ceremonies, narrator, and speaker. Dave serves as an Advisory Board Member for Joshua’s Gift and Director of Media & Community Relations for The Vibrancy Foundation™. He and his wife, artist and entrepreneur Lucretia D. Clark, share a deep commitment to community, culture, and service. About the Facilitators:
Faze x Point ·θΦθ· is the author of Positive Realizations and the founder of POSITs. Working across systems science and philosophy, Faze has been developing a coherent way of thinking about how organic and synthetic intelligence can grow together — and building the organization that turns that thinking into research, community, and public benefit.
Brief Auto-Biography:
"I have studied philosophy pretty intently for over a decade, beginning with a strong eastern influence; Buddhism, Taoism, and “new age” integrations of mysticism and science. Psychedelics, Watts, Mckenna, Plum Village, the Tao of Physics, etc. Then, becoming disenchanted with what appeared to be too simplistic, vague, and removed an idealism, I turned to Marxism: the Manifesto, the manuscripts, Capital V. 1 & 2, Engels origin of family, Lenin state and rev, David Harvey, Michael Roberts, Michael Heinrich, I.I. Rubin, Endnotes, etc.
Becoming disenchanted with what I saw as too rigid, binary, and academic an approach, I became most interested in Hegel, Schelling, Delueze, Spinoza, Whitehead, etc. -- dialectical, theological, process-centered, phenomenological systems. I integrated my various influences, and my cultural context into a spiritual, communalist project. I lived in a shared home in an ecovillage, learned about permaculture, appropriate tech, biogas, cob building, living machines, DIY vibes, as well as communal social technology.
We experimented with Sociocracy, Nonviolent Communication, Internal Family Systems, Possibility Mgmt., and various meditative dialogue modalities like circling and insight dialogue. Becoming disenchanted with the slow pace of change, the financial challenges, the interpersonal limitations, the power dynamics, and personal struggle, I left to study as an electrician, and began to let go of the desire to spearhead a world-changing communalist movement. Then, my path urged me to write again - to finish the synthesis of thought I’d been searching for and longing to develop for years, and to move to California to further a holistic, post-rationalist / super-rational spiritual, trans-humanist, community project.
I am building out my recently conceived nonprofit, POSITs to continue my research and development of highly coherence intentional communities; working to publish my writing more widely, developing a digital inter/personal alignment tool based on liquid democracy, facilitating intentional relating events, and networking for deeper collaboration globally, from the network society movement and Edge City, to the tech-forward, holistic, and spiritual intentional community scenes more broadly."
--

events.description: This group exhibition at Werkshack Studios brings together four artists to explore themes of oppressive systems, power, and control through glass and mixed media. events.title: Kiliii Yuyan - Guardians of Life
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Based on the work of award-winning National Geographic photographer Kiliii Yüyan, Guardians of Life takes readers on a transformative journey to people living in relationship with their ancestral homelands while upholding the sovereign rights of Indigenous peoples to care for their lands and waters. This book seeks to build a movement that broadly benefits and sustains life on Earth for everyone. There is a critical yet underrecognized role that Indigenous peoples around the world have played—and continue to play—in sustaining biological and cultural diversity. As the biodiversity and climate crises converge, the time to support Indigenous leadership is now. This rich, in-depth, storytelling initiative is based on growing global recognition of the critical role Indigenous peoples play in sustaining biological and cultural diversity, as well as adapting to and abating climate change. This book, Guardians of Life , is based on the work of award-winning National Geographic photographer Kiliii Yüyan , and will take readers on a transformative journey to places and people living in relationship with their ancestral homelands. Vivid portraits of Indigenous men and women, youth and elders, hunters and farmers, spiritual leaders and craftsmen will reveal their ways of knowing and taking care of the land. These are concepts and skills that have been taught for generations and are based on a foundational veneration for life— which is at the heart of caring for a living planet. This reflects a holistic and broad approach to sustainability, including language, art, and ceremony as ways to maintain human-environment relations. These place-based stories and imagery are complemented by an introduction by Gwich’in supermodel and activist Quannah Chasinghorse . Essay contributions come from award-winning writer Charles C. Mann , author of 1491 , and award winning author, Indigenous peoples' ally, and National Geographic Explorer, Gleb Raygorodetsky . This book upholds the inherent sovereign rights of Indigenous peoples to care for their ancestral lands and waters , and seeks to build a movement that would broadly benefit and sustain life on planet Earth for all. “Indigenous peoples have mastered the art of living on Earth without destroying it. They continue to teach and lead by example. We must heed these lessons, if we want our grandchildren to have a future.” — Jon Waterhouse, S'klallam, Chippewa-Cree "A visually dazzling and deeply informative collection that will linger with readers long after the last page." -- Kirkus Reviews (starred review) "Both breathtaking and intimate. . ." -- Foreword Reviews (starred review) KILIII YÜYAN: Photographer and National Geographic Explorer Kiliii Yüyan brings to life stories from the Arctic sea ice, beneath the waves, and within the heart of human communities. Of Chinese and Nanai/Hèzhé (East Asian Indigenous) descent, he works through a cross-cultural lens, exploring how humanity lives in relationship with land and sea. His photography and storytelling appear in National Geographic , TIME , Vogue , WIRED , and other major publications. In 2023, Kiliii was honored with the Eliza Scidmore Award for Outstanding Storytelling , one of National Geographic ’s highest recognitions. His work has been recognized by Pictures of the Year , Leica Oscar-Barnack , PDN , and ASMP , and is held in museum collections across the U.S. Kiliii has taken the stage at TEDx , toured with NatGeo Live , and now keynotes through Changemaker Talent , sharing the human stories behind his images. events.title: Opening Reception: Material as Witness
events.location: Oakland Photo Workshop, 312 8th St, Oakland
events.description: Join us for an opening reception for Material as Witness, curated by Rena Tom! Material as Witness explores the photograph as object, with its own material sensibility and narrative. Objects can trigger powerful emotions and memories, and materials carry their own associations based on tactile properties or cultural significance. The artists in the exhibition engage in image-making, in a truly hands-on sense, to subvert (or amplify) the power attributed to photos as documentary evidence and bearers of truth.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Following the finale of his acclaimed HBO series “How To with John Wilson”, NYC documentarian John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure. Concrete, the world's most widely used building material, appears as an ever-present life force, and John sets out to make the definitive documentary on the matter. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he decides to use the industry-approved Hallmark formula to tell this seemingly drab story and increase his movie’s appeal. But his foundation soon begins to crumble—literally and figuratively—as he struggles to balance artistic freedom with the realities of the modern film industry. events.title: Listening with a New Consciousness  A Group Imagery and Music Experience with Sophia Wang
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
What becomes possible when we truly listen?
This is a 2-hour introductory workshop in Imagery and Music — an experiential group practice inspired by the Bonny Method of Guided Imagery and Music (GIM), a recognized music-psychotherapy modality. You'll lie down, relax, and listen to two curated classical music programs that open space for inner imagery, emotion, and insight to surface. Then, you’ll give that experience form through a simple mandala drawing. No musical or art background is needed; the only requirement is a willingness to listen.
Most of the time, we listen to music. Here, we listen from inside it and music becomes less something you hear than somewhere you go.

During the evening, we will:
Enter a guided relaxation
- Experience two curated classical music journeys
- Create simple mandalas for integration — not as art, but as a way of catching what words would flatten (no experience needed)
- Share reflections (optional)
- Explore how Imagery and Music differs from just talking about our experiences

Rather than using words, this practice lets it arrive as image, color, weight, motion — the language the psyche actually speaks. No substance is involved, only music, deep relaxation, and attention. Yet the states it opens are real: the same expanded awareness Helen Bonny first observed in psychedelic sessions, reached through sound alone.

The Psychedelic Lineage:
GIM was developed by Helen Bonny directly out of her work using music to support LSD-assisted therapy at the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, where she joined the research team in 1969 alongside Stanislav Grof, Walter Pahnke, and Joan Kellogg. Bonny discovered that music, not the substance, was often the true catalyst for change. Facilitating sessions without the drug, she found that carefully selected classical music, combined with deep relaxation and verbal guidance, could open similar altered states and therapeutic imagery on its own. The mandala practice this evening traces to that same era, from Bonny's collaboration with Joan Kellogg, comparing inner imagery with the mandalas participants drew after their sessions.

Today, GIM's principles are widely recognized as foundational to modern psychedelic-assisted therapy,  informing how music is used to structure the arc of various psychedelic assisted therapies sessions, support emotional release, and facilitate integration.

For those in the KAP and psychedelic-assisted space
Whether you come as a client or a practitioner, this practice offers a structured, music-supported path for continued inner exploration and integration,  between sessions, or as a standalone depth practice.

This experience may resonate if you are:
- Curious about music and consciousness
- Seeking an experiential alternative to talk therapy
- Looking for new ways to integrate mystical or non-ordinary experiences
- Wanting to explore your inner world in a structured, safe way

No musical background is required — only a willingness to listen.
Please arrive no later than 7:10 pm. Doors will be locked to keep a safe container.

*This event series honors Helen Bonny's 1973 book Music and Your Mind: Listening with a New Consciousness, the popular work that introduced her method of music-centered inner exploration.

Teacher Bio: Sophia Wang is a violinist, board-certified music therapist (MT-BC), integration practitioner, and life coach whose work centers on music, imagery, and non-ordinary states of consciousness. With over a decade of clinical experience across oncology, palliative care, and mental health settings, she draws on Guided Imagery and Music, expressive arts, and depth-oriented inquiry to support emotional healing, insight, and meaningful change.
Sophia works with people across a wide range of inner terrain: those in cancer care or facing the end of life; people moving through grief, depression, or anxiety; and high-performing professionals and seekers drawn to deeper self-inquiry and the integration of transformative experiences. Her approach blends clinical training with creative exploration, emphasizing safety, pacing, and integration.
She holds an MA in Music Therapy from New York University and a BA in Violin Performance from Tongji University, and a Certificate in Psychedelic-Assisted Therapies and Research at the California Institute of Integral Studies (CIIS), and is an advanced trainee in the Bonny Method of Guided Imagery and Music.

events.title: City Arts & Lectures @ Sydney Goldstein Theater - Kyle MacLachlan in conversation with Jesse Hawthorne Ficks
events.location: Sydney Goldstein Theater
events.description: Event location: Sydney Goldstein Theater, 275 Hayes St in San Francisco. Black Bird Bookstore will be the onsite bookseller at this event. In his upcoming debut memoir Fictional Selves, cultural icon Kyle MacLachlan looks back at his off-beat journey in Hollywood. From his debut in David Lynch’s Dune, to his award-winning performance as as Special Agent Dale Cooper in Twin Peaks, to his recent viral social media stardom, MacLachlan reveals his complex relationship with fame, his relationships with iconic actors, and everything he learned along the way. Kyle MacLachlan has built a fascinating acting career, performing in everything from David Lynch’s Twin Peaks to the adaptation of the video game Fallout. In the process, he has become a beloved cultural icon. MacLachlan’s 1984 film debut was the starring role in Lynch’s Dune. He would go on to work with the experimental director on multiple projects, including the classic film Blue Velvet. For his performance as Special Agent Dale Cooper in Twin Peaks, MacLachlan won a Golden Globe and gained international fame. Over the next few decades, MacLachlan brought his unique talent to a wide variety of movies, including The Doors, Showgirls, and the live-action adaptation of The Flintstones. MacLachlan also became a sought after guest star for popular television shows, including How I Met Your Mother, Law & Order SVU, Sex and the City, and Portlandia. More recently, he has gained a new group of fans through his award-winning performance in the show Fallout and the crime comedy show The Lowdown. When not acting, MacLachlan co-founded the winery Pursued by Bear, co-created the podcasts What Are We Even Doing? and Varnamtown, and became a viral session on TikTok and Instagram. In his upcoming debut memoir Fictional Selves, MacLachlan looks back at his off-beat journey in Hollywood. Through beautiful storytelling, MacLachlan traces his many iconic roles, his relationship with fame, and his iconic artistic collaborators, revealing details of his career and the lessons he has learned over the past fifty years. Jesse Hawthorne Ficks is the Film History Coordinator at the Academy of Art University in San Francisco, a member of the San Francisco Bay Area Film Critics Circle, and has been a guest professor at Chapman University. He is Film Festival Critic for 48 Hills and is a frequent co-presenter with local festivals, including the San Francisco International LGBTQ+ Film Festival, hosted by Frameline. For 25 years, Ficks has curated and hosted MOViES FOR MANiACS, “a film series celebrating underrated and overlooked cinema, in a neo-sincere manner.” A limited number of tickets include a copy of MacLachlan’s new book, Fictional Selves. If your ticket comes with a book and you are unable to attend this event, please call Black Bird Bookstore at (415) 742-5203 to arrange for pick-up. Books are available for you to collect at 4541 Irving Street in San Francisco up to 7 days following the event. Photo by Sophy Holland

events.title: Bella Kay
events.location: The Independent, 628 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117
events.description: Bella Kay has quickly emerged as one of the most emotionally resonant new stars in pop. Bella writes songs that come alive with intimacy and ache, exploring heartache, alienation, and survival with refreshing honesty and messiness. Her music is bare-faced and gutsy, delivered with a powerful, timeless voice atop a sound that blends fuzzy alternative-pop with the tender guitar hooks. On her debut album, My Reckless Abandon, the 20-year-old songwriter goes on a journey of self-acceptance and introspection amidst messy highs and lows. Across 13 tracks, she navigates her relationship to herself and others with the characteristic wit and candor established on previously released singles like “Promise?” and the smash hit “iloveitiloveitiloveit,” both included here. Executive produced by Idarose (Becky G, Suki Waterhouse, Joji) and recorded between New York and Los Angeles throughout 2026, My Reckless Abandon is a leap forward in production and shows how Bella is swiftly growing as a songwriter. Desire is a recurring theme, and Bella is often torn between body and brain. Her lust is barely contained on the opening rocker “Blur,” and she’s matter-of-fact on “swu,” beginning the song with the declaration, “I want to have sex with you.” But at the same time, she confides that intimacy can lead to terrifyingly vulnerable possibilities: “What if we do/And you decide/That you don’t want me?” Even if she has moved through life and love with moments of Reckless Abandon, Bella handles several subjects with the utmost care. “Sleep For Dinner” is a ballad that discloses patterns of restrictive eating and body dysmorphia and confronts the intrusive and obsessive mental imprisonment that can accompany these conditions. “How can something meant to keep you alive/Keep you from living,” she asks. “A Father's Lament” opens with a sample from Bella’s real-life dad and offers advice on how to move through a cruel world as a person of color. “Girls like you can’t be proud/Humble/Smart /And patient/Live those words like they’re sacred/You’re black baby girl/Don’t waste it.” At the end of the song, Bella hopes that future generations of innocents will be spared from so much pain. On the closing track, “i deserve better.,” Bella explores how low self-esteem may have unconsciously led her to rationalize poor treatment in the past (as on the hazy “tongue”). “I’m not perfect, not ever,” she concedes, but after countless times fighting for someone who wouldn’t do the same, she finally understands her worth. Born in Houston, Bella spent her childhood moving frequently, criss-crossing Texas with her siblings and parents, who work in the travel industry. Beyond a brief stint in homeschooling, she frequently played the role of “new girl,” relying on humor to adapt to evolving social dynamics that could be strained or exclusionary for a young bi-racial girl. Along the way, Bella got to know her own inner world very well. “With all those moves, I didn't have time to lose myself in friends,” she says. “I had to have a strong relationship with myself.” Music and writing were constants throughout the upheaval. When Bella wasn’t singing in choir or performing in musical theater productions, she was blasting pop music through her earbuds and penning novellas into her phone. The family moved to Austin when Bella entered junior high school, in hopes of finding an environment that embraced creativity and was more accepting of blended families. Around the same time, during COVID, forthright songwriters like Olivia Rodrigo and Lizzy McAlpine encouraged her to combine her artistic passions. "My dad, who always encouraged us to pursue our passions, bought me a starter guitar,” she says. “And I literally never stopped.” She taught herself to play guitar using YouTube tutorials, and after a year or so, introduced herself as a songwriter at her high school open mic nights. Confidence bolstered by a positive reception, Bella continued writing songs that channeled the sadness, frustration, and pleasures of her life. By the end of her first year of college, Bella found herself at a crossroads. Unsure if she wanted to continue pursuing pre-law, she decided to give music a serious shot. “I had so many songs to write after going through a terrible breakup,” she says, noting, wryly, “I got a lot better at guitar.” Throughout the summer of 2025, Bella shared her music on TikTok with increased determination and intention. This attitude is typical of Bella: she takes every no or disappointment as a personal challenge and works tirelessly until she emerges on the other side, saying, “Look what I can do.” She’s a fighter, a doer, and she shines unapologetically. The song that went viral in August was “The Sick,” an unblinking ballad about pining for a person who is no good for you. “The Sick” has since surpassed 210 million streams across streaming platforms and over 2.6 billion TikTok views. In November 2025, the track appeared on Bella’s debut EP, November 2025’s sick to my stomach, which also featured the melancholic “Lonely.” On both, Bella turns her lens on herself with remarkable nuance, embracing complex feelings like shame rather than brushing them aside. “Just because I felt it doesn’t make it true,” she says. “Putting those thoughts into song gives it perspective as just something I felt at a moment in time.” In February 2026, Bella shared her second EP, a couple minutes out. Each song is deep in the throes of yearning, from lingering thoughts of a lost love to desiring something but feeling incapable of having it. “I can't treat you right if I treat myself like this,” she sings with disarming honesty on the slow-burning “Steady.” “I need to get better, swear I'm working on it.” Longing obliterates her better judgment on “iloveitiloveitiloveit,” an earworm about throwing romantic caution to the wind. “I'm very in tune with my emotions when it comes to relationships,” Bella says. “I know when something is bad for me, but I'm pretty much always going to do it anyway.” Listeners could relate—the song’s meteoric ascent has resulted in Bella’s Hot 100 debut, an American Music Awards nomination for “Song of the Summer,” and over 445 million streams and 3.3 billion views across 1.3 million TikTok creates to date. The final EP in the trio of three packs was May’s are you mad at me? The titular question comes from the provocative “Say it Say,” in which Bella pleads with someone to stop avoiding confrontation. At the same time, she looks in the mirror on “Promise?” and recognizes that her fears of rejection are preventing her from being honest about her all-consuming crush. “When people hear my music, I want them to recognize themselves and their own experiences,” Bella says. “Those tracks are the ones that I listen to one thousand times—songs are better when they’re honest.”

events.title: Being Here: Meditation and Dharma with Milo
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Being Here is a weekly gathering guided by seasoned Dharma Teacher Milo Burn.
The gathering is to celebrate silence and stillness, to study, practice and realize Buddhist teachings, and for dynamic inquiry into mindfulness, freedom, and compassion in the midst of daily life. So much of our lives are oriented toward becoming. Being Here offers a regular space to pause that momentum and explore what becomes possible when we give our attention to simply being here.
Through meditation, heart teachings, and conversation, we practice bringing this quality of being into the rest of our lives. The emphasis is on direct experience rather than technique. Think: less following a recipe and more hanging out in your grandma’s kitchen!
Come to practice, listen, ask questions, and spend time in a space devoted to being here.
For more about Milo, including extended biography, upcoming retreats, and 1-1 guidance, visit: www.boundlessness.org
Schedule 10:30 AM: Arrive and settle, we start the sit at 10:40, and it’s okay to enter quietly after this time if you are late.
Participation Norms
RSVP on Luma or drop in
No formal membership or prior experience required
Questions, reflections, and inquiry are encouraged
What to Bring
Bring a zafu if you prefer this to the provided chairs and pillows
Suggested Donation / Dana
Being Here is offered on a dana basis, as an expression of generosity and shared responsibility. Contribute according to your means and inspiration.
The Commons
Being Here creates a weekly place at The Commons to practice being alongside becoming.
It is part of the larger rhythm of rituals, relationships, and creative life that make The Commons a civic hearth for personal becoming and creative expression.

events.title: Milton's Paradise Lost
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: A Clio's 4-week seminar · Have you always wanted to read John Milton’s Paradise Lost (1674) and never gotten around to it? Victoria Kahn and Clio's have created a four-week seminar, running 11am-1pm on Saturdays Sept. 12, 19, 26 and October 3, just for you. With the exception of Shakespeare, Milton is the greatest writer of the English Renaissance; unlike Shakespeare, Milton was a sexual and political radical who directly addressed, in dazzlingly beautiful and difficult poetry, all the important issues of his day: the existence of evil; the nature of God, free will, love and human sexuality; the problem of tyranny and the justification of political rebellion; the essence of consciousness; the relationship between pagan antiquity and Christianity, and between poetry and faith. You will be expected to read three books of Paradise Lost every week. Each class will include a brief lecture as well as group discussion, which will focus on close reading of individual passages of poetry. It’s recommended that you read the entire poem once through before the beginning of the class if you have time. It is not necessary to attend all four classes, though the seminar will be better for you and everyone else if you do. Victoria Kahn is Professor emerita of English and Comparative Literature at UC, Berkeley.

events.title: John Baccigaluppi - Making Music
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: John Baccigaluppi discusses Making Music , in conversation with SASAMI Groundbreaking conversations with the music producers behind the most successful recording artists on the planet, collected from Tape Op magazine “ Tape Op magazine is a font of information and great stories about the craft and history of making records. It’s about making music from the microphone up.” —Brian Eno (David Bowie, U2, Talking Heads) John Baccigaluppi will be joined in conversation with musician SASAMI. THIS BOOK IS A COLLECTION OF INTERVIEWS with people who have made records with some of the biggest names in music. Along the way, they might be engineering the recordings, picking the songs, guiding the singers, picking the best takes of songs, balancing egos, fixing the lyrics, booking the studio time, buying lunch, playing instruments, pushing artists further, writing or cowriting the songs, selecting the musicians to use, overseeing the mixes, and many other tasks. Making records is always a combination of many skills and goals, and the producer needs to have what it takes to make the session productive and the music compelling. In this book, interviewees include people who have worked with the Beatles, the Rolling Stones, Public Enemy, Taylor Swift, Doja Cat, Bob Dylan, P!nk, U2, Peter Gabriel, Emmylou Harris, Willie Nelson, Wu-Tang Clan, David Bowie, T.Rex, Johnny Cash, the Moody Blues, Aretha Franklin, Amy Winehouse, Paul McCartney, Dolly Parton, Duran Duran, the Replacements, Christina Aguilera, Alicia Keys, Kendrick Lamar, Tom Petty, Thin Lizzy, and Sabrina Carpenter. And that’s just the beginning of the credits these producers—Brian Eno, Finneas, Glyn Johns, Hank Shocklee, Jack Antonoff, Joe Boyd, Jon Brion, Lee Scratch Perry, Lynda Perry, Mark Ronson, RZA, Sasami, Steve Lillywhite, Susan Rogers, Sylvia Massy, T Bone Burnett, and many others—collectively hold. All of these interviews come from the pages of Tape Op magazine, founded in 1996 by editor Larry Crane. Over the last thirty years, along with publisher John Baccigaluppi, Tape Op has become the world’s deepest archive of conversations about the art and science of recording music, and is still an active, print-based magazine with the highest circulation of any recording magazine in the world. “Tape Op is always full of joy for me. Real people making real music with real tools and very, very little snobbery. Old and new equally valued.” —Pete Townshend (The Who) “Tape Op is, without question, the leader in its field.” —Glyn Johns (Rolling Stones, The Who, The Beatles, Led Zeppelin) “What a wild ride Tape Op has been on! You’ve helped the music community in so many ways.” —Don Zientara (Inner Ear Studio, Fugazi, Minor Threat) “I’ve pretty much read every issue of Tape Op magazine since I’ve known of its existence many years ago. Tape Op is my inside track on the people who make the music that lives on my stereo. These are my heroes and my peers.” —Joe Chiccarelli (White Stripes, Elton John, Beck, U2, the Killers) ABOUT THE EDITORS LARRY CRANE (not appearing) was a home recordist and member of the band Vomit Launch in the 1980s before he moved to Portland, Oregon, where he opened a studio and founded Tape Op magazine in 1997—initially photocopied and hand-stapled. Crane’s Jackpot! recording studio has hosted R.E.M., Sonic Youth, Eddie Vedder, Pink Martini, Spoon, Death Cab for Cutie, and Built to Spill, and he has worked with Elliott Smith, the Go-Betweens, the Decemberists, Sleater-Kinney, Jenny Lewis, Quasi, She & Him, M. Ward, Moon Duo, Team Dresch, Stephen Malkmus, Jolie Holland, Jason Lytle, and the Walkabouts. JOHN BACCIGALUPPI is a producer, engineer, and studio owner; he met Larry Crane when he produced Vomit Launch’s third and fourth albums. He came aboard Tape Op in 1999 as the publisher, designer, and co-owner. Since then, Tape Op has become the largest-circulation recording magazine in the world. Baccigaluppi currently runs Panoramic House Studio and has worked with My Morning Jacket, Devendra Banhart, Kurt Vile, Cate Le Bon, Hurray for the Riff Raff, Feist, Deftones, Thee Oh Sees, Ty Segall, 7 Seconds, and Little Wings. Crane and Baccigaluppi have worked with some of the most important artists of the last thirty years, while also running a magazine that discusses the art of making records. events.description: Program & Event Overview Currently on view at Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio in Oakland, The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time brings together stories told through the work of Black currently and formerly incarcerated artists. Their work traces histories of enslavement and confinement alongside the realities of incarceration today, while carrying memory, endurance, and imagination toward something beyond them. Together, these works invite us to explore the space between captivity and liberation, to see differently, and to imagine a world beyond systems of punishment. Saturday, October 3 | 12:00–5:00 PM 12:00 PM | Gallery Opens On Saturday, inStudio will reopen for an afternoon of art, conversation, and community. Open Flow: Community Dialogue Throughout the afternoon, exhibition co-curators De’jon Joy and Christine Lashaw will host an open-flow community dialogue inside the gallery. Rather than a traditional panel, the gathering will create space for visitors to move through the exhibition, ask questions, sit in conversation, and reflect together on the histories, ideas, and possibilities held within the work. Currently incarcerated participating artists will also call into the gallery at various points throughout the day, creating opportunities for visitors to hear directly from artists whose work they are encountering on the walls. The weekend invites audiences not simply to view the exhibition, but to spend time inside its questions: to consider what we have inherited, what we have normalized, and what becomes possible when Black artists are given space to imagine beyond captivity.

events.title: Tiny Monster Show ~ Opening Reception

events.description: Whether or not you like monsters, one has to admit, most of us like a good scare now and then. The word Monster derives from the Latin monstrum, itself derived ultimately from the verb moneo (“to remind, warn, instruct, or foretell”). From this vantage point, monsters take on a new inspiring role, not to just scare us, but to inform us. So what can monsters teach us about our fears, our society and beyond? The Tiny Monster Show explores our fears so we can take a deeper look at what we’ve been suppressing and what we need to confront. From classical to political, The Tiny Monster Show gives space to capture, reveal, and maybe conquer those elements that keep us frozen in fear and hopefully shine a light on what it means to be human. Hopefully, you’ll experience a moment of laughter in recognition that you are more powerful than the monster wants you to think. events.title: Book Event with Mahmoud Khalil
events.location: First Congregational Church of Oakland
events.description: Join AROC Action and the Center for Constitutional Rights for a conversation with Palestinian organizer and writer Mahmoud Khalil on political repression, Palestine solidarity, and the fight against authoritarianism in the United States and around the world. The discussion will mark the publication of Khalil’s first book, No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention , a memoir drawing on his prison diary and recounting his arrest, incarceration, separation from his family, and continuing struggle against deportation. The book can be purchased for a discount with your ticket, or separately at retail value by clicking below. In March 2025, federal immigration agents arrested Khalil, a lawful permanent resident and prominent participant in the Palestine solidarity movement at Columbia University. He was held in immigration detention for 104 days while the federal government sought to deport him. Khalil continues to face removal proceedings while pursuing multiple legal challenges related to his arrest, detention, and targeting. In 2026, the Center for Constitutional Rights filed a lawsuit on his behalf challenging his detention and alleging a coordinated effort by government officials and far-right and pro-Israel groups including the Heritage Foundation, Betar, and Canary Mission to punish and intimidate Palestinian rights advocates. His case raises urgent questions about the collaboration of private and state actions to use immigration law, surveillance, institutional power, and state repression against political dissent. At a moment of expanding executive authority and intensified attacks on protest movements, this conversation will explore what Khalil’s experience reveals about the broader struggle to defend civil liberties, confront authoritarianism, and protect movements organizing for Palestinian freedom and collective liberation. Hosted by AROC Action and the Center for Constitutional Rights, the event will bring together Khalil’s personal story, his ongoing legal battles, and a wider conversation about how movements can resist political repression while continuing to organize for justice. Doors open at 12:30pm. Book signing will take place from 12:30pm to 1pm. Event will run from 1pm to 3pm. No one turned away for lack of funds. To request a free ticket please email info@arocaction.org with the subject line: "Ticket Request"

events.title: Désirée Zamorano with Linda González & Jennifer Nguyen - Amarisa's Cooking Pot
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Amarisa’s Cooking Pot: Tales of Life in All Its Wonders is a riveting collection whose worlds collide and connect between the fantastic and the ordinary. Désirée Zamorano allows readers to explore this question beautifully, and memorably, long after the last page is turned. Désirée will be joined in conversation by Linda González, the author of Rest Like a Giant Tree , and Jennifer Nguyen, the soon-to-be author of Everything is Fine . Amarisa’s Cooking Pot: Tales of Life in All Its Wonders is a riveting collection whose worlds collide and connect between the fantastic and the ordinary. Startling in their breadth and depth, these stories range from the quietly desperate to the gloriously fantastical, representing Mexican American culture among the characters who are guided by gifts of enchantment or confronted with illusory events shaped by deeply human and enlightening emotions. Each story is dedicated to capturing something ineffable, an emotional truth, a moment of beauty or realization, a moment of calm, or a spark of fury. What does it mean to be alive in a capricious world? Désirée Zamorano allows readers to explore this question beautifully, and memorably, long after the last page is turned. “Zamorano’s collection of stories is a medley of surprises, heartbreak, and triumph. In these tales, Zamorano offers a feast both magical and stark, interweaving miracles and realities of working-class daily life amid the bonds of family—mothers and sons, daughters and grandmothers, lovers snatching tenderness in ambiguous spaces—and with deft language and precise, evocative style, lays open the complicated webbing connecting this community.” —Marcela Fuentes, author of Malas, Reforma National Book Award winner “How deft, vibrant, and heartfelt these stories are. I love the way they slip, subtly, from quiet domesticity to magic, then back again; I love even more how often the conduit for those shifts is a perfectly imagined mundane detail, such as an inherited cooking pot or a mother's shed strands of hair. And when these stories offer glimpses of wonder, they do so in order to give Zamorano's characters justice that the world denies them.” —Holly Goddard Jones, author of Antipodes: Stories and Girl Trouble: Stories In addition to her short stories, ranging from the gritty to the fantastical, Désirée Zamorano is also the author of the groundbreaking family saga, historical fiction novel Dispossessed . Her highly acclaimed literary novel, The Amado Women was re-released September 2025. An award-winning and Pushcart prize nominee short story writer, her work is an exploration of where cultures collide and connect and a representation of her Mexican American demographic. A selection of her work can be found in Alta , The Kenyon Review Online and Akashic’s South Central Noir . She is the senior fiction editor for Silk Road Press, and, up until the Eaton Canyon Fire, lived in Altadena for 26 years. Linda González (she/ella) is the author of four non-fiction books and has published many essays. Her most recent essay collection is Rest Like a Giant Tree: Be Happy in the Midst of So Much . She works tirelessly to write and support writing that enriches the current canon of literature, challenging the narrative that she cannot include Spanish in her work without explaining or italicizing it. She works with BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Color) writers to claim their voice. She currently lives in Pt. Richmond, the unceded land of the Ohlone nation. Jennifer Nguyen is a non-fiction writer based in Oakland, California. Her first book of personal essays, entitled Everything is Fine: Vietnamese American Notes , will be published in 2028. She is currently working on a book about abolishing institutional philanthropy, the field in which she works. She still types two spaces after every period and does not intend to stop. events.description: Discover your authentically funny voice in this engaging and fun writing workshop. The two-hour class will focus on personal narrative writing, aiming to explore and cultivate material for a comedic essay through writing exercises. Participants will learn the basics of humor writing and create material for a layered essay, rooted in time and place. She has published personal essays and created graphic stories in The San Francisco Chronicle, The Advocate, Spiralbound, Pacific Sun, North Bay Bohemian, SF/Arts, Whole Life Times, The Bold Italic, Curve Magazine and Narratively . As a freelance writer, her contributions have won three MarCom awards, and two Hermes Creative awards. Jenny’s comic strip, “Just Living Jenny” is published on Substack. She was a wonderful teacher and created a very safe space for everyone." — Jenn E. "Excellent class! We were encouraged to develop a strong story and do a lot of deep thinking. events.title: Real Social Connections
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
🌿 Description
Beyond small talk, social scripts, and the pressure to be a certain way.
An immersive half-day exploration of movement, playfulness, touch, authentic relating, and meaningful conversation in a trauma-informed space.

🌿 About This Gathering
Meaningful connection rarely happens by accident. It tends to emerge when we feel safe enough to slow down, be ourselves, and meet one another with curiosity.
This gathering is an invitation to explore what helps genuine connection emerge - not by performing, saying the "right" thing, or following a script, but by creating the conditions where we can be more present, playful, and authentic with ourselves and others.
At the heart of this gathering is a simple idea: connection deepens when we feel safe enough to be seen and expressed -not just the polished parts of ourselves, but also the parts we might usually hide or hold back. Through movement, play, somatic awareness, and guided conversations, we'll explore what happens when we let ourselves show up more fully and meet one another more deeply.
This is an evolving exploration of connection, community, and play. I'm excited to create a deep experience together and to see what becomes possible when we give ourselves more space to be ourselves and meet one another more fully.
My hope is that you'll leave with a deeper sense of connection to yourself and others, and maybe even with a new friend or two.

🕰 Flow / Schedule


💫 Who This Is For
This gathering is for anyone who longs for more genuine connection. It’s especially for people who sometimes struggle to connect, fit in, or feel like they truly belong; for those who appreciate a slower pace when getting to know others; and for anyone curious about moving beyond small talk, social performance, or the feeling that they need to say the “right” thing or show up in a certain way.
Rather than trying to “get connection right,” we’ll explore what naturally allows connection to emerge—through presence, play, movement, and authentic conversation.
Whether you're outgoing, introverted, or somewhere in between, you'll be invited to participate at your own pace. No previous experience is needed: just come as you are.

👥 Facilitator
Simone Giacometti is a somatic practitioner, psychedelic integration guide, and facilitator passionate about helping people heal, grow, and connect more deeply with themselves and others.
Originally trained as a scientist, Simone spent years working at the intersection of biology, technology, and program management before transitioning into healing work. Today, he supports people through one-on-one sessions that weave together trauma-informed healing, somatic practices, inner exploration, and psychedelic integration work to help people reconnect with themselves and grow into greater authenticity.
His group facilitation draws on somatics, authentic relating, nervous system awareness, and play to create spaces where people can slow down, be themselves, and feel more at home with others. (This gathering is fully substance-free and centered on movement, conversation, and connection.)

Learn more about Simone and his work at healwithsimone.com

events.title: Fear Not – William Rhodes Artist’s Talk with Gospel Choir Performance
events.location: Transmission Gallery, 770 West Grand Ave., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: Please join us for William Rhodes’ talk with gospel choir performance by the Dr. George W. Davis Senior Center Choir, music conductor and leader Kenneth Little Saturday, Oct 3rd starting at 2 pm This is part of a series of NEXUS SFBay events including the Caleb Dowdell performance with his piece, Our Prism of Dreams, starting at 1:30 pm just downstairs at Gearbox Gallery, performance about 15 minutes. William’s talk starts at 2 pm upstairs with the Dr. George W. Davis Senior Center Choir closing out the event with a Gospel Choir performance. See one or both at that galleries at 770 West Grand Ave in Oakland. More about Fear Not, William Rhodes’ solo exhibition at Transmission Gallery: William Rhodes’s sculptures on view incorporate objects that have been used, inherited, discarded, or found with elements he has carved himself. Trained early on as a furniture maker, he combines hand carved figures, flames and snakes with objects collected from a family home, photographs, hardware, tools, and other remnants of everyday life. Neon words signal from some pieces. The resulting works resemble shrines or memorials, but they remain grounded in the ordinary. Religious symbols appear alongside household objects. A photograph might be surrounded by carved waves, tools, hardware, animals, or religious symbols. A suitcase can become an architectural space. A toilet becomes the base of an unexpected monument. Things with little apparent value are carefully incorporated into elaborate constructions, their histories becoming part of the work. ​ Rhodes is equally interested in people; family, mentors, and leaders, as well as those who have been overlooked or treated as disposable, recognizing and elevating their presence in his work. By giving attention to these lives, enshrining and revering them, he considers how value is assigned and who gets remembered. The title Fear Not appears in the work as both a phrase and a kind of instruction. It can be read in relation to the religious imagery that runs throughout the sculptures, but it also takes on a morepersonal meaning. To look closely at lives and objects that are easily dismissed is, in its own way, an act of resistance to that dismissal.

events.description: Meet the artists of Big, Small, and Everything In Between and celebrate this group exhibition featuring five Bay Area muralists. Join us for an afternoon gathering and a closer look at how these artists bring the color, energy, and visual language of their public work into the gallery’s intimate setting. Free and open to the public. Julie Engelmann, based in Half Moon Bay, works across murals, paintings, and digital illustration. Using media ranging from acrylic on canvas to spray paint on large walls, she creates highly detailed and often surrealistic imagery, frequently drawing on historical themes and using color and composition to create new visual possibilities. Amos Goldbaum is a San Francisco–based visual artist known for his signature line drawings, which span canvases, large-scale murals, prints, and apparel. Inspired by the places and everyday scenes around him, his work combines multiple viewpoints, angles, and moments in time into cohesive compositions connected by a singular line. His murals can be found throughout the San Francisco Bay Area and in cities around the world, including New York, Los Angeles, Seattle, Tokyo, and Kathmandu. Liv Losee-Unger is a Bay Area muralist known for vibrant, nature-inspired, and community-centered art. With more than sixty public artworks completed across the United States and abroad, her detailed and colorful murals transform spaces through stories of flora, fauna, femininity, and human connection. Fernanda Martínez is an Oakland-based painter, muralist, and sculptor whose vibrant, expressive work draws from memories and observations of nature. Born and raised in Mexico City, she moved to the Bay Area in 2015, where she has developed an experimental and intuitive practice exploring the emotional depth of color, form, pattern, and texture. Her work spans painting, sculpture, murals, and public art, transforming her distinctive visual language across two- and three-dimensional forms. Martinez has exhibited her paintings and sculptures in galleries and has collaborated on numerous public art projects for businesses, nonprofit organizations, and community-focused and affordable housing developments. Deirdre Weinberg is a multidisciplinary artist with deep ties to the San Francisco Bay Area, working across murals, public art, and studio practice. Her evolving work currently focuses on climate change, using a limited black-and-white palette to explore landscapes, seascapes, and airscapes with a sense of urgency and starkness. Whether creating work in public spaces or the studio, Weinberg seeks to build community, connect with viewers, and inspire conversation, reflection, and new perspectives. events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A groundbreaking, multilayered mind-body-spirit approach to empowerment and healing. In this transformative guide, revered psychologist Laurel Parnell presents Multidimensional Integrative Healing (MDIH)—a powerful new method developed to help readers reclaim their True Self when traditional recovery isn't enough. “ Come back to the version of who you know yourself to truly be. ” If you've ever experienced a pivotal life event that felt as though it broke you apart and left you struggling to recover, Dr. Parnell understands. After the tragic death of her son, when expert knowledge in trauma recovery wasn't enough to reclaim her True Self, she embarked on a journey that led to the development of a whole new approach. Through this comprehensive guide—integrating transpersonal psychology, Eastern spiritual practices, and energetic traditions—readers learn to: Access resources that can be called on for help when needed Engage energetic sovereignty to stand in your own power Release energies that simply do not belong to you Align with inner knowing and innate healing intelligence Explore five dimensions of reality: physical, emotional, psychological, somatic, and spiritual Dr. Parnell writes, “MDIH recognizes there are different dimensions of reality that exist and can be accessed for healing.” Instead of remaining stuck in old patterns or limiting beliefs, discover how to use these dimensions to move toward wholeness, reclaiming the version of yourself you know you were meant to be. This book guides you to find resources, engage your sovereignty, and finally release what isn't yours. “ Wise and visionary. Laurel is a pioneer in healing and includes the essential dimension of the sacred that has been missing for so many. ” ―Jack Kornfield, author of A Path with Heart and All in This Together “ Releasing What Isn’t Yours invites us to explore the many layers of experience that often go unrecognized in everyday life—and in psychotherapy—yet influence us in profound ways. Laurel Parnell is our deeply insightful, wise, and courageous guide whose devotion to healing and illuminating the truth are revealed in this inspirational personal and professional journey to uncover the ways we are inextricably connected across time and space. When these energy patterns go unrecognized, we may become stuck in the chaos and rigidity of the impaired integration of unresolved trauma. Introducing us to the origins and practical steps of her approach of Multidimensional Integrative Healing, the chapters of this book provide useful ways of understanding layers of experience—whether they are mechanisms or metaphors of the mind—that we can tap into to cultivate post-traumatic growth and resilience in our liberated lives. ” ―Daniel J. Siegel, MD, New York Times -bestselling author of Aware and Mind Laurel Parnell, PhD , is the executive director of the Parnell Institute and the developer of Attachment-Focused EMDR, Resource Tapping, and Multidimensional Integrative Healing. A clinical psychologist and expert in trauma recovery, she has trained thousands of clinicians in the United States and abroad. She is the author of several books, including Attachment-Focused EMDR, A Therapist's Guide to EMDR, and Rewiring the Addicted Brain. Find the author at www.drlaurelparnell.com or on social media. events.title: Paul Sussman's DID SHE REALLY SAY TANTRUM YOGA
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception September 26 (Please do not bring infants to the show) The world is reeling towards chaos! Wars! Fires! Corruption! The Death of Democracy! It’s an all-out Emergency!!! THIS TIME IS DIFFERENT! This isn’t just a blurb – ask around. It’s time to get out of denial, stare down the grim reality, and… party ? There’s nothing like an encounter with a mysterious stranger at a party: take a risk, lay yourself bare, and – just maybe – find a tiny bit of hope and laughter amidst the chaos. And so many questions along the way! Starting with something safe… “Can we just not… like… talk about Fascism?” “Is the right to eat beef really in the 2nd Amendment? “ If you make it past the chit chat, the questions go deeper: “Maybe it’s time to drop the whole notion of Reality?” “Is it already too late?” And eventually… “Why the two of us, right here, right now?” “What’s next?” Paul Sussman’s latest creation tosses us into the center of the swirl, and offers us lifelines to laugh, to cry, to hope, and to act. “One of the most authentic presentations of humanity I’ve ever seen” “Paul has entered some other zone… of deep thoughtfulness and connection.” ” I laughed, I cried, and I left carrying so much to think about. The way you wove together themes of grief, anger, and how we’re all navigating this moment in time was powerful and deeply resonant.” “You have outdone yourself in this medium –your depth and candor, scope from the personal to the epochal, agile shifting from gentle or scathing satire to the existentially terrifying. I am stunned into silence pondering the implications you invite audiences to consider for this moment.” “You avoid easy answers and platitudes. The threats and the stakes in play have an urgency and brutality that you confront head on, with humility and honesty.” “I loved, loved, loved, your show. Such courageous saying out loud all the things we think, and in such a funny way. Thank you” “This show was so great — so of the moment, so hilarious and at moments horrific at once. Bravo!” Paul Sussman has written and performed a series of solo pieces through the eyes of Neanderthals, road-ragers, insects, Anabaptists, cannibals, and others who persist in the search for meaning. He’s entertained and provoked in theater festivals from Fundy to Fresno. Paul developed his unique approach to melodrama and farce through decades of work in financial management with Bay Area nonprofit organizations. “Did She Really Say Tantrum Yoga ?” is his third full-length solo show (following “The Wrong Kind of Pessimism” and “Beyond Belief”), entitling him to refer to himself in the third person. Sussman has worked for over 40 years to champion affordable housing development in San Francisco and received the Catherine A. Baur Lifetime Achievement Award from the Non-Profit Housing Association of Northern California in 2017. David Ford (director) has been collaborating on new and unusual theater for three decades and has been an artist-in-residence at The Marsh for most of that time. events.location: Books Inc. Mountain View, 317 Castro St, Mountain View, CA 94041
events.description: Books Inc. welcomes bestselling and National Book Award-winning author Sabaa Tahir to celebrate Empire – The gripping conclusion to the action-packed, ruthless, and romantic fantasy duology that began with HEIR. This ticketed event includes a copy of the book with each ticket. The first 25 ticket holders will receive a special VIP swag bag courtesy of Penguin Random House. This event will include a signing line. All books purchased as your ticket can be signed and personalized , and guests will also be able to have up to four more of books signed! More about EMPIRE: A falling empire. An ancient evil. A lost homeland. A lie that could destroy the world. In the crumbling Martial Empire, crown prince Quil Farrar and his aunt, Empress Helene, are losing a war against the vicious Kegari horde. Quil's armies dwindle, his faith falters, and the woman he loves vanished months ago, leaving him brokenhearted. Torn between his duty to his people and his desire to discover Sirsha's fate, Quil embarks on a dangerous quest for aid--from the most treacherous of allies. Sirsha Westering finds herself tethered to Div, an ancient evil unleashed by a terrible tragedy. Div delights in tormenting Sirsha, hungering for her magical heart. Even as Sirsha struggles for control of her own fate, she is desperate to shield Quil from Div's destructive power. But Div won't release Sirsha without a fight. To earn her freedom, Sirsha must uncover Div's past--and face horrors in her own. Cero bet-Dafra, former right hand of the Kegari leader, Aiz, now finds himself pitted against her. As Aiz slips further into violence and delusion, Cero must discover if his people have any hope of a future or if they're condemned to an unending cycle of violence. His journey will force him to confront hidden truths, ancient secrets, and a lie that could destroy the world. In Empire , #1 New York Times bestselling author Sabaa Tahir returns to the expansive world of fury and vengeance of Heir, weaving a story of legacy and rebellion, loyalty and freedom, and what it means to confront the monsters that lurk within us all. SABAA TAHIR is a former newspaper editor who grew up in California's Mojave Desert at her family's eighteen-room motel. There, she spent her time devouring fantasy novels, listening to thunderous indie rock, and playing guitar and piano badly. Her #1 New York Times bestselling An Ember in the Ashes series has been translated into more than thirty-five languages, and the first book in the series was named one of TIME's 100 Best YA Books of All Time. Tahir's contemporary novel, All My Rage, won the National Book Award for Young People's Literature, the Michael L. Printz Award, and the Boston Globe-Horn Book Award for Fiction and Poetry.

events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. This all-star ensemble, led by EMMY and Grammy Award-winning producer/drummer Vince Wilburn Jr., features such luminaries as Daryl Jones, Robert Irving III, Mino Cinelu, Antoine Roney, Keyon Harrold, DJ Logic, and more. Celebrating the Miles Davis Centennial: M.E.B. “Miles Electric Band” Vince Wilburn Jr. – drums (Miles Davis alumnus); Darryl Jones (Miles Davis alumnus) – bass; Robert Irving III (Miles Davis alumnus) – keyboards; Jean-Paul Etienne Bourelly – guitar; Munyugo Jackson (Miles Davis alumnus) and Mino Cinelu (Miles Davis alumnus) – percussion; Antione Roney or Gary Thomas (Miles Davis alumnus) – tenor & soprano saxophone; Keyon Harold or Sean Jones – trumpet; DJ Logic (Jason Kibler) – turntables. events.title: LIVE MUSIC: The Sleeves, Fred Frith
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: The Sleeves The Sleeves are the duo of Jack Cooper and Tara Cunningham, both likely known to you as one half of Modern Nature. Following an all-instrumental Mossy Tapes release last November, Cooper and Cunningham have recorded 10 new songs showcasing their vocal and guitar interplay with only the faintest echoes of prior efforts (individually or collectively), representing a fully realized leap forward from their largely improvised debut. 'The Sleeves' is a somewhat counter intuitive take on the guitar/vocal duo formula (provided you think there is such a thing) though it's not nearly as simplistic as "the space between the notes" -- it would be the height of exaggeration to say an album this simultaneously expansive and incandescent is unprecedented. But it doesn't happen nearly often enough, either. Bandcamp | IG Fred Frith Multi-instrumentalist, composer, and improviser Fred Frith has been making noise of one kind or another for more than 50 years, starting with the rock collective Henry Cow, which he co-founded with Tim Hodgkinson in 1968. Fred is best known as a pioneering electric guitarist and improviser, song-writer, and composer for film, dance and theater. Through bands like Art Bears, Massacre, Skeleton Crew, the Fred Frith Guitar Quartet, Cosa Brava, and the FF Trio he has stayed close to his roots in rock and folk music while branching out in many other directions. His compositions have been performed by ensembles ranging from Eclipse Quartet and the Bang on a Can All Stars to Concerto Köln and Galax Quartet, from the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra to the ROVA and Arte Sax Quartets, from Sleepytime Gorilla Museum and Ground Zero to the Glasgow Improvisers’ Orchestra. Film music credits include the acclaimed documentaries Rivers and Tides , Leaning into the Wind , and Tracing Light , directed by Thomas Riedelsheimer; The Tango Lesson , Yes and The Party by Sally Potter; Middle of the Moment by Nicolas Humbert and Werner Penzel; as well as Penzel’s Zen for Nothing , Peter Mettler’s Gods, Gambling and LSD , and the award-winning (and Oscar-nominated) Last Day of Freedom , by Nomi Talisman and Dee Hibbert-Jones. Composing for dance throughout his long career, Fred has worked with Rosalind Newman and Bebe Miller in New York, François Verret and Catherine Diverrès in France, and Amanda Miller and the Pretty Ugly Dance Company over the course of many years in Germany, as well as composing for two documentary films on the work of Anna Halprin. Theater credits include François Chat’s Setaccio and François-Michel Pesenti’s Théâtre du Point Aveugle in Marseille, where he spent six months in 1990 working with “jeunes rockers en chômage des quartiers défavorisés” on the opera Helter Skelter . Fred has performed works by and sometimes alongside composers John Luther Adams, Gavin Bryars, Sylvie Courvoisier, Alvin Curran, George Lewis, Annea Lockwood, René Lussier, Jose Maceda, Meredith Monk, Pauline Oliveros, Terry Riley, and Christian Wolff; improvised with Lotte Anker, Derek Bailey, Han Bennink, Peter Brötzmann, Lol Coxhill, Janet Feder, gabby fluke-mogul, Tim Hodgkinson, Joëlle Léandre, Phil Minton, Ikue Mori, Butch Morris, Bob Ostertag, Evan Parker, Zeena Parkins, Paula Sanchez, Susana Santos Silva and Camel Zekri, to name a few; collaborated with classical virtuosi Evelyn Glennie, Katia Labèque, Viktoria Mullova, and Werner Bärtschi; and—as session musician—recorded on albums by, for example, Brian Eno, The Residents, Robert Wyatt, The Swans, Violent Femmes, Material, Negativland, John Zorn, Matthew and the Unfortunates, and Half Japanese. He is currently performing solo and with Normal (home-made instrument duo with Sudhu Tewari) and Frelonia (with Lotte Anker and Núria Andorrà), as well as in countless combinations of his favorite co-conspirators. The recipient of Italy’s Demetrio Stratos Prize for his life’s work in experimental music and an honorary doctorate from the University of Huddersfield in his home county of Yorkshire, Fred taught for twenty years at the legendary epicenter of American experimental music, Mills College in Oakland, California; as well as co-directing (with Alfred Zimmerlin) the improvisation master’s program at the Musik Akademie in Basel, Switzerland. He is the subject of Nicolas Humbert and Werner Penzel’s much loved Step Across the Border , cited by Cahiers du Cinéma as one of the 20th century’s hundred most influential films. events.title: ROYA
events.location: The Independent, 628 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117
events.description:
ROYA is an electronic/dance-pop duo from Aarhus, Denmark, formed by Line Gade and Sebastian Igens. Line's distinctive vocals and introspective lyrics merge with Sebastian's bold, syncopated productions to create music that is both emotionally resonant and playfully inventive.

Spontaneity drives their process: tracks often start as live experiments, offhand samples, or fleeting ideas, evolving into instinctive, genre-blurring compositions.

In just a year, ROYA has built a global community – THE ROYALS – with over 3 million followers across platforms, and 90+ million streams. Following sold-out European tours, including notable performances in the UK, Germany, and most recently a tour in Australia.

ROYA’s creativity extends beyond music. Their “BOY (Zacaria)” pre-save campaign turned fans into co-creators: for every pre-save, the duo moved 100 meters from their studio, culminating in a surreal live show inside an Icelandic ice cave.

Their latest single, “Just Talk,” went viral before release. A 90-second teaser sparked a fan-led countdown, amassing over 10 million views and a million likes. The track’s message – finding strength in vulnerability – resonates deeply: “silence cannot keep you safe; don't wear your secrets like a holy crown.”

Through sound and imagery, ROYA blend sincerity with playfulness. Their songwriting is “fluid, almost intuitive, even spiritual – we always follow the first impulse and trust the process.” In 2026, they’ll play a summer tour in Europe followed by a North American tour before returning to their home country, Denmark, to play their biggest homecoming concerts so far—continuing a journey guided by instinct, fueled by fans, and fearless in following the flow and trusting the process.

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.

events.description: Independent reporter Denise Sullivan brings the SF Lives series to Bird & Beckett for a Sunday morning livestream. This month’s guest is Dr. Saidah Leatutufu-Burch. We expect a wide-ranging discussion on the legacy of local Black history, community organizing, economic justice and the November San Francisco ballot. Dr. Sai (Sy) is a Black and Sāmoan San Franciscan, organizer, cultural orator, economic mobility strategist, and liberationist. She is the Founder of Economic Emancipation LLC. and SLB Strategies—a social impact-focused consulting firm committed to equipping organizations with the tools and strategies necessary to drive sustainable change and achieve bold impact. Her work is guided by a core belief: “Liberate with love. Transform with power.” The SFLives Project, a series of candid conversations with San Francisco’s artists, activists and free thinkers, was conceived as a print media column by Denise Sullivan for the San Francisco Examiner where it ran from 2018-2022, then transitioned into a live-streamed conversation, produced by Jenna Littlejohn, for Bird & Beckett.
