events.title: Death Café with Christine Comaford, End-of-Life Doula
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: EOLPeace is holding a community gathering at Book Passage to explore death and the dying process. We will follow the format of Death Café, which was created by Jon Underwood in London approx. 12 years ago. It is a gently moderated conversation where all experiences are welcome, and tea and cookies will be served. Each month we come together to explore the sacredness of our mortality through a new theme. We Follow The Death Cafe Guidelines: Confidentiality: Everything Shared Is Private Or Not For Attribution. Acceptance: We Welcome All Experiences And Only Give Advice If Asked. Respect: All Perspectives Are Honored. Sharing: Everyone Has An Opportunity To Speak. If you know anyone who has experienced a death recently, is supporting a loved one through the death process, and/or is simply curious to demystify death and explore what it means to them, all are welcome. We will have plenty of wonderful book recommendations about death and the grieving process on display and available for purchase at the meeting. Want email reminders? Visit www.eolpeace.com . Christine Comaford's Bio: For 25+ years Christine has had the honor to walk 60+ people through their death process. She views death as a graduation after a life well-lived. This guides the work she does with patients and their families to release fear and anxiety, regrets, guilt, shame, and to do their forgiveness work. Along the way, her patients complete unfinished business (usually around relationships and communication). The result is a peaceful death. Christine’s Experience: INELDA & EOLPC-TRAINED END OF LIFE DOULA EOLPC TRAINED PSYCHEDELIC CARE CERTIFIED REIKI MASTER CERTIFIED NEURO LINGUISTIC PROGRAMMING MASTER SHAMANIC & INDIGENOUS WISDOM PRACTITIONER AFFILIATED WITH UCSF PALLIATIVE CARE, BY THE BAY HEALTH AND ANX HOSPICE Christine Comaford - photo courtesy of self. Event details: This event will be hosted by EOLPeace at Book Passage's Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.title: Gary Wolf with Kevin Kelly - The Quantified Self
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Science has given us tools and methods that allow us to observe things that were once imperceptible—and this book shows what we can learn when we use them to look at ourselves. “This book is a perfect roadmap to how to actually do personal science… [It outlines] what one needs to do to [answer] questions that matter… whether about a chronic degenerative disease or some other challenge.” - Eli Pollard, renowned patient advocate and Executive Director, World Parkinson Coalition Written by science journalist Gary Wolf, co-founder of the Quantified Self movement, this book teaches readers how to use proven scientific methods to answer their own health questions. At a time when trust in expertise is fractured and people are divided not just politically but over how to know what’s true, The Quantified Self makes the case that science belongs to everyone—and proves it by putting the method in the reader’s hands. Wolf teaches ten reasoning patterns adapted from the history of scientific practice and illustrates them with dozens of personal narratives. Across chapters on pain, mood, cognition, sleep, digestion, heart health, and hormones, readers learn a practical method for answering the health questions that matter most to them. “This book is a gift to anyone who has ever wanted to take their life seriously as a site of learning. It is a profoundly practical, clear, kind, hard-earned manual for self-research, and a foundational starting point for current and future health scientists.” - Eric Hekler, PhD, Professor of Public Health and Design, UC San Diego “You are in charge of your own well-being. That could sound like a threat, but it’s really a promise. What is important to you? What mystery are you trying to solve? What’s a hunch you want to test? Quantified Self: Learning to Observe will give you the tools, language, and strategies you need to reason your way to a better life.” - Susannah Fox, author of Rebel Health: A Field Guide to the Patient-led Revolution in Medical Care and former CTO of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services "Most self-tracking books promise miracles. This one promises something more useful: a method. These experts have distilled nearly two decades of the Quantified Self community into a working guide for asking better questions about your own body and getting answers. The quietly radical claim here — that careful observation, not better sensors, is what turns data into understanding — will be useful to everyone trying to learn more about their health." - Harlan M. Krumholz, MD, founder of the Yale Center for Outcomes Research and Evaluation and author of The Expert Guide to Beating Heart Disease Gary Wolf writes about science and technology. A former executive editor of Wired Digital and contributing editor at Wired magazine, he cofounded the Quantified Self movement in 2008. His first book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe , will be published by Workman in October, 2026. He currently works with the Personal Science Research Group to build tools, develop methods, and publish case studies that support small scale empirical science. He lives in Berkeley, California. Kevin Kelly is Senior Maverick at Wired, an award-winning magazine he co-founded Wired in 1993. He is co-chair of The Long Now Foundation , a membership organization that champions long-term thinking. He is founder of the popular Cool Tools website, which has been reviewing tools daily for 20 years. He is also the author of multiple best-selling books about the future of technology. His newest is Excellent Advice for Living , a book of 450 modern proverbs for a pretty good life. He is best known for his radical optimism. Gary Wolf - photo courtesy of the publicist; Kevin Kelly - photo credit: Christopher Michel Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Everyone wants more from you right now. Leadership wants speed, AI, new tools, more output with the same people. Your team wants clarity, a say, and a little more time. You're in the middle, doing most of the deciding, most of the communicating, most of the steadying.
This is a 90-minute working session, not a lecture. A room of managers with the same job as you, working on what's actually on your plate.
WHO IT'S FOR: Managers and team leads taking a team through AI rollouts, restructuring, new systems, fast growth, or priorities that keep shifting. People leaders holding the team's worries while still accountable for delivery.
LEAVE WITH: A clear read of where leadership, you, and your team each sit in the change, and what each one needs. One sentence to say up this week. One thing to give your team. And having been heard by people who do your job.
COME WITH: One real situation you're leading through right now. We work solo first, then in pairs where your partner listens and doesn't advise, then in small groups of five. What's said in the room stays in the room.

events.description:
What becomes possible when you design with emotions at the center, not around them?
Most systems change work is technically significant but often lacks an intentional emotional foundation. This 2-hour session treats that as a design challenge. We give you the tools, the frameworks, and the constraints. You bring the real material: your own experience of doing this work, the relational dynamics inside your teams, and the systems you're trying to change.
We move through four design layers: what you're actually feeling, what that creates between people, what emotional conditions make systems genuinely generative, and what all of it means when AI is part of the design.
What you'll takeaway:
Learnings on the language and embodiment of emotions.
Tangible relational tools that you can take back to your org.
Connection that can only come when you lead with vulnerability and emotion.

events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. 

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Nik Sharma is the bestselling author of cookbooks celebrated for blending culinary science with deeply personal storytelling: Season, The Flavor Equation, and Veg-Table. A former molecular biologist, Sharma brings a unique lens to the kitchen, where flavor is both a feeling and a formula. He serves as Editor in Residence at America's Test Kitchen, where he hosts the James Beard nominated YouTube show Flavor Forward with Nik Sharma, is a co-host of the show In the Test Kitchen on Netflix, and is a cast member on America’s Test Kitchen show on PBS. Sharma is the creator of the award-winning blog Nik Sharma Cooks (formerly A Brown Table), and his writing and photography have been featured in The San Francisco Chronicle, The New York Times, The Guardian, and The Wall Street Journal, among others. He lives in Los Angeles, California, where he's always dreaming up his next recipe. Paolo Lucchesi is the editorial director of Resy. Prior to Resy, he worked at the San Francisco Chronicle and Eater, both as an editor and reporter. He has written several books, including “ Flour + Water: Pasta ” and “ A Burger to Believe In .” He lives in San Francisco. Fundamentals of Flavor - Building on the science-forward thinking of The Flavor Equation and the accessibility of his award-winning Veg-Table , Nik Sharma’s latest cookbook brings fascinating technical know-how to exciting everyday recipes. In these pages, Sharma explores the four powerful elements of nature and their profound influence on how we cook, delving into such topics and dishes as: Fire: How caramelization deepens the flavor of Caramelized Shallot and Feta-Labneh Dip Earth: How salt's minerality brings crispness to Salt-Baked New Potatoes with Gochujang Vinaigrette Air: Why drying out cookie dough results in perfect Extra Rich Chocolate-Cinnamon Crinkle Cookies Water: Why sous vide is the best way to cook a hearty, tender loaf of Icelandic Rye Bread And much more. With more than 150 evocative photographs and 20+ infographics that simplify scientific principles for visual learners, this is a beautiful, foundation-building reference book for home cooks who approach their meals with a hunger for knowledge and big flavor.

events.title: Dr. Shefali - Raising Conscious Daughters & Raising Conscious Sons (SF)
events.location: Walt Disney Theater 104 Montgomery Street Presidio San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: Please join us in celebration of bestselling author Dr. Shefali and her compassionate and insightful new books, Raising Conscious Daughters & Raising Conscious Sons. Dr. Shefali will be joined by her co-hosts: Shirin Aryanpour, the founder of Illuminate Her Path, with more than 16 years of experience as a physical therapist, and Geno La Placa, an Executive Leadership and Life Coach, Speaker, and Retreat Facilitator specializing in emotional and intuitive leadership. “In this insightful and compassionate book, Dr. Shefali helps parents understand the immense pressures girls face today... A timely and important book for every parent of girls.” — Dr. Laura Markham, author of Peaceful Parent, Happy Kids Raising Conscious Daughters by bestselling author Dr. Shefali is a powerful wake-up call, a hands-on guide, and a pathway forward to reclaim how daughters are seen, supported, and raised in the 21st century. Something unprecedented is unfolding in the inner lives of our girls today. On the surface, they are excelling and achieving in ways that would seem unimaginable to previous generations. Yet beneath this success lies a far more urgent and unsettling truth: Girls are unraveling at alarming rates. Anxiety, perfectionism, and self-harm are surging, exposing a devastating paradox between the confident, high-achieving facade the world applauds and the fragile, unmoored self that struggles silently within. In a digital age that commodifies attention, comparison, and worth, this inner fracture is no longer slow or subtle. Into this urgent moment comes Raising Conscious Daughters , the groundbreaking new book from clinical psychologist and bestselling author Dr. Shefali, founder of the revolutionary Conscious Parenting movement. Drawing on real-life clinical cases, interviews with children and parents, and deeply practical, prescriptive guidance, Dr. Shefali offers a radical reorientation of how we understand girls today. In this book she shows parents how to raise daughters who: Trust their inner voice Set boundaries with confidence and clarity Stay emotionally connected to their authentic self At a time when girls appear more capable than ever yet feel more fragile within, Raising Conscious Daughters stands as a one-of-a-kind guide for helping them grow into empowered, worthy and resilient beings. "Wise, compassionate, and enormously relevant, this book offers parents a powerful new framework for raising emotionally healthy, resilient boys.” — Dr. Laura Markham, author of Peaceful Parent, Happy Kids Raising Conscious Sons by bestselling author Dr. Shefali is a clarion call, a practical resource, and a hopeful invitation to radically reimagine how boys are understood, nurtured, and raised in the 21st century. Boys today are standing at a critical crossroads unlike any generation before. They are bombarded with impossible and contradictory mandates: Be tough but never vulnerable; be sensitive but never weak; be strong but never domineering. Caught between these warring expectations—and shaped by a digital world that amplifies comparison, disconnection, and performative identity—boys are now experiencing an unprecedented crisis of masculinity, marked by alarming rates of suicide, aggression, isolation, and apathy. In Raising Conscious Sons , clinical psychologist and bestselling author Dr. Shefali—founder of the revolutionary Conscious Parenting movement—offers a bold and urgently needed map for helping boys reclaim their sense of purpose and their capacity to engage meaningfully with life. Drawing on real-life clinical cases, interviews with children and parents, and practical, prescriptive guidance, she shows parents how to raise sons who: Feel emotionally secure and connected to their inner world Develop confidence grounded in integrity rather than dominance Step into purpose with clarity, empathy, and self-discipline At a time when boys are flooded with messages about masculinity yet lack guidance on how to embody it, Raising Conscious Sons stands as a one-of-a-kind guide for helping them stay emotionally connected, authentic and grounded in who they are. Dr. Shefali is a clinical psychologist, a New York Times bestselling author, and the founder of the Conscious Parenting movement, redefining how families understand selfhood, connection, and the inner life of children. She works where psychology meets consciousness, tracing the hidden forces that shape identity, relationships, and the way we inhabit the world. Trained at Columbia University, she has spent decades guiding families to move beyond patterns of control and fear toward presence and authenticity. Her work brings Western psychology and Eastern wisdom into lived practice, creating a path for children—and the adults who raise them—to know themselves fully. Shirin Aryanpour (Founder, Illuminate Her Path) Bio: Shirin Aryanpour is the founder of Illuminate Her Path, an impact-driven platform and community devoted to empowering women through wellness, connection, and authentic sisterhood. With more than 16 years of experience as a physical therapist, Shirin has guided individuals of all ages and backgrounds on their journeys toward healing and well-being. A two-time breast cancer thriver, her personal healing journey deepened her commitment to women's health, equity, and empowerment. Geno La Placa (Executive Coach & Mentor) Bio: Geno La Placa is an Executive Leadership and Life Coach, Speaker, and Retreat Facilitator specializing in emotional and intuitive leadership. A former hedge fund CFO and due diligence expert, she brings extensive executive and financial experience to her transformational coaching work. Geno holds certifications from the Berkeley Executive Coaching Institute, Dr. Shefali's Conscious Parenting Method™, and Dr. Gabor Maté's Compassionate Inquiry. Her work integrates neuroscience, NLP, somatic psychology, emotional intelligence, and intuitive intelligence to help leaders develop greater clarity, confidence, and purpose. events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Learn to create a garden that is a sanctuary for peace, reflection, & spiritual growth with this guide to mindful gardening & sacred spaces. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Thursday, October 8 at 7:00 PM when author & gardener Janaki Sandy Gaal comes to the store to present her new book S oulful Sanctuaries: Cultivating Sacred Spaces . She will be joined in con In Soulful Sanctuaries , Janaki Sandy Gaal—known as “The Rose Lady”—invites readers to reimagine gardens of any size as places of renewal, healing, and connection to the natural world. Blending practical gardening wisdom, meditative practices, and heartfelt storytelling, this richly photographed book offers a meaningful approach to cultivating an outdoor space that feels personal, restorative, and spiritually alive. Drawing on decades of experience as an organic gardener, garden designer, and consulting rosarian, Janaki shares guidance on organic gardening, year-round cultivation, and creating garden altars that reflect each reader’s own intentions and beliefs. Featuring photography by her daughter, Rebecca Gaal, Soulful Sanctuaries is both an inspiring guide and a keepsake gift book rooted in family, beauty, and spiritual practice. Here’s what makes Soulful Sanctuaries meaningful: • Mindful Gardening for Every Space: Helps readers turn gardens of any size into places to slow down, reconnect, and cultivate meaning. • Practical Organic Gardening Wisdom : Includes sustainable practices, year-round cultivation, and insights from Janaki’s experience as a consulting rosarian. • Spiritual Practices Made Personal: Offers meditative practices, intention-setting, and guidance for creating garden altars. • A Beautiful Keepsake Gift Book: Rebecca Gaal’s photography creates an immersive experience for gardeners, spiritual seekers, and anyone seeking a more restorative living space. Soulful Sanctuaries is a mindful gardening book and spiritual gardening guide for readers interested in sacred spaces, organic gardening, garden sanctuaries, meditation, and connecting more deeply with nature. JANAKI SANDY GAAL is an author, educator, gardener, and longtime student of Ram Dass. An organic gardener, garden designer, and consulting rosarian, she has dedicated her life to relieving suffering—from her early work as an ICU nurse to opening her garden to the public. Through writing and teaching, Janaki explores the connection between spirituality, nature, and everyday life, encouraging reflection, presence, and healing through simple practices such as gardening, cooking, and connecting with the natural world. She lives on Maui, Hawaii, surrounded by ʻohana. REBECCA GAAL is a creative strategist and visual storyteller whose work bridges environmental science, public health, and visual communication. A Fujifilm X Photographer, her work has been exhibited and published internationally by The Nature Conservancy, The American Scholar, Harvard University Center for the Environment, Adobe, and the National Institutes of Health. She is Director of Partnerships at the Santa Barbara Wildlife Care Network and Executive Producer of Wild Rescue, an IMAX 3D film exploring the intersection of wildlife and human worlds. She lives in Ventura, California.

events.description: Tonight four pochos from different corners and dimensions of Aztlan come together for a poetic and rasquache reimagining of the lyrics of foundational Mexican American singer songwriter Lalo Guerrero. Featuring pendejadas, poetics, y musica from Marisol Medina-Cadena, Louis “El Panadero” Gutierrez, soledad con carne, and Josiah Flores. MC’d by the Pocho poeta Josiah Luis Alderete. This evento is part of the Lalo Guerrero Legacy Festival happening at the Freight and Salvage on November 6th and 7th and is also a PBS(Pocho Broadcasting Company) production. Louis “El Panadero” Gutierrez is a 24th street organic intellectual, Mission poet, and neighborhood archivist. His familia has owned the iconic La Reyna Bakery for over 40 years. Marisol Medina-Cadena is a fourth generation Californian; Bay Area on her mom’s side and LA County on her pop’s side. She is a San Francisco based comedian and storyteller by way of the dirty D, aka Pasadena, California. When she's not being a sad clown she's doing boring things like research and collecting intel of all things pochismo and San Pancho. As a proud member of (PBS) the Pocho Broadcast Service, she takes her duty very seriously to make audiences he-he and ha-ha. soledad con carne is an intergalactic Chicanx punk poet. They are a poet of the root that cracks the concrete on occupied Fernandeño-Tataviam Land: otherwise known as the San Fernando Valley. Part-time poet turned melodic storyteller, Chicano singer/songwriter Josiah Flores puts music to the parts of life most tend to hide from. From the foothills of south San Jose to the foggy avenues of San Francisco, he calls the Bay Area his home. Influenced by the likes of Stoney Edwards, Freddy Fender, and Willie Dunn, if one were to sit in a dimly-lit corner of their local watering hole, hunched over a beer, they would find Josiah’s songs sitting down next to them.

events.title: Dorothy Lazard at Clio's!
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: Behind the Desk at the Main. · Join Heyday for another installment of Heyday Presents , an ongoing conversation series presented in collaboration with Clio's Books. Over the course of her 20-year-tenure at the Oakland Public Library’s flagship branch—known as “the Main”— Dorothy Lazard built a career helping residents connect with the city’s past and present, eventually becoming the keeper of Oakland’s local history archives. In her new book, Behind the Desk at the Main , published by Heyday, Lazard offers an insider’s look at the modern American library. Through personal stories and decades of experience, Lazard demystifies the work of librarians and reveals how libraries serve as vital hubs—and defenders—for knowledge, connection, and civic life. She will be joined in conversation by East Bay Yesterday host and producer Liam O'Donoghue . Dorothy Lazard was born in St. Louis and grew up in San Francisco and Oakland. A librarian for forty years, she joined the staff of the Oakland Public Library in 2000. From 2009 until her retirement in 2021, she was the head librarian of OPL’s Oakland History Center, where she encouraged people of all ages and backgrounds to explore local history. Lazard's first book, What You Don't Know Will Make a Whole New World , was the 2023 recipient of the Oscar Lewis Award in Western History from the Book Club of California. She lives in Oakland. Liam O’Donoghue is the host and producer of the East Bay Yesterday podcast and co-creator of the Long Lost Oakland map. He also writes a monthly feature about the East Bay for SF Gate. His journalism has appeared in outlets such as KQED, Oaklandside, Berkeleyside, Mother Jones, Salon, and elsewhere. In 2018, he was honored by the East Bay Express as “the best journalist-turned-historian” and presented with a “Partners in Preservation Award” from Oakland Heritage Alliance. O’Donoghue’s quotes on Oakland-related issues have appeared in media outlets including New York Times and Washington Post. About Heyday Heyday is an independent nonprofit publisher specializing in publications that explore California's natural history, art and culture, Indigenous perspectives, and social justice. This series is part of our Heyday Presents program. Heyday Presents features Heyday authors in conversation with notable luminaries and thought leaders. Heyday Members receive free VIP access to Heyday Presents program and a curation of our top new releases, among a host of other perks. Heyday members and Clio's members receive free admission!

events.title: Jonah Raskin, Marc Zegans, Larry Beckett read some of their poetry, and Jonah introduces his latest book
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Jonah Raskin introduces his most recent book of cultural writings, Keeping the Beat (Regent Press, 2026), a collection of original, groundbreaking reviews and essays about the writers of the Beat Generation, plus their contemporaries and fellow travelers. Jonah’s five and a half decades’ output of short and long-form literary/cultural criticism and journalism has traced three-quarters of a century of outsider American socio-political life, with an eye on the American imperial project that frames it. Lately, he’s also produced a fair amount of poetry. Jonah will bring some of his poems to the table to join with poets Marc Zegans and Larry Beckett, who will present some of their own poetry, principally recent work. Larry will also sing a poem of Paul Verlaine, in his own translation, accompanying the poem/song on piano. The Book of Immaculate Perception / Madrigals is a tête-bêche (flip book) by Marc Zegans and Larry Beckett in which two poem cycles, “Madrigals” by Beckett and “The Book of Immaculate Perception” by Zegans can be read from their respective fronts-to-backs in a single spine format. The project developed when Marc sent Larry the manuscript for “The Book of Immaculate Perception,” a micro-chap tracing the circle from raw awareness through life mediated by language to simple awareness regained, and Larry, responding enthusiastically, shared with Marc a thematically resonant series of madrigals inspired by his daughter that trace the life arc forward from conception. The confluence between these poem-cycles extends beyond shared narrative lines to independently formed yet common imagery and complementary methods of composition. In each body of work, you will find compactness of speech, form that liberates line, and an easy flow from poem-to-poem that animates and enriches the experience of reading these two sets of poems in each other’s company. Larry Beckett’s poetry ranges from songs to blank sonnets and 100-page narrative works. His lyric, “Song to the Siren,” is a modern standard. In the years since, he’s written the postmodern epic, “American Cycle,” including the long narratives Paul Bunyan, Wyatt Earp, Amelia Earhart, and he has reinvented Sonnets. “The Book of Merlin” is a recovery and translation of the 6th-century Brythonic poet, and “Romances Without Words / In Solitary” is the first translation of the prison manuscript of Paul Verlaine. “Beat Poetry” is a study of the poets and poetry of the fifties San Francisco Renaissance. These madrigals are to a child from conception on. They’re dedicated to his daughter, Susannah Beckett. Marc Zegans’s seven collections of poems include Lyon Street (Bamboo Dart Press, 2022) and The Snow Dead (Červená Barva Press, 2020). Ghost Book (Kite String Press, 2024), a fine art photo book collaboration with photographer Tsar Fedorsky, is held in the special collections of the Boston Athenaeum, the Getty Research Institute, Yale University’s Haas Family Arts Library, Haverford College, the Peabody Essex Museum, and others. Marc reviews poetry for Liberated Words in his column, “On the Cutting Edge.” Films based on Marc’s poems appear regularly at festivals around the world. He lives by the coast in Northern California.

events.title: WILL DOWNING
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: They say a man’s “ soul ” is his spiritual essence. Life’s twists and turns can lift that soul high into the sky or send it crashing to the ground below. Unfortunately, 2023 started with the latter for Will Downing, following the unexpected and soul-crushing loss of his daughter, Aron Siobhan Downing, in January. As a father, he was devastated…heartbroken. As an artist, he sought solace and comfort through his craft…facing the hurt head-on and exploring multiple themes of love to begin the healing. Persevering through the pain, Downing is poised to finish the year with his soul rising…literally! The Prince of Sophisticated Soul is ready to share his 7- song masterclass in triumph over tragedy, Soul Rising ! Celebrating an insane 35 years in the “ bizness ” and 27 Albums to his credit, Will Downing will not be stopped! Flexing on his international appeal, the lead single "What Part of My Love" shot to the top of the UK Soul Chart Top 30 and parked there. Those who no longer listen to new releases as the collective work it was intended to be should make an exception in this case. Although not a "concept" album, the pieces of Soul Rising fit together beautifully as a single statement and should be enjoyed as such. We all know about the smoothness, but there's a brand-new kind of...Dare I say..."Funkiness", that I think is here to stay! You (and your speakers, Headphones) etc….. will feel the difference right off the jump, with the lead-off cut, “Closer to Me”, when that bass and drum start hitting a little differently. The familiar writing and production tandem of Downing and guitarist Randy Bowland turns the heat up a bit from their usual formula. With keyboardist Mike Logan Sr. and background vocalist Ms. Monet rounding out the groove, I dare you not to move somethin'! House of Love, another Downing/Bowland collab, gives me "Maze" vibes, however unintended, but that's never a bad thing! To the extent that over the last 4 decades, these two surviving entities may have directly or indirectly influenced each other, I'll welcome that musical baby into the fold every time with open arms and ears. Make no mistake...Will Downing didn't forget the "smooth" that made the Man the Myth the Legend! Nor did he abandon his world-famous knack for what he affectionately calls "interpretations" of classic hits. He plucked an absolute diamond of a gem from arguably one of the finest early 70's albums, The Stylistics, Round Two, and their hauntingly enchanting, “You're As Right As Rain”! If you've ever "slow-dragged" with a blue light in the basement, you will be transported to afros, platforms, bell-bottoms, and Brut cologne...if you know you know, but I digress. In addition to assistance from long-time collaborator Ronnie Foster, Downing recruits the sweet trumpet of solo Artist and one-half of 90's duo Imprompt2, Johnny Brit t, to seal the vibe. Soul Rising then takes a solemn turn to the heart and very "Soul" of this release. Downing, maybe for his own well-being, had to stare his tragedy down squarely and turn art into therapy. “Till We Meet Again” serves as a father's sweet hand-off to God to care for his angel Siobhan, until they're joined again divinely as father and daughter in heavenly reward. An unimaginable undertaking for a parent attempting to channel pain into art. The song is introduced by the actual last New Year's Day voicemail exchanged by Downing and Siobhan, which contains no hint of the drama to unfold just 10 days later. Downing makes the song a true family affair, with daughter Aja and wife Audrey Wheeler Downing lending their supportive voices. A passionately moving, albeit gut-wrenching tribute, but well done. Given that dynamic, it's understandable that the final three tracks all lean into a theme of "Love". Starting with the aforementioned smash, “What Part of My Love”, but pivoting back to that new "funk" vibe with “Love You Right”, this time with Hubert Eaves IV joining the revival. An intentional sequence, I would think, to lift and restore the spirit of Soul Rising ! I think the final cut, “Love of A Lifetime”, as a message, speaks simultaneously of what we seek in both a personal relationship and the love of a father to a child. Maybe that wasn't the intent, but given the circumstances, I heard both. Love is love! Family…, Will Downing dug deep for this one. Even down to the Album cover, an original piece of artwork by Frank Morrison. Realize, recognize, and appreciate a real man, a real artist, and a real father with his Soul Rising !

events.description: When three modern groove masters of modern funk and soul-jazz converge, sparks are bound to fly. The Breaks brings together guitarist Eddie Roberts (The New Mastersounds), drummer Stanton Moore (Galactic), and organist Robert Walter (The Greyboy Allstars)—three musicians whose collective groove has shaped the sound of contemporary funk for over two decades. Rooted in the tradition of late-’60s organ trios and hard-hitting boogaloo, The Breaks pushes the sound forward with deep-pocket rhythms, tight arrangements, and fearless improvisation. Eddie Roberts’ sharp, melodic guitar work dances effortlessly over Stanton Moore’s explosive New Orleans-infused drum grooves, while Robert Walter’s signature Hammond organ tones tie it all together with grit and soul. Between them, they’ve logged countless tours, recorded landmark albums, and collaborated with a who’s-who of the modern jam, funk, and jazz worlds. But in The Breaks, the chemistry feels spontaneous—three kindred spirits locking into a groove and letting it ride. From sweaty club sets to major festival stages, The Breaks deliver a sound that’s both deeply rooted and constantly evolving—a raw, joyful celebration of rhythm and musical conversation.

events.title: Angela Johal: Intersecting Colour
events.location: Slate Contemporary Gallery, 5510 College Ave, Oakland
events.description: Join us at SLATE Contemporary Gallery on Saturday, October 10 from 4-6pm for an artist reception in celebration of our newest exhibition, “Angela Johal: Intersecting Colour.” This exhibition invites viewers to explore how hue and tone interact across vividly painted color fields. Johal approaches each painting as a puzzle to solve, seeking balance among dichotomous realms—physical and spiritual, light and dark, vivid and subdued—creating compositions that reveal how each color shifts, responds to, and is transformed by those around it. Steeped in color theory, Johal’s work is deeply informed by the human eye’s natural passage through dimension. This exhibition features abstracted geometric compositions that, when meditated on, transform into natural landscapes, animal-like forms, and shifting light.

events.title: Wisdom Healing Qigong with Hiromi Vardy
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Experience the deep benefits of Zhineng (Wisdom Healing) Qigong. This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Through simple, time-honored movements, the nervous system unwinds, the mind becomes more spacious, and the heart opens. Over time, practitioners often feel more resilient, centered, and connected — both inwardly and outwardly.

Tickets are sliding scale $10-$25 - Please arrive at least 5-10 minutes early.

 Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back 

Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts.

While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga.

After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today.

Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

events.title: King Lear
events.location: Z Space's Steindler Stage
events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. Can he transform in time to reclaim what is sacred before the clown show becomes the new order? Ritual and spectacle collide in Michael Socrates Moran ’s bold, contemporary staging of Shakespeare’s epic tragedy, featuring a cast of 30, including the “irrepressible” ( SF Chronicle ) J Jha ( Angels in America, Mahābhārata ) as Lear; renowned performer, singer, and writer Rinde Eckert ( Ghost Quartet ) as The Fool; and music composed by Paul Dresher and performed live by the Dresher | Davel Invented Instrument Duo .

events.title: Devon Gilfillian
events.location: The Independent, 628 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117
events.description:
Time Will Tell is the album that Devon Gilfillian has been preparing to make his entire life. But some things needed to happen first—namely, he needed his life to change, for the road to wind through a few curves and over a few bumps before the classically modern and magnetic soul singer could write these songs. He needed to confront his family’s mortality. He needed to endure a relationship whose cracks nearly broke him. He needed to take control of the way he made his records, to believe that he and his closest confidants had what it took to shape the record of his life. Here’s how they did just that.

You should first know that Devon’s father, Nelson Gilfillian, likes to keep it clean. A father of three now at the edge of 70, he hits the gym five times a week and generally watches what he eats. Though he raised his kids just west of Philadelphia, he lives now just east of Nashville, in the rural outskirts of Lebanon. A lifelong musician and wedding singer, Nelson’s one indulgence these days might be his Wednesday night trips into the city, where he plays congas in a weekly R&B and jazz jam at the Flamingo Cocktail Club.

Devon, then, was stunned and confused when his mom called in September 2023 to say that Nelson, then 67, had suffered a heart attack. His own father had died at that age, but the prognosis for Nelson seemed much better—a few stints, then back home to Lebanon. Nelson is the reason Devon is a musician, having taken the kid to guitar lessons and fed him the great records. So the son did what he assumed the father would want: He walked onstage in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, played his show, and flew home the next morning.

In a matter of weeks, Gilfillian wrote “Glad to Be Here,” a bittersweet and beautiful ode to existence, to slowing down long enough to remember what a gift it is to be alive at all. Like the sun slipping through closed curtains on a cold day, “Glad to Be Here” is the aching and grateful country-soul centerpiece of Time Will Tell , his fourth album and honest account of the extreme highs and lows that come with living. Nelson’s health scare coincided with the protracted and painful end of a long relationship that Gilfillian steadily realized was making him worse in almost every way that counted. The dozen songs of Time Will Tell first document the work it took for him to reach the end of that road—and, then, the sense of liberation and burgeoning joy he has found at the start of a new one. Time Will Tell does what classic soul and country records often do best: share the troubled state of someone’s heart in exquisite detail and look for a way forward.

Not long after Gilfillian moved to Nashville a dozen years ago, he wrote a song for his parents—his mom, Ginny, specifically. They were still up north, and he missed them. It was called “Home,” the first tune he’d written that he felt like he could share without qualms. It was a breakthrough for Gilfillian, who suddenly understood that writing and singing could function as therapy, that his talents were a ready-made outlet for his troubles and maybe his triumphs. That sensibility was clear on Gilfillian’s first three albums, especially the ecstatic eruptions of 2023’s Love You Anyway . Even his full-length, friend-studded cover of Marvin Gaye’s What’s Going On, released amid the turmoil of 2020, felt personal in that way, like he was looking for a sanctuary of his own in song.

But that idea became something of a life raft for Gilfillian in the intervening years. As he struggled to save a relationship into which he’d put so much time and love, he found himself

writing about differences that he slowly recognized as irreconcilable. Gilfillian, for instance, is a morning person; as he realized his partner truly blossomed at night, he mourned the distance that lifestyle discrepancy created between them with “Moonflower,” a neo-soul wonder about respecting but regretting what makes someone themselves. And on “Black Dog Rabbit Hole,” he took frank stock of the impact the tension was having on his own wellbeing, how he was using his own depression and addiction as an escape hatch for an increasingly bad situation.

Gilfillian and his longtime drummer and friend Jonathan Smalt intuitively understood that the best way to capture the feelings in these songs was to cut them as quickly as possible. Gilfillian and Smalt have worked with several ace producers in the past, including Shawn Everett and Jeremy Lutito, but they felt like they finally knew enough to try it themselves. They asked Dave Cobb if they could borrow Nashville’s legendary RCA Studio A, then recruited a few ace engineers and producers—Reid Leslie, Michael Harris, Ran Jackson—to help man the varispeed tape machines and make a few key calls. They built a band of session aces and strong sets of string and horn players, then tracked most of the vocals with single takes. Neal H Pogue, the producer legendary for his work with the likes of OutKast and TLC, was so passionate about Gilfillian’s demos that he enlisted as executive producer, eventually mixing the album himself. Everyone wanted the songs to feel like the epiphanies that had shaped them, for the recordings to reflect the realness of Gilfillian’s circumstances when he wrote them.

It absolutely worked. “Black Dog Rabbit Hole” is a riveting hard rock snapshot of mania, Gilfillian’s voice switching between falsetto frailty and a tormented bellow as he tries to find his way out of a spiral. Gilfillian has never made anything quite so raw, quite so cutting. With its gospel surges, ringing bells, and jittery guitars, “Hold On (Hourglass)” races like a nervous heart, a sleepless and agitated Gilfillian wondering if his commitment to holding on is just a way of fooling himself. On “IRL,” where a boom-bap beat undergirds an organ’s psychedelic whirr before the whole thing snaps into a funk strut, Gilfillian gets stuck in the conflict between leaving and staying, between indulging what his body wants and his mind needs. The song is so unmitigated it feels like you’re listening to a real-time argument he’s having with himself about his future. These aren’t breakup songs so much as exacting maps of Gilfillian’s relatable inner conflicts as he tries to find ways to be happy—ways of being, like his father, simply glad to be here at all.

Gilfillian ends Time Will Tell not with an apology but with a permission slip. As magnetic as a Cat Stevens staple but as warm as a Sam Cooke ballad, “You Can Hate Me Now” acknowledges that no end is ever easy, that all the effort in the world still won’t make a split feel smooth. “There’s no other way underneath the pain,” he sings, his voice trying not to break beneath the strain. Given the song title, it is staggering how likable Gilfillian seems in this moment, how vulnerable he is being about his own failure and frailty. “We just gotta go through,” he continues. What else is there in life or on an album like Time Will Tell than to go through ? To get to where we’re going, we’ve got to suffer a little. Time Will Tell is the sound of Gilfillian doing exactly that but realizing what a blessing it is to be here at all, with the chance to hurt and learn and ultimately move on.

events.title: Artist Talk – Patricia Guthrie: Get Up Stand Up
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: One purpose of art is to support and communicate political messages. Using color, letters, and shapes, Patricia Guthrie’s abstract quilts deliver political messages relating to the government, international relationships, and global warming. She creates artwork using cotton fabric, wool batting, dyes, and machine stitching. Bio: After retiring as a professor and department chair of Human Development and Women’s Studies at California State University East Bay, Patricia Guthrie decided to actively engage in the visual arts. She began taking community-based art classes: drawing, photography, quilt making, and printing on fabric. Quilt making and all its aspects has become her passion. Guthrie hopes her quilts encourage viewers to move beyond art that is merely pleasing to the eye to seek a deeper meaning. Her work has been shown nationally and internationally including Schweinfurth Memorial, Art Center, Auburn, New York; International Quilt Museum, Lincoln, Nebraska; Philadelphia Museum of Art, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; and Tuch + Technik Museum, Neumunster, Germany. This is Guthrie’s second solo show at Mercury 20 Gallery. Gallery Hours: Friday and Saturday, 12 – 5 pm (and by appointment) Opening Reception: Saturday, September 12, 3 – 5 pm ﻿Oakland Art Murmur / First Friday: October 2, 5 – 9 pm

events.title: Angelica Page - Bountiful: Growing Up with Geraldine Page
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: An intimate examination of Oscar Award-winning film and stage actress Geraldine Page, written with compassion and honesty by her only daughter, Angelica Page. Bountiful: Growing up with Geraldine Page is the first book about legendary screen and stage actress Geraldine Page, presenting a one-of-a-kind look at her body of work and private life. Includes insider stories of her stage and film career (nominated for four Tony Awards and eight Academy Awards, Oscar winner for The Trip to Bountiful ), her relationships with other renowned actors including her husband and Angelica’s father Rip Torn, Actors Studio founder Lee Strasberg, and her interactions with other legends including James Dean, John Wayne, Jackie Kennedy, and many more. Angelica Page, daughter of Geraldine and Rip Torn, skillfully weaves in stories of her own coming of age: being mesmerized by her mother’s stage performances as a child and a rebellious young adult; learning to swim in Grace Slick’s guitar-shaped pool; enduring a chaotic home life, immersing herself in the 1970s and 80s NYC underground of CBGBs, Max’s Kansas City, and the Mudd Club. This is as much a theatrical history lesson as a first-person survival guide to life in the fast lane. A love song sung by the daughter of a remarkable artist who should not be forgotten any time soon. Includes more than 40 rare photos from family archives. “A definitive memoir by a brilliant actress about a truly beloved American actress, mother and hero.” —Elizabeth Ashley, actor “Supercharged with boundless talent, emotion and at times unrequited love, Angelica Page’s portrait of the great Geraldine is one for the ages.” —Sandra Bernhard, actress “Be warned, this book is dangerous; it can make you regret never having lived through the thrilling, dangerous times Geraldine Page lived in and partly created. In these trying times, she is an important reminder of the potential of the individual, in art and in life.” —F. Murray Abraham, actor Angelica Page is an American actress, director, producer, and writer and the only daughter of legendary actors Rip Torn and Geraldine Page. She has appeared frequently onstage on- and off-Broadway, earning an Outer Critic’s Circle nomination for best Solo Performance, the Helen Hayes Award for Best Actress, and the New York People’s Choice Award for Best Supporting Actress. She is the creator of the critically acclaimed one-woman show Turning Page on which Bountiful is based. When not touring the US, she lives in Mexico. Angelica Page - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating There will be a signing line or meet and greet following the presentation.

events.description: Meet & Greet Book Signing Only • SF Ferry Plaza Market 11:00 AM PT Food Demo // 11:30 AM PT Book Signing Please join us for a special meet and greet signing event with Heather Hardcastle, following her Foodwise demo at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market. Gluten free as it should be--fresh, simple, and for the whole family,--The Flour Craft Bakery & Cafe Cookbook includes seventy-five impeccable, seasonal recipes for every time of day. The Flour Craft Bakery & Cafe Cookbook empowers readers with simple and approachable recipes for mouthwatering cakes and cookies, pastry and savory bakes, everyday treats and holiday centerpieces, plus fresh salads and soups--all naturally gluten free. 75+ recipes cover breakfast, brunch, lunch, teatime, and dessert, from coffee cakes to focaccia, scones to tartines. Heather Hardcastle combines alternative flours including rice, millet, nut flours, and starches to achieve a perfect crumb and oven-fresh texture. Flour Craft breaks down the process in an approachable way, teaching readers how to combine a few key flours in the correct proportions to yield excellent results every time. The cornerstones of the book are the "Master Recipes," classics of baking to be practiced and adapted. The full Flour Craft experience is brought to life for the reader with a glossary of ingredients and terms curated to build confidence for bakers of all skill levels. “We can finally enjoy renowned Flour Craft Bakery & Cafe’s recipes at home. This beautiful book is full of breads, cakes, and pastries I cannot wait to make, not only for those who eat gluten-free but for everyone else too.” —Aran Goyoaga, author of Cannelle et Vanille "I’ve savored many gluten-free focaccia slices, sourdough waffles, and sweet treats at Flour Craft Bakery & Café over the years. I’m thrilled that I can finally make every recipe in my own kitchen! Heather reveals her baking secrets in this gorgeous book furnished with luscious photographs and recipes that everyone will love—whether they eat gluten-free or not." —Alanna Taylor-Tobin, author of Alternative Baker "Heather's passion for fresh, uncompromisingly delicious cooking and baking has made her gluten-free bakery and cafe a favorite among Northern California food lovers. This book brings the magic home, allowing even beginner cooks to recreate the wonderful flavors of Flour Craft in their own kitchens." —Erika Lenkert, Editor-in-Chief, GFF Magazine "For those who are searching for gluten-free dessert recipes on a regular basis, Flour Craft's cookbook is a treasure trove of information." —SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE Heather Hardcastle understood where gourmet GF was headed before everyone else. In the early 2000s, diagnosed with gluten intolerance, and passionate about food and cooking, Hardcastle left her well-established career and enrolled at the Culinary Institute of America, determined to learn the nuances of great pastry and solid classical technique. Her dream was always to turn her passion and knowledge into a thriving business, creating delicious, high-quality gluten-free baked goods. In 2013, she opened the first Flour Craft Bakery. events.title: The Tiny Monster Show ~ Artist Talk
events.location: The Grand Gallery, 560 2nd Street, Oakland
events.description: Whether or not you like monsters, one has to admit, most of us like a good scare now and then. The word Monster derives from the Latin monstrum, itself derived ultimately from the verb moneo (“to remind, warn, instruct, or foretell”). From this vantage point, monsters take on a new inspiring role, not to just scare us, but to inform us. So what can monsters teach us about our fears, our society and beyond? The Tiny Monster Show explores our fears so we can take a deeper look at what we’ve been suppressing and what we need to confront. From classical to political, The Tiny Monster Show gives space to capture, reveal, and maybe conquer those elements that keep us frozen in fear and hopefully shine a light on what it means to be human. Hopefully, you’ll experience a moment of laughter in recognition that you are more powerful than the monster wants you to think.

events.title: April Snow, LMFT - Big Feelings, Big Joy
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “My purpose in writing this book is not only to teach you what high sensitivity is—because it’s so much more than what people assume—but also to show you that, contrary to what you may have thought, this trait can be an immense gift. It’s not just big messy emotions, getting lost in your head, or being flooded with anxiety. Highly sensitive people are the emotional leaders, healers, problem solvers, and changemakers of the world.” — Excerpted from BIG FEELINGS, BIG JOY by April Snow, LMFT In BIG FEELINGS, BIG JOY: The Essential Practices to Reclaim Your Strengths as a Highly Sensitive Person , licensed psychotherapist and sensitivity expert April Snow delivers a practical and empowering toolkit for Highly Sensitive People (HSPs) to embrace their sensitivity and chart their own path to joy. Drawing from her clinical experience with thousands of HSPs and her own life as a highly sensitive person, Snow makes it clear that sensitivity is a core part of who you are—something to value and nurture, not change. Through simple language and relatable stories, this book offers a three-part framework rooted in self-acceptance and honors sensitivity as a gift that can bring meaning, creativity, and a deep sense of connection. In BIG FEELINGS, BIG JOY , readers discover key practices and insights to help them understand their needs, manage overstimulation, and embrace their sensitive nature with confidence: Honor your sleep and downtime: Learn why HSPs need more rest than most and discover simple changes to your daily routines and environment for optimal restoration. Tend to your nervous system: Practice easy strategies to manage overstimulation, navigate emotional lows, and regain a sense of calm and clarity. Set boundaries with compassion: Gain tools for advocating for your needs in relationships, work, and daily interactions—so you can protect your energy without guilt. Embrace sensitivity as your strength: Experience how sensitivity can fuel creativity, intuition, deep empathy, and meaningful connections. With this book, April Snow encourages readers to confidently honor their needs, celebrate their sensitivity, and build a life that reflects their true selves—full of joy, balance, and deeper connection. "A warm and wise book that offers a fresh take on sensitivity and what it means to navigate the world as a highly sensitive person. Grounded, practical, and deeply validating, it will resonate with anyone who has ever felt they experience life more intensely than those around them." - Tom Falkenstein, psychotherapist and author of The Highly Sensitive Man " Big Feelings, Big Joy is a must-read for any highly sensitive person who is tired of being told to "grow a thicker skin." Snow gives you practical tools to honor your nervous system and step into sensitivity as the superpower it can be. With the book's blend of wisdom and warmth, I know it's one I'll be recommending for years to come." - Melody Wilding, LMSW, author of Trust Yourself: Stop Overthinking and Channel Your Emotions for Success at Work " Big Feelings, Big Joy is a must-read for HSPs ready to reclaim the gifts of being sensitive. As an HSP myself, life can feel like a lot, and I’ve often wished I could turn my sensitivity off. This book is a refreshing reminder of the ways sensitivity can enrich our lives, especially when it’s understood and supported. April gets it—she brings both personal and professional experience together in a way that feels validating and hopeful, with practical strategies readers can actually use to thrive." - Sharon Martin, DSW, LCSW, author of The CBT Workbook for Perfectionism and The Better Boundaries Workbook April Snow, LMFT, is a licensed psychotherapist, author, and consultant. She specializes in working with highly sensitive people to help calm the storm of overload, guilt, and self-doubt to allow their innate sensitive strengths to shine through. Deeply committed to changing the narrative of what it means to be highly sensitive, April supports HSPs around the world through her Sensitive Circles community, Sensitive Sessions workshops, and Sensitive Stories podcast. In addition to Big Feelings, Big Joy she has written Find Your Strength: A Workbook for the Highly Sensitive Person. April holds a Master’s Degree in Integral Counseling Psychology and is a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in California where she lives with her wife. In her free time she enjoys being at the beach, curled up in bed, on her yoga mat, spending quality time with her nieces and nephews, or seeing live music. events.title: Left Coast Writers® Laurie McAndish King - Wild Thing, I Think I Love You!
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Please join us for a reading by Laurie McAndish King from her new book, Wild Thing, I Think I Love You! This event is organized by the Left Coast Writers and hosted by Book Passage. Wild Thing, I Think I Love You! is a journey into the complicated, surprising, and often intimate connections between humans and wild animals. From close encounters in the field to quieter moments of recognition, these essays explore what draws us to the wild—and what happens when habitat recedes. Hunt for renegade she-lizards in the Chiricahua Wilderness Learn about the “Dogs Saving Cats” program to help save cheetahs Track Namibia’s rare black rhino—and learn why “dehorning” backfired By turns curious, funny, and deeply felt, Wild Thing, I Think I Love You! explores connection, responsibility, and the enduring allure of the wild. "Whether she's describing a thrilling adventure with massive beasts of the jungle or experiencing a moment of awe in a butterfly sanctuary, the work is captivating ... entertaining ... Engaging and packed with countless intriguing factoids about the natural world." -Kirkus Reviews (Recommended review) "Our Verdict: GET IT" "The Bald Eagles of Klamath Basin have been called the greatest gathering of eagles outside of Alaska. And King has done the hard work for you-rousing before dawn, wearing five layers of insulation to fend off the icy air ... The best thing about King's essays is that you already know Laurie. She is your pal, your sister, your shadow-person who does the adventure with you and then says just the thing you wish you'd said." -Allen Fish, Director, Golden Gate Raptor Obvservatory "King's powerful piece on saving wild elephants is a moment you should not miss-even if it hurts." -Natalie Lefevre, Editor, Ethical Traveler Laurie McAndish King is an award-winning writer whose subjects include a one-legged toucan, an elephant orphanage, the alleged medicinal qualities of rhino horn, and the basics of eagle sex. King’s essays and photography have appeared in Smithsonian magazine, the Washington Post , the San Francisco Chronicle Magazine , Travelers’ Tales’ The Best Women’s Travel Writing , Lonely Planet’s The Kindness of Strangers , and other magazines and literary anthologies. King’s three books of travel stories—insightful, poignant and often quite funny—are celebrated for the way they inspire and entertain readers. Her latest book, Wild Thing, I Think I Love You: Curious Encounters with Wildlife around the World , is due out in September, 2026. Connect at laurieking.com Laurie McAndish King - photo courtesy of the author Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. events.description: Laura Malone, Carnivale, Oil on Linen, 60” x 48”, 2021, Photo courtesy of the artist Present Figures brings together five California painters whose works exist within the figurative language of portraiture, simultaneously expanding and disrupting it. Centered around themes of intimacy, boundaries, and embodied emotion, each artist takes an individual approach to media, scale, and the capacity of the human form to be both a site of identity and a vessel of metaphor. Engaging in profound considerations of what it is to be human—our physicality, sense of self, relationships, consciousness, and creativity, these artists invite us to engage with these shifting, eternal questions and reflect on our own experiences—be they practical, peaceful, disturbing, humorous, fragmented, spiritual, or otherworldly. As individuals, choices that begin with who and what to portray later manifest in stylistic and material communiquès that boldly and poetically reveal themselves to the world. Collectively, the psychologically charged spectrum of the group reminds us of the myriad ways our sentience can be narrated. Like Anais Nin said, “We don’t see things as they are, we see them as we are.” Bio: With Present Figures, Laura Malone expands her practice to curation. Malone invited four artists to show alongside her, chosen for their unique and diverse approaches to representing the figure: two Southern California artists — Cindy Craig and Shannon Rae Fincke — and two from the Bay Area — Nina Katz and Heidi Brueckner. Collectively their work has been shown across the globe in Europe, Asia, and the United States. Malone’s artwork was featured in The Crocker Kingsley National Art Competition and included in “Disrupted Realism,” juried by John Seed, who wrote the book of the same name. Malone currently resides in Oakland, CA and has been a member of Mercury 20 since 2023. Gallery Hours: Friday and Saturday, 12 – 5 pm (and by appointment) Opening Reception: Saturday, September 12, 3 – 5 pm ﻿Oakland Art Murmur / First Friday: October 2, 5 – 9 pm

events.title: Artist Talk – Tara Esperanza: Close to Home
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: Tara Esperanza, Guardians, 2026, acrylic-on-panel, 20” x 16”, Photo courtesy of the artist Whether painted in California or Oaxaca, the works in Close to Home begin with the same impulse: to slow down and look closely. Working on a more intimate scale than in her previous work, Tara Esperanza found herself drawn to quiet moments of observation, where familiar plants reveal unexpected beauty through color, form, and light. Created between two places that have become part of her life, these paintings are less about geography than about attention. Though rooted in different landscapes, each painting is shaped by the same curiosity and sense of wonder inspired by the resilience and sculptural elegance of plants. For many years, succulents have been Esperanza’s way of exploring themes of adaptation, diversity, and endurance. Through this body of work, the smaller scale invites viewers to slow down, look closely, and discover that what is closest to us often has the most to reveal. Bio: Tara Esperanza resides in Oakland, California, where succulents thrive year-round. When she is not painting, she enjoys running and capturing images that later inspire her work. Esperanza earned a BFA in Painting, graduating cum laude from the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, and studied plein air painting in Brittany, France. A representational painter inspired by nature, she has dedicated years to portraying the remarkable beauty and diversity of succulents. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery in Oakland, CA, since 2020. Her work has been shown at the Women’s United Art Movement Virtual Gallery, as well as numerous group exhibitions. In 2025, Esperanza received Best of Show at the Annual National Juried Painting Exhibition at Emerald Springs Art Center in Oregon. Her paintings have been featured in Create! Magazine, New Visionary Magazine, and other publications, and are held in private collections throughout the United States. events.title: Paul Sussman's DID SHE REALLY SAY TANTRUM YOGA
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception September 26 (Please do not bring infants to the show) The world is reeling towards chaos! Wars! Fires! Corruption! The Death of Democracy! It’s an all-out Emergency!!! THIS TIME IS DIFFERENT! This isn’t just a blurb – ask around. It’s time to get out of denial, stare down the grim reality, and… party ? There’s nothing like an encounter with a mysterious stranger at a party: take a risk, lay yourself bare, and – just maybe – find a tiny bit of hope and laughter amidst the chaos. And so many questions along the way! Starting with something safe… “Can we just not… like… talk about Fascism?” “Is the right to eat beef really in the 2nd Amendment? “ If you make it past the chit chat, the questions go deeper: “Maybe it’s time to drop the whole notion of Reality?” “Is it already too late?” And eventually… “Why the two of us, right here, right now?” “What’s next?” Paul Sussman’s latest creation tosses us into the center of the swirl, and offers us lifelines to laugh, to cry, to hope, and to act. “One of the most authentic presentations of humanity I’ve ever seen” “Paul has entered some other zone… of deep thoughtfulness and connection.” ” I laughed, I cried, and I left carrying so much to think about. The way you wove together themes of grief, anger, and how we’re all navigating this moment in time was powerful and deeply resonant.” “You have outdone yourself in this medium –your depth and candor, scope from the personal to the epochal, agile shifting from gentle or scathing satire to the existentially terrifying. I am stunned into silence pondering the implications you invite audiences to consider for this moment.” “You avoid easy answers and platitudes. The threats and the stakes in play have an urgency and brutality that you confront head on, with humility and honesty.” “I loved, loved, loved, your show. Such courageous saying out loud all the things we think, and in such a funny way. Thank you” “This show was so great — so of the moment, so hilarious and at moments horrific at once. Bravo!” Paul Sussman has written and performed a series of solo pieces through the eyes of Neanderthals, road-ragers, insects, Anabaptists, cannibals, and others who persist in the search for meaning. He’s entertained and provoked in theater festivals from Fundy to Fresno. Paul developed his unique approach to melodrama and farce through decades of work in financial management with Bay Area nonprofit organizations. “Did She Really Say Tantrum Yoga ?” is his third full-length solo show (following “The Wrong Kind of Pessimism” and “Beyond Belief”), entitling him to refer to himself in the third person. Sussman has worked for over 40 years to champion affordable housing development in San Francisco and received the Catherine A. Baur Lifetime Achievement Award from the Non-Profit Housing Association of Northern California in 2017. David Ford (director) has been collaborating on new and unusual theater for three decades and has been an artist-in-residence at The Marsh for most of that time. No one knows your heart like a best friend.

events.location: Bookshop West Portal 80 West Portal Ave San Francisco, CA 94127
events.description: Bookshop West Portal is hosting a debate between the two candidates running for Congressional Representative of CA’s 11th District, Supervisor Connie Chan and Senator Scott Weiner. This seat, previously occupied by now-retired Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi, represents the city of San Francisco. The bookshop has a tradition of hosting political candidates for Q&A’s during election cycles as a service to our community, to uphold civic discourse and ensure our community is politically informed. In that spirit, this event is FREE and open to the public. San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan and State Senator Scott Weiner will debate at 6pm on Saturday , October 10th . Our aim is for you to walk away with a better understanding of each candidate’s positions and policies as such, this event will be moderated by James Kass and will not include an audience Q&A portion. James Kass is the Executive Director of KALW Public Media, the Bay Area’s independent public media organization. A longtime cultural strategist and civic storyteller, he is the founder of Youth Speaks and the international Brave New Voices network. His work has focused on the intersection of media, culture, young people, and civic life. A FREE RSVP is required, and we will be checking confirmations at the door. This will sell out quickly. Seating is first come, first served, and we anticipate standing room only, so please take commute time and parking difficulty into account. You, as an audience member, are encouraged to write down ONE question (on a notecard that will be provided upon your arrival) to be considered by the moderator. Your questions will be read by the moderator to the candidate, who will then address your concerns. All questions will be anonymous, and we will not be taking verbal questions from the audience. If you wish to submit ONE question in advance to be considered as a debate topic/question, please do so through this Google Form . We respectfully ask that you keep any questions to their responsibilities as a national representative, as local issues are the responsibility of our district supervisors and city council. **KALW is a public add free radio that has been in the Bay Area for 85 years. They will be recording this event and posting it on their channel. It will not be live, but by coming to this event you are consenting to being audio (not visually) recorded.

events.description: $15 gen admission / $45 with signed book Co-presented with Kearny Street Workshop The National Book Award finalist and New York Times bestselling author of Pachinko returns with a breathtaking contemporary epic. In American Hagwon, Min Jin Lee has crafted an unforgettable, panoramic novel where the smallest of gestures can have enormous repercussions. Once comfortably middle class in Korea, John and Helen Koh and their three children—Bo, DH, and Mido—find their lives upended, first by a shocking betrayal by John’s oldest friend, then by the 1997 Asian financial crisis. Desperately striving to regain their footing, they leave Seoul for Sydney and eventually settle in Southern California—where new vistas of opportunity open up for the children as their parents, strangers in a strange land, must adjust to a new life in which their experience and education mean little. In conversation with Andrew Sean Greer. Doors at 6:00pm.

events.title: Queen Budapest
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the Népstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans. The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favorite tracks— "Bohemian Rhapsody,” "Crazy Little Thing Called Love," "I Want To Break Free” and "We Are The Champions." With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the country’s top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity. events.title: Every Saturday Night
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the most influential R&B singers of his generation · Musiq Soulchild, born Taalib Johnson, is one of the most influential R&B singers of his generation. Weaned on Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, and Donny Hathaway, Musiq pioneered the "neo-soul" movement of the early millennium. events.title: RISING - Susan Edsall's Buen Camino
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Susan has a perfect life, a perfect love, and perfect happiness. When she suddenly undergoes an unexpected loss, her perfect life ends. Consumed by excruciating pain, she finds it impossible to imagine any future worth living. Until, on an ordinary trip to the grocery store, she hears The Voice. The trouble is, Susan doesn’t believe in Voices. And yet, when The Voice tells her to walk the Camino de Santiago in Spain, she obeys despite knowing nothing about this ancient pilgrimage. With only her pack and her pain, Susan begins a journey through unrelenting rain and temperatures that rarely get above 50 degrees. With the help of some improbable Spiritual Guides, a little bit of magic, and the Camino itself, Susan must face her past to have any hope of creating her future. Alone on stage, she becomes 23 characters to take the audience on her solitary walk through 540 miles of rain, resentment, and redemption. Buen Camino is a moving story about grief leading to surrender, and ultimately to freedom. A published writer, performer, and career consultant, Susan Edsall grew up in Montana and now lives in Kailua Kona, Hawaii. Author of the forthcoming novel Bitterroot , she has also written two memoirs, Into the Blue: A Father’s Flight and a Daughter’s Return and Saved . She premiered Buen Camino at the SOLO STARS Series in Los Angeles in December 2024, winning their Encore Award. Susan brought the show to United Solo on 42nd Street in New York City in March 2025 and the Hollywood Fringe Festival in June 2025. Buen Camino enjoyed a full run with Gilded Balloon at the 2025 Edinburgh Festival Fringe. She also performed at the Philadelphia Fringe and in several theaters in Vermont.
