events.title: Goldenvoice Presents USA & Canada Tour 2026 Palace with Rollo Doherty
events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
PALACE ARE BACK WITH “KID” AND MASSIVE TOUR OF USA + CANADA

Palace have been making music together for over a decade. What started out as carefree jam sessions between Leo Wyndham, Rupert Turner and Matt Hodges in an airless studio in North London has burgeoned into a project that has amassed a global audience more akin to a community than a fanbase.

Their early EPs - Lost In The Night (2014) and Chase The Light (2015) - were recorded in the band’s beloved aforementioned studio, The Arch, and established a DIY ethos that remains intrinsic to the spirit of the band to this day. Four albums followed; So Long Forever (2016), Life After (2019), Shoals (2022) and Ultrasound (2024): each one a musical exploration of a particular feeling in a particular place during a particular time; ranging from grief and the loss of a relationship to the emergence of new love and light. Consequently, it's not easy to sonically classify Palace. Their sound varies from the atmospheric and ethereal to the more grounded notes of Blues and Americana, yet in every song there is still something remarkably identifiable as Palace: an ineffability to the feelings conjured up by the music. In a word, transcendent. Perhaps it is this feeling of transcendence which resonates so deeply with their supporters; loyal fans who, by the time Palace had made their Coachella debut in 2024, welcomed them home to a sold-out show at London’s Hammersmith Apollo.

In early 2025, Palace took a career leap that harkens back to their DIY origin. They released the Greyhound EP on their own label, Palace Presents - a collective they'd started in 2016 as a monthly night at The George Tavern in East London, which had quietly grown into something more intentional. A positive and protected space as Leo described it, away from the usual constraints of the music industry. The EP followed a sold-out run across the USA and Canada to growing crowds of dedicated fans.

Kid was released in April 2026, together with the announcement of a 30 date tour of the USA and Canada in the Fall of 2026, culminating in a show at the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles. “Kid is about longing for a child an ocean away. It’s the ache we feel for our people when we’re separated from them. It doesn’t feel like a sadness or heaviness, but more an affirmation of that love, a primal release sung into the sunset as the road flies by."

The journey from an airless studio in North London to the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles is a long one, and by doing things their way, Palace have managed to arrive still recognisably, unmistakably themselves

events.description: Opening Reception September 19 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Balinese scooters. Portuguese military installations. Brazilian waxes. Indian ashrams. events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: Janaki Sandy Gaal - Soulful Sanctuaries
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: In Soulful Sanctuaries , Janaki Sandy Gaal—known as “The Rose Lady”—invites readers to reimagine gardens of any size as places of renewal, healing, and connection to the natural world. It is an ideal read for anyone interested in creating sacred spaces, garden sanctuaries, and connecting more deeply with nature. Create a garden that becomes a sanctuary for peace, reflection, and spiritual growth with this meditative guide to mindful gardening and sacred spaces. In Soulful Sanctuaries, Janaki Sandy Gaal—known as “The Rose Lady”—invites readers to reimagine gardens of any size as places of renewal, healing, and connection to the natural world. Blending practical gardening wisdom, meditative practices, and heartfelt storytelling, this richly photographed book offers a meaningful approach to cultivating an outdoor space that feels personal, restorative, and spiritually alive. Drawing on decades of experience as an organic gardener, garden designer, and consulting rosarian, Janaki shares guidance on organic gardening, year-round cultivation, and creating garden altars that reflect each reader’s own intentions and beliefs. Featuring photography by her daughter, Rebecca Gaal, Soulful Sanctuaries is both an inspiring guide and a keepsake gift book rooted in family, beauty, and spiritual practice. Here’s what makes Soulful Sanctuaries meaningful: • Mindful Gardening for Every Space: Helps readers turn gardens of any size into places to slow down, reconnect, and cultivate meaning. • Practical Organic Gardening Wisdom: Includes sustainable practices, year-round cultivation, and insights from Janaki’s experience as a consulting rosarian. • Spiritual Practices Made Personal: Offers meditative practices, intention-setting, and guidance for creating garden altars. • A Beautiful Keepsake Gift Book: Rebecca Gaal’s photography creates an immersive experience for gardeners, spiritual seekers, and anyone seeking a more restorative living space. Soulful Sanctuaries is a mindful gardening book and spiritual gardening guide for readers interested in sacred spaces, organic gardening, garden sanctuaries, meditation, and connecting more deeply with nature. Janaki Sandy Gaal is an author, educator, gardener, and longtime student of Ram Dass. Her reflections explore the connection between spirituality, nature, and everyday living. She knew from a young age that she wanted to relieve suffering, first as an ICU nurse and later by opening her garden to the public. She is an Organic gardener, Garden Designer, and Consulting Rosarian. She learned that helping others connect with the beauty of nature inspired an irreplaceable kind of joy. Through her writing and teaching, Janaki encourages readers to cultivate reflection, presence, and healing through simple daily practices, including gardening, cooking, and connecting with the natural world. She lives on the island of Maui in Hawaii surrounded by Ohana. Janaki Sandy Gaal - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Ranging from Treuer’s upbringing on the Leech Lake reservation in Minnesota to the experiences of his parents, a Jewish Holocaust refugee and the first American Indigenous woman judge, The Savage Mind reveals the terrifying essence of our nation: frontier violence, which has defined our country, our culture, and our very selves. events.title: Designing Everyday Rituals for Extraordinary Times with Betty Ray
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
How do we give meaningful shape to the moments and transitions that matter in our lives?
Join us for an interactive Flamekeeper Workshop with Betty Ray, founder of the Center for Ritual Design, exploring how we can create rituals that help us honor important experiences, transitions, and intentions.
Ritual doesn’t have to be religious, elaborate, or handed down to us. Drawing from her work in human-centered ritual design, Betty will help us explore how simple, intentional words, actions, symbols, and gatherings can create meaning, connection, and a sense of transition.
Together, we’ll apply these ideas to concrete moments in our own lives and communities—exploring how we might design rituals for the people and spaces we care for, as well as how ritual can help the Contemplarium honor the human journeys of our neighbors.
Through conversation, reflection, and hands-on exercises, we’ll practice creating rituals that bring deeper meaning to moments that deserve to be marked.
Betty Ray is an educator, facilitator, and founder of the Center for Ritual Design. A 2020 Mira Fellow and former Director of Innovation at the George Lucas Educational Foundation, she has developed human-centered approaches to helping individuals, communities, and organizations create meaningful rituals and rites of passage.
This session is part of the Flamekeeper Workshop series and will be moderated by Seanan Fong, Founding Director of the SF Contemplarium.

events.title: August Lamm - You Don't Need a Smartphone
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: In this revelatory manifesto, anti-tech activist August Lamm gives you the courage and confidence to ditch your smartphone once and for all. When I owned a smartphone, my life was bad. I knew this. What I did not know was that I had a choice. August Lamm wasted her youth on the internet. In her late twenties, burnt out as a social media influencer, she sold her smartphone and switched to a dumb phone. Immediately, her mental health improved, her attention span increased, and her curiosity returned. Since then, she has made it her mission to help others do the same. Lamm started using a smartphone at age 14, so she knows how it feels to come of age glued to a screen—and how hard it is to break free. Filled with moving stories and practical suggestions, You Don’t Need a Smartphone proves that living without a computer in your pocket is not only possible but ideal. Offering guidance on selecting a new phone, navigating without GPS, meeting people offline, and overcoming obstacles like digital tickets and dual-factor authentication, You Don’t Need a Smartphone is as urgent and radical as its title, and a new blueprint for a fulfilling life in the Information Age. “The essential guide to putting down your phone — and coming back to real life.” —Catherine Price, #1 NYT bestselling author of How to Break Up With Your Phone "Accessible... Warmly inspirational for those seeking liberation from their digital devices." — Kirkus August Lamm is a writer and visual artist. She is the author of one art book, Crosshatching in Pen & Ink, and a forthcoming novel. August Lamm - photo credit Andy Henley Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our SF Ferry Building store. events.title: Jennifer Liss' "WIDE EYE" Meet & Greet
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: A whimsical adventure story about a young girl, a wacky museum, and a local monster, exploring the transformative power of imagination. Northern California author Jennifer Liss will be at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore chatting with her fans and signing copies of her children's book Wide Eye . She'll be at the store on Sunday, October 11 from 2:00 PM - 3:00 PM so come on down and join the fun! Every year, 10-year-old Meridian spends her summer with Grandpa Frank on Wide Eye Lake, where she helps out at his quirky museum dedicated to the mysterious Wide Eye monster. But this year, something is different. Tasked with organizing the museum's old files, Meridian stumbles across more than just faded photos and scribbled sightings of mysterious paw prints. Hidden among the clutter are some old mementos that unlock a long-buried family secret—one that turns her entire world upside down. Not only does Meridian have a family mystery to solve, but this summer she has to avoid 2 prankster classmates who just so happen to be vacationing nearby. Summer at Wide Eye Lake really isn't turning out to be the magical escape it used to be. Can Meridian rediscover the magic of the lake and the local stories she once loved, or will her family be forever changed? Wide Eye is a heartwarming, family-focused middle-grade adventure that explores the power of imagination and the healing nature of friendship. JENNIFER LISS writes books for kids and teens. She is the author of the middle grade novel Wide Eye. Jennifer has also written more than fifty books for struggling readers. She is a recipient of the Highlights Foundation Lee Bennett Hopkins Scholarship and the Boyds Mills PJ Library Scholarship and is a regional coordinator for the Society of Children's Book Writers and Illustrators (SCBWI). Jennifer lives in Northern California with her family.

events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A story of recovery, love, and loss—a memoir of healing ourselves and the natural world. Moving through the intensely personal and kindred terrain of love, recovery, and loss, An Armsfull of Birds is a climate memoir that tells the story of developing deeply held commitments to ourselves, to those we love, and ultimately to the ailing natural world. Cara will be joined in conversation by Neal Allen, a coach and co-author of the recent New York Times Bestseller Good Writing. Cara Benson did not come to love easy. As a low bottom addict, she crawled through subway tunnels and partnered with an abusive man. When she came face to face with her own death, she chose life. Her journey of survival led her into recovery, to climbing mountains, and ultimately to Jon, the man with whom she cultivated a relationship that began as “second chance lovers” and slowly developed into one as lifetime partners. Years later, Benson unexpectedly found herself in devastation as she came to terms with losing Jon to suicide. As she retreated into her grief, she also retreated into the woods of upstate New York, exploring the forests not as the avid hiker she’d become in recovery, but as a meanderer who had lost her way. Here she found more grief in her observation of the effects of climate change. In confronting her loss, Benson came to realize that the lessons she learned from loving Jon in sickness, health, and death could be applied to her relationship with the non-human world. From squirreling away oak acorns for reforestation of a logged property to maintaining feeders for the birds Jon adored, Benson’s daily life became a sort of field guide for how to live with a deep and abiding commitment to the future of the planet despite challenging odds. Moving through the intensely personal and kindred terrain of love, recovery, and loss, An Armsfull of Birds is a climate memoir that tells the story of developing deeply held commitments to ourselves, to those we love, and ultimately to the ailing natural world. “I opened it up to read the first few pages and then spent five hours reading the rest. Beautifully done. Poignant, human, authentic.” —Jenny Lawson, The Bloggess and #1 New York Times bestselling author of How To Be Okay When Nothing Is Okay "This is a book about many profound things, but one of them is healing, and in particular the healing possibilities of the physical world around us. Of course, as Benson recognizes, healing needs to—and can—go both ways. A valuable book!" —Bill McKibben, author of Here Comes the Sun “Cara Benson feels everything so deeply and tells her stories so honestly. Part recovery story, part eco-travelogue, part grief memoir, An Armsfull of Birds is a nuanced, thoughtful book about what it means to live fully, even when that means surviving your most beloved people. A memoir that will break your heart and put it back together again.” —Amy Shearn, award-winning author of Animal Instinct and Unseen City Cara Benson has been published in The New York Times, Boston Review, Orion, Sierra Magazine, The Brooklyn Rail, Los Angeles Review of Books , and selected for Best American Poetry . Her first book, a collection of prose poems called (made) , was well reviewed in The Huffington Post and The Brooklyn Rail , among other publications. She has received a New York Foundation for the Arts Fellowship and the bpNichol Award. Benson lives in a former church on the ancestral homelands of the Stockbridge-Munsee Band of Mohican Indians in upstate NY. An Armsfull of Birds: A Personal Field Guide to Love, Loss, and Commitment is her first memoir. Neal Allen is a coach and writer. He co-authored the recent New York Times Bestseller Good Writing: 36 Ways to Improve Your Sentences (Penguin Avery 2026) with his wife, Anne Lamott. In his private practice Neal draws from historical, psychological, and spiritual perspectives to design practical tools that aim toward freedom. A former journalist and corporate executive, he has written for newspapers, general interest magazines, and literary journals. Other books are Better Days: Tame Your Inner Critic (Namaste Books, 2023) and Shapes of Truth: Discover God Inside You (2021). Neal holds master’s degrees in Political Science and Eastern Classics. Anne and Neal live in Marin County. events.title: Michael Douglas - One Helluva Ride
events.location: Golden Gate Theatre 1 Taylor Street San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Don't miss this one-night-only conversation with Academy Award-winning actor and producer Michael Douglas celebrating the release of his new memoir, One Helluva Ride . A signed bookplate edition of the book is included with each ticket. Beginning with his fractured childhood and a complex relationship with his superstar father, Kirk Douglas, Michael Douglas finally gives the full and uncensored account of a remarkable life. One Helluva Ride reveals incredible behind-the-scenes stories featuring a Who’s Who of Hollywood, many of them never revealed before and some outrageously funny, with an unflinching honesty about his sometimes bad-boy life. More About One Helluva Ride Beginning with his fractured childhood and a complex relationship with his superstar father, Kirk Douglas, Michael Douglas finally gives the full and uncensored account of a remarkable life. One Helluva Ride reveals incredible behind-the-scenes stories featuring a Who’s Who of Hollywood, many of them never revealed before and some outrageously funny, with an unflinching honesty about his sometimes bad-boy life. Initially dismissed as just the handsome son of a legendary movie star, at age thirty-one he shook up Hollywood when he won his first Oscar for producing the five-time Academy Award-winning classic film One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest. Told he would never be more than a “TV actor,” he quit the hit series The Streets of San Francisco to become an international movie star, with a list of classic films that have grossed billions of dollars, winning a second Oscar for his riveting performance as Gordon Gekko in Wall Street. “I can’t think about my life without thinking of my movies,” Douglas says, and he recounts his career through twelve of his most iconic films, including One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest, The China Syndrome, Romancing the Stone, Jewel of the Nile, Fatal Attraction, Wall Street, War of the Roses, Basic Instinct, Falling Down, The American President, Traffic and Behind the Candelabra. These movies not only captured the cultural zeitgeist but often defined it. Yet as Douglas’s fame grew, so did his personal struggles. He recounts the full, unfiltered story of his turbulent first marriage; infidelity and affairs with some of the most beautiful actresses in Hollywood; his own serious struggle with alcohol, drugs and rehab; the heartbreaking fight to save his son from an addiction that sent him to prison; and his against-all-odds battle with stage IV cancer. He saw Catherine Zeta Jones on a movie screen and instantly fell for her. Their incredible love story transformed his life and proved all the tabloids wrong, enduring after twenty-five years of marriage. Father, son, husband, actor, producer, brother and friend. This is the real, raw, deeply honest and vulnerable Michael Douglas you didn’t know—until now. --- --- --- Michael Douglas is a legendary actor and producer. Throughout his career, he has received two Academy Awards, a BAFTA Award, five Golden Globe Awards, a Primetime Emmy Award, and two Screen Actors Guild Awards. He was honored with the AFI Lifetime Achievement Award in 2009, two Honorary Cesars in 1998 and 2016, a Film Society at Lincoln Center Gala Tribute in 2010, a Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award in 2004, and a Star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2018. Douglas has also served for twenty-seven years as a United Nations Messenger of Peace. events.title: Melissa King - The Girl Who Became King
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Join us at the Ferry Building for a meet-and-greet celebration of award-winning chef, author, television personality, and activist Melissa King to mark the release of her new memoir, The Girl Who Became King . This intimate, captivating, and heartfelt memoir explores family, food, and Melissa's journey to finding her voice as a queer Chinese American chef. Embracing my love of food has empowered me to embrace every layer of who I am: my Chinese heritage, my American upbringing, and all the parts of me that felt too much and not enough. When I chose myself, I set her free. Just me. The girl who became king. As a kid, Melissa King lived for the moment she would come from elementary school, grab her prized Chinese meat cleaver, and prepare dinner for her family. She already knew cooking was her future, but she didn’t know how hard she’d have to fight to make that dream a reality. Growing up, King felt like she was stuck in a box that was only getting smaller. Her Shanghainese and Cantonese immigrant parents had certain expectations—none of which included going to culinary school or falling in love with women. American culture also dictated that kitchens were a man’s world. But trying to live by these rules felt like no life at all. Determined to forge her own path, she fought her way into the demanding world of Michelin- starred kitchens, while discovering a home in the queer community. When she entered Top Chef as a reluctant contestant, inspired by her grandmother’s advice to follow her heart, she began embracing the flavors, culture, and parts of herself she had once forgotten. This journey of self- discovery through food leads her back to her parents, where love creates room for their strengths and imperfections. In this heartfelt memoir, Melissa King shows that empowerment comes from embracing all the different ingredients that make up who you are, and models the hard-won courage it takes to believe in yourself against the odds. **** Melissa King is a James Beard Award-winning chef, author, and television personality. She is the author of the cookbook Cook Like a King: Recipes from My California Chinese Kitchen , which won the 2026 James Beard Award. She is the winner and fan favorite of Bravo’s Top Chef: All Stars L.A. and holds the record for the most challenge wins in the show’s history. Known for her modern California Chinese cuisine, she is a leading voice shaping conversations through food, cultural storytelling, and advocacy. A queer Shanghainese Cantonese American, she grew up in Los Angeles’s San Gabriel Valley. Her work has since taken her beyond the kitchen into television, fashion, and culture, including hosting Tasting Wild for National Geographic, curating the 2022 Met Gala menu, and being featured in global campaigns for Levi’s and GAP. She lives in San Francisco. events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

events.title: 3RD EAR PRESENTS: Mystic Songs of India - Exploring the Wisdom & Poetry of Kabir Through Folk Songs with Priyal Maheshwari
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this immersive workshop, we explore the deeper esoteric meanings within the poetry of Indian mystic saints such as Kabir and Guru Nanak through the indigenous folk songs of the Malwa region of Central India. These songs belong to a living oral tradition that has been carried forward for over 600 years.

Priyal will guide us through this journey by singing and interpreting these songs while accompanying himself on traditional instruments like the Tambura and Kartaal. Printed translations will be provided, allowing participants to follow along and join in the singing if they wish. After each song, we will pause for reflection, creating space for participants to share whatever arises within them. We will also spend time in shared silence, gently turning inward to experience the stillness pointed to in the songs.

Priyal will also share stories from the life of Kabir, insights into India’s oral traditions, and reflections on his own journey — how he encountered his Guru and how these teachings have shaped his life. Through song, storytelling, collective reflection, and silence, this workshop invites us to touch something deeper within ourselves — a space where boundaries soften, and a sense of oneness with each other and the world begins to emerge.

About Priyal Maheshwari:

Priyal Maheshwari is a musician and yoga teacher whose journey bridges the worlds of science, spirituality, and the arts. After graduating from Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur and spending six years in the IT industry, he felt an inner calling to step away from the corporate path and dedicate his life to the transformative power of music and wellness practices. Through his work, Priyal integrates music, yoga, and meditation as tools for healing and self-discovery. His approach helps people reconnect with the deeper aspects of their being and cultivate a more balanced, integrated way of living.

Alongside extensive training in classical music, Priyal has immersed himself in the oral traditions of saint poets such as Kabir, Nanak, and Meera. He continues to learn directly from PadmaShri Prahlad Singh Tipanya ji, one of the foremost carriers of Kabir’s singing tradition from the Malwa region of Central India. These teachings have deeply shaped Priyal’s own musical journey, grounding it in devotion, simplicity, and the timeless wisdom of the saints.

Priyal regularly shares his music in concerts, satsangs, and community gatherings. He also organizes retreats and collaborative events with Prahlad ji and his ensemble, creating spaces where participants can experience the confluence of music, spirituality, and collective harmony.

events.title: Elephant Gym: More Real Than Dreams (with Band Member Q&A)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Elephant Gym successfully completed a world tour spanning 60 cities across 23 countries. However, behind this achievement lay an unseen crisis of disbandment, along with hidden conflicts and struggles. What does it truly mean to be a band? The film was first screened in October 2025 at the Kaohsiung Film Festival, one of Taiwan’s leading film festivals, and will also be shown in theaters in both Japan and Taiwan. While their world tour across 23 countries and 60 cities was a major success, the film reveals the untold story behind it—including a looming breakup crisis during its preparation, as well as the band’s internal conflicts and struggles. “If your dreams were to become reality, what price would you be willing to pay?“ Elephant Gym, an instrumental band from Kaohsiung, Taiwan, has been creating indie music since its formation in 2012. Their sound blends complex rhythms with irregular time signatures and sophisticated melodies. In Taiwan, their avant-garde musical style often raised the question: who would even listen to this? However, in 2024, they embarked on a world tour covering 23 countries and 60 shows, including three performances in the Philippines. They captivated audiences worldwide and firmly established their presence. Yet behind the glamorous stage, there were deep struggles. Between guitarist Tell Chang and bassist KT Chang—who are siblings—there were conflicts between family ties and band dynamics. Drummer Chia-Chin Tu had to make the difficult decision to leave another band. And just before the world tour, the band faced a crisis that nearly led to their breakup—filled with unseen pain and clashes. Still, they chose to believe in their music and in their bond, and continued moving forward. From a niche genre to the global stage, Elephant Gym asks through their musical journey: What is a band made of people with different backgrounds? What does it mean for people to connect? Between dreams and reality, they found their own “truth.” Come witness that answer in theaters. Band member Q&A (over Zoom) to follow the screening! events.title: Author talk: No to Nuclear with Linda Pentz Gunter and Eric Wolfe
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Please join us for a discussion with the author of No to Nuclear: Why Nuclear Power Destroys Lives, Derails Climate Progress and Provokes War . Linda Pentz Gunter and Eric Wolfe speak in conversation on Sunday, October 11th at 7 pm. Trump is pushing for nuclear power expansion, to enrich himself and his billionaire tech friends. But does anyone else really benefit? In No To Nuclea r, Pentz Gunter moves beyond the science and statistics, centering the stories of the Nuclear Age around the inherent colonialism and corruption of the nuclear industry and the Indigenous communities who have been preyed upon for profit and left to pay a terrible price. She takes us to Native American and First Nations communities, to the nomadic Tuareg of Niger and Aboriginal lands in Australia, where Black, Brown and Indigenous communities, far from the countries who profit, have been forced to mine the uranium that fuels the nuclear industry. She finds similar stories where atomic bombs have been tested, in the Marshall Islands and French Polynesia. And she reminds us that animals, who we disregard so cruelly, are harmed, too. Finally, the book urges us to rediscover the beauty and the miracle that is Planet Earth and to embrace justice first, if we are to have a chance to prevent the worst of the climate crisis and avoid nuclear war. Linda Pentz Gunter is the founder and executive director of the US-based non-profit Beyond Nuclear. She also created and writes for her organization's news platform, Beyond Nuclear International. A former full-time journalist, she continues to contribute feature stories to the Morning Star (UK) and Ralph Nader's Capitol Hill Citizen . Eric Wolfe has been active in peace, environment, and labor issues for 60 years. He helped organize the Clamshell Alliance in 1976 to oppose construction of the Seabrook reactors. Through his puppet show, Burnt Toast: Trouble in the Nation’s Breadbasket , he advocated for non-violent direct action against nuclear power in 20 states, including California. Acres of Clams , his feature-length documentary about the Clamshell Alliance, was released in 2024. Eric has lived in San Francisco since 1988 with his wife, science writer Susan Freinkel.

events.title: Santiago Cruz
events.location: The Independent, 628 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117
events.description: Santiago Cruz is one of the most important pop artists in Colombia and Latin America. With more than 20 years of career, the singer-songwriter from Tolima has become an essential name in the international pop music scene, earning multiple recognitions over the years. With 10 albums released to date, Santiago has received 6 Latin GRAMMY nominations (Best Singer-Songwriter Album: 2010 Cruce de Caminos, 2015 Equilibrio, 2017 Trenes, Aviones y Viajes Interplanetarios, 2023 Nueve; Record of the Year: 2013 Desde Lejos; Best Singer-Songwriter Song: 1.200 Kilómetros in 2023). In September 2021, he published his first book, Diciembre, otra vez — a collection of real-time stories recounting different moments of his life, his artistic journey, his perspective on music, the industry, and social issues, as well as his personal transformation. He was a judge on La Descarga, a prime-time show on Caracol TV. In 2023, he released his ninth studio album Nueve, produced by Juan Pablo Vega, and toured with his Después de la Tormenta Tour, performing 25 shows across Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, and nine U.S. cities — including an unforgettable sold-out concert at Bogotá’s Movistar Arena. In 2024, he kicked off Un Tour Íntimo de Verdad in Mexico, selling out shows in Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Querétaro, with additional performances in Toluca, Monterrey, and Puebla. With Un Tour Acústico de Verdad, the singer-songwriter played five shows in the United States and continued through 14 cities in Colombia, selling out three nights in Bogotá, Bucaramanga, and Medellín. In 2025, he released his tenth studio album, Quince de Caminos, a celebration of the 15th anniversary of Cruce de Caminos (his most significant album to date). The record features 2025 versions of the hits that made up the original album and includes collaborations with Junior Zamora, Monsieur Periné, and Juan Pablo Vega. Alongside the album, Quince de Caminos, La Gira was launched, featuring more than 40 shows across the United States, Mexico, Colombia, Argentina, Chile, Spain, Ecuador, the Dominican Republic, and Guatemala. In 2026, his eleventh album, Fragmentos, will be released. The record will feature 11 unreleased singles, along with a tour that will take him to different cities across Colombia, Latin America, Europe, and the United States.

events.title: Debra Silverman - I Don't Believe in Astrology
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Renowned psychotherapist and astrologer Debra Silverman offers an accessible guide to the life-changing benefits of astrology, combining wisdom from both fields to help readers remember the truth of their soul's expression through the eyes of self-love. This paperback edition will feature a special limited purple cover, while supplies last! In a chaotic, confusing, and divisive world, Debra Silverman introduces astrology as the medicine for accepting our human nature--its idiosyncrasies and dilemmas. Through an application of both therapy and astrology, this breakthrough guide equips readers with tools that release self-judgment, inner criticism, negativity, and misunderstanding. Every sign struggles with psychological issues. Understanding the unique topics relative to your sign, it’s no surprise you are quirky. Learning how to accept who you are and love yourself unconditionally through the lens of astrology is at the heart of this book. Debra Silverman teaches you how to step away from the struggle of your ego and see yourself with the calm objectivity of your soul. You will learn to love what you see—not just your best qualities but everything about you. She shows you how to aim for the high road of your personality. Most of all, you will cultivate compassion for all the other signs in the zodiac. Learn the meaning of the sun, moon, rising sign, Mercury, and Saturn. Using Debra’s method combining the wisdom of astrology and psychology, readers will remember the truth of their soul’s expression, seen through the eyes of self-love. “A lovely piece of writing, light on its feet, landing blows when they are needed, comforting when required but never pulling punches.” —Sting “I have a feeling it might open your heart and mind to parts of yourself you’ve yet to discover.” —Julianne Hough, bestselling author, entertainer, and entrepreneur “A sparkling gem... This is essential reading for these times!” —Colette Baron-Reid, bestselling oracle expert, author, and artist "In a sea of books on astrology, Debra’s stands out." —Gabby Bernstein, #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Universe Has Your Back Debra Silverman is an astrologer, psychotherapist-trained educator, and author who has spent nearly five decades building a disciplined, system-based approach to astrology rooted in temperament, pattern recognition, and human behavior. At a moment when astrology is both ubiquitous and flattened into algorithmic shorthand, Silverman has become one of the field’s most consequential institutional voices, known for codifying chart literacy into frameworks that can be taught, applied, and carried forward across relationships, work, and personal change. Silverman’s work is anchored in clinical training and long practice. She earned a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Dance from York University and a Master’s degree in Clinical Psychology from Antioch University, then built a career working with individuals, couples, and families while developing a methodology that treats the birth chart as a structured vocabulary rather than entertainment. Her signature emphasis on the Four Elements gives audiences a clear entry point into temperament, conflict style, and stress response, translating complex archetypal material into language that holds up in conversation and decision-making. In 2016, she founded Debra Silverman Astrology, formalizing her methodology into a global education platform spanning multi-level curriculum, mentorship, retreats and intensives, and advanced practitioner training. At the center is Applied Astrology School, a structured program that has trained thousands of students worldwide, supported by trained mentors and advanced cohorts. Silverman also developed the 4E process, an elements-based methodology practiced through individualized sessions and certification retreats by trained facilitators, extending her work beyond instruction into a defined practice model. Within contemporary astrology, Silverman is widely regarded as a trusted authority for method and rigor. Her work has trained thousands of students and practitioners in a shared vocabulary and practical tools, while also serving as an on-ramp for a growing mainstream audience looking to engage astrology as a framework for self-understanding. Over decades, she has built a curriculum-driven ecosystem rooted in accountability, and her teaching has become a primary source of institutional knowledge in a field often dominated by shorthand. Silverman has also made her mark as a published author. Her first book, The Missing Element: Inspiring Compassion for the Human Condition (Findhorn Press), introduced her Four Elements framework to readers looking for language around temperament, patterns, and the parts of themselves they tend to judge, and it was later selected for Aaron Rodgers’ book club in 2022. Her second book, I Don’t Believe in Astrology: A Therapist’s Guide to the Life-Changing Wisdom of the Stars (St. Martin’s Essentials, April 2025), begins with a skeptic’s premise and builds a therapist’s argument, treating the chart as a practical framework for self-observation and accountability rather than a matter of belief. Debra’s influence extends well beyond her school. Across platforms, she has built a large, highly engaged audience of adult learners, particularly women, who return to her work for language around temperament, relationships, and the patterns that repeat until someone finally names them. She also hosts The I Don’t Believe in Astrology Podcast , a natural extension of her teaching, where she breaks down her framework in real time, defines terms with precision, and translates the chart into behavior you can recognize in yourself and in the people closest to you. That combination of institutional teaching and public-facing explanation has placed Silverman in a rare position: both a leading trainer within the field and a trusted interpreter for the broader culture. She has been sought out by public figures and creatives across industries; notable supporters and collaborators include Zach Bush, Gino Wickman, Aaron Rodgers, Sting, Tommy Chong, Jennifer Aniston, Julianne Hough, and India Arie. Taken together, her books, education platform, trainings, retreats, and media work operate as a cohesive body of instruction, with a shared vocabulary that students return to and practitioners carry forward. events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.title: You Don't Need a Smartphone
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: A guide to getting your life back · Who are you without your smartphone? At this rate, you'll never find out. In just two decades, the smartphone has gone from fiction to luxury to necessity. August Lamm's new book, You Don't Need a Smartphone makes a radical and discomfiting claim: that we can still choose to live without it, and furthermore, that we may soon lose the right to choose. Other books treat the symptoms of screen addiction with self-control and wellness hacks. They demonstrate how to live with the smartphone. This is the first book to demonstrate how to live without it. Part-manifesto, part-memoir, part-guidebook, You Don't Need a Smartphone provides everything you need to reclaim your life from the tyranny of screens. Lamm will be in conversation with Clio's co-founder Timothy Don about choosing life without screens. August Lamm is a writer, visual artist, and anti-tech activist. She is the author of one art book, Crosshatching in Pen & Ink, and a forthcoming novel.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: KiNG MALA
events.location: The Independent, 628 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117
events.description: What would you give for a chance to be the most omnipotent version of yourself? To finally be rid of the petty human desires that keep you from achieving greatness? To finally have it all, everything you’ve ever wanted? What would you trade? What are you willing to lose? What would you do for power? These questions are at the core of KiNG MALA’s debut album, And You Who Drowned In The Grief Of A Golden Thing . Across its wide-ranging 12 tracks – which seesaw between invigorating industrial pop and delicately refined R&B balladry – the singer-songwriter spins a tale as equally rooted in a sci-fi nightmare as it is in reality. The album follows the classic storyline of a hero’s journey to redemption, focusing on two non-descript, fictionalized characters: a human and an all-mighty entity. The front half is packed with the wonder of “what if.” What would an exchange for power look like? And more importantly, what would it sound like? (Think the experimental, living aesthetic of Bon Iver’s 22, A Million or Dijon's Absolutely , she offers – but with more bite.) The back half of the project provides answers – and it’s not pretty. By the story’s end, the human not only lacks power, but everything that made then human as well. “It's what we become, because the real dark shit that happens to women, you are never the same,” KiNG Mala shares. And at a time when the world is embracing such left-of-center storytelling, KiNG MALA is primed to emerge at the forefront of dark-pop’s new wave. “Everyone's being weird as fuck right now,” she says, citing world-building artists like Charli xcx and Chappell Roan and movies like The Substance . “We're moving into this space where we can be fucking freaks and finally be angry and disgusting – it's all manifesting.”

events.title: MUSIC MONDAY PRESENTS: SANG SIS!
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Featuring Nate’ THESOULSANGER & Mirraje · Two powerful women. Two distinctive voices. One soulful night of music. NATE’ THESOULSANGER Some artists find their voice. Nate’ THESOULSANGER inherited hers. Born and raised in Oakland, Nate’ comes from a rich musical heritage as a descendant of the Grammy-winning Gospel Hummingbirds . Raised in a legacy of faith, storytelling, and soul, music was never simply something she discovered it was part of her foundation. An award-winning vocalist, international recording artist, songwriter, producer, actress, event host, and co-founder of SoulGlo Productions, LLC , THESOULSANGER has built a career that refuses to be confined to one genre. Her sound moves through soul, gospel, R&B, hip hop, theater, and beyond , bringing authenticity, power, and unmistakable Oakland soul to every performance. Throughout her career, she has shared stages and studios with artists including Patti LaBelle, Kelly Price, Carlos Santana, MC Hammer, LaRussell , and Grammy-winning producer Narada Michael Walden , with whom she has developed a longstanding creative relationship. Her voice is also woven into Bay Area music history. Nate’ created and recorded the memorable hook for Mac Dre’s “Make You Mine,” a song that became part of his enduring musical legacy. Her credits span radio, film, theater, live production, and recording. A Bay Area Rising Star and Best Vocalist award recipient , she has received KMEL airplay, contributed vocals to the Warner Bros. film The Invasion , and established herself as a trusted creative force both onstage and behind the scenes. At Yoshi’s Oakland , Nate’ has become such a familiar presence as a headliner, host, featured vocalist, producer, and collaborator that she earned the affectionate nickname “Ms. Yoshi’s.” Whether singing, producing, acting, hosting, mentoring, or creating opportunities for others, Nate’ brings the same qualities to every room: authenticity, excellence, soul, and connection. Singer. Songwriter. Producer. Actress. Host. Mentor. Community Builder. Oakland soul in every room she enters. Nate’ THESOULSANGER. The THE is intentional. CHRISTIE “MIRRAJE” MALONE Christie “Mirraje” Malone was born to sing. The daughter of blues musician George “Bluestone” Malone , Mirraje began singing at the age of three and writing songs and poetry by age nine. A gifted singer, songwriter, and natural stage performer, music has been woven into her life from the very beginning. Growing up in Los Angeles, Mirraje’s journey has been shaped by love, loss, perseverance, and an unwavering desire to create. After caring for her mother and experiencing her passing, Mirraje stepped away from singing and writing for four years. The memory of her mother—her greatest inspiration, biggest fan, and loudest cheerleader—eventually reignited her passion and gave her the courage to dream and create again. As she embarked upon her solo career, Mirraje recognized the extraordinary musical journey that had already taken shape. She has shared the stage with celebrated artists including Stevie Wonder, Evelyn “Champagne” King, Morris Day, Zapp, Club Nouveau, Cameo, Sugar Hill Gang, and Klymaxx . Mirraje’s musical influences span genres and generations, with Anita Baker holding a special place among her favorites. Her eclectic love of music allows her to find inspiration in the experiences, thoughts, emotions, and sounds that surround her. Rather than allowing her artistry to be defined by a particular genre or category, Mirraje creates from a place of freedom and authenticity. In her own words: “Life is unpredictable and unique. It should never be defined by genres or categories; nor should our music be. I just do what feels good.” SANG SIS! Together, Nate’ THESOULSANGER and Christie “Mirraje” Malone bring two extraordinary musical journeys to one stage for SANG SIS! —a celebration of powerful women, authentic voices, soulful storytelling, and music that refuses to be put in a box. Rooted in different musical legacies but connected by soul, these two women bring experience, grit, passion, and undeniable vocals to Yoshi’s Oakland for a night designed to make you feel something.

events.title: Return to Center: Exploring Stability, Mobility & Ease with Vickie Russell Bell
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves..



Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition.

Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.

events.title: Half-Day Silent Unguided Retreat
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice.
This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods.
There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of
meditation, all are welcome.

The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive
between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before
the first bell.

The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation:
9:30 AM – 10:10 AM
10:20 AM – 11:00 AM
11:10 AM – 11:50 AM

A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period.
The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between
sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom.
Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep
voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire
morning.

You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during
a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and
the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice
elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell.

The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website.

Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by
12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely
manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

events.title: Danny O'Dea - Packages
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Packages is a novel about the stories we tell to survive—and the ones that haunt us when survival isn’t enough. At once tender and unsettling, Packages announces a bold new literary voice and marks the arrival of a writer unafraid to look directly at the cost of looking away. Set against the charged intimacy of a Southern college town, Danny O’Dea’s debut follows Michael McKnight, a young man orbiting grief, desire, and moral uncertainty as he navigates friendship, sexuality, faith, and the quiet violence of complicity. When a series of mysterious packages begin arriving at an off-campus house, Michael finds himself drawn into a web of secrecy that forces him to confront not only what his peers are capable of, but what he himself is willing to ignore. Moving fluidly between memory and present action, Packages is both a coming-of-age story and a reckoning—about masculinity, queerness, guilt, and the ways institutions and friendships fail the most vulnerable. With prose that is sharp, intimate, and darkly funny, O’Dea captures the intoxicating freedom of youth alongside its moral blind spots, asking how responsibility is formed, deferred, or abandoned altogether. "Peter Hoffman is like nobody else. He is Hollywood at its aggressive, hard-bargaining worst, and at its noble, idealistic best. If you want to know how the entertainment business really works, which is to say, how the money works and the deals and the law and the morality— and there is a morality! —read his book. Peter has been in the belly of the beast (A-list version), and he has seen it all with his wide-open eyes. This is actually existing Hollywood, and Peter is the rare person with the brains, guts and patience to explain it all." -Henry Bean Danny O'Dea is a writer whose work examines grief, masculinity, and the quiet violence of looking away. His fiction is concerned with the stories we tell to survive—and the cost of believing them. Packages is his debut novel. Danny O'Dea - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. Free Admission / Open Seating There will be a signing line or meet-and-greet following the presentation.

events.title: WHO IS SINGING? Embody and Celebrate the Cosmic Nature of Sound: Improvise Icaros, Ragas, and Medicine Melodies with Silvia Nakkach
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In these immersive sessions, Silvia invites you to experience sound as a living, cosmic force — where everything sings: plants, waters, stars, and even silence itself. Across traditions, shamans and sound practitioners have attuned to this hidden music, expressing it through “medicine melodies” that arise as spontaneous transmissions from nature and the spirit world.

•	Enter the voice as a portal of spirit and shakti awakening, where Sound becomes a vehicle for healing, joy, and cosmic connection.
•	Explore the idea that all of existence is alive with sound — plants, waters, stars, and even silence —inviting us into a field of deep listening.
•	Learn to engage “medicine melodies” as spontaneous transmissions from nature and the spirit world, expressed through voice and simple instruments.
•	Experience initiatory sound practices drawn from Icaros (Peruvian Amazon), Afro-Brazilian invocations, Indian ragas, mantric improvisation, and healing invocations.
•	Cultivate contemplative listening, tonal centering, and free your voice as forms of musical divination and attunement.
•	Develop greater clarity, neural coherence, emotional resonance, and spiritual receptivity through vibrational formulas.
•	Be guided by Silvia Nakkach’s decades of sound shamanism into the ecstatic, contemplative, and transformative power of your sonic presence. 

You’ll learn to offer medicine melodies as tools for group facilitation and mystical communion. No singing experience needed — only your willingness to listen, feel, and let the voice reveal its sacred intelligence.


Teacher Bio: 
Silvia Nakkach M.A., MMT, also known as Saraswati Devi, is a Grammy-nominated composer, interdisciplinary vocal artist, Hindustani raga musician, and multihyphenate educator and scholar. Nakkach has released 18 albums, authored the book "Free Your Voice", and offered significant scholarly contributions to the academic study of music and sound therapies. She is a former clinical psychologist who serves on the faculty of the California Institute of Integral Studies’ East-West Psychology Department. Silvia is also a Music Mentor at the CIIS’s Center for Psychedelic Therapies and Research. You can listen to her explorations of sound, spirituality, and the human experience on her podcast "Beyond Music." She is the founding director of the International Vox Mundi School of Sound, with centers in Japan, South Korea, Brazil, India, and across the US and the Bay Area. Visit:voxmundiproject.com.

events.title: Grace Lin's "THE LITTLE STONE BUDDHA"
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Tuesday, October 13 at 6:30 PM when award-winning and New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Grace Lin comes to the store to share her latest picture book The Little Stone Buddha. Grace will sign copies of her book after the presentation. When a small stone Buddha falls off a cyclist's wagon, he lands in a neglected part of a busy city street. People often throw trash here, turning this part of the city into a rather unpleasant sight. But as passersby begin to notice the little stone Buddha, they start to wonder: what if we each made a small change that brightened this shared part of our community? Inspired by a true story, The Little Stone Buddha shows us how a small action—or, in this case, a small Buddha—can change a moment, which can change a decision, which can change the spirit, which can, in the end, change everything . GRACE LIN is the award-winning and bestselling author and illustrator of over thirty books, including A Big Mooncake for Little Star (a Caldecott Honor); A Big Bed for Little Snow; Where the Mountain Meets the Moon (a Newbery Honor ); Chinese Menu; The Gate, the Girl, and the Dragon; The Year of the Dog ; and the Ling & Ting series. Grace lives in Massachusetts and invites you to connect with her at gracelin.com .

events.title: Marion Nestle Author Talk • Sugar Coated: Unboxing the Hidden Forces Shaping America's Favorite Breakfast Food
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Marion Nestle is Paulette Goddard Professor of Nutrition, Food Studies, and Public Health, Emerita, at New York University and a Visiting Professor of Nutritional Sciences at Cornell University. An internationally recognized expert on food policy and nutrition, her work explores the scientific, political, and corporate forces that shape what we eat. She is the author or co-author of sixteen books, including the groundbreaking Food Politics , What to Eat , Soda Politics , Unsavory Truth , and her memoir, Slow Cooked . Her newest book is The Fish Counter , and What to Eat Now , a fully revised edition of What to Eat , will be published later this year. A longtime public voice on food policy, Nestle writes the acclaimed Food Politics blog and has received numerous honors, including the James Beard Leadership Award and the 2023 Edinburgh Medal for contributions to science and the humanities. Dianne Jacob is a journalist and food writing teacher based in the Bay Area. She is the author of the multiple award-winning book Will Write for Food: Pursue Your Passion and Bring Home the Dough Writing Recipes, Cookbooks, Blogs, and More . Dianne writes a free monthly newsletter about food writing on Substack. Sugar Coated: Unboxing the Hidden Forces Shaping America's Favorite Breakfast Food - World-renowned food politics expert Marion Nestle joins forces with former cereal executive Lisa Sutherland to examine what cereal boxes reveal about American culture and food politics. If you want to understand how the food business works, just have a look at a box of breakfast cereal. Hardly anything on supermarket shelves is bigger, bolder, or more deliberately designed. The fiercely competitive industry that brings us Cheerios, Froot Loops, and Trix sells a distinctly American dream: indulgence and health in one convenient package. Cereal boxes chronicle our shifting national obsessions with health, ingredients, dietary advice, and American culture. They show us what sells food: cartoons for kids, athletes for men, weight loss for women. And hidden in the history of cereal package designs, we find clues to the corporate lobbying that shapes agricultural policy, health claims, and labeling regulations.

events.title: Romance Author Kathleen Reidy Live at a Wine Bar!
events.location: 32 West Portal Ave. San Francisco, CA 94127
events.description: Bookshop West Portal is thrilled to host debut romance author Kathleen Reidy to celebrate her new novel, Engineering A Love Story . Set in San Francisco in the early 2000s during the dot-com boom, this book is a perfect feel-good read, best enjoyed with a glass of wine. As such, this event will be held at Hardware Coffee Co., a coffee shop, flower shop, and wine bar on West Portal Ave.! (Only a few doors down from our store.) Books will be available to buy on-site. Join us to get swept off your feet by this sizzling romance set in our very own city. Kathleen will be joined in conversation by Karen Nelson, author of The Last Summer at Feather River and The Sunken Town. We hope to see you there! This event is FREE to attend. Seating is first-come, first-served. (RSVPs are optional, but encouraged for our planning purposes.) About the Book: At the height of the boom, ambition is easy — love is the real gamble It's the year 2000--dot-coms, Bush v. Gore, and sky-high San Francisco rents. But while the country swoons with irrational exuberance, Chelsea Lefevre's life is deflating faster than a tech bubble. She'd had everything she thought she was supposed to want: a house on Boston's North Shore, exquisite wedding china, a Waspy mother-in-law. A safe, steady marriage. But after a mortifying slip-up, Chelsea finds herself heading into the 21st century alone. Her lifeboat? A new job advising tech execs, taken to escape the misogyny she endured as a software engineer--only to discover she has a surprising knack for spotting the next hot thing. Determined just to stay afloat, Chelsea doesn't have time to wonder if anything beyond safe and steady is possible. Then, on a West Coast assignment, she meets Seth Murphy, a magnetic sales executive at one of the country's hottest startups. Professional boundaries make him off-limits, but she can't resist his pull. What begins as a secret, casual affair soon jeopardizes Chelsea's career, her newfound independence--and her heart. Witty and warm, Engineering a Love Story questions how much a smart woman can risk when she's the only female in the room. About the Author: Kathleen Reidy is a writer and public librarian based in the Boston area. She holds a master’s degree in library science and spent more than a decade in the tech industry. Her short fiction has been published by Puddingstone Press and WayWords . She lives with her husband and daughters. Engineering a Love Story is her first novel.

events.title: Portrait of an Artist As a Young Woman
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: The revolution had a sex life. · The late 1960s told young women to get free—sexually, politically, artistically. And for many, those freedoms were exhilarating. But liberation could also create contradictions of its own. In Alexis Krasilovsky’s new novel, Portrait of an Artist as a Young Woman , an aspiring filmmaker plunges into the art and sexual experimentation of the era, navigating desire, ambition, creative possibility, exploitation, and old hierarchies in new clothes. Judy Juanita’s Virgin Soul , meanwhile, follows a young Black woman drawn into the revolutionary politics of the Black Panther Party, where idealism, danger, race, sex, and power collide. Krasilovsky and Juanita—whose own lives intersect with the histories their novels revisit—come together at Clio’s to interrogate the mythology of liberation from the inside. What did “free love” offer women, and what did it demand of them? Could radical movements escape the inequalities of the society they wanted to overthrow? And what did it take for a woman to insist on being not someone’s muse, girlfriend, comrade, or supporting character, but an artist and political actor in her own right? Moving between fiction and lived history, from the New York art world and the emergence of women filmmakers to the Black Panthers and Oakland, their conversation asks what happens when women tell the story of a supposedly liberated generation for themselves. Alexis Krasilovsky is an award-winning filmmaker, author, and Professor Emerita of Cinema and Television Arts at California State University, Northridge. A member of Yale’s first coeducational graduating class, she made End of the Art World , featuring Andy Warhol, Robert Rauschenberg, Jasper Johns, Roy Lichtenstein, and other major artists. Her decades-long work on women and filmmaking includes the documentary Women Behind the Camera and the books Women Behind the Camera: Conversations with Camerawomen and Shooting Women: Behind the Camera, Around the World . Her new novel, Portrait of an Artist as a Young Woman , will be published by City Point Press in September 2026. Judy Juanita is an award-winning poet, novelist, playwright, and essayist whose work spans race, gender, radical politics, and California life. Her semi-autobiographical novel Virgin Soul follows a young Black woman drawn into the Black Panther Party in the late 1960s. Her recent books include the memoir California Fever Dream and Abortion (or Woman as Threefold Murderess) . Her poetry collection Manhattan my ass, you’re in Oakland won the 2021 American Book Award from the Before Columbus Foundation, and her essay collection DeFacto Feminism: Essays Straight Outta Oakland examines race, gender, politics, and spirituality through the perspective of a Black activist and self-described “feminist foot soldier.”

events.title: Yotam Ottolenghi - Ottolenghi Simple Too
events.location: Dominican University of California Angelico Hall 20 Olive Ave San Rafael, CA 94901
events.description: Join Yotam Ottolenghi for an intimate and energizing evening celebrating his forthcoming Fall 2026 cookbook, Simple Too , the long-awaited follow-up to his bestselling Ottolenghi Simple. Eight years after redefining “flavor without fuss,” Ottolenghi returns to explore what “simple” means now — in a world of endless notifications, long commutes, and minds split between podcasts, WhatsApp groups, and homework help. In conversation, he’ll share how Simple Too was born from real life: recipes that work with you, not against you — dishes you can begin with half a plan and still end with a deeply satisfying meal. Expect laughter, honesty, and that signature Ottolenghi spark as he declares, “The lemon is back!” and explains why bold flavor remains at the heart of simplicity. Drawing from the book’s vibrant themes, Ottolenghi will dive into the ingredients and techniques that quietly shape this new collection: beans simply dressed, black chickpeas, sesame in generous handfuls, sweet- and-spicy balances, pasta cooked directly in its sauce, and whole meals roasted start-to-finish in a single tray (with far less washing up). He’ll also introduce the new “Fundamentals” chapter — fifteen fridge-ready flavor builders like spring onion oil, green salsa, za’atar oil, confit tomatoes, and chilli crisp — the small things that make big differences on the busiest weeknights. Through stories from the writing process with co-author Verena Lochmuller, practical tips, and reflections on finding pleasure in cooking even when you’re already tired, Ottolenghi will reveal how SIMPLE TOO is less about doing less — and more about making everyday cooking feel generous, achievable, and full of joy. Yotam Ottolenghi is one of the most influential voices in contemporary food, renowned for his vibrant, vegetable-forward cuisine and imaginative approach to everyday cooking. Born in Jerusalem and based in London, he is the author of numerous acclaimed cookbooks — including Plenty, Jerusalem, Simple, Flavor, and Sweet — that have transformed how home cooks and chefs around the world think about seasonality, texture, and spice. His work extends beyond books to successful delis and restaurants, where bold combinations, fresh produce, and multicultural inspirations meet. Throughout his career, Ottolenghi has championed cooking that feels both joyful and accessible, proving that deeply flavorful food doesn’t have to be complicated. Yotam Ottolenghi is a New York Times bestselling cookbook author who contributes to the New York Times Food section and has a weekly column in The Guardian. His Ottolenghi Simple was selected as a best book of the year by NPR and the New York Times; Jerusalem, written with Sami Tamimi, was awarded Cookbook of the Year by the International Association of Culinary Professionals and named Best International Cookbook by the James Beard Foundation. He lives in London, where he co-owns an eponymous group of restaurants and the fine-dining destinations Nopi and Rovi. Yotam Ottolenghi - photo credit Jonathan Lovekin Event details: Presented by Dominican University's Institute for Leadership Studies (ILS) and Book Passage. events.description: Sitting at the forefront of contemporary jazz · 'Well, at least nobody could ever accuse us of releasing too much music!’ quips GregCarmichael on the release of their latest EP “The Empire of Lights”, ‘but I think our fans know by now that we’re a little obsessive about only releasing music when we have something ready that we really love.’ The four tracks on their latest release visit familiar themes for longtime fans, from the western shuffle of “8,000 Miles” to the reggae flavours of “Alisio”, the upbeat joy of “Back to Back” to the laid back groove of “Other People”. ‘We hope there’s something here for everyone,” says Miles Gilderdale, “we’re very lucky that over the years we’ve found fans that just get what we’re doing, so we can wear our influences on our sleeves and not have to try and fit into any one style.’ With over 35 years of recording and touring, the band’s longevity may be due in part to that spirit of never trying to fit in, but to just making music that they love. ‘I feel really grateful that we’ve been on such a long journey with our fans and they’re still there with us.’ Greg says, ‘We talk after shows, and it’s always such an honor to hear the stories of how our music has been the soundtrack to so many people’s lives.’ This EP is the first of a series of shorter musical releases that will eventually combine into a full album.’ Miles says, ‘We know that these days people listen to our music in lots of different ways, but I think we all remember the thrill of bringing a new record home and listening from start to finish, so we try and make sure everything we release works in that way as well as on playlists.’ The Empire of Lights will be released to all music platforms worldwide on June 13th, 2025, and a limited run of CDs will be pressed to be available to purchase at live shows.

events.title: Patrick Wolff Quartet
events.location: The Dawn Club, San Francisco
events.description: Patrick Wolff is a saxophone and clarinet player with a long history in the jazz scenes of New York City and San Francisco. He has performed or recorded with Albert "Tootie" Heath, Matt Wilson, Grant Stewart, Louis Moholo-Moholo, Dena Derose, and many other jazz greats. Since moving to San Francisco in 2009, Wolff has played and recorded regularly in the bands of Marcus Shelby, Richard Sears, Graham Connah, Adam Shulman, and Diana Gameros. Outside of the jazz world, he has had an eclectic mix of work including long stints in West African pop/funk group Asiko, prog metal band Kayo Dot, and with fuji music legend Adewale Ayuba. With six albums released under his name, Wolff has made his mark as a bandleader with various groups playing his original compositions, and with classic jazz quartets and quintets focused on repertoire of the bebop and hard bop eras. His playing is characterized by a focus on lyricism and an embrace of the whole lineage of jazz styles. Wolff is also a passionate jazz educator and advocate. For four years, he hosted and produced a weekly fearure show on KCSM 91.1FM ("Have You Heard"), exploring the work of emerging and underrated jazz artists, and continues to dj for the station on occasion. He was the Faculty Director at the Stanford Jazz Workshop from 2008-2013, and currently teaches jazz history, composition, and ensemble classes at the San Francisco Conservatory of Music and the College of San Mateo throughout the year, and at the Stanford Jazz Workshop in the summer.

events.title: Dana Bash: The Elections That Changed the World
events.location: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California
