events.title: Lyndsay Faye - Raven
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Gothic and atmospheric, Raven is an aching tale of loss, freedom, death, and resurrection by the celebrated author of Jane Steele and Dust and Shadow . “A clever, darkly funny, and enthralling tale that keeps us turning the pages, even as it explores themes of love and loss, deception, death, and resurrection. Here Faye has performed alchemy, turning the words on the page into gothic gold.” — Lisa Unger An orphaned young woman in antebellum Maryland is pulled into a maelstrom of passion, pain, and occult power in this Gothic homage to the life and works of Edgar Allan Poe. Raven Helen Alan has always been haunted by witchcraft. Since the death of her beloved mother, she has soothed herself by speaking words into spells—a proclivity enhanced by time spent with her aunt’s library of occult books. After an itinerant childhood, Raven is relieved to finally settle down with Aunt Berenice in her Baltimore townhouse. There she finds a long-sought sense of belonging with the family of enslaved workers in her aunt’s household, especially the brilliantly odd youngest daughter Pym. Raven’s infatuation with her friend only grows more intimate as the girls become women together. But when the household is threatened with financial ruin, Raven must set out to earn her own living. Taking a job as a paid companion, Raven arrives at the crumbling Moldavia Manor. Her charge is a delicate young invalid named Lenore Legrand who haunts the Gothic structure like a phantom. Living with them is Lenore’s devoted older cousin Travanion, who spends his days searching ancient texts for an Elixir of Life that might cure Lenore. Raven finds herself inexorably drawn to both cousins as well as the to secrets hidden in the shadows of Moldavia Manor. But those secrets may just be the death of her... “A literary high wire act—combining clever homage with creativity and passion, a celebration of all things Poe, and treasures galore for fans to discover. Raven is the new essential gothic—layered, compelling, witty and entirely entertaining.” —Hank Phillippi Ryan Lyndsay Faye is the internationally bestselling author of eight critically acclaimed novels and two short story collections. She has been published in fifteen languages, nominated for two Edgar Awards, and received an American Library Association award for Best Historical Novel. A notable writer of Sherlock Holmes pastiches including Dust and Shadow and Observations by Gaslight , she also particularly enjoys upending classical literature, as in Jane Steele , which transforms Jane Eyre into a feminist serial killer. A true New Yorker in the sense that she was born elsewhere, Faye lives in Queens with her husband Nicholas and her cat Prufrock. Lyndsay Faye - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. Free Admission / Open Seating There will be a signing line or meet-and-greet following the presentation.

events.title: The Language of Trees
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: How Trees Make Our World · Robert Macfarlane writes “There is no lone tree language, but a forest of tree languages.” In The Language of Trees , Katie Holten invites us to enter some of these forests. She created a Tree Alphabet to translate a compendium of well known, loved, lost and new writing. She takes readers on a journey from creation myths and cave paintings to the death of a 3,500 year-old cypress tree, from Tree Clocks in Mongolia and forest fragments in the Amazon to Emerson’s language of fossil poetry, unearthing a grove of beautiful stories along the way. Listening, speaking, reading and writing are how humans communicate and make sense of the world. The alphabet is how we organize information and knowledge; our networked world depends on it. Trees, the font, lets us renew our relationships with language, landscape, perception, time, memory and reading itself by slowing the reader down to decipher words in the woods. Katie Holten will be in conversation with writer and editor Marthine Satris to discuss our relationship with literature and landscape and the unexpected and imaginative language inspired by the beauty of the natural world. Katie Holten is an award-winning artist and environmental activist. Holten's work investigates the entangled relationships between humans and the natural world. At the root of her practice is a call for Rights of Nature and a commitment to fighting the climate and biodiversity emergency. Her collaborative research based work explores the inextricable relationship between organic systems and human-made systems. She has created Tree Alphabets , a Forest Alphabet , and a Wildflower Alphabet to share the joy she finds in her love of the more-than-human world. Her work has appeared in The New Yorker, The New York Times, Artforum, and The Guardian. She is a visiting lecturer at the New School of the Anthropocene. Katie Holten’s book The Language of Trees was published in 2023 and became an instant bestseller. Holten lives between New York City and Ireland. If she could be a tree, she would be an Oak. Marthine Satris is a writer and editor living in Oakland. She is the Associate Publisher at Heyday, the nonprofit press in Berkeley, where she edits books about California's history, culture, and natural world. Her own poetry and prose have been published in The Georgia Review, The San Francisco Chronicle, Antiphony Journal, Santa Clara Review, Ballast Journal , and elsewhere. She is a frequent contributor to Oakland Review of Books.

events.title: Relatefulness with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other

Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli.

Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment.

This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. 

We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance!

What We’ll Explore

Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice:
Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group.
Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society.
Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly.
Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of.

Why Come?

You may be looking to:
Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected.
Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context.
Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns

This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun!

What Not to Expect

This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur.

It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. 

Here’s what NOT to expect:
A space free of conflict or triggers.
When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others.
No enforced hierarchy of emotions.
Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important.
Expression without attunement.
We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence.

Other logistics and notes

Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time!

We hope to see you at a future event! 

Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you.

More about the facilitators

Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring.

When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws.

In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance.

Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

events.title: Passages of Babel: Translation and the Book Arts of Servane Briand
events.location: San Francisco Center for the Book, 375 Rhode Island St, San Francisco, CA 94103
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Co-presented with San Francisco Center for the Book Center for the Art of Translation and San Francisco Center for the Book join Litquake to present an evening showcasing the sculptural artists' books of Bay Area artist Servane Briand. The event centers on Passages of Babel, her investigation into language and translation, and what is lost or invented in the act of moving meaning from one tongue to another. All three books in the series will be on view: Arise by Any Other Name, A Comme Babel, and Making Sense, each made in collaboration with poets and translators. The evening will feature a reading by Servane Briand and her collaborators, Patrick Fenton and Samuel Mignot. Following the reading, Olivia Sears will lead a conversation with Patrick, Samuel and Servane to reflect on translation understood not as a shift between two languages but as a collaborative, multi-dimensional process bridging text, physical structure, and design. Whether you are an avid reader of translated literature, a contemporary art lover, or a design enthusiast, this evening offers a rare chance to engage with books as living, multidimensional sculptures and to experience translation as a physical, tactile journey. Doors at 6:00pm.

events.title: Clara Lee & Eddo Kim Author Talk • Korean Soups: Korean Soups: Recipes for Soups and Stews That Nourish, Restore, and Delight
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Clara Lee is a chef and co-founder of Korean American food company, Queens. She is originally from New York and has been living and cooking professionally in San Francisco since 2015. Clara delights in making food that is nostalgic, simple, and inspired by family, drawing her culinary creativity from her favorite farmer friends. Eddo Kim is a former educator and grant writer, and currently co-founder of Queens, a Korean American food company. He previously founded and ran an international education nonprofit for a decade before moving to San Francisco and transitioning into the food industry. Clara Lee and Eddo Kim are the co-founders of Queens, a San Francisco-based food company creating traditional Korean pantry ingredients using locally sourced ingredients. Queens originally started as a specialty Korean grocery offering artisanal goods and thoughtfully produced ingredients curated from Korea, alongside freshly prepared Korean foods made with seasonal, locally grown produce. It later expanded to include an all-day cafe and in-house product line of packaged foods. Their products can now be found at markets and grocery stores across the country. Their work has been featured in the New York Times, San Francisco Chronicle, Bon Appetit, Forbes, and more. Korean Soups is a definitive guide to learning about the ingredients, inspirations, and traditional Korean techniques for preparing the soul-warming broths, soups, stews, and hot pots at the heart of Korean cuisine. Featuring more than 50 inspiring and delicious recipes, readers will learn how to make Spicy Braised Chicken Stew for a quick and comforting midweek meal, refreshing Cold Cucumber Soup in summer, Thinly Sliced Beef Bulgogi Hot Pot for entertaining guests, Kimchi and Soybean Sprout Soup to nourish and restore, and more. To accompany are 13 foundational side-dish recipes, including rice, kimchi, and pickles, for perfectly pairing with soup. Authors Clara Lee and Eddo Kim offer an experts’ guide to shopping for a thoughtfully curated, well-stocked Korean pantry and invite you into their home kitchen to help you turn these ingredients into magical guks, tangs, jjigaes, and jeongols through their simple and straightforward methods and recipes.

events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: The best-selling author of "Fed Up" shares her brave and intimate memoir which shows how women's anger can lead us towards change. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Wednesday, October 14 when best-selling author Gemma Hartley comes to the store to share her new memoir No One Loves an Angry Woman: An Exvangelical Coming-of-Rage Story. Gemma will be joined in conversation by Tracy Clark-Flory and will sign copies of her book after the presentation. “A seething read that burns to the bone.” —Tia Levings, New York Times best-selling author of A Well-Trained Wife Gemma Hartley grew up in an Evangelical household where she was raised to become an obedient wife from the time she was a little girl. A sexual assault as a teenager upended her evangelical world, and that coupled with an upbringing steeped in purity culture led her to internalize guilt, silence… and anger. The good girl conditioning of the church demanded that Hartley seek the narrow path of womanhood that emphasized service to others, to swallow the discomfort and rage that simmered just below the surface – but when political events reawakened her trauma, she began to come apart at the seams. Here she unravels the threads of her upbringing to weave a new story, one where women’s anger is not sinful and dangerous – it is information, and often the most rational response there is. Whether or not you’ve ever set foot in a church, Christian patriarchal norms have shaped American culture in ways that are far-reaching and insidious. From restrictive legislation that takes away women’s bodily autonomy to cultural norms that expect women to pick up after their husbands and joyfully give up their careers to care for children—these are all standards informed and fed by Christian culture. Tying together her Christian upbringing together with a feminist examination of society today, Hartley tells her personal story, but it’s bigger than that: No One Loves an Angry Woman is the story of a cultural awakening.

events.title: How Can We Lower Our Risk of Dementia? The Science of Brain Aging
events.location: 473A Haight St, San Francisco, CA 94117, USA
events.description:
🧓 How much say do we actually have in how our brains age?
We're all going to age, but the path our brains take along the way is not entirely out of our hands. In this talk, clinical scientist Dr. Breanna Bullard explores the science of successful aging: what actually happens inside the brain over the decades, why some people stay sharp well into later life while others don't, and how much of that difference is within our control.

Drawing on her research at UC Berkeley and her clinical work with patients and families facing dementia, Dr. Bullard walks through the modifiable risk factors that carry the most weight for long-term brain health, along with common myths worth retiring. She's passionate about translating dense neuroscience into guidance people can actually use to take care of their brains.

Attendees will leave with a practical picture of what successful aging looks like from the neck up, plus a concrete set of evidence-based habits to start putting into practice today. 🧠

events.title: Psychedelic Breathwork with Matt Barkin
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
By increasing the flow of oxygen or Prana in our bodies, we can begin to move and release tension.

In this class we shift our focus from the realm of thoughts to the intricate web of electrical signals within our bodies. Regardless of whether you've faced significant stress or trauma, this approach offers profound benefits to the nervous system. The accumulation of daily stressors can strain our bodies and without releasing this tension through expression, it can manifest as depression, anxiety, or disease over time.

In this class we

- Lay down for a guided short meditation.

- Practice the breathwork sequence together for around 30 minutes.

- Relax and recover.

- Optional sharing and snacks afterwards.


We have 26 trillion cells in our bodies and they all need oxygen. Come breathe with us and calibrate your nervous system!


NOTE: Doors close 10 minutes after the start of class. This event is in-person only.

Matt Barkin has been studying breathwork and meditation for over 15 years. His training is rooted in the ancient practices of Buddhist Vipassana and Kriya Yoga. His goal as a guide is to help students awaken their self-healing potential with the breath! Learn more about Matt here https://mattbarkin.com/breathwork/

events.title: The Meaning of Dinosaurs
events.location: Nirvana Soul Coffee, 315 S 1st St, San Jose, CA 95113, USA
events.description:
🦕 What can 66 million year old bones teach us about how to live right now?
Dinosaurs were the dominant large animals on Earth for well over 100 million years, and they still manage to captivate generation after generation of humans. But beyond their entertainment value, what is the meaning of dinosaurs, and what important knowledge might we extract from their ancient remains?
Scott D. Sampson, PhD, is a dinosaur paleontologist, nonprofit leader, author, and science communicator known to many as Dr. Scott the Paleontologist, host of PBS Kids' Dinosaur Train. He has appeared in numerous television documentaries, served as a science advisor for various media projects, and authored several books, including How to Raise a Wild Child.
In this presentation, Scott takes us on a journey through deep time to ask what dinosaurs can teach us at this pivotal and perilous moment in history. Spoiler alert, we still have much to learn from these amazing creatures.
Expect a talk that is equal parts wonder and reflection, built for anyone who ever loved dinosaurs as a kid, or still does. 🌎🕰 Event Details

events.title: Anhad Naad Collective
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Formed in 2019, Anhad Naad Collective is a genre-defying ensemble rooted in the exploration of South Asian musical traditions and their intersections with global genres. The collective had its debut concert in 2020 in San Francisco, led by core members Divya Purohit Vyas and Jun Ishimuro (of Qb Moda Jazz). Initially, their work centered around blending South Asian raga-based music with the soulful textures of jazz, R&B, and Black musical traditions. With a flexible and evolving lineup of collaborating artists, Anhad Naad Collective has performed at notable Bay Area venues including Bird & Beckett, Integral Yoga Institute, the Golden Gate Park Bandstand, and events such as San Francisco’s Summer of Music hosted by Noise Pop. In 2023, the group expanded its focus to delve deeper into South Asian spiritual music, with a special emphasis on Sufi Qawwali traditions. Anhad Naad treats the spiritual dimension of Sufi poetry and music with deep reverence, often seeking guidance from poets and experts from Pakistan and India. Lead vocalist Divya Purohit Vyas has previously been a part of Bay Dervish in Alameda, a spiritual music collective associated with Sufi Way, led by the late Kiran Rana and Jeanne Rana. Anhad Naad Collective Current Members: • Divya Purohit Vyas – Vocals • Irum Aftab – Vocals • Vivek Anand – Vocals, Harmonium • Rajnish Kamat – Vocals • Jun Ishimuro – Flute, Digital Audio Workstation (DAW)

events.title: West Coast Beat: The SF Roots of Rolling Stone
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: $15 (includes museum admission) Sponsored by Reed Schmidt Co-presented with Counterculture Museum Today’s shiny exteriors and inscrutable billboards can’t entirely obliterate San Francisco’s defining role in literature, activism, visual arts, and, yes, music. That storied history includes the 1967 founding of Rolling Stone. As both Peter Richardson and Charles Ponce de Leon relate in recent books, for a decade (before decamping for NYC), the magazine was at the vanguard of West Coast counterculture, launching dozens of journalists’ careers and setting new standards for writing about music and culture. Where better, then, to reunite folks with first-hand knowledge of those SF roots, including Ben Fong-Torres and Marianne Partridge, than at the new Counterculture Museum? Music journalist James Sullivan will take us back in time, as together we compile a scrapbook of the music, writing, and memories that defined the magazine—and the moment. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Every Saturday Night
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

events.description: "Jinx is a guitar virtuoso who seamlessly moves from rockabilly to jazz to twang and back again, sometimes in the same song. Those with a liner note obsession will remember Jinx’s playing on En Vogue’s “Free Your Mind.” (San Francisco Chronicle) Jinx Jones boasts a prolific career spanning from the 1990s, during which he has been a prominent figure in the San Francisco Bay Area jazz scene. His musical journey, deeply rooted in R&B and Soul collaborations with luminaries such as Solomon Burke and En Vogue, has laid a solid groundwork for his ventures into the realms of soul jazz and hard bop. Jones' distinctive approach to jazz is deeply influenced by the venerable traditions set forth by iconic guitarists such as Wes Montgomery, Kenny Burrell, Barney Kessel, and George Benson. “You've heard fretboard prestidigitator Jinx before: he lent studio guitar and bass to En Vogue's hit, "Free Your Mind." Professionally impressive as it is, though, that credit does not represent his own chosen styling. Jinx's headlong endeavors draw freely and unto satiation from classic rocka-billy, vintage jazz, and spartan honky tonk….” D. C. Larson, Crackerjack Magazine, UK In recent times, Jinx Jones has achieved international acclaim with the release of his latest solo jazz album, "Blue Gardenia." This album showcases his guitar artistry, striking a perfect balance between delicacy and energy, reminiscent of the soulful and profound styles of the genre's legendary masters. “Jinx Jones is out there. Four or five nights a week, the great guitar player with the immaculate pompadour can be found at various Bay Area venues, working the stage, doing his thing. The Colorado native came up serving as a sideman to rock ’n’ roll royalty, playing with the likes of Chuck Berry and Solomon Burke.” Aidin Vaziri, San Francisco Chronicle

events.title: Juice
events.location: The Independent, 628 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117
events.description:
Between their tight grooves, radiant harmonies, heartfelt lyrics, and jaw-dropping solos, there’s no simple, easy way to summarize New York City five-piece Juice.

Pulling from pop and rock, hip-hop and R&B, ‘90s alternative, modern electronic, folk, and more, their complexity is their strength: All six members are multi-instrumentalists from different musical backgrounds and upbringings, each one bringing his own unique flavor to the band. The result is a “multi-dimensional rock” identity that has continuously evolved over the past decade, as the band members themselves – Ben Stevens (vocals, keys), Christian Rose (vocals, violin), Kamau Burton (vocals, guitar), Daniel Moss (guitar), and Rami El-Abidin (bass) – went from students at Boston College to professional touring musicians and seasoned recording artists.

Juice’s sound may be ever-evolving, but their bold energy is evergreen: The goal, both on stage and on record, is not just to connect on a human level, but to breathe life into every room. While they pack a punch on record, Juice shine their brightest onstage, bringing their music to life for all to see, hear, and feel. The band have played countless national tours over the past ten years, including four headline tours and support slots opening for bands like flipturn, Ocean Alley, and The Dip.

events.title: Goldenvoice Presents 50 Years of Punk | Anarchy In The U.K. Sex Pistols (Steve Jones, Paul Cook, Glen Matlock) feat. Frank Carter with Starcrawler
events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
On the afternoon of his first appearance onstage with the Sex Pistols, last summer at Bush Hall, Frank Carter’s peaceful afternoon stroll on the streets of Shepherd’s Bush was interrupted by a stranger sat outside a pub. “Big shoes,” the man shouted; nothing more, nothing less.

“That’s all he said,” Carter reports. “And I just replied ‘thanks for noticing’, and off I walked. But I thought, ‘Fucking hell, we’ve not even played one note yet’. At that point I felt like I was melting. I realised I had to get my shit together here.”

As if the matter was ever in doubt, hours later, he did just that. The stranger’s assertion that anyone stepping up to the microphone with the band who terrorised a nation faces one of the tallest orders in rock and roll – make no mistake, filling big shoes requires big cojones – overlooked the fact that he was speaking to one of the few singers, and perhaps even the <

Such was its success, in fact, that this short series of concerts has blossomed into a busy diary. This year, Carter and the Pistols – drummer Paul Cook, guitarist Steve Jones and bassist Glen Matlock – are set to perform in Australia, New Zealand, Japan, the United States of America, mainland Europe, the United Kingdom, and elsewhere. They’ll headline halls and appear at festivals. In March, the group will top the bill at a Teenage Cancer Trust concert at the Royal Albert Hall, of all places. Much more of this and they’ll be playing at Buckingham Palace.

For anyone who might be wondering, they’re doing these things because, in 2025, the Pistols are sensational once more. And they’re doing it is because they want to.  “What I live by now is, if it ain’t fun, I ain’t doing it,” the always reliably blunt Steve Jones says. “I’m too fucking old to be putting up with a bunch of old shit and acting like everything’s cool just to keep the ball rolling. Those days are gone. If it ain’t fun, honestly, I’m out of here. I ain’t got the energy for any crap any more.”

The credit for bringing Frank Carter into the orbit of the Pistols belongs to Glen Matlock’s youngest son. As a member of the erstwhile group Dead!, Louis Matlock had seen the singer leading the charge while touring the UK as special guests to Frank Carter & The Rattlesnakes. Night after night, he witnessed the fearlessness of a performer who approached live music as if it were a collision sport. Big shoes be damned, if you’re looking for a singer, the son told the father, Frank’s your man.

“Louis said, the guy you need is Frank Carter,” Glen Matlock says. “So I got his number off him and we arranged to have a coffee. I didn’t know much about him but Louis was always going on about him. So we had a play with him and Paul – Steve was out of the country – and Paul liked him, as did I, so we told Steve. I also went to see the Rattlesnakes at the Roundhouse [in Camden Town], where they did two sold out nights, and I was impressed. Then Steve came over [from his home in Los Angeles] and we started rehearsing and that was it.”

Asked to nominate the exact point at which he realised that this new version of the Sex Pistols became a force to be reckoned with, Paul Cook replies that it was during the marching-boots style drum intro to Holidays In The Sun, the first song on the first night at Bush Hall. “As soon as we did Holidays… I thought, ‘Yeah, this is working,” he says. “This is going to be brilliant. This is going to be fantastic.” I was at the back there, looking at Frank with his red hair, and I was kind of getting flashbacks a little bit. I just thought, ‘Wow, this is how it was and how it should be’.”

Naturally, Carter himself needed no introduction to the Sex Pistols. Raised in a home in the satellite town of Watford that groaned from the weight of vinyl LPs, as a 14-year-old, he would listen to his father’s copy of the epochal Never Mind The Bollocks… Here’s The Sex Pistols whenever his parents were out of the house. Smitten by its irresistible mix of fury and wit, blood and thunder, like countless other artists-to-be before him, he was at once captivated. Its guiding light helped lead him to the stage, and, in time, to <

“The one thing I took from the album that I put immediately into the way I perform was just the energy of it,” Carter says. “I’ve heard records that <

So, please, let us not be in any doubt as to his credentials as an MC of chaos. In 2008, 36 years after two members of the Pistols challenged each other to a fight after discovering they were playing different songs onstage at the 100 Club, at the same venue, as the singer with Gallows, Carter chased an audience member who had thrown a pint of lager onstage up the venue’s stairs and out onto Oxford Street <

He even helped orchestrate his own Great Rock and Roll Swindle. In 2009, after Warner Bros. signed Gallows for a million quid, the group handed their new label the pummelling and furious Grey Britain, an album that seemed designed to repel the casual listener. “Britain is fucked,” Carter said at the time. “Grey Britain is all about what’s going on socially, politically and economically in the UK, and how it affects us.”

Sound familiar? As in, there is no future in England’s dreaming? Of course, in 2025, bands and artists are less inclined than they once were to sing about issues that affect and bedevil an entire nation. With social media replacing punk rock as the fastest route into the public bloodstream, rock and roll has entered an introspective phase. Just as well, then, that the Pistols’ State of the Union Address remains as pressing, and as prescient, as ever. Inevitably, in the (almost) half century that has elapsed since a pair of Millwall supporting hot dog vendors in Piccadilly Circus unwittingly provided Steve Jones with the title for his group’s sole bona fide album – “never mind the bollocks,” they would say, meaning “don’t bother with that…” – London and Britain have changed almost beyond recognition. But at street level, the problems and frustrations remain the same.

The Pistols themselves, though, <

It’s different, too, because in 2025 the group’s personnel no longer comprises elements of soap opera, or pantomime. Instead, unity and teamwork are the makings of the new machine; the cohesion of drums, bass, guitar and voice in the service of the songs. In this iteration, the rock and roll itself is allowed to shine, timeless and evergreen. There is no swindle. The people who wrote and played the music back in ’76 and ’77 are able to enjoy it anew.

“Don’t forget, the three of us learned to play together,” Glen Matlock says. “It was all pretty much at a similar level of competency when we started out. And we kind of grew together as musicians.” And now? “Put it this way,” he adds, “someone who is close to the band, I won’t say who, said it’s the first time they’ve seen us coming offstage with smiles on our faces since ’96. Which is good, because life’s too short for all that bollocks, really.”

As for what might come after the Sex Pistols have said hello and goodnight to audiences across the globe, no one is saying because no one seems to know. The promise of new music that was extinguished by a television interview with Bill Grundy and the subsequent shellshock of a young band receiving too much of everything, far too soon for anyone, may never be realised. But who can say for sure? At least for now, there’s no point in asking - you’ll get no reply.  But what we do have, for sure, is Frank Carter and the Sex Pistols whipping up a storm across the globe in a manner that is familiar but fresh, old but new. Catch it while you can, for as long as it lasts. Because we won’t see their kind again.

events.title: Embodiment Practice: Mindful Movement + Stillness with Suzanne (Zan) Beahrs
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest.

Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. 

Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. 

Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. 

Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space.

Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like.

About Suzanne (Zan):
With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley

Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons): 
IG @suzannebeahrs suzannebeahrs.com

events.title: Maggie Tokuda-Hall's "BATHTIME FOR SNOW MONKEYS"
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: The acclaimed author and illustrator share a new picture book written in haiku, offering a window into the world of snow monkeys in Japan. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Thursday, October 15 at 5:00 PM when acclaimed local author Maggie Tokuda-Hall and illustrator Yas Imamura come to the store to share their latest picture book, Bathtime for Snow Monkeys. Maggie and Yas will sign copies of their book after the presentation. At the Jigokudani monkey park in Nagano, nihonzaru—Japanese macaques—have a unique way of de-stressing from life in a cold climate: gathering in their very own onsen, or hot spring “spa,” to lounge and snack. Peek into this magical world in the mountains, hushed by snow, where the macaques reign over their onsen, huddling together. As a playful baby monkey splashes, the others don’t want to join in, and as the baby’s amusing antics wind down, parents and little ones reading the story will happily snuggle together like the macaques, warm and safe. Maggie Tokuda-Hall’s soothing narration, written entirely in haiku form—as befits its Japanese subject and natural themes—pairs with gorgeous illustrations by Yas Imamura. An author’s note offers insight into the habitat displacement and human intervention that led to the monkeys taking over this toasty, tranquil gathering spot. MAGGIE TOKUDA-HALL is the author of numerous award-winning, best-selling children's and young adult books including Love In the Library ; The Mermaid, The Witch, and the The Sea duology; Squad; and The Worst Ronin . She has been called "... one of the most unflinching voices in contemporary genre literature." Her writing has been featured in Harper's Bazaar, Electric Literature, Densho, and more. Maggie is also a founding member and national leader of Authors Against Book Bans. She lives in Oakland, California, with her husband, children, and objectively perfect dog YAS IMAMURA is an illustrator based in Portland, Oregon, working primarily in gouache and watercolor. She is best known for her work in children's publishing, including Love In the Library by Maggie Tokuda-Hall, The Very Oldest Pear Tree by Nancy I. Sanders, a Yoko Ono biography titled Can You Imagine? by Lisa Tolin, and more. Yas occasionally teaches as an adjunct faculty member at Pacific Northwest College of Art.

events.title: Somatic Healing 101: The Missing Link to Lasting Change
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
A somatic workshop to understand your nervous system, reconnect with your body, and learn practical tools for real transformation...
Have you ever known exactly what you "should" do, but still found yourself stuck in the same patterns?
Maybe you've read the books, listened to the podcasts, journaled, reflected, and tried to think your way into change. Yet anxiety, overwhelm, self-sabotage, emotional reactivity, procrastination, or feeling disconnected from yourself keep showing up.
That's because lasting transformation doesn't happen through the mind alone. It happens through the body.
In this immersive workshop, you'll learn the foundations of somatic healing and nervous system regulation, and why working with your body is often the missing piece when it comes to creating meaningful, sustainable change.
We'll explore how stress, emotions, beliefs, and protective patterns are stored in the body, and why healing becomes more effective when we include the nervous system in the process.
You'll learn:
What somatics actually is (and why it's becoming more popular)
Why mindset work alone isn't enough to create real, lasting change
How your nervous system influences your emotions, behaviors, and daily experiences
Simple somatic tools you can use to feel more grounded, present, and connected
How to work with your body instead of constantly trying to push through or override it
This workshop isn't just educational — you'll also experience somatics firsthand through guided practices, including breathwork, body awareness, grounding exercises, mindful movement, and embodiment practices designed to help you reconnect with yourself and your body's wisdom.
You'll leave with:
A clear understanding of what somatic healing is and how it works
Practical tools you can immediately integrate into daily life to finally feel more calm and present
Greater awareness of your nervous system and stress responses
Simple ways to deepen your connection to your body, emotions, and intuition
A new approach to personal growth that feels supportive, sustainable, and effective

Whether you're completely new to somatics or looking to deepen your understanding of holistic healing, this workshop will give you a strong foundation and simple practices you can return to anytime!
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.
Instagram: @annaalexbee
Podcast: RADIANT YOU (available on all podcast platforms)
Website: www.annabolender.com

events.description: The best-selling author of Fed Up deconstructs her Evangelical upbringing and shows how women’s anger can lead us towards change “A seething read that burns to the bone.”—Tia Levings, New York Times best-selling author of A Well-Trained Wife Gemma will be joined in conversation by Amanda Montei, the author of Touched Out: Motherhood, Misogyny, Consent, & Control . Gemma Hartley grew up in an Evangelical household where she was raised to become an obedient wife from the time she was a little girl. A sexual assault as a teenager upended her evangelical world, and that coupled with an upbringing steeped in purity culture led her to internalize guilt, silence . . . and anger. The good girl conditioning of the church demanded that Hartley seek the narrow path of womanhood that emphasized service to others, to swallow the discomfort and rage that simmered just below the surface—but when political events rewakened her trauma, she began to come apart at the seams. Here she unravels the threads of her upbringing to weave a new story, one where women’s anger is not sinful and dangerous—it is information, and often the most rational response there is. Whether or not you’ve ever set foot in a church, Christian patriarchal norms have shaped American culture in ways that are far-reaching and insidious. From restrictive legislation that takes away women’s bodily autonomy to cultural norms that expect women to pick up after their husbands and joyfully give up their careers to care for children—these are all standards informed and fed by Christian culture. Tying her Christian upbringing together with a feminist examination of society today, Hartley tells her personal story, but it’s bigger than that: No One Loves an Angry Woman is the story of a cultural awakening. “This is a book you’ll be pressing into people’s hands for years. Come for the memoir, leave with a whole new relationship to your own fury.” —Amanda Montell, New York Times best-selling author of The Age of Magical Overthinking “Not only is this book packed with mic-drop wisdom; its gorgeous prose will demand to be read, reread, and read again.” —Reema Zaman, author of I Am Yours “Hartley’s account of unlearning fear, questioning faith, walking away from white patriarchy, and finding freedom on the other side is searing and compelling.” —Soraya Chemaly, author of Rage Becomes Her “A brave, bold, timely, and intimate exploration of how Christian patriarchy harms girls and women . . . The honesty and rigor of this book is a gift.” —Amanda Montei, author of Touched Out “Hartley’s tour de force will enliven, embolden, and wake you up.” —Kate Manne, author of Down Girl Gemma Hartley is the author of Fed Up: Emotional Labor, Women, and the Way Forward . Her work has been featured in outlets including Harper’s Bazaar , Women’s Health , Glamour , the Washington Post , CNBC, Redbook , Cosmopolitan , Good Housekeeping , Teen Vogue , Huffington Post , and more. She is an experienced interviewee, speaker, and podcast guest, and has made appearances on shows including Good Morning America and Cheryl Strayed’s Dear Sugars . She lives in Reno, Nevada. Amanda Montei is the author of TOUCHED OUT: Motherhood, Misogyny, Consent, & Control , available now from Beacon Press, as well as the memoir Two Memoirs (Jaded Ibis Press) and a collection of prose, The Failure Age (Bloof Books) . Her essays, criticism, and interviews have been featured at The New York Times Magazine, The New York Times Opinion, The Guardian, ELLE, TIME, The Cut, Mother Tongue, Slate, Electric Literature, Vox, Rumpus, Salon, The Believer, Ms. Magazine, Poetry Foundation, and in numerous literary journals. She was a 2020 Best American Essays notable. events.title: David Benac - Rainforest Radicals
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Rainforest Radicals presents the first history of one of the most innovative and successful environmental organizations of the late twentieth century. Rainforest Action Network emerged in 1985, when it took over a fledgling effort to protect rainforests from transnational corporations funding the expansion of tropical cattle ranching. It excelled at using nonviolent, civil disobedience in dramatic campaigns that captured the attention of the public, media, and RAN’s corporate adversaries. As a result, two decades later rainforest conservation went from a niche academic topic to a fixture in American popular culture, the rights of Indigenous people had gone from ignored or romanticized to at least considered in discussions of the management of their ancestral homelands, and RAN had scored a series of victories over some of the planet’s largest corporations. In Rainforest Radicals David Benac traces the evolution of RAN and radical, transnational grassroots environmentalism through the four campaigns identified at the group’s founding: rainforest beef, Hawai‘ian rainforests, tropical timber, and multinational development banks. Forty years after RAN’s inception, there is much to learn from how it organized people in small towns and large cities across the United States, created alliances that spanned oceans, and inspired a new movement that integrated human rights, Indigenous sovereignty, and environmental protection to challenge multinational corporations, national governments, and neocolonial corporate-led globalism. Through more than thirty oral histories, including those of key players from different eras of RAN’s history as well as leaders from other environmental and Indigenous rights organizations, Rainforest Radical s provides unparalleled insight into the network. “This history of Rainforest Action Network is necessary for our times. From civil disobedience in Hawai‘i to raucous protests in the aisles of Home Depot and annual auto shows in the 1990s, the pages of Rainforest Radicals offer uplifting stories of solidarity and blueprints for successful (and not-so-successful) actions. I could easily see this being a sort of guidebook for grassroots activists today.”—Allyson P. Brantley, author of Brewing a Boycott: How a Grassroots Coalition Fought Coors and Remade American Consumer Activism David Benac is an associate professor of history and public history coordinator at Western Michigan University. He is the author of Conflict in the Ozarks: Hill Folk, Industrialists, and Government in the Courtois Hills . events.description: An Evening with Jonn Del Toro Richardson Experience world-class blues, dinner, and drinks — all in one intimate setting. SHOW · 6:30 PM · DOORS 5:15 PM Admission: $15 - $25 When Diunna Greenleaf's Blue Mercy won the 2005 International Blues Challenge in Memphis, the guitar player was Jonn Del Toro Richardson, and he left town with the Albert King Award for the competition's most promising guitarist. A year earlier he had played guitar behind Pinetop Perkins at the Majestic Theatre in Dallas, on a bill with Robert Lockwood Jr., Honeyboy Edwards and Henry Townsend, for a live album that took the 2008 Grammy for Best Traditional Blues Album. His own debut, Tengo Blues, which he produced with Anson Funderburgh for VizzTone in 2015, won the 2017 Blues Music Award for Best Emerging Artist Album. He spent years making other people sound like legends. He learned exactly how they did it.   about Jonn Del Toro Richardson Richardson built the Houston end of his reputation as a sideman before he was a bandleader, and the credits show it: Diunna Greenleaf's Blue Mercy, then a Grammy winning night behind Pinetop Perkins with three more Delta elders on the same stage. events.title: Anna Voloshyna Author Talk • Ukraïne: Recipes and Stories from Kyiv to the Black Sea
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: This event is part of Litquake, San Francisco's Literary Festival, taking place October 8–24 throughout the Bay Area. For the full Litquake schedule, visit litquake.org Anna Voloshyna is a Ukrainian-born chef and the author of BUDMO! and UKRAÏNE . Raised in Ukraine and now based in the East Bay, she began her career as a food photographer and stylist before moving into hosting Eastern European pop-up dinners and writing cookbooks. Her work focuses on sharing Ukrainian and Eastern European cuisines through narrative-driven recipes, immersive culinary experiences, and storytelling—using food to preserve culture and foster connection. Paolo Bicchieri is a writer living on the coast. Their work has appeared in the San Francisco Chronicle, the Seattle Times, the Irish Times, Eater, and more. They run the food, writing, and food writing series Kitchen Table. Ukraïne: Recipes and Stories from Kyiv to the Black Sea - Experience the joy and resilience of Ukrainian cuisine in this visually rich, travelogue-style cookbook filled with 100 traditional and modern recipes that highlight the comforting dishes, distinctive flavors, and time-honored techniques that make this food so extraordinary. Ukrainian chef Anna Voloshyna traveled across the diverse regions of her homeland―from the mountains to coastline, cities to grasslands, forests to wine country―collecting recipes, stories, and friendships to answer the question: What is Ukrainian cuisine? In these pages, she takes you along on this appetizing and fascinating journey. Vivid and poignant storytelling transports you to the boisterous streets of Kyiv where food carts sell aromatic sausages; to cool root cellars, a fixture in Ukrainian households, their walls stocked with jars of preserved and fermented deliciousness; and to the front line of the war where Voloshyna cooked a meal for fifty soldiers fighting for their country. Stunning photos bring you to the fields of sunflowers that blanket the steppe every summer; the shimmering waters of the Black Sea, brimming with marine life; and the imposing Carpathian peaks where flocks of sheep wander, their milk used to make beloved bryndza cheese. A treasure trove of recipes, drawn from all these places, bring a taste of Ukraine to your table, including: Beet and Plum Lemonade Cold Soup with Fresh and Fermented Tomatoes Grilled Sardines with Dilly Potatoes Mom’s Chicken and Potato Roast Lamb Plov with Apples and Chickpeas No-Churn Sunflower Seed Butter Ice Cream Plus, Sour Cucumbers, Beet Kvas, Mushroom Salt, Smoked Honey, and more pantry staples that will enhance your everyday cooking At a critical juncture in the nation's history, this cookbook seeks to preserve Ukraine's rich culinary heritage. By documenting recipes along with countless stories and images in a lustrous package, Ukraïne captures the very essence of the place while offering an acknowledgment of the country’s enduring spirit and a way to keep its culinary identity alive, preserving its past and ensuring its future.

events.title: Deconstructing Yourself with Michael Taft
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. 

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

events.title: Litquake's A 22nd-Century Conservation Ethos for California
events.location: KALW
events.description: California’s landscapes have long been shaped by deep relationships between people and place. But that relationship has changed dramatically over time, especially with the rise of European American settlement and the erasure of Traditional Ecological Knowledge. Panelists Obi Kaufmann , creator of the California Field Atlas series; Laura Cunningham , award-winning author of A State of Change ; and earth scientist and professional mountain biker Dillon Osleger examine how modern society has grown increasingly estranged from the natural world. Together, they imagine a new conservation ethos—one rooted in restoration, resilience, and reciprocity—and ask what it would take for Californians to leave the state healthier, more biodiverse, and more ecologically whole at the end of the 21st century than at its beginning. Moderated by Leslie Carol Roberts . Doors at 6:30pm.

Pony is everyone's favorite party guest--until his friends start making him the main attraction. First, Mouse wants him to give pony rides. Next, Raccoon makes him the star of the petting zoo. Then, Pig turns him into the target of the "Pin-the-Tail" game. After being poked in the face, Pony has had enough. No. More. Parties. Will Pony ever join in the fun again? events.title: Our Loving Companions (San Francisco)
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Our Loving Companions is a groundbreaking immersive theater experience celebrating the beautiful bond at the heart of pet ownership. A bond strong enough to propel us through deeply painful loss, time and again. Over 90 minutes, audiences journey through the laughter, devotion, inexplicable joy, and grief that define our relationships with our animal companions. Most shows will have a facilitated discussion afterwards for those who desire to partake. A portion of each $100 Companion Circle Ticket is donated to Bay Area animal charities to support animals in need. “The Bridge” by Jay Cross “What We Know” by Stephanie Weisman “A Dog Dreams” by Jeffrey Fisher Smith ”A Little Bird Told Me” by Marilyn Anderson “Must Love Pitbulls” by Jenny Mead “Tomorrow” by Alan Stewart “Outside the Box” by Emily Turner “A Good Dog” by Laura Neill “Ellie’s Goodbye” by Leslie Corn “Like a Dog”by Anya Martin “For The Love Of Buddy” by Dyanna Morrison “Roll Over, a monologue from the cat’s point of view” by Tommy Our Loving Companions is the result of a shared artistic vision between Grief Dialogues founder Elizabeth Coplan and co-producer and playwright Alan Stewart . Recognizing the need for an animal-centered immersive experience, Coplan envisioned a space that honors the distinct and deeply personal nature of the creatures who share our homes, our routines, and our unconditional love. Stewart, a producer, playwright, Dramatist Guild Foundation Fellow, and former trustee of San Francisco’s Magic Theatre, brings a distinctive artistic voice shaped by his first career as a veterinary internist and a lifelong belief in the human-animal bond as a language of the heart. Together, they create theater that invites audiences not only to witness grief, but to experience it in a way that clarifies, deepens, and transforms. As founder and Artistic Director of The Marsh, Stephanie Weisman brings a deep appreciation for work that blends storytelling with emotional truth, making her collaboration with Our Loving Companions a natural and meaningful fit. She is delighted to welcome Grief Dialogues to both The Marsh San Francisco and Berkeley—spaces long dedicated to bold, intimate, and transformative performance. Through hundreds of productions each year, alongside classes, youth programs, and live music, The Marsh has become a home for stories that matter. Stephanie’s own work in grief-centered theater, including her play 180 Days, To Die. To Live. , reflects that same commitment to exploring life’s most tender moments with honesty and care. And at home, her own loving companions—Marsh mascots Marsha and Junior—are never far from heart, a daily reminder of the deep bonds this experience so beautifully honors. Under the consulting direction of Dani Davis , Our Loving Companions living, immersive theatrical experience invites audiences to move through a curated landscape of short plays, poetry, music, sculpture, shared reflection, and personal stories. Blending warmth, tenderness, reverence, and moments of gentle humor, the production explores death, loss, and remembrance through what follows the final goodbye…the empty leash, the quiet food bowl, the space at the foot of the bed. Each performance is carefully choreographed behind the scenes to create an atmosphere fostering connection, validation, and collective witnessing for those grieving animal companions. In a culture where pet loss is sometimes dismissed as “lesser,” this experience affirms that love is not measured by species, and grief is not ranked by hierarchy. Michael Bud serves as Creative Producer and Director of Design for Our Loving Companions , shaping the audience experience from arrival through reflection. Working across promotion, staging, production design, and visual storytelling, he translates the project’s artistic and emotional vision into a cohesive immersive environment. His role supports both the creative flow of each performance and the deeper intention to witness, honor, and hold space for those mourning the loss of cherished animal companions. Pamela Hollings (she/they) is a theater-maker, working as a director, dramaturg, educator, actor, deviser and writer, depending on the project. Her career has focused on developing new work; working with playwrights as both director and dramaturg and as a devisor of new work, often site-specific. She is an ensemble member of Aviva Arts (formerly foolsFURY) where most recently they served as a co-writer, dramaturg and performer for Burning Wild a climate catastrophe devised piece performed outdoors in both Sonoma County and San Francisco. She was the Curation & Education Director at 3Girls Theatre, and the Board Chair (2013-2021), as well as an ensemble member (2018-2022) of foolsFURY Theater and the former Artistic Managing Director of both The Yat/Bentley Centre for Performance, SF Bay Area and Soup Kitchen Theatre, Melbourne, Australia. They trained in Theatre Direction at Australia’s National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA) whose distinguished alums include Cate Blanchett, Sara Snook, Baz Luhrmann and many more. Pamela is also a breath practitioner / voice teacher working at the intersection of theatre, education, ritual and somatic wellness. Anna Takayo Walden is a San Francisco-based theatre artist, AEA actor, and the Founding Artistic Director of San Francisco Classical Theatre, a site-specific classical theatre company that launched in June 2026 with a sold-out inaugural reading of Chekhov’s The Seagull directed by Carey Perloff. She is a Directing Fellow at Oakland Theatre Project, a member of the Actors Reading Collective, and Associate Artistic Director of Hawaii Public Theatre. As a director, Anna is drawn to work that lives in the body and in space — theatre that asks audiences not just to watch, but to feel, move, and reckon. Her practice is rooted in classical text, physical theatre, and ensemble, with a particular interest in immersive and site-specific forms that dissolve the boundary between story and world. As a performer, Anna’s credits span classical theatre companies across the United States and internationally, She holds an MA in Acting from the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London and an MFA in Classical Acting from The Shakespeare Theatre Company at George Washington University, Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Every Saturday Night
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

events.title: Lost Kings
events.location: The Independent, 628 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117
events.description: Consisting of the Los Angeles-based duo Rob Gainley and Nick Shanholtz, Lost Kings have emerged as a powerhouse within the electronic music scene, amassing over one billion streams globally and capturing the attention of nearly a million monthly listeners on Spotify. Known for their unique sound and dynamic production, Lost Kings have collaborated with major artists like Wiz Khalifa, A$AP Ferg, Ty Dolla $ign, Mod Sun, Loren Gray, Marc E. Bassy, GASHI, and many more, showcasing their ability to elevate each collaboration with their distinctive style. From their debut single “Bad” in 2015 to recent releases like “Here For You”, “Remind Me”, and “Dreams,” Lost Kings have proven their versatility and staying power in the industry. Their catalog includes popular EPs such as Paper Crowns and Lost Angeles (2019) and It’s Not You, It’s Me (2021), with each project reinforcing their reputation as hitmakers. Beyond streaming success, the duo has captivated audiences with standout performances at iconic festivals like Coachella and Lollapalooza, and have sold out shows in major markets across North America. In 2025, Lost Kings are entering a bold new chapter by embracing speed house. The duo aims to bring an American twist to the genre, fusing its underground energy with their commercial successes. With this shift, they’re poised to redefine their sound and further expand their reach into new electronic music territory.

events.title: Wisdom Healing Qigong with Hiromi Vardy
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Experience the deep benefits of Zhineng (Wisdom Healing) Qigong. This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Through simple, time-honored movements, the nervous system unwinds, the mind becomes more spacious, and the heart opens. Over time, practitioners often feel more resilient, centered, and connected — both inwardly and outwardly.

Tickets are sliding scale $10-$25 - Please arrive at least 5-10 minutes early.

 Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back 

Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts.

While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga.

After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today.

Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

events.title: Founder Group Coaching and Peer Support
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + North Studio
events.description:
Building something can be lonely. Decisions keep coming, the relationships around the work get complicated, and there is not always a place to say what is actually happening.
This is a weekly group coaching and peer support circle for founders, builders, creators, side hustlers, and small business owners.
Bring one real situation: a decision you are stuck on, a co-founder or team tension, a difficult conversation, or simply the feeling that you are carrying too much of it alone.
You can be coached, reflect for someone else, or listen. The group is small and facilitated. There is no pitching and no pressure to arrive with a polished story.
One person brings a real situation.
The group listens before offering perspective.
We slow the problem down enough to see the person, relationship, and system around it.
The person chooses a next move that feels honest and workable.
Who it is for
Founders, creators, builders, side hustlers, and small business owners actively carrying responsibility for something they are building.
People who want useful support and honest peers, not another networking event.
What you leave with
More clarity about one real situation.
A decision, conversation, or experiment to take forward.
The experience of not carrying the work alone.
What to bring
One real situation from your work or leadership. Confidentiality matters. Stories stay in the room; learning can leave with you.
Facilitated by Nima Imani
Founder of InsightsOut and ICF-certified leadership coach.
All workshops: https://insightsout.work/eventsCoaching
Book a 30-minute call with Nima: https://insightsout.work/coaching

events.location: ARTogether Center, 1200 Harrison Street, Oakland
events.description: What story gets left behind when the world decides whose memory counts? Untold Stories is our attempt to connect the dots, to trigger the memories that complete what’s been erased. As truth seekers from many different walks of life, we’ve made this exhibition a space to hold the true stories so often erased by a system that does not honor immigrants, refugees, Black Americans, queer folks, and those who carry the truth close. This exhibition allows us to rest in the rememory that Toni Morrison left us in the pages of the untold stories she once uncovered. “Untold Stories” is our dedication to that work, as ARTogether’s 2026 Artist-in-Residence Mentorship Cohort: Aylin Ayee, Bronche Taylor, Donny Phan, Jacquie Verbal, Ji Young Lee, Kia Lat, Sabri Tunca, and Tea Sherman. Our work spans mixed media, painting, textile art, installation, and performance, holding space for the stories that have not yet been told. We invite you to join us in dialogue about Untold Stories. **Everything related to this exhibition is fueled by human creativity; no artificial intelligence is condoned.

events.title: Heaven Looks Like Us: Palestinian Poetry
events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Poetry has always served as a mode of resistance in Palestinian culture. In defiance of dispossession and decades of military siege, of a nakba that never ended, of historical and cultural obfuscation, of unrelenting violence and thousands of martyred people, the “power to narrate,” as Edward Said wrote, remains a necessary tool for self-determination. As Palestinian history remains haunted by exile, violence, and grief, there’s more here that’s also true: queer and feminist perspectives, eco-poetry, meditations on love and time, and lineages of protest. These poems reclaim that power to narrate, bridging borders, languages, and generations to forge new conversations around resistance and liberation. Featuring Haymarket Books' Heaven Looks Like Us anthology contributors Zeina Hashem Beck, Janine Mogannam, Deema Shehabi, Jen Siraganian, Priscilla Wathington, and Omar Zahzah. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Sugar Coated
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: Marion Nestle in conversation with Cari Borja · We are what we eat. Or so the saying goes. But what determines what we eat in the first place? Who decides? And how much of what we think of as personal choice is shaped long before we ever reach for something on the supermarket shelf? For more than half a century, Marion Nestle has been asking these questions ~ about food, nutrition, public health, politics, corporations, and the systems that determine what ends up on our plates. Now, at 90, she remains one of the clearest and most influential voices in American food studies. Her newest book, Sugar Coated , takes on one of the most ubiquitous and contested ingredients in our food system. Moving beyond whether sugar is simply “good” or “bad,” Nestle examines the powerful industry built around it and the ways corporate interests, marketing, science, public policy, and our deeply human attraction to sweetness shape what we eat. It is a subject that reaches far beyond dessert. From her iconic Food Politics , which exposed the food industry’s influence on nutrition and public health, to the newly updated What to Eat Now , Nestle has spent a lifetime asking: Who benefits from the way our food system is organized? How are our desires shaped? And how free are our choices? But this evening at Clio’s will go beyond any one book. Cultural anthropologist and Clio’s founding member Cari Borja will sit down with Nestle to talk about her life’s work: what has changed, what stubbornly has not, the questions that continue to sustain her—and what she sees differently at 90. Their conversation will also turn to how we learn to eat. If we are what we eat, when do we begin becoming what we eat? From children first discovering food, to teenagers and college students making choices independently, who, or what, is doing the teaching? Drawing from Nestle’s decades as a professor at NYU and Borja’s work as a senior advisor to Alice Waters with the Edible Schoolyard Project, School Supported Agriculture, and the larger movement of edible education, including UC Berkeley’s Edible Education 101 ~ they will consider what happens when we teach young people not simply what to eat, but how to understand the cultural, ecological, economic, and political systems behind what is on their plate. Because perhaps “we are what we eat” has never simply been about nutrition. What we eat carries culture, memory, pleasure, identity, agriculture, economics, and power. Beginning with Sugar Coated and moving across an extraordinary lifetime of thinking, teaching, writing, and questioning, Nestle and Borja will ask: How do we choose what to eat in a world constantly trying to choose for us? And after a lifetime devoted to understanding food, what does Marion Nestle believe matters now? Marion Nestle is Paulette Goddard Professor of Nutrition, Food Studies, and Public Health, Emerita, at New York University, which she chaired from 1988-2003 and from which she officially retired in September 2017. She is also Visiting Professor of Nutritional Sciences at Cornell. She earned a Ph.D. in molecular biology and an M.P.H. in public health nutrition from the University of California, Berkeley, and has been awarded honorary degrees from Transylvania University in Kentucky (2012) and from the City University of New York’s Macaulay Honors College (2016). In 2023, she was awarded The Edinburgh Medal for contributions to science and society.

events.description: Harmony Korine’s debut feature is an audacious, lyrical evocation of America’s rural underbelly, and an elegy in the southern-gothic tradition of William Faulkner and William Eggleston. Shot in Korine’s native Nashville—standing in for the tornado-ravaged Xenia, Ohio—the rough-hewn film follows two young friends, Tummler and Solomon, as they ride around town, huffing glue and hunting stray cats, their every local encounter charged with vaudevillian anarchy as well as deep pathos. At once transgressive and empathetic, disturbing and undeniably beautiful, Gummo is a one-of-a-kind portrait of angelic and devilish souls caught in a cultural void, circumscribed by poverty and the depleted, alienated spiritual life of late-twentieth-century America. events.description: “What Happens to a dream deferred? Does it dry up, like a raisin in the sun …or fester like a sore and then run?
