events.title: Obi Kaufmann with Victoria Schlesinger - California Inside Out
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: In a provocative new work blending manifesto, philosophy, and ecological inquiry, the bestselling California Field Atlas series creator challenges readers to reimagine humanity's relationship with the living world. Obi Kaufmann will be joined in conversation by Victoria Schlesinger, the editor-in-chief of Bay Nature. This fall, award-winning creator of the California Field Atlas series, Obi Kaufmann, publishes his most probing and philosophical book to date: California Inside Out: Mapping an Ecology of Mind(on-sale: October 6, 2026). With this compact, pocket-sized volume, the San Francisco Chronicle and Los Angeles Times bestselling author recenters radical kinship with the more-than-human world, advancing an environmental worldview rooted in the recognition of nature’s agency and humanity’s inseparable relationship to place. Part manifesto, part lyrical meditation, California Inside Out interrogates the stories that estrange people from the living systems that surround them and searches for new language capable of restoring that connection. Kaufmann challenges the assumptions that promote extractive thinking and sets out to tell another story; one aimed at helping Californians leave the state at the close of the 21st century healthier, more resilient, and more ecologically whole than it was at the century’s start. Deriving inspiration from Traditional Ecological Knowledge, the lessons of deep time, and the blueprints of renowned naturalists including Aldo Leopold, Gary Snyder, and Robin Wall Kimmerer, Kaufmann sketches the contours of an emergent conservation ethic for the 22nd century. Rejecting the inherited “man versus nature” model, he proposes creative frameworks for realizing equity and mutuality between humans and the wider living world. Kaufmann’s approach is deeply Socratic, inviting readers to consider provocative questions: What if wildfire were revered rather than reviled? What if humans respected the creative capacity of other species? What if watersheds have volition and rivers were accorded legal rights? At the heart of California Inside Out is a quest to find the new premises—or long-forgotten verities—that may reveal enough intrinsic value in nonhuman entities to inspire people to retrieve their responsibility as stewards of the systems upon which all life depends. For the notion that wilderness exists separate from human development is ahistorical, Kaufmann reminds us. “The structural makeup of habitat spaces is largely the product of a consistent, multimillennia-long project of human stewardship,” he observes, invoking Indigenous traditions and technologies that have shaped the American West for thousands of years. Everything from faunal biogeography to soil fecundity has been shaped by human hands, human history, and increasingly, human policy: “California’s landscape is an ecological artifact of human activity.” With California Inside Out, Kaufmann challenges readers to consider what kind of landscape will emerge from continuing along with a now centuries-long protocol of human activity that is driven primarily by extraction and capital utility—and appeals to the reader to ensure that another story, a better story, prevails. "Obi Kaufmann’s books are like bibles to me. They explain California’s natural beauty better than anything I’ve read before.” —DAVE EGGERS “A full immersion into the astonishingly varied natural worlds. Gorgeous.” —CBS SAN FRANCISCO "Obi leaves no leaf unturned in his quest to capture the wonder and fragility.” —SUNSET "Kaufmann’s gaze easily ranges from the micro to the macro. As a reader you are invited to join him on a journey of discovery—not as a passenger but as an active partner.” —SAN FRANCISCO CHRONICLE “An original contribution to the genre … Immersive.” —LOS ANGELES REVIEW OF BOOKS Obi Kaufmann is an artist, conservationist, and the bestselling and award-winning author of The California Field Atlas series. Kaufmann is a former board member of the California Wilderness Coalition and winner of the 2019 Mark Dubois River Protection Award. Notable recent illustration projects include a 2022 residency with the National Wildlife Federation as the illustrator for the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing and a 2025 writing and painting residency for the National Gallery of Art in Yosemite. In 2026 he will participate in an authors' residency in Stockholm with the Swedish Institute. His most recent book is California Inside Out: Mapping an Ecology of Mind (2026). When he is not backpacking, the painter-poet can be found at home in the East Bay, posting trail paintings @coyotethunder on Instagram. Victoria Schlesinger is editor-in-chief of Bay Nature . Schlesinger has worked as a raft guide in Colorado, a backpacking counselor in the Trinity Alps, and spent the better part of her 20s researching and writing a book about ecology in Central America. Her journalism career began at California Wild magazine and the Point Reyes Light newspaper, and she has since earned two master’s degrees from Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism. Her articles have appeared in Harper’s Magazine , Mother Jones , Audubon and The New York Times , among many other outlets, and she’s been on staff with Discover , PBS Frontline, Plenty , and California Lawyer . She lives in Berkeley with her husband and daughter. events.title: Versus
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: A relentless one-of-a-kind sensory assault chock-full of hyper-kinetic fight scenes, gangster shootouts, sword-slashing violence and gory zombie horror, Versus was a key title amongst the barrage of innovative horror and action movies that appeared as if from nowhere from Japan at the turn of the millennium, leading to a new wave of appreciation for Asian extreme cinema. A mysterious face-off in a wooded clearing between two escaped convicts and a carload of sharply dressed yakuza holding a beautiful woman captive ends in hails of bullets and showers of blood. The location for this violent encounter is the mythic Forest of Resurrection, the site of the 444th portal of the 666 hidden gates that link this earthly domain to the netherworld - and it didn't get this name for nothing. As one of the surviving prisoners escapes with the girl into the darkness of the forest, disgruntled gangsters soon become the least of their worries as an earlier battle between a lone warrior against hordes of zombie samurai is carried over from a millennium ago into the present day... Toshiro Mifune stars as Isaburo Sasahara, an aging swordsman living a quiet life until his clan lord orders that his son marry the lord's mistress, who has recently displeased the ruler. Reluctantly, father and son take in the woman, and, to the family’s surprise, the young couple fall in love. But the lord soon reverses his decision and demands the mistress’s return. Against all expectations, Isaburo and his son refuse, risking the destruction of their entire family. Director Masaki Kobayashi's Samurai Rebellion is the gripping story of a peaceful man who finally decides to take a stand against injustice. events.title: Exploding Stars, Dark Energy, and the Runaway Universe
events.location: The New Parkway Theater, 474 24th St, Oakland, CA 94612, USA
events.description:
💥 What could possibly outshine an entire galaxy?
Some of the most energetic and fascinating objects in the universe are exploding stars known as supernovae. These huge outbursts come from the violent deaths of stars and can briefly become brighter than the entire galaxy that contains them. The atoms needed to build life are forged inside stars and then scattered across space during these explosions.
In this talk, Dr. Jeffrey Silverman, who earned his PhD in Astrophysics at UC Berkeley studying supernovae with Professor Alex Filippenko, explains why these events matter so much to science. Observations of distant supernovae provided the first evidence that the expansion of the universe is actually speeding up rather than slowing down, a completely unexpected discovery tied to one of the biggest unsolved mysteries in modern physics: dark energy.
Silverman, now a data scientist and longtime science communicator, brings both his astrophysics background and a talent for public outreach to this exploration of dying stars and the mysteries they leave behind. ✨

events.title: DAMIEN ESCOBAR
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the most influential and impactful violinists in modern history · Hailed as one of the most influential and impactful violinists in modern history, two-time Emmy award-winning artist Damien Escobar has spent nearly two decades cementing his legacy as the “King of Strings”. He’s inspired listeners, broken barriers, and created a blueprint for other contemporary violinists who aspire to top the charts and make their way onto main stages around the world. And his work is just getting started. The Jamaica, Queens native, who is known for his charisma, sincere humility, and undeniable talent, has always believed the key to his success is rooted in his humble beginnings. It is the main source that keeps him connected to his fans and cultivates his unending love for performing. And if you’ve heard his story, you know that Escobar’s journey after Juilliard (from which he graduated at the age of 12) wasn’t easy! But his passion and vision took him from playing for straphangers on NYC subways to serenading everyone from Oprah to the Obamas while achieving several lifetime goals in between— including an NAACP award nomination, topping the 100 Billboard charts, and selling 1M+ records. In 2023, Escobar sold out venues across the nation with his “Victory Lap” tour — an inspiring experience intended to empower audiences to celebrate their lives and all they’ve overcome. Escobar has a lot to celebrate on his musical journey, with his song “Taboo” earning the #1 song in the country and topping the Billboard charts, as well as the release of his highly anticipated album, Gemini. Escobar is letting it be known that his reign as the King of Strings will not cease. He’s on a mission to prove there’s astonishing power in instrumental music, and he intends to motivate listeners and make an impact on mainstream music like never before. With the release of his studio album, “Gemini”, Escobar is showing no signs of slowing down.

events.title: DellaMorte DellaMore: Cemetery Man (Presented by MEDIA MELTDOWN MOVIE MADHOUSE)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: DELLAMORTE DELLAMORE: CEMETERY MAN (1994) “I’d give my life to be dead…” From director Michele Soavi ( The Church , Stage Fright ) comes a macabre masterpiece, 1994’s CEMETERY MAN , also known aptly as DELLAMORTE DELLAMORE (Of Death, Of Love). This Italian-French-German co-production stars British actor Rupert Everett ( My Best Friend’s Wedding) as Franceso Dellamorte, a graveyard keeper tasked with putting the dead that rise each night. Despite his gristly job, Dellamorte is a romantic at heart. But is he free to find love, or is fate bound to something far darker? And what does the Angel of Death have to do with all of it? Inspired by Tziano Sclavi’s novel Dellamorte Dellamore and his comic character Dylan Dog (who was visually based on Everett), this film is equal parts scary, comedic, and sexy, with surprising surreal and philosophical developments as the plot develops. A must see film, straight from the cold expanse of Hell to ring in Halloween! MEDIA MELTDOWN MOVIE MADHOUSE Gender jesters Piranha Psychotronica and Kafka X bring you a new experience in cinematic depravity… Media Meltdown Movie Madhouse! Prepare yourself to enter into a world of face-flaying forgotten and forsaken films… Made-for-TV, Direct-to-Video, VCR games, underground cinema, and more wiley weirdness than your minds can handle! In a world dominated by AI, CGI, mega streaming platforms, and cinematic universes, Media Meltdown celebrates the amateur, the low-budget, the handmade, the experimental, and the weird! Commit yourself every 3rd Sunday to … MEDIA MELTDOWN MOVIE MADHOUSE! events.title: Dominican University Faculty Lecture Series - From Snake Oil to Social Media
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: From Snake Oil to Social Media: Deciphering Medical Truths in the Wellness Age Our desire for health, longevity, and bodily control makes us susceptible to the promise of quick cures. Today’s wellness landscape prioritizes algorithmic advice, viral detoxes, and AI diagnoses. Relying on unverified remedies is far from new. To understand how we navigate medical "truth,” we can look across history, psychology, and modern healthcare systems to see how information spreads, why it takes root, and who stands to profit. Join Dominican University faculty members Vivian Delchamps Wolf, Sophie Whynacht, and Michael Skolnik for a panel exploring the boundaries of medicine, wellness, and trust. Drawing connections from 19th-century medicines to modern influencer culture and politicized care, the panelists will examine why mythical cures persist, how digital culture shapes our relationship with our bodies, and how patients can build critical information literacy in an age of digital noise. The 90-minute session will feature short presentations from each panelist followed by an open audience Q&A. This conversation brings together interdisciplinary faculty from Dominican University: Vivian Delchamps Wolf (PhD, UCLA English, 2022) is an Assistant Professor of English at Dominican University of California (DUC). Her research and teaching focus upon 19th-century American literature and feminist disability studies. Peer-reviewed articles have been published or are forthcoming in the J19: The Journal of 19th-Century Americanists, Disability Studies Quarterly, the Emily Dickinson Journal, and Literature and Medicine. Her monograph, Resisting Diagnosis: Women’s Disability Literature of the 19th-Century U.S., argues that women writers use literature to challenge patriarchal medicine and racialized pathologization and to imagine expansive forms of care. Wolf serves or has recently served professional organizations including the Modern Language Association, C19: The Society of Nineteenth-Century Americanists, and the Health Humanities Consortium through conference organizing, committee work, and disability advocacy. Sophie Whynacht, Ph.D. is an Assistant Professor of Psychology at Dominican University of California, where she leads the Body Image and Stigma (BIAS) Research Lab. She is also a Licensed Psychologist and the founder of Embodied Psychotherapy and Counseling, a private practice specializing in the clinical treatment of eating disorders, body image concerns, and related mental health challenges. Her academic work centers on the psychological and sociocultural factors that drive body image issues, weight stigma, and disordered eating. Dr. Whynacht’s writing on body image is featured on Psychology Today. Michael Skolnik , Academic Director of the Healthcare Executive MBA program, who brings deep expertise in healthcare leadership, institutional strategy, and the systemic challenges patients face when navigating medicine, technology, and misinformation. Vivian Delchamps Wolf, Sophie Whynacht, Ph.D., Michael Skolnik - photos courtesy of the organizers

events.title: SHAAN MERCHANT: SURVIVOR LEGENDS
events.location: Books Inc. Palo Alto, 855 El Camino Real, Palo Alto, CA 94301
events.description: The tribe has spoken: Journalist, cultural critic, and lifelong Survivor fan Shaan Merchant will be at Books Inc. Palo Alto for a reading and signing of his new book, Survivor Legends: The Players Who Changed the Game (Unofficial & Unauthorized)! Shaan will be joined by Survivor winner Yul Kwon! About the book: A deep dive into the players who shaped Survivor—and how their stories helped define reality TV. [Book not endorsed by or affiliated with any creator or producer of the show] For more than 25 years, Survivor has reigned supreme as one of the most influential shows on American television. Each season, castaways from across the country arrive on a secluded island with the same ultimate goal: to outwit, outplay, and outlast for the $1 million prize. The game is physically grueling and psychologically unforgiving. While the structure of the game remains familiar, what has made Survivor endure—and evolve—is the players at the center of the it. Survivor Legends tells the stories of the players who left an indelible mark on the series, through narrative profiles that revisit the show’s most influential figures. From early rule-breakers and strategic innovators like Richard Hatch and Cirie Fields, to unlikely heroes and enduring icons, like Parvati Shallow and Mike White, these players didn’t just change how the game was played—they shaped how audiences understood competition, character, and authenticity. Through their stories—who was celebrated, who was vilified, and how those judgments shifted—this book offers fresh insight into beloved contestants while revealing how American ideas about identity, morality, and power have changed across a quarter century of reality television. Featuring exclusive interviews from players including Sandra Diaz-Twine, Tyson Apostol, John Cochran, Carolyn Wiger, and more, Survivor Legends is a vivid, player-centered portrait of one of television’s most enduring cultural phenomena. Based in New York City, Shaan Merchant is a journalist, cultural critic, and lifelong Survivor fan. His work has been featured in the New York Times, Slate, Salon, Washington Monthly, Condé Nast Traveler, Insider, Philadelphia Inquirer , and more. In 2006, Yul Kwon became the first Asian American winner of the CBS reality show, Survivor . He returned in 2020 to compete in the 40th season, Survivor: Winners at War . Currently, Yul is Vice-President and General Manager of the Paradigms of Intelligence ( Pi ) research team at Google. Other roles he’s held at Google include VP/GM for Local Search, product lead for the Google-Apple Exposure Notifications project, and chief-of-staff to Alphabet's President of Global Affairs. Earlier in his career, Yul worked as a product management director at Meta, a regulator at the Federal Communications Commission, a management consultant at McKinsey & Company, an attorney at two law firms, and the owner/operator of a frozen yogurt chain (Red Mango). In the public sector, he’s served as an adjunct instructor at the FBI Academy, a legislative counsel in the U.S Senate, and a judicial clerk on the U.S. 2nd Circuit Court of Appeals. Yul received his B.S. in Symbolic Systems from Stanford University, and his J.D. from Yale Law School.

events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.title: Exploding Stars, Dark Energy, and the Runaway Universe
events.location: The New Parkway Theater, 474 24th St, Oakland, CA 94612, USA
events.description:
💥 What could possibly outshine an entire galaxy?
Some of the most energetic and fascinating objects in the universe are exploding stars known as supernovae. These huge outbursts come from the violent deaths of stars and can briefly become brighter than the entire galaxy that contains them. The atoms needed to build life are forged inside stars and then scattered across space during these explosions.
In this talk, Dr. Jeffrey Silverman, who earned his PhD in Astrophysics at UC Berkeley studying supernovae with Professor Alex Filippenko, explains why these events matter so much to science. Observations of distant supernovae provided the first evidence that the expansion of the universe is actually speeding up rather than slowing down, a completely unexpected discovery tied to one of the biggest unsolved mysteries in modern physics: dark energy.
Silverman, now a data scientist and longtime science communicator, brings both his astrophysics background and a talent for public outreach to this exploration of dying stars and the mysteries they leave behind. ✨

events.description: FREE Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Co-presented with City Lights and New York Review of Books First published in 1922, and rich in startling neologisms and other forms of verbal play, Trilce is a blazingly vivid revelation of what poetry can be, at once a love poem, a poem of erotic urgency and frustration, a poem of family life, of political fury, a lament for the dead, a work of intense privacy and an address to the world. Their incisive commentary on these legendarily challenging poems opens them up to new understanding while inviting readers to find their own pathways to and through them.

events.title: The Psychology of Climate Change: Why We Struggle to Act
events.location: Nirvana Soul Coffee, 315 S 1st St, San Jose, CA 95113, USA
events.description:
🌍 Why does something as urgent as climate change leave so many of us paralyzed instead of motivated?
Climate change is not just a problem of engineering and policy. At its core, it is a product of human thought, behavior, and motivation, which means psychology has something important to say about it. Join Gregory Feist, Professor of Psychology at San José State University, for a look at why so many people either deny the crisis outright or freeze up when confronted with its scale.
Drawing on decades of research into creativity, motivation, and the psychology of science, Feist will unpack the mental habits and biases that make climate change uniquely hard for our brains to process. He will also explore what basic psychological principles suggest about breaking through denial and inaction, and how that understanding might translate into real solutions.
This talk offers a grounded, evidence-based way to think about one of humanity's biggest challenges, from the inside out. 🌱

events.title: Going to the Moon?
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: What Earthlings should expect. · The Moon inspires myth, song, poems, and journeys. Mysterious and elegant, it lights the night, generates tides, and affects Earth’s climate. Since human beginnings, the Moon has been our common heritage owned by no one, shared by all peoples; a revered object, not a destination. And yet, in the present, global forces race and compete to claim lunar resources. What plans are underway? Do the peoples of our planet have a say? Can poetry, or any art, make a difference? What will it be like to look up at an inhabited Moon? When she found out that a poem would be sent to the Moon in a time capsule, former Santa Clara County Poet Laureate Sally Ashton realized her resistance to the forces of lunar exploitation is in very real conflict with her excitement at being part of a lunar landing. Her book, Going to the Moon , explores this paradox and the fraught relationship of humans with conquest and the non-human world. Join her conversation with Dr. Persis Karim, faculty emerita at San Francisco State University, as they ponder the Moon, consider the progress of the lunar goldrush, and explore our role in the revived race to space at this transformational moment in human history—the colonization of the Moon. Sally Ashton is a poet, writer, teacher, and editor-in-chief of DMQ Review , an online journal featuring poetry and art. Publishing in three genres, she is the author of five books of poems including Listening to Mars (Cornerstone Press, 2024). San José State University faculty emerita, she continues to teach workshops locally and online. Her poem “4.6 Billion Years” is archived on the Moon with the Lunar Codex. Her new book of nonfiction, Going to the Moon , (Duke University Press, 2026) explores her personal experience and the global race to space. www.sallyashton.com Persis Karim , Ph.D., is poet, essayist, editor, and retired San Francisco State University professor of Comparative and World Literature. She is the editor of three anthologies of Iranian diaspora writing and her poetry has appeared in a number of national and local publications. Co-director of the documentary, “The Dawn Is Too Far: Stories of Iranian-American Life,” she is also an avid birdwatcher, moonchaser, and gardener.

events.description: Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Monday, October 19 at 7:00 PM when Marina Richie comes to the store to present her new book Feathered Forest: Aloft with Birds in Ancient Trees . Marina will sign copies of her book after the presentation. A narrative of perception change, memoir, and kinship, Feathered Forest is a soaring ode to birds and wild trees. “Luminous. You can feel the deep, cool shadow of the great Western forest and the flicker of bird color flashing across it. The kind of book that inspires contemplation but also action.” —Bill McKibben, author of Here Comes the Sun Beginning with an ascent of a 200-foot-tall Douglas-fir with a bird biologist, author Marina Richie leads us from her home in Central Oregon into the ancient forests of Cascadia, a bioregion which rivals the Amazonian rainforest in significance for climate and biodiversity. Birds are guides to intricate and imperiled communities thriving at every level, from understory to midstory to overstory. They steer us to cool havens within multilayered, centuries-old groves that are critical refugia in a time of climate crisis. Their songs and flights show us what we must protect for the future of threatened birds, forests, and humankind.

events.title: Bonnie Garmus with Kate Schatz - Peck & Peck
events.location: Calvary Presbyterian 2515 Fillmore St San Francisco, CA 94115
events.description: We are honored to welcome Bonnie Garmus to Calvary Presbyterian for an evening celebrating the release of Peck & Peck. The author of the global sensation Lessons in Chemistry returns with an irresistible, delightful, and tender literary novel set in the publishing world of 1980s New York City about a young man whose life turns upside down when he is hired by the most prestigious, secretive, and dysfunctional poetry journal in the world: the renowned Peck & Peck . Bonnie will be joined in conversation by Kate Schatz, a feminist author, educator, and public speaker. Presented in partnership with Calvary Presbyterian San Francisco A MOST ANTICIPATED BOOK FOR COUNTRY LIVING AND BOOKPAGE Find originality. Reward creativity. Burn the rest. It’s 1982, New York City. Crime is on the rise, muggings are in the streets, and Batter Gray, recent college graduate with a skill that no one wants—an “ear” for poetry—is worried about his future. While all of his friends have real jobs, he’s folding T-shirts at the Gap. As for love? No. Not unless you count Sallie Mae, the student loan tyrant. He hears from Sallie all the time. But when Batter gets a dream job at Peck & Peck , the most prestigious poetry quarterly in the world, his life moves into the literary fast lane. Soon Batter is knee-deep in the secret war between the two Editors in Chief, the famous Peck brothers—twins and enemies—as well as being privy to the private affairs of their thirty-nine editors, whose professed mission is the same: Find originality. Reward creativity. Burn the rest. And by burn, they mean incinerate. Because at Peck & Peck , “good” isn’t good enough, “interesting” doesn’t cut it, plagiarists aren’t tolerated, and parolees run the mailroom. Still want to submit your poem? Go with God. Welcome to another dazzling and unforgettable novel from Bonnie Garmus. If you loved Lessons in Chemistry , you will love Peck & Peck. “Tender-hearted… [Garmus] packs the novel with the antic humor and colorful characterizations that drew readers to her debut. There’s much to cherish in this charming tale.” — Publishers Weekly “[People are] hungry for another Bonnie Garmus hit. Thankfully Peck & Peck is here to feed those gaping mouths... With the trappings of the literary world, and the heart of a bildungsroman, Peck & Peck vows to fill the void in all our hearts with a needed dash of wit and poignancy." — Literary Hub, Most Anticipated Books of 2026, Part Two “Garmus applies her unique comic sensibility to the story of Batter Gray… charming… with some really lovely things to say about poetry.” — Kirkus "I'm absolutely over the moon about Bonnie Garmus' new novel. It is EXACTLY what I needed to read right now. Charming, uplifting, soulful, and original, this is the perfect successor to Lessons in Chemistry . If you loved Elizabeth Zott, you will adore Batter Gray. Book clubs will adore this novel. I loved it." —Kristin Hannah, #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Nightingale and The Women Bonnie Garmus is a coffee-dependent American novelist. Her debut novel, Lessons in Chemistry , was a Good Morning America Book Club Pick, a Goodreads Choice Best Book of the Year, spent nearly two years on the New York Times bestseller list and was named by Times readers as one of the top 100 books of the 21st century. Translated into over forty languages, Lessons in Chemistry was honored with sixteen international literary awards and made into an Apple TV limited series. Peck & Peck is her second novel. KATE SCHATZ is a feminist author, educator, and public speaker. She's the New York Times- bestselling author of the "Rad Women" book series; the novel Where the Girls Were; the 33 ⅓ book Rid of Me: A Story ; and Do the Work: An Anti-Racist Activity Book , co-written with W. Kamau Bell. She lives in the Bay Area with her wife, three children, and pets. In all she does, Kate is committed to sharing radical histories that shine light on the marginalized people who've truly made America (and the world) great: the people of color, the immigrants, the queers, the punks, the weirdos, the artists, the workers, and the women. Additional books will be available for purchase at the event

events.description: Grammy Award winner and three-time Tony Award nominee Shoshana Bean can currently be seen starring in The Lost Boys musical on Broadway. Shoshana made her Broadway debut in the original cast of Hairspray, appeared Off-Broadway in the 2000 revival of Godspell, and appeared in Songs for a New World at City Center Encores. Regionally, she appeared in Sarah Silverman’s The Bedwetter , won an IRNE Award for her performance as Fanny Brice in Funny Girl , and earned a Jeff Award nomination for her portrayal of CeeCee Bloom in the pre-Broadway musical production of Beaches . She has appeared in Bloodline, Bill and Ted Face the Music , Great Performances: 50 Years of Broadway’s Best, and recently filmed a solo concert special for PBS.

events.title: Return to Center: Exploring Stability, Mobility & Ease with Vickie Russell Bell
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves..



Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition.

Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.

events.title: Half-Day Silent Unguided Retreat
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice.
This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods.
There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of
meditation, all are welcome.

The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive
between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before
the first bell.

The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation:
9:30 AM – 10:10 AM
10:20 AM – 11:00 AM
11:10 AM – 11:50 AM

A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period.
The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between
sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom.
Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep
voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire
morning.

You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during
a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and
the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice
elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell.

The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website.

Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by
12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely
manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

events.title: Erin French with Tanya Holland - The Lost Kitchen Volume 3
events.location: Calvary Presbyterian 2515 Fillmore St San Francisco, CA 94115
events.description: We are honored to welcome Erin French to Calvary Presbyterian for an afternoon celebrating the release of The Lost Kitchen Volume 3: Seize the Supper. The stunning third volume in The Lost Kitchen cookbook series from Erin French, award-winning restaurant founder and New York Times -bestselling author of Finding Freedom, The Lost Kitchen, and Big Heart Little Stove Erin will be joined in conversation by Tanya Holland, the author of Tanya Holland's California Soul: Recipes from a Culinary Journey West [A Cookbook]. Presented in partnership with Calvary Presbyterian San Francisco Erin French brings you perfectly crafted meals for dining outside the box and living in the moment in her latest cookbook, Seize the Supper . From her beloved home and restaurant, the Lost Kitchen in Freedom, Maine, come hearty main dishes balanced with crisp, bright salads and sweet and spiced desserts. Her well-rounded meals are made with true comfort and seasonal nourishment that are perfect for carrying you from shorter days and late-afternoon feasts to snowy winter nights sitting by the fire to picnics that welcome the blooming of spring. In simple yet rewarding steps, French shares delicious recipes that will foster connection and inspiration around the table. From flavorful salads and sides such as Soft Polenta with Honey & Ricotta, Roasted Asparagus with Tarragon Vinaigrette, and Pear, Walnut & Blue Cheese Waldorf to rich mains including Provençal Roasted Chicken, Fried Halibut, and Buttermilk Leg of Lamb with Fennel & Orange to irresistible desserts like Baked Vanilla Spice Puddings with Cherry Compote and Rosemary Maple Ice Cream, French’s recipes are filled with warmth, heart, and meaningful tips for embracing the joy of now. Erin French , a born-and-raised Mainer, is the owner and chef of the Lost Kitchen, a fifty-seat restaurant in Freedom, Maine, listed among Time ’s World’s Greatest Places to visit and Bloomberg ’s " 12 Restaurants Worth Traveling Across the World to Experience.” With two New York Times bestsellers to her name, Finding Freedom and Big Heart Little Stove , Erin is featured in three seasons of the Magnolia Network series The Lost Kitchen and Getting Lost with Erin French, where she travels the country searching for new experiences and culinary inspiration, streaming on HBO Max. Erin knows the importance of simple pleasures found in gathering for thoughtfully prepared meals. Her love of Maine and sharing its delicious heritage with dinner guests has garnered several James Beard nominations and the attention of The New York Times , Martha Stewart Living, The Wall Street Journal, The Boston Globe, and Food & Wine, as well as NPR’s All Things Considered, CBS News Sunday Morning, and Today. After more than a decade in business, the Lost Kitchen has become so much more than a restaurant, now boasting a farmer’s market, overnight cabins, a retail shop, and a café called the Little Lost Kitchen. Tanya Holland is an award-winning chef, restaurateur, cookbook author, educator, media personality, wine professional, and U.S. State Department Culinary Diplomat. A French-trained chef with more than four decades of experience, she is best known as the founder and executive chef of Oakland’s Brown Sugar Kitchen, where she earned national recognition for modern African American cuisine and thoughtful, inclusive hospitality. Holland is the author of Brown Sugar Kitchen and Tanya Holland’s California Soul and has appeared on Food Network’s Melting Pot, Bravo’s Top Chef, and other programs. Her work has been featured in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Bon Appétit, Gourmet, House Beautiful, and O, The Oprah Magazine. She serves on the James Beard Foundation Board of Trustees and, in 2026, joined the University of Virginia as a Senior Lecturer. Across food, wine, teaching, media, and diplomacy, Holland creates memorable experiences that bring people together around the table. events.title: Somatic Breathwork Journey: Emotional Release, Clarity & Nervous System Reset
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Come breathe, release, & reset...
Somatic Breathwork is an embodiment experience designed to take you out of your thinking mind and into the deep intelligence of your body — where true healing, clarity, and release happen. It allows your body to express and discharge stored emotions, stress, and old narratives that may be weighing you down.
Somatic Breathwork uses circular connected breathing together with rhythmic music to produce a cathartic emotional release. This release may be in the form of moving, shaking, yelling, crying, laughing, or simply deep stillness.
It gives your body the opportunity to express emotions or actions that may otherwise be unacceptable in modern social settings, allowing your nervous system to process traumas and restore balance.
Using the breath, you’ll engage your body’s innate ability to heal — sweeping out any defenses, blockages, restrictions, or pains that hold you back from showing up as your truest self.
Many participants experience profound emotional release, newfound clarity, and a grounded sense of calm even after a single session.
This experience is designed to:
Move you out of your mind and into your body's electrical network
Release stuck energy, emotions, or trauma responses
Reset your nervous system into grounded calm and clarity
Break old patterns and reconnect you to your authentic self
Increase compassion, presence, and emotional resilience
Support cathartic release in a safe, guided container
Participants often report:
Deep emotional release
More calm, peace, and clarity
Release of anger, grief, frustration, or stagnant energy
Increased presence, awareness, and intuition
Breakthrough insights about their life, patterns, and purpose
Feeling more open, soft, and connected to themselves and others
What to expect:
✨ Opening Check-In & Introduction
✨ 60-Minute Guided Somatic Breathwork Journey
✨ Integration & Optional Group Sharing
Whether you're seeking release, clarity, a reset, or simply a moment to reconnect with yourself — this session is for you.
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.
Instagram: @annaalexbee
Podcast: RADIANT YOU (available on all podcast platforms)
Website: www.annabolender.com

events.title: Alexander Maksik with Anthony Marra - Passengers
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A taut, emotionally gripping, and surprisingly funny novel about a father and daughter stranded in an airport at the end of the world, Passengers is a story of loving across gaps—between parent and child, between things said and unsaid—and what happens when the outside world finally mirrors the chaos within. ​This is Maksik’s most timely and accomplished novel yet! Ivan is a solitary man in his seventies, set in his ways and haunted by the failures of his past. His smart and cynical daughter, Nina, is in the twilight of her twenties and has long kept a distance from her sentimental father. But when Ivan proposes a trip to Europe in hopes that it will bring them closer together, Nina reluctantly agrees. They meet at LAX, where their departure is delayed. And delayed again. And again. As the hours drag on, their sharp, caustic and wide-ranging conversation reveals a lifetime of misunderstandings, unhealed wounds, and stubborn love. Soon more flights are canceled, security tightens, airport staff grow evasive, and it becomes clear to Ivan and Nina that something is wrong. They begin to suspect that they’re being held prisoner—sequestered from the world without explanation. At last, the surreal starts to overtake the mundane, and their need to escape—and to protect each other—turns increasingly urgent. What begins as a piercing portrait of a father and daughter becomes a novel of eerie suspense, as Nina and Ivan navigate not only their fractured bond but also a world teetering on the brink of collapse. A story of loving across gaps—between parent and child, between things said and unsaid—and about what happens when the outside world finally mirrors the chaos within, Passengers is Maksik’s most timely and accomplished novel yet. “A beautiful, unsettling novel about the depths of love, the burden of nostalgia and the maddening impossibility of translating feeling into language.”—Imbolo Mbue, author of Behold the Dreamers “A novel of surpassing beauty and among the most moving portraits of parenthood I’ve ever read. It also happens to be exceptionally funny, propulsive and wise—an example of the alchemy that occurs when a writer finds the work he was born to pursue. Passengers is Alexander Maksik’s masterpiece.”—Anthony Marra, author of Mercury Pictures Presents "Maksik's best to date. Passengers is really about how we're all trying to get somewhere different, somewhere better--to a place where we can be closer to those we love, during this one precious life we have. I could not put it down."—Adam Ross “This is the stuff we live for—a spinning dream of a book, pure heart-in-your-throat magic. I can’t say this enough: read it, today, now.”—Paul Yoon, author of The Hive and the Honey , winner of The Story Prize “ Passengers is a tour de force that reveals just how deeply two ordinary people can love one another…This superb novel takes on the very hardest stuff of life and never looks away.”—Ben Fountain, author of Billy Lynn’s Long Halftime Walk “Maksik’s latest, Passengers, is propulsive and fierce and uncompromising in its humanity. And funny too, in often unexpected ways. Also, my kind of book in that it doesn’t waste a single word. It's kept me intensely good company these past few weeks. Seems to me: A necessary book for these batshit times.”—Peter Orner Alexander Maksik is the author of You Deserve Nothing , a New York Times and IndieBound bestseller; A Marker to Measure Drift , which was a New York Times Notable Book, as well as a finalist for the William Saroyan Prize and Le Prix du Meilleur Livre Étranger, and the basis of the 2023 motion picture Drift ; Shelter in Place , named one of the best books of the year by the Guardian and the San Francisco Chronicle; and The Long Corner , a New York Times Book Review Editor’s Choice, and named one of the best books of the year by The Australian . Maksik is the recipient of a Guggenheim Fellowship, a Pushcart Prize and The Sewanee Review’s Andrew Lytle Prize. His books have been translated into a dozen languages. Anthony Marra is the author of the New York Times bestselling novels A Constellation of Vital Phenomena and Mercury Pictures Presents , as well as the story collection The Tsar of Love and Techno. Alexander Maksik - photo courtesy of the author; Anthony Marra - photo credit Paul Duda Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

Halloween (1978) On a cold Halloween night in 1963, six-year-old Michael Myers brutally murdered his 17-year-old sister, Judith. He was sentenced and locked away for 15 years. But on October 30, 1978, while being transferred for a court date, a 21-year-old Michael Myers steals a car and escapes Smith’s Grove. He returns to his quiet hometown of Haddonfield, Illinois, where he looks for his next victims. Halloween III: Season of the Witch (1982) When a terrified toy salesman is mysteriously attacked and brought to the hospital, babbling and clutching the year's most popular Halloween costume, an eerie pumpkin mask, doctor Daniel Challis is thrust into a terrifying Halloween nightmare. Working with the salesman's daughter, Ellie, Daniel traces the mask to the Silver Shamrock Novelties company and its founder, Conal Cochran. Ellie and Daniel uncover Cochran's shocking Halloween plan and must stop him before trick-or-treaters across the country never come home in this terrifying thriller. When a runaway grim reaper tries to save a life, she clashes with a skeptical Guardian, forcing them to form an unlikely partnership beyond the grave. Darcy Moore is tired of death. Which would be fine and good ... if she wasn’t a Grim Reaper. Determined to outrun her designation as the villain, Darcy decides she won’t be dragging her next assignment to the underworld. She’ll be saving him instead. Unfortunately for Darcy, there’s a complication in her plan. Guardian Angel Gabriel Aetos doesn’t tolerate threats to his little corner of the world, and a Grim Reaper showing up at his bar is as deadly as it gets. But when he realizes Darcy is not as she seems, Gabriel must decide if he can trust his growing feelings or hold on to his long-standing grudge. But magic doesn’t come without consequences. events.title: WHO IS SINGING? Embody and Celebrate the Cosmic Nature of Sound: Improvise Icaros, Ragas, and Medicine Melodies with Silvia Nakkach
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In these immersive sessions, Silvia invites you to experience sound as a living, cosmic force — where everything sings: plants, waters, stars, and even silence itself. Across traditions, shamans and sound practitioners have attuned to this hidden music, expressing it through “medicine melodies” that arise as spontaneous transmissions from nature and the spirit world.

•	Enter the voice as a portal of spirit and shakti awakening, where Sound becomes a vehicle for healing, joy, and cosmic connection.
•	Explore the idea that all of existence is alive with sound — plants, waters, stars, and even silence —inviting us into a field of deep listening.
•	Learn to engage “medicine melodies” as spontaneous transmissions from nature and the spirit world, expressed through voice and simple instruments.
•	Experience initiatory sound practices drawn from Icaros (Peruvian Amazon), Afro-Brazilian invocations, Indian ragas, mantric improvisation, and healing invocations.
•	Cultivate contemplative listening, tonal centering, and free your voice as forms of musical divination and attunement.
•	Develop greater clarity, neural coherence, emotional resonance, and spiritual receptivity through vibrational formulas.
•	Be guided by Silvia Nakkach’s decades of sound shamanism into the ecstatic, contemplative, and transformative power of your sonic presence. 

You’ll learn to offer medicine melodies as tools for group facilitation and mystical communion. No singing experience needed — only your willingness to listen, feel, and let the voice reveal its sacred intelligence.


Teacher Bio: 
Silvia Nakkach M.A., MMT, also known as Saraswati Devi, is a Grammy-nominated composer, interdisciplinary vocal artist, Hindustani raga musician, and multihyphenate educator and scholar. Nakkach has released 18 albums, authored the book "Free Your Voice", and offered significant scholarly contributions to the academic study of music and sound therapies. She is a former clinical psychologist who serves on the faculty of the California Institute of Integral Studies’ East-West Psychology Department. Silvia is also a Music Mentor at the CIIS’s Center for Psychedelic Therapies and Research. You can listen to her explorations of sound, spirituality, and the human experience on her podcast "Beyond Music." She is the founding director of the International Vox Mundi School of Sound, with centers in Japan, South Korea, Brazil, India, and across the US and the Bay Area. Visit:voxmundiproject.com.

Simple orders for Inspector O, until he realizes they have led him far, far off his department's turf and into a maelstrom of betrayal and death. events.title: Erin French Book Signing • The Lost Kitchen Volume 3: Seize the Supper
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Erin French , a born-and-raised Mainer, is the owner and chef of the Lost Kitchen, a fifty-seat restaurant in Freedom, Maine, listed among Time’s World’s Greatest Places to visit and Bloomberg’s "12 Restaurants Worth Traveling Across the World to Experience.” With two New York Times bestsellers to her name, Finding Freedom and Big Heart Little Stove, Erin is featured in three seasons of the Magnolia Network series The Lost Kitchen and Getting Lost with Erin French, where she travels the country searching for new experiences and culinary inspiration, streaming on HBO Max. Erin knows the importance of simple pleasures found in gathering for thoughtfully prepared meals. Her love of Maine and sharing its delicious heritage with dinner guests has garnered several James Beard nominations and the attention of The New York Times, Martha Stewart Living, The Wall Street Journal, The Boston Globe, and Food & Wine, as well as NPR’s All Things Considered, CBS News Sunday Morning, and Today. After more than a decade in business, the Lost Kitchen has become so much more than a restaurant, now boasting a farmer’s market, overnight cabins, a retail shop, and a café called the Little Lost Kitchen. The Lost Kitchen Volume 3: Seize the Supper- The stunning third volume in The Lost Kitchen cookbook series from Erin French, award-winning restaurant founder and New York Times bestselling author of Finding Freedom, The Lost Kitchen, and Big Heart Little Stove. Erin French brings you perfectly crafted meals for dining outside the box and living in the moment in her latest cookbook, Seize the Supper . From her beloved home and restaurant, the Lost Kitchen in Freedom, Maine, come hearty main dishes balanced with crisp, bright salads and sweet and spiced desserts. Her well-rounded meals are made with true comfort and seasonal nourishment that are perfect for carrying you from shorter days and late-afternoon feasts to snowy winter nights sitting by the fire to picnics that welcome the blooming of spring. In simple yet rewarding steps, French shares delicious recipes that will foster connection and inspiration around the table. From flavorful salads and sides such as Soft Polenta with Honey & Ricotta, Roasted Asparagus with Tarragon Vinaigrette, and Pear, Walnut & Blue Cheese Waldorf to rich mains including Provençal Roasted Chicken, Fried Halibut, and Buttermilk Leg of Lamb with Fennel & Orange to irresistible desserts like Baked Vanilla Spice Puddings with Cherry Compote and Rosemary Maple Ice Cream, French’s recipes are filled with warmth, heart, and meaningful tips for embracing the joy of now.

events.title: KISS & TELL LITERARY SALON
events.location: Books Inc. Alameda, 1344 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501
events.description: Meet featured authors Lexi Sharabianlou and C.C. Dador, this month's featured authors of the Kiss & Tell Literary Salon, celebrating their new books, The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium, and Merry Ex-Mas! Hosted by Rebecca Hunter and Addie Woolridge and members of Bay Area Romance Writers Association. Please join us. About the The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium: A magical witness protection program, a town in need of saving, and a sorceress-in-training . . . oh, and the human woman she's not supposed to fall for. The Blue Moon Café has a little bit of everything (except, you know, decent coffee). In the tiny town of Pine Hollow, barista and fledging sorceress Talula Smith runs The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium, aka the worst coffee shop in town. The café's horrible reputation hides its true purpose: providing new identities and safe passage to at-risk magical beings while keeping humans far, far away. That is, except for town local Dahlia. Dahlia's devastating dimples, addiction to Talula's cocoa recipe, and keen observation skills keeps the smitten barista scrambling to ensure that her magical abilities (or, lack thereof) stay a secret. But when big game hunters start preying on magical beings, her powerful sorceress mother is called away to track them down, leaving Talula and her barely-there magic in charge of The Blue Moon. With the impending Samhain festival to organize, magical refugees to help, half of the town turning against her, and her ever-growing feelings for Dahlia, Talula's magical destiny feels further away than ever. But as the hunters set their sights closer to home, it'll be up to Talula to master her craft, trust her heart, and bring her magical and human communities together . . . before she loses everything she loves. "You're in for a treat! The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium is deliciously delightful and absolutely adorable! I loved it!" -Sarah Beth Durst, New York Times bestselling author of The Spellshop Lexie Sharabianlou earned her Master’s in creative writing from the University of Edinburgh. She has sold cupcakes, taught high school English Lit, and written audio tours for zoos. By day, she’s a copywriter for a makeup company (yes, she gets to name the makeup). By night, she writes stories about magic, food, and falling in love. She lives in the San Francisco Bay Area. Tell your dog she says hi. She is the author of The Blue Moon Café & 24-Hour Occult Emporium and The Blue Moon Diner & Drive-In Movie Theater. About Merry Ex-Mas : Fall in love. Again. And again. This irresistible holiday time loop rom-com is perfect for fans of In a Holidaze and The Holiday Swap . Which man from her past will make the perfect Christmas present? All Marygrace Silva wants for Christmas is a date to impress her big, boisterous family. Instead, a disastrous setup and an awkward run-in with her ex-best friend Robbie leave her wishing for a holiday miracle. Then a slip on the ice lands her in a time loop—reliving Christmas Eve with a different ex each time. There’s Flynn the finance bro, Dale the rising music star, Jamie the fitness influencer. Glamorous? Sure. Perfect? Not so much. Between caroling and cookie baking, Marygrace is checking exes off her list—but somehow, Robbie keeps showing up too. Maybe the love she’s been searching for has been there all along ... With a sprinkling of sugar and just the right amount of spice, this romance about family, friendship, finding your voice, and the promise of “what-if” is a holiday treat you won’t want to miss. “An enjoyable time-loop holiday rom-com about choosing one’s own path and finding one’s voice.” — Library Journal C.C. Dador writes heartwarming romances filled with big laughs, cozy vibes, and sexy moments you’ll want to snuggle up with again and again. Like her work in event planning, C.C. is all about swoon-worthy details and making sure her readers are having their best day. C.C. is a first generation Filipino American and currently lives in the D.C. metro area. When she isn't writing, C.C. can be found enjoying seasonal drinks and hunting for the perfect gifts for friends and family.

events.title: The Boxes We Put Nature In: Rethinking How We Study the World
events.location: Guildhouse, 420 First St, San Jose, CA 95113, USA
events.description:
🌊 What if the boundaries we impose on nature prevent us from seeing how it actually works?
Scientists often divide the natural world into neat categories: ocean and seafloor, land and water, surface and subsurface. But nature rarely follows those boundaries, and the categories we create can shape what we notice, what we miss, and what we choose to protect.
Geological oceanographer Ivano Aiello explores this idea through three surprising case studies. At the bottom of the Mediterranean, an extraordinary ecosystem blurs the line between ocean and seafloor. In Monterey Canyon, repeated maps reveal a landscape that is constantly being reshaped. And after the Moss Landing battery fire, the way scientists defined something as simple as the “surface” determined whether contamination was detected or missed.
Together, these stories reveal how the boundaries we create can change what we see, what we understand, and how we respond to our messy, interconnected natural world. 🌍

events.title: Witches of the Wheel — Lindsay Merbaum
events.location: Fabulosa Books, 489 Castro St, San Francisco, CA 94114
events.description: In her metaphysical mystery Witches of the Wheel , Lindsay Merbaum weaves a spellbinding tale of mythology, bartending, and queer belonging. Gold grows up knowing only a few things about herself: something lets her see ghosts and read her neighbors' secrets, and her mother seems to hate her. But when she strikes out on her own, she stumbles into a job at The Wheel, a literally-underground lesbian bar where a coven gathers every Thursday and each entrance requires a painful sacrifice. It feels like the first place she's belonged. But the bar, its patrons, and its history are more complicated, and more dangerous, than Gold ever realized. As she entangles herself in her new community, she learns more about herself than she wanted to know--and attracts an ancient goddess's deadly attention.

events.title: The (Deeply Misunderstood) Evolutionary Science of Attraction
events.location: The Foundry SF, 1425 Folsom St, San Francisco, CA 94103, USA
events.description:
💘 What if everything evolutionary psychology told you about dating was wrong?
For decades, a buzzy branch of science has spread a deeply flawed story about romantic relationships, cloaking itself in the language of incontrovertible Darwinian fact. Evolutionary psychology claims our minds were shaped by primal drives that pit the genders against each other, from the myth that men are wired to be promiscuous to the notion that wealth, status, and beauty are the ultimate aphrodisiacs.
In this talk, UC Davis psychology professor Paul Eastwick, author of Bonded by Evolution and co-host of the Love Factually podcast, draws on original experiments from his own lab to reveal that these stories bear little resemblance to how attraction really works. Success in relationships does not hinge on finding the universally good partner, he argues, but on compatibility.
Popularity may shape first impressions, but its influence fades fast. And once we look at what men and women actually want, the supposed gender differences tend to evaporate. Eastwick reveals attraction as a process of finding, and often creating, a compatible connection. 💫

events.title: The Limits of Computer Decision-Making: Where Human Judgment Still Matters
events.location: Donkey & Goat Winery, 1340 Fifth St, Berkeley, CA 94710, USA
events.description:
🤖 How did a set of math rules from the 1940s end up defining what it means to be rational?
In the 1940s, mathematicians and engineers set out to build machines that could make critical decisions under uncertainty. Within a decade, they had invented tools that not only launched modern computer science but quietly rewrote what it means for a human being to make a "rational" choice.
Benjamin Recht, a professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences at UC Berkeley, will draw on his new book The Irrational Decision to trace how these academic rules for machines came to define rationality in economics, public policy, and everyday culture.
Ben will walk through where automated decision systems have thrived, from accelerating computers to regulating pharmaceuticals to powering e commerce, and where they break down. The pattern he has found is consistent: these systems excel in well defined spaces with clear rules and measurable goals, and turn brittle or absurd outside them.
The talk will close with a genuinely open question. How do we keep using these powerful tools without surrendering human judgment and agency in the process? 🧮

events.title: Memoirs: Writing Against Silence or Erasure
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley CA 94705
events.description: FREE, $10–$15 suggested donation Co-presented with Memoir Nation These four memoirists are, in different ways, writing into spaces where their experience has been minimized, misread, or actively suppressed. Judy Juanita's California Fever Dream spans sixty years of writing focused on Black activism and feminism. In I Love You So Many, journalist Terria Smith shares lessons learned from a career sharing stories about the richness of Native people’s lives. Elena Dudum's They Told Me Back Home Would Be Beautiful is a call to action against institutional silencing and censorship. Finally, Caroline Paul has spent her career writing women into adventure narratives that historically excluded them, most recently in Why Fly. Brooke Warner and Grant Faulkner, co-founders of the Memoir Nation podcast and online community, will guide a compelling discussion on the power of this truth-telling form. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Sonny Buttar's The Daughters of Rosebud, with Vanessa Hua
events.location: Bookshop West Portal 80 West Portal Ave San Francisco, CA 94127
events.description: Join us to celebrate Sonny Buttar's stunning debut novel, The Daughters of Rosebud . This multigenerational family saga will leave you at once heartbroken and hopeful. Sonny will be joined in conversation by Vanessa Hua , bestselling author of Coyoteland. This event is FREE to attend. Seating is first-come, first-served. (RSVPs are optional, but encouraged for our planning purposes.) You don't need to have read the book beforehand to enjoy the event, but we do recommend reserving your copy ahead of time. About the Book: In a heart-wrenching debut, author Sonny Buttar delivers a multigenerational family saga at once haunting and hopeful. Teacher Salma Chaudhry lives a quiet life, avoiding all attachments. But after a call from her estranged father, the protective shell she lives within starts to crack and the trauma she's buried for eighteen years emerges. Salma and her older sister Asma were inseparable growing up in small-town Rosebud. While Asma was bold and fearless, Salma tried to keep the peace in their fractured family. But amid their mother's decline and their parents' rigid expectations, Asma makes a choice that tears the family apart. The fallout changes everything--and forces Salma to choose between her sister and her parents. Salma has spent years trying to forget. But as she recollects her past and considers reconciliation with her father, a young student opens a surprising connection to Asma's past. In finally facing her history, Salma finds the bravery to love and hope again. The Daughters of Rosebud is a powerful exploration of sisterhood, family loyalty, and the courage it takes to heal. About the Author: Sonny Buttar was born in Pakistan and raised in England and the American Midwest. Her first novel, The Daughters of Rosebud, will be released in October 2026. About the Conversation Partner: Vanessa Hua is the nationally bestselling author of Coyoteland, A River of Stars and Forbidden City , and the story collection Deceit and Other Possibilities , a New York Times Editors’ Pick. A National Endowment for the Arts Literature Fellow, she has also received a Rona Jaffe Foundation Writers’ Award, the Asian/Pacific American Award for Literature, a California Arts Council Fellowship, and a Steinbeck Fellowship in Creative Writing, as well as honors from the de Groot Foundation, the Society of Professional Journalists, and the Asian American Journalists Association. She was a finalist for the California Book Award, the Northern California Book Award, and the New American Voices Award. Previously, she was an award-winning columnist for the San Francisco Chronicle . She teaches at the Warren Wilson MFA Program, Sewanee Writers Conference, and elsewhere. This fall, she is an Ann-Getty Endowed Visiting Artist-Scholar at the University of San Francisco. Her debut narrative nonfiction, Uprooted, is forthcoming.

events.description: Drummer/Vibraphonist/Saxophonist Smith Dobson V has been performing in the Bay Area for nearly twenty years. Originally from Santa Cruz, Ca., Dobson is a member of an important Jazz family. His father, the late Smith Dobson IV, was a world renown Pianist and director of the Jazz series at the Garden City in San Jose for over twenty years, where he accompanied artists’ like Art Pepper, Stan Getz, Bobby Hutcherson, Harold Land, Chet Baker, Red Norvo, Tal Farlow, and Lee Konitz, to name a few. Also in the family, Grandfather Smith III is a Jazz Accordionist, Grandmother Norma, Mother Gail, and Sister Sasha are all Jazz Vocalists. The family often performed as a group at the Garden City, and other venues, as well as many local schools and workshops. As a child, Smith V had the opportunity to study with legendary Jazz Drummer Albert “Tootie” Heath, who said of his pupil, “He has the talent, determination and persistence as a musician, combined with the dedication necessary to succeed… improvisational skills totally advanced, excellent sensitivity, both solo and as an accompanist… my most talented student!” Smith has had the honor of working with some of the great Jazz artists, locally and internationally, such as Bobby Hutcherson, Red Rodney, John Handy, Sheila Jordan, Red Holloway, Pete and Conte Condoli, Phillip Harper, Hal Stein, Noel Jewekes, Ben Goldberg, Graham Connahs’ Sour Note Seven, Darren Johnstone, Will Bernard, and Kenny Brooks.

events.title: Nafissa Thompson-Spires: The Four Wives and Five Deaths of Richard Milford
events.location: Museum of the African Diaspora, 685 Mission St, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Co-presented with Museum of the African Diaspora From the author of the multi-award-winning, National Book Award–longlisted, “vivid, fast, funny, way-smart, and verbally inventive” (George Saunders) story collection Heads of the Colored People, comes a sly, spry, literary debut novel. We find ourselves in 1920s Oklahoma, just far enough out of Tulsa, just long enough after the Race Massacre of 1921. For as long as anyone can remember, the Milfords have led plentiful lives on the backs of the townspeople of Newville. On the ominous brink of the Great Depression and at the height of Prohibition, Richard Milford is an infamous moonshiner and womanizer who, it seems, finally crossed the wrong person at the wrong time. He’s dead and buried with only his women to mourn him, but a question remains: Who killed him, and why? Top suspects are his four “wives,” but as their stories burst to light, the very idea of a true story comes apart before our eyes. In conversation with Margaret Wilkerson Sexton. Doors at 5:30pm.

events.title: Nara Aziza Smith - Homemade
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Join us as we welcome Nara Aziza Smith (@naraaziza), the best-dressed culinary creator in digital media, who is bringing her signature style to 80 delicious, homemade family-friendly recipes in her debut cookbook HOMEMADE. You may think you know Nara Smith—the glamorous outfits, the soothing ASMR voice, the beautiful family, the seemingly effortless approach to making food from scratch—but behind it all is a working mom with a relatable goal: preparing nourishing whole foods for herself and her family. Tickets include a copy of the book, the chance to get your copy personally signed, and a photo with Nara. A NOTE FROM NARA “This cookbook means the world to me. It holds the way I live and cook at home. It’s about slowing down, making things with your hands, and finding whimsy in the everyday. I’ve put together the recipes that I cherish so much and are things I either grew up eating or now serve to the people I love most. They’re simple, from scratch, and meant to be made and shared often.” —Nara Aziza Smith ABOUT THE BOOK You may think you know Nara Smith—the glamorous outfits, the soothing ASMR voice, the beautiful family, the seemingly effortless approach to making food from scratch—but behind it all is a working mom with a relatable goal: preparing nourishing whole foods for herself and her family. Nara grew up in Germany inspired by her grandmother’s cooking and the intention behind it. While working as a model, she soon met and married supermodel Lucky Blue Smith and started a family. When she was diagnosed with an autoimmune disease and eczema, she found that she could manage her symptoms by cutting out most processed foods. She turned her scratch-cooking expertise in a new curated direction while sharing her cooking online with compelling and elevated content. In her eagerly awaited and beautifully photographed first cookbook, Nara shares recipes from simple to complex, such as: Cinnamon Toast Squares , a quick breakfast beloved by Nara’s toddlers and better than anything you can find in stores Baked Fall Vegetable Salad with Miso-Sherry Dressing , a gorgeous salad that fuels Nara for long workdays Soy-Glazed Flank Steak with Plum Herb Salad , a beautiful, nourishing meal made from whole ingredients Lucky’s Oat Chocolate Chip Cookies , Nara’s husband’s recipe for the best American classic In HOMEMADE , Nara brings ease and elegance to the creation of homemade food—inspiring readers to elevate their own reality, in the kitchen and beyond in their daily life. Nara Aziza Smith is a globally recognized lifestyle creator, entrepreneur, and model. With a South African mother and a German father, she grew up in Frankfurt, first learning to cook by watching her father and grandmother in the kitchen. While working as a model, she met her husband, supermodel Lucky Blue Smith, and gradually began her growing curiosity for cooking from scratch and the intention behind it. Nara now resides in Connecticut with Lucky and their four children. She continues to build her authentic brand and grow her multi-million follower digital and culinary empire. events.title: Jad Youssef Author Talk • Lebnani: A journey through family, food & the flavour of Lebanon
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Jad Youssef is chef patron of the award-winning Lebnani in Reigate, Surrey which Jay Rayner highly praised in The Observer: ‘one taste of its gloriously zingy Lebanese flavours and you know you’re in the right place.’ Jad was born in Beirut during the Lebanese Civil War, the youngest of six siblings. He learnt to cook in his mother Khadija’s kitchen and in his father’s pastry shop before training at the Ecole Hoteliere in Beirut. After early work in local hotels and restaurants, he moved to Oslo in 2000 as Head Chef at Jeppe Restaurant, later relocating to London to lead the kitchen at Fakhreldine in Piccadilly and serve as Executive Chef at the Levant Group. In 2009, Youssef founded Yalla Yalla in Soho, one of London’s first Lebanese street food restaurants, expanding to Fitzrovia and Shoreditch in the following years. The restaurant received wide critical attention and achieved a cult following. His signature dish, Sawda Djej (chicken livers with pomegranate molasses), developed an equally devoted following and was named one of Time Out London's "100 Best Dishes." After time in Hong Kong, Youssef and his wife Aga returned to the UK to open Lebnani in Reigate, Surrey, in 2020. The restaurant was named Best Restaurant in Surrey by Muddy Stilettos in 2024, awarded an AA Rosette, and was the recipient of the Be Inclusive Hospitality Middle Eastern Food Award in 2025. Jad has also appeared at Meatopia, Taste of London, and Taste of Hong Kong, served as a judge on Celebrity MasterChef UK, appeared on BBC's MasterChef, and worked with Miele among many others. His work has been featured in The Times, The Observer, Financial Times, The Guardian, and numerous other publications. Lebnani - In Lebnani , celebrated chef Jad Youssef invites readers to experience the warmth, generosity and soul of Lebanese cooking through recipes passed down through generations of his family. In his debut book, Jad returns to the dishes and memories that shaped his life in Beirut and beyond, celebrating Lebanese food as it is truly lived and eaten. Featuring 84 authentic recipes from his family’s kitchen in Lebanon and his award-winning restaurant Lebnani in Surrey, the book reveals secret spice blends, time-honoured techniques and beloved family dishes that bring people together around the table. Chapters echo the rhythm of daily life - Lebanese Mornings, Mezza at Home, Tabkha (everyday meals), Mashawi (grills), Sandwiche (street wraps), Helweyet (sweets) and Namlieh (the pantry) - reflecting the meals and moments that shape Lebanese identity. Family stories are woven throughout, tracing how food sustained Lebanese families through conflict, change and celebration. From gathering wild za’atar to mornings spent collecting trays of freshly baked mana’eesh, Jad’s memories root Lebanese cuisine in gratitude, connection and resilience. With evocative imagery and heartfelt storytelling, Lebnani offers a rich portrait of a culture where food, memory and family life are deeply intertwined.
