events.title: Write Your Heart Out with Britta Stromeyer
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: "There is no greater agony than bearing an untold story inside you." – Maya Angelou Ever feel like your life has a million stories waiting to be told, but you aren't sure where to start? Join us for this soulful, 90-minute workshop designed to help you pause, reflect, and put pen to paper. Whether you want to craft "mini-stories" from your favorite memories or simply use journaling to make sense of the beautiful chaos of daily life, this workshop is your safe space to explore. What to Expect Guided Prompts: We’ll move past "dear diary" with creative triggers that spark vivid memories and deep insights. The Art of the Mini-Story: Learn how to capture a life lesson or a fleeting moment in just a few paragraphs. Clarity & Connection: Use writing as a tool to de-clutter your mind and find the "why" behind your experiences. Low Pressure, High Expression: No "writer" credentials required—just you, a notebook, and an open heart. Whether you’re looking for a new creative outlet or a way to process your journey, come discover how powerful your own narrative can be. Leave with a clearer mind, a fuller heart, and at least one story that’s uniquely yours. Meet Your Instructor Britta Stromeyer is a member of the National Book Critics Circle. Her writing appears in The Common, World Literature Today, Tupelo Quarterly, Beyond Words Magazine, Necessary Fiction, On the Seawall, Flash Fiction Magazine, Bending Genres Journal, Marin Independent Journal, and other publications. Britta was a finalist for the Bellingham Review Tobias Wolff Award for Fiction 2021. She is a frequent reader for the CLMP’s Firecracker Awards. A former editor for Tuxedo Literature & Arts & FastForward Magazine, Britta holds an MFA from Dominican University, CA, an M.A. from American University, and a Certificate in Novel Writing from Stanford University. Read more at brittastromeyer.com . What students are saying about Britta: "Britta was thoughtful and full of wisdom. This class was inspiring and thought provoking. I left inspired and full of possibility!" - Rebecca R. "As the first writing class I ever took, Britta’s workshop was an excellent way to kickstart my writing efforts. The rapidly paced and diverse prompt-writing exercises were challenging, thought-provoking and fun at the same time." - Laurie W

events.title: Stacey Gordon - The Pearl Farmers
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: This layered multigenerational novel follows three sisters upholding their family’s Tennessee pearl farm legacy. Rich with emotional depth and anchored by the pearl’s symbolism of beauty born from irritation, this story of resilience will captivate fans of Ann Patchett, Celeste Ng, and Claire Lombardo. Three estranged sisters—Helen, Anna, and Penn Lockshire—are bound by the shimmering but fragile legacy of their family’s freshwater pearl farm in rural Tennessee. When the business that once made them famous faces collapse, the sisters are pulled back into each other’s lives and forced to reckon with old betrayals, unspoken resentments, and the complicated truth of their inheritance. Soon, what began as a fight for survival becomes a reckoning with the myths that shaped them and the secrets buried in the family’s past. From the discovery of a rare pearl in 1981 to the struggles of a failing farm in 2008, the Lockshire sisters must navigate love, loss, ambition, and forgiveness to decide whether their heritage is a blessing to preserve—or a burden to escape. Rich with emotional depth and anchored by the pearl’s enduring symbolism—a thing of beauty born from irritation—this sweeping story of family, identity, and resilience will captivate readers of Celeste Ng and Claire Lombardo. “Gordon expertly handles her ambitious narrative and sprawling cast . . . A textured tale of renewed kinship and self-discovery.” —Kirkus Reviews “Heart-warming story of sisterhood, purpose, and family legacy.” —BookLife Reviews “ The Pearl Farmers was such a satisfying read . . . It’s an uplifting tale that resonates in these times.” —Ann Bancroft, author of Almost Family “I fell in love with Penny, Helen, and Anna, and was pulling for these three sisters to find a way back to each other. The Pearl Farmers is Yellowstone meets Little Women —but with way better jewelry!” —Emma Tourtelot, author of No One You Know Stacey Gordon grew up in the Appalachian foothills of southern Ohio and began her career as a trade journalist covering the cultured pearl and jewelry industries, visiting farms across Asia and companies around the world. For the past twenty-five years she’s worked in marketing and user experience design for the Silicon Valley tech industry. This is her debut novel. She lives with her family in Alameda, California. events.title: Kirk Lombard - The Shadow Stream
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A throwback to family-reads-of-yore, this epic follows a troubled boy and a host of hilariously vexed animals who must save a river before it’s dammed, so they can save themselves. Perfect for ages 10+ and all adults! School Library Journal: Review of the Day “Kirk Lombard’s The Shadow Stream is a book of great originality, a book like no other, propelled by brilliant storytelling and original thinking (and fish!) that will engage readers of all ages — a perfect family book.” — Mark Kurlansky, author of Cod and Salt and World Without Fish Gabriel (“G” for short) is wasting away in the Abiddon County Juvenile Center when he’s introduced to the Shongunk River by his dying uncle. The river valley — trash-heaped but chock-full of mysteries and fish — wins G over. But, as G has learned, good things can’t last. The Shongunk is scheduled to be dammed by a local developer. In a matter of days, it will cease flowing, and all of the talkative creatures who live in the river valley will be as homeless as G. Just as G decides it’s no time to accept his fate, so too do the animals. To inspire an uprising, a young trout is nominated to make a fateful journey up the river; a raccoon swears a violent oath against humans; and a newly sober buck leads his skittish flock out of harm’s way. Together with G, they show there is power in all of us, even the smallest minnow. Kirk Lombard is an author, angler, sustainable fishmonger and tuba player who worked inside the juvenile rehabilitation system. His first book, the award-winning Sea Forager’s Guide to the Northern California Coast , was described as “poetry” for fish, by NPR. He lives in the Bay Area with his family, raising his children on herring and sea shanties. events.title: Sovereignty Through Sound: Mantra, Resonance & Return with Radhika Vekaria
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
What if sound is something you felt in the body as much as heard in your ears? Long before it was music, sound served as medicine, prayer, and portal — a technology for shifting consciousness that predates language itself. Join Grammy-nominated artist and teacher Radhika Vekaria for an immersive afternoon built around direct, felt experience: exploring mantra and the intelligence of sound through your own body, breath, and voice.

Through direct practice and philosophical insight, this session works with sound as an organizing intelligence, one that refines focus, strengthens presence, and cultivates inner coherence. This is active work: chanting, mudras, and breath practice done together as a group.

You will explore:
- The relationship between sound and resilience
- The deeper meaning behind mantra
- Chant as a practice of clarity and courage
- Mudra and Nāda yoga as embodied extensions of the practice

Rooted in yogic philosophy and grounded in contemporary life, this immersion offers an approach to cultivating steadiness, awareness, and peace.

No prior experience is required.

The afternoon closes with a 75-minute live performance with Radhika singing in a communal setting, drawing on the same deep lineage that guides the whole workshop.


Teacher Bio:
Radhika Vekaria is a Grammy®-nominated artist and composer working at the crossing point of Sanskrit and Vedic sacred sound and contemporary music. Her voice draws on devotional and contemporary vocal styles as well as Hindustani classical tradition — she studied for several years under Meher Paralikar, a disciple of Padma Bhushan Pandit Ajoy Chakrabarty of the Patiala-Kasur gharana — alongside classical piano trained since childhood. That grounding shows up in every performance: precise, disciplined, and unmistakably rooted in lineage, even as the music itself moves into new territory.

Her project SAPTA: The Seven Ways, an exploration of Vedic mantra, became a healing practice for everyone who encountered it, and made her the first mantra artist to perform at SXSW in 2022. Her 2025 album Warriors of Light earned a Grammy nomination and extended that same inquiry into how ancient sound moves through a contemporary ear. Named after Radha, the Vedic symbol of devotion, she treats sacred sound as a living practice — one she has carried from concert stages to sacred gatherings across the globe. Radhika has performed at Harvard, Omega Institute, the Grammy Museum, and prestigious venues like Estelle Manor and Naviva, reflecting the wide lens through which she is able to convey this wisdom and reach people.

Growing up in a British East African Indian family, Radhika was immersed in Vedic rituals since childhood. Learning music from early infancy and with continuous exploration of the multiple arenas of Vedic traditions and philosophy, she has a refreshing approach to how this wisdom can be imbibed and applied in the world today. In 2022, her live audio rooms online reached over 100,000 people with meditation and mantra sessions.

She offers a room an experience of return — voice and mantra used deliberately to move people from thinking into feeling, from the head to the heart. That instinct shapes both her performances and her workshops: through similar sessions, she works directly with people's own relationship to sound and voice, drawing on the same tradition and training behind her stage work. For a space built around inquiry and embodied practice, she brings a performance to be moved by, and a practice to be moved through.

Explore more at www.radhikavekaria.com

events.title: Artist Talk – Andrea Brewster: Draft
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: Andrea Brewster, Draft 1, 2026, giclee print, woven vellum, 10″ x 10″, photo courtesy of the artist Andrea Brewster’s new body of work, Draft, begins with the fundamental structure of weaving: warp and weft, whose interlacing creates both fabric and an underlying grid. She approaches the grid not as a rigid system, but as a living structure capable of variation, interruption, rhythm, and ambiguity. The work draws from weaving drafts, diagrams that function as instructions for generating complex patterns, resembling a form of pre-digital code. The term “draft” also refers to an initial idea or work in progress, connecting structure with imagination and instruction with image.This connection between weaving and digital systems is central to Brewster’s thinking. Although digitally constructed, these pieces retain the appearance of hand-drawn marks, creating a tension between material and virtual, order and improvisation. Through line, color, repetition, and interruption, Brewster explores the relationship between visible patterns and the structures beneath them. Bio: Andrea Brewster is a multidisciplinary artist who investigates the intersection of nature, fiber art, and technology through intricate forms and layered textures. Brewster earned a B.A. in Sculpture from Pomona College and an M.F.A. in New Genres from the San Francisco Art Institute. A 1993 NEA grant recipient, she has exhibited widely in the San Francisco Bay Area, with solo shows at Mercury 20, The Lab, and Southern Exposure, as well as group exhibitions at Metal Haus Gallery, Chandra Cerrito Contemporary, The Oakland Museum, and the Peninsula Museum. Her work has been featured in fiber art exhibitions in Ireland and the U.S. She has participated in the Djerassi Resident Artist Program, and in 2025, her AI work appeared at Load Gallery, Barcelona, and in the book Neo Botanica. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery since 2020. events.title: Artist Talk – Jill McLennan: harm_less
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: Jill McLennan, Walter, 900 years old, watercolor, collage, ink, 26″x20″. photo by artist Jill McLennan’s work gives voice to the harmless, reflecting on the federal government’s decision to rescind the definition of harm (2026) as it applies to the protection of animals and their habitats, listed under the Endangered Species Act (1975). In her art, she depicts animals adapting, inventing new ways to thrive amidst human impact. Using sumi ink, a brush, and mulberry paper, she paints mammals, birds, amphibians, plants, trees, and rivers. Then, tearing the paper, she applies these images to wood panels. Adding watercolor and handmade paper, she creates a transformation from reality to wonder. McLennan states, “The animals are here alongside us, they have always been here, and it is our duty to ensure that they remain, that their habitat is here on earth for generations to come. May my art be a message to harm less, a cry to the present and a hope for the future.” Bio: Jill McLennan creates paintings, collages and prints inspired by her surroundings and the stories that she collects. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery since 2007. She is an active member of her neighborhood, Jingletown Arts, Business + Community (JABC), organizing Open Studios as well as beautification projects. She recently printed a series of linoleum blocks with poems, telling stories of migration and climate change, through a residency at the Kala Art Institute in Berkeley, CA. McLennan has completed two public art projects: Jingletown Birds at 401 Derby and Emeryville Perspectives at 65th and Christie Streets. Both are cut steel fences depicting the local shoreline with birds, designed by McLennan and executed by local metal fabricators. Her work was accepted to the deYoung Open in 2020 and 2023. As an artist and teacher, she is deeply invested in protecting her environment, inspiring the youth, and spreading hope and joy into the world. events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . 🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: ZenThai Massage Daylong with Anjuli and Alok
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Join Anjuli and Alok for an incredible opportunity to study the practice of ZenThai Massage and develop your sensitivity and awareness through touch. 

Dive into the world of ZenThai Massage with experienced practitioners Alok and Anjuli, who have over 20+ years of experience as therapists and teachers. Their welcoming and supportive approach helps students feel safe and empowered as they hone their healing touch skills. Join them for a rewarding day of exchanging deeply nourishing bodywork and gaining the tools and guidance needed to further refine your own practice.
Anjuli & Alok have traveled the globe, studying under esteemed master teachers and crafting their unique style of bodywork. During this daylong immersion, they'll share their ZenThai practice, blending Thai Massage and Shiatsu techniques passed down by their mentor Gwyn Williams from Australia. Rooted in Thai Medicine and Buddhist Zen philosophy, their approach emphasizes respect, balance, and compassion. They'll also cover Chinese Meridians and specific acupressure points, enriching the practice even further.

ZenThai Shiatsu is an exceptional therapeutic technique that incorporates joint mobilization, mindful passive stretching, acupressure, and a focus on breath. With proper body mechanics, the practice truly becomes an effortless dance between giver and receiver. As yogis themselves, your teachers will be emphasizing the most fluid and easeful ways to offer compressions and stretching in this course, encouraging the giver to stay present with the receiver’s experience.

This training welcomes everyone, whether you're a yoga teacher, massage therapist, or simply interested in well-being and bodywork. You'll wear comfortable clothing and work on a mat. They’ll guide you through simple practices to enhance sensitivity and intuition, focusing on the client's experience while caring for your own body as well. You’ll practice both giving and receiving throughout the immersion, regardless of prior yoga or massage experience. Feel free to come alone or with a friend—no partner required.


In addition to all that you will learn during the immersion, you’ll also receive a complete manual, videos, and have access to our community.

Come with a friend or solo - no partner needed.

There will be a one hour break for lunch.

In this course you will learn:
+ How to give a full body sequence and bring someone up to seated
+ How to cultivate energy and develop sensitivity
+ How to use your full body and weight for effective and deep massage
+ Bio-mechanics to give a massage with the least effort
+ Thai Yoga moves to adjust, balance and correct yoga postures
+ Basic principles of Chinese Meridians and Acupressure points
+ Tools to work with special conditions and injuries
+ An introduction to mindfulness and breathing

events.title: Robin Rosenbluth, Rosanne Annoni & Georgine Hodgkinson - She Writes Press Event
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Mothers and Daughters: Writing Formative Relationships in Memoir What does it mean to reckon with the past and find yourself on the other side? In this panel, three She Writes Press memoirists, Robin Rosenbluth, Georgine Hodgkinson, and Rosanne Annoni, explore the profound and complicated ways their mothers shaped them, and the unexpected journeys that led each of them home to herself. From a young white woman navigating the semi-nomadic communities of 1970s Kenya while carrying the wounds of the U.S. foster care system, to a spiritual seeker tracing the long arc between a childhood vision of Christ and a solitary winter at Gampo Abbey, to a college professor who upended her carefully controlled life for the wilds of Puerto Rico's cryptocurrency scene, these are stories of displacement, desire, and hard-won transformation. Moderated by She Writes Press publisher Brooke Warner, this panel is an invitation to explore those moments that break us open and the unlikely places where healing takes root. Each of these memoirs reminds us that growing up isn't something that happens only in childhood, and that our mothers, for better or worse, are the first maps any of us is given to navigate ourselves and our lives. Robin Rosenbluth is a former foster teen who advocates for finding permanent homes for older foster youth. She has worked in the nonprofit sector in New York as a fundraiser, an adjunct professor at Columbia University and New York University. She has studied memoir and the craft of writing with many renowned authors and writes a Substack, My Jagged Journey as a Debut Writer . Robin and her wife have raised two children who now have families of their own. She lives in Brooklyn, New York. Rosanne Annoni was a successful psychotherapist for thirty-five years in the Bay Area before becoming an ordained teacher of the Diamond Approach in 2000. She has taught students and mentored teachers in the United States, the UK, and the EU. In 2024, she was awarded an Emerging Writer Fellowship from Aspen Words. She is married, has one son, and lives with her husband and dog on Cape Cod. Georgine Hodgkinson is a professor of communication studies at Cosumnes River College in Sacramento, where she also served as program coordinator for Re-Emerging Scholars, a program for formerly incarcerated students. Her published scholarship includes book chapters, journal articles, and essays exploring politics, gender, and spirituality. In 2025, she was a People’s Choice Winner for the Amy MacRae International Memoir Award. A certified yoga instructor who loves to run and play pickleball, Georgine splits her time between Dorado, Puerto Rico, and Folsom, California, with her husband, Mark. Brooke Warner is publisher of She Writes Press, a memoir coach, and author of Write On, Sisters!, Green-light Your Book, What's Your Book?, and three books on memoir. She’s a TEDx speaker, weekly podcaster (of “Write-minded” with co-host Grant Faulkner of NaNoWriMo), and publishes a weekly newsletter, Writerly Things, on Substack at brookewarner.substack.com . Robin Rosenbluth, Rosanne Annoni, Georgine Hodgkinson, Brooke Warner - photos courtesy of the authors Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.title: Kevin Waite - The Boundless Biddy Mason
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Prize-winning historian Kevin Waite uncovers an extraordinary story of survival in this first book-length biography of Biddy Mason. The narrative follows Mason's journey from the cotton South to metropolitan California, detailing how she crossed the continent, broke free from slavery, and built Black Los Angeles. Through the lens of the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the dawn of Jim Crow, Waite reveals Mason's profound impact on California's history. Los Angeles’s leading Black property owner entered the city as a piece of property herself. Born enslaved in 1818, Biddy Mason was forcibly transported 3,000 miles to California before winning her freedom in a landmark 1856 court case. By the time of her death, she had become one of the wealthiest African Americans in the West – an entrepreneur, philanthropist, and founding mother of Black Los Angeles. The Boundless Biddy Mason: An Odyssey from Slavery to Freedom Across the American West, Kevin Waite’s masterful biography of Mason – the first full-length study of her extraordinary life – places Mason at the center of a larger American story: the expansion of slavery into the West, the legal battles that tested freedom’s meaning, and the rise of a vibrant Black Los Angeles community she helped build. Waite documents Mason’s early years in Mississippi and follows her forced journey across the continent, as one of roughly 1,500 enslaved African Americans who were trafficked from the slave states to the frontier. Her enslaver, Robert Smith, a convert to Mormonism, marched Mason and her children from Mississippi to Utah and ultimately to California. Despite the state’s constitutional ban on slavery, Smith became the largest slaveholder in California, with fourteen people under his control. But it wasn’t until Smith attempted to relocate his human chattel to Texas that the law intervened. A pitched legal battle in Los Angeles resulted in freedom for Mason, her three daughters, and ten other women and children. From that moment forward, Mason reshaped her destiny – and the destiny of her city. She built a respected practice as a nurse and midwife, invested shrewdly in downtown real estate, cultivated influential alliances, and helped found Southern California’s first Black church. Her canny ability to disarm her denigrators with kindness and competence earned Mason a reputation as a leader. Award-winning historian Kevin Waite ably connects Mason’s life to the nation’s great upheavals: the westward expansion of slavery, the Civil War and Reconstruction, and the dawn of Jim Crow. In doing so, he restores Mason to her rightful place in American history, detailing her role as a survivor of forced migration, a litigant in a landmark freedom suit, and an architect of Black Los Angeles. Mason’s legacy in Los Angeles endures to this day, not only as founding member of the First African Methodist Episcopal Church but also in the public works she inspired. “In this astute work of historical recovery, Kevin Waite has provided us with a definitive, modern biography of the remarkable Biddy Mason…a tremendous achievement and a cautionary tale for our own fraught times.” ―Manisha Sinha, author of The Rise and Fall of the Second American Republic: Reconstruction, 1860–1920 “Combining meticulous scholarship with taut, propulsive prose, Kevin Waite tells the story of how the quietly extraordinary Biddy Mason helped break slavery's hold on Southern California. Absorbing and revelatory, this is history at its best.” —Nathaniel Philbrick, National Book Award–winning author of In the Heart of the Sea and The Rush “Kevin Waite has written the book we’ve needed for a long time. Biddy Mason was a most extraordinary woman. With great care and exhaustive research, Kevin Waite has written her biography as part of the stories of enslavement and emancipation as well as faith and community at the western edge of the United States.” —Kelly Lytle Hernández, author of Bad Mexicans Kevin Waite is Anne Stark Watson and Chester Watson Distinguished Professor of History at the University of Texas at Dallas. His first book, West of Slavery , won the 2022 Wiley-Silver Prize and was shortlisted for three other awards, including the Lincoln Prize. His writing appears in The Atlantic , the Los Angeles Times , The Washington Post , Slate , National Geographic , and The New Republic . Kevin moonlights in the TV and film industry, most recently as the writer and producer of a six-episode docuseries on the American Revolution for National Geographic and Disney+. events.title: How They Did It: Getting Unstuck
events.location: Page Street Co-Writing, 297 Page St, San Francisco
events.description: $25 Co-presented with LitCamp You know the feeling. You're moving along, racking up the word count on your novel (or memoir, or creative nonfiction project) when suddenly you hit a wall, a dead end, a what-the-heck-am-I-supposed-to-write-next fork in the road. Call it writer’s block, or a crisis of confidence, or just the universe conspiring against you. But whatever you call it, it's happened to every writer. Join us as four authors, Samina Ali (Pieces You'll Never Get Back), Diana Kapp (The Last Free Women), Jason Roberts (Every Living Thing: The Great and Deadly Race to Know All Life), and Parini Shroff (Some People) share their strategies for pushing past the roadblocks and getting the words flowing again. Moderated by Page Street founder Janis Cooke Newman (A Master Plan for Rescue). Plus, we'll serve complimentary Prosecco, wine, and NA drinks. Tickets support both Litquake and LitCamp. Doors at 3:00pm.

events.title: Embodied Anatomy:  A Guided Meditation & Live Ambient Music Experience with Dr. Karah Charette and Spencer Sussman
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
What if you could slow down enough to listen to your own biology?

Join us for an immersive journey through the living landscape of the body, blending guided somatic meditation with live ambient music. Moving through four inner organ systems, including the brain, heart, lungs, and digestive system, we will explore the felt experience of embodied anatomy through rest and curiosity. 

Each part of the journey offers an invitation to notice the subtle rhythms, sensations, movements, and processes happening within you. What would it be like to pause and feel the shifting activity of the brain, the pulsing and presence of the heart, the movement of breath through the lungs, and the deep, rhythmic work of digestion? 

Through poetic guidance, sensory imagery, gentle movement, and spacious periods of rest, you will be invited to turn your attention inward. 

Gentle ambient music will accompany the journey, creating an evolving soundscape that will support your relaxation, curiosity, and deep listening.

Come lie down, get comfortable, move if you feel called to, and listen closely.No experience needed. Arrive as you are.

Bio: Dr. Karah Charette, PT, DPT, RYT is a somatic pelvic health physical therapist, movement educator, and dancer. Drawing from her studies in Body-Mind Centering® and Authentic Movement, she guides gentle, sensory-based experiences that support deep listening and embodied awareness.

Spencer Sussman is a producer, composer, and trombonist from the SF Bay Area. His nature inspired ambient sound design creates immersive, meditative listening experiences grounded in warmth, resonance, and spaciousness.

events.title: THE AZAR LAWRENCE EXPERIENCE
events.location: Bach Dancing & Dynamite Society (Douglas Beach House), 311 Mirada Rd, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019
events.description:
Azar Lawrence is an internationally celebrated saxophonist, composer, and bandleader, and one of the great torchbearers of spiritual jazz. Emerging from the powerful Los Angeles music tradition, he’s known for his deeply expressive sound, high‑energy performances, and his belief in music as a force for healing, elevation, and cultural memory.

This performance highlights music from Lawrence’s new recording Turn the Music Up , a vibrant chapter in his catalog that celebrates joy, ancestral memory, and creative freedom. Over his extraordinary career, Lawrence has performed with giants such as McCoy Tyner, Miles Davis, Freddie Hubbard, Woody Shaw, Elvin Jones, Buster Williams, and Pharoah Sanders. His sound channels the spirit of John Coltrane while remaining unmistakably his own—expansive, soulful, and spiritually charged. With The Azar Lawrence Experience, he brings this legacy forward through a powerful ensemble rooted in master musicianship, improvisational fire, and deep spiritual intention.

The Azar Lawrence Experience is more than a concert — it is a transmission of sound, spirit, history, and uplift.

Azar Lawrence – Sax; Lynne Fiddmont – Vocals; Brian Swartz – Trumpet ; Taka Mori – Guitar; Robert Turner – Piano; Gerald Brown – Bass; Yayo Morales – Drums

events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . events.title: Lucid Dreaming: The Art of Navigating Your Own Mind with Nisha and Norma Burton
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Lucid dreaming is not reserved for the special few. Rather, it is a trainable skill, and a doorway into the deeper practice of psychonavigation, the art of moving through your own psyche with clarity, intention, and skill. In this workshop, mother-daughter teaching team Norma Burton and Nisha Burton will guide participants through foundational practices that many cultures throughout history have used to work with dream and the subconscious.

Participants will be introduced to lucid dreaming as an accessible, learnable practice, along with complementary inner pathways like dreamwork, shadow work, and drumming journeys. Together, these tools can help build a working map of one's own inner world, supporting healing, sharpening intuition, and strengthening the kind of discernment that can be very useful in a world saturated with noise and division. The workshop is also intended as a foundation for anyone preparing for or integrating psychedelic experiences, offering grounded skills for navigating altered states.

During the workshop, participants can expect to:
- Learn the fundamentals of lucid dreaming and how to begin cultivating it through simple, evidence-informed techniques
- Explore dreamwork and shadow work practices for interpreting dreams and identifying unconscious patterns
- Begin building a personal practice, starting with dream journaling, to carry these tools into daily life
- Learn both beginning and advanced lucid dreaming techniques 

Rooted in nearly thirty years of Norma's work in Buddhist practice, Jungian shadow work, and trauma healing, and brought into the present through Nisha's own experience with lucid dreaming, this workshop offers an intergenerational approach to teaching — practical, embodied, and grounded in decades of lived experience.

Website:  luciddreaminglucidliving.com
Instagram:   @lucid_dreaming_lucid_living


Teacher Bios:

Norma J. Burton is a pioneering expert in complex trauma healing with over 40 years of counseling experience. She did M.A. and Ph.D. work at Berkeley's Graduate Theological Union, and M.Div. at Pacific School of Religion with specializations in Hospice Chaplaincy and Psychology. Her distinguished career began with a decade of leadership in domestic violence advocacy, where she served as Director of battered women's shelters around the country, before serving at the National Coalition Against Domestic Violence headquarters.

In the early 1990s, Burton developed the Journey to Completion™, an innovative spiritual-psychological, trauma healing process now practiced internationally. Building on this foundation, she founded and directed The Circle of Trust Healing Center in 2014, a state-certified addiction recovery and mental health facility. Under her leadership, the center conducted groundbreaking studies demonstrating the superior effectiveness of holistic approaches in achieving lasting addiction recovery. Burton's unique blend of academic rigor, clinical expertise, and innovative methodology has positioned her at the forefront of transformative healing practices.

Nisha Burton is a lucid dreaming practitioner, award-winning filmmaker, and emerging technologies consultant. Raised in a shamanic lineage, she grew up traveling the world as a child to study directly with wisdom keepers.  She carries ancestral knowledge of altered states and soul work passed through Choctaw, Santee, and Cree lines, a Yoruba lineage rooted in her father's work, and a Druidic thread on her mother’s Celtic side. From an early age, she was steeped in the disciplined art of navigating one's own psyche with skill - above all through staying impeccable by doing the deep, ongoing work of shadow integration. This lineage-rooted foundation shapes how she guides others through altered states today. Along with linage based knowing she has also extensively studied Tibetan Dream Yoga, Jungian Dream Analysis, and dream researchers such as Stephen LaBerge. As co-founder of Lucid Living Inc., she delivers Lucid Dreaming workshops globally. Nisha has co-authored three books on consciousness exploration: Navigating Liminal Realms (Findhorn), Lucid Dreaming Lucid Living (Red Wheel/Wieser), and The Psychonaut's Oracle (Schiffer). She speaks internationally on consciousness navigation and AI innovation.

events.title: Danny Rosen & J Grabowski w/ Starry Skemes: A Two-Way Book Party & Concert
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Two-Way Mirror books celebrates the release of its latest books: Danny Rosen ‘s A Love Poem Called War and J Grabowski ‘s POMPEI: or The Notes Are In The World , with music by J Lee’s Starry Skemes . Publisher Marina Lazzara hosts. Each morning Danny Rosen pees on the bank of the largest unnamed tributary to the East Branch of Big Salt Wash which flows into the Colorado River several miles below Fruita, Colorado. Early on he learned to swing a hammer and that changed everything. He has been a poet, publisher, teacher, geologist, astronomer, and carpenter. In the middle of his journey he found himself running an astronomical observatory in the heart of the Namib Desert under the southern sky where he cultivated an optimistic outlook based on his familiarity with big space and deep time. He is the author of Suspended Erosion (2024), The Tuscan Journals & Other Poems (2022), Primate Poems (2016), Ghosts of Giant Kudu (2013), and That Curve (2006). He founded Lithic Press in 2007 and has run Lithic Bookstore since its opening in 2015. An inveterate rock hanger, he has collaborated with beavers on a variety of landscape installations. J Grabowski is an artist from New York whose practice explores drawing, writing, painting, sculpture, movement, and music. He cofounded PUSH Press, the Heliopolis Project (2010-2015), POMPEI and Turtle Records. Previous publications include Time Landscape (Bird & Beckett, 2017). J.Lee is a San Francisco is a San Francisco multi instrumentalist, songwriter, improviser, modular synthesist and visual artist. He is a member of the indie psych rock band Starry Skemes and the experimental rock band Warm Spell. He has formerly played with the Rabbles, Static Faction and Aerosol Species.

events.location: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, San Francisco
events.description: For generations, public broadcasting has been America’s largest classroom and most trusted source of information—a vital pillar of a well-informed democracy. But things are shifting fast. Media is more fragmented than ever, streaming giants keep changing their business models, and funding battles are ongoing. events.title: Maria Geyman Author Talk • With Tea: Culture, Accoutrements, and Rituals
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Maria Geyman is a board-certified naturopathic doctor and writer on culture, food, and beauty. With Tea is her first book. Her work has been featured in NYT, Goop, Vogue. She lives in Brooklyn, NY with her husband and two kids- Mona and Simon. Lauren Haynes is an herbalist, writer and the founder of Wooden Spoon Herbs. Her work centers around connection with the natural world through medicinal plants, and has been featured in Bon Appetit, The New York Times, Vogue and New York Magazine. She lives in Napa, California with her partner. Tea is the most consumed drink in the world after water, and a new generation is creating fresh ways of thinking about and drinking tea. Thoughtful, detailed, and visually stunning, this elevated, category-defining book explores tea’s health benefits and creates a framework for the new wave of recipes and tea rituals. Divided into three richly illustrated sections, each adorned with delicate watercolors and photography by a Vogue staff photographer, Part One explores tea culture, the importance of teas and herbs throughout history, and how tea culture can be found and enjoyed anywhere. Part Two brings tea into daily life with brewing techniques, recipes, accoutrements, rituals, and hosting tips. Part Three focuses on wellness and incorporating specific teas and herbs into health and beauty routines. Tea culture sits at the intersection of food, wellness, fashion, and beauty—and With Tea connects them seamlessly. Whether a seasoned connoisseur or a curious beginner, this is the ultimate celebration of tea, making it the perfect gift for tea lovers everywhere.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Return to Center: Exploring Stability, Mobility & Ease with Vickie Russell Bell
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves..



Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition.

Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.

events.title: Half-Day Silent Unguided Retreat
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice.
This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods.
There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of
meditation, all are welcome.

The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive
between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before
the first bell.

The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation:
9:30 AM – 10:10 AM
10:20 AM – 11:00 AM
11:10 AM – 11:50 AM

A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period.
The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between
sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom.
Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep
voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire
morning.

You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during
a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and
the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice
elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell.

The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website.

Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by
12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely
manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

events.title: NEW DATE: Henry J. Evans - Bombs, Bacon, and Bankruptcy
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Crisis leadership can be the toughest type of leadership—and the most crucial to master. Whether the stakes are literally life-and-death or just feel that way, this is the essential guide to keeping your team at their best when things are at their worst. Successfully navigating a crisis doesn’t require an innate talent for high-pressure situations. It requires understanding why we act the way we do when business as usual is disrupted—and how to stay calm, think clearly, and execute on the right priorities. Henry J. Evans has spent decades studying, practicing, and coaching other leaders through crises. He’s seen firsthand that whether a crisis is as deadly as roadside bombs during counterterrorism operations, as frustrating as bacon shortages during a pandemic, or as stressful as a family business on the edge of bankruptcy, the strategic, interpersonal, and emotional challenges are the same. Drawing on psychology, brain science, vivid true stories, and proven tools and tactics, Evans shows readers how to: Juggle the demands of today’s crisis without dropping the ball on tomorrow’s priorities. Decide when to trust data and AI and when to trust their gut instincts. Hold people accountable without destroying their sense of Emotional Safety.® Take care of the team’s needs without sacrificing the leader’s well-being. This is an invaluable guide for entrepreneurs, corporate leaders, and anyone trying to guide a team through tough times. It includes practical tools for honing your resilience, reaction times, listening and communication skills, threat assessment, emotional regulation, and more. Henry J. Evans is the founder and CEO of Dynamic Results, a strategy and culture transformation firm. While building a global leadership firm, Evans concurrently spent more than 20 years in counterterrorism and national security under four U.S. presidential administrations, holding a Top Secret security clearance. He has logged more than 16,000 hours of executive coaching and 6,000 hours of strategic planning facilitation with leaders across more than 80 countries. A sought-after keynote speaker and international MBA instructor, Evans is the bestselling author of Winning with Accountability and co-author of Step Up . He lives in San Francisco. Henry J. Evans - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. Free Admission / Open Seating There will be a signing line or meet and greet following the presentation.

events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Alex George is a self-taught baker, recipe developer, and food blogger whose TikTok channel, Lily P Crumbs, features her viral baking videos. She has been featured on Good Morning America and The Jennifer Hudson Show and collaborated with brands like Bob’s Red Mill and Domino Sugar. She lives in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Becky Duffett is an award-winning food writer living and eating in San Francisco. Her work has appeared in Food & Wine, Bon Appétit, The New York Times, the San Francisco Chronicle, and the San Francisco Standard. She served as the deputy editor at Eater SF, reporting breaking news during the pandemic, while running the largest dining website in the Bay Area. She’s also a former cookbook editor and classically trained cook, graduating from the professional program at San Francisco Cooking School. She was a commis at Petit Crenn, and currently bakes at Kantine. In the Mood to Bake: Extraordinary Treats from Lily P Crumbs - Alex George, a.k.a. Lily P Crumbs, brings her joyful, over-the-top baking style straight to your kitchen. Known for her viral quest to test every chocolate chip cookie recipe she could find, George draws inspiration from the beloved snacks of the 1990s and early 2000s treats like Philadelphia Cheesecake Snack Bars, Confetti Snacking Cake, Salted Malted Blondies, and Baklava Monkey Bread . Her “more is more” approach invites home bakers to embrace bold flavors, playful textures, and the uninhibited joy of childhood sweets. In this debut collection, she guides readers through cookies, bars, breakfast bakes, cake-adjacent creations, and imaginative ice cream treats, all infused with her signature humor and warmth. Whether you’re whipping up Carrot Cake Scones or building Key Lime Pie Ice Cream Sandwiches , you'll rediscover the simple delight of dessert. With vibrant photography and endlessly creative sweets, In the Mood to Bake is a fresh, fun upgrade to the home-baking canon.

events.title: SCOTT LAMBRIDIS: ST. ULPHIA'S DEAD
events.location: Books Inc. Pruneyard, 1875 S Bascom Ave, Campbell, CA 95008
events.description: Join us at Books Inc. Campbell to celebrate author Scott Lambridis on the debut of his first novel, St. Ulphia’s Dead ! About the Book Disgraced medical researcher Mirs and his skeptical new supervisor Jo arrive on the remote island of St. Ulphia to investigate an outbreak of mass psychosis. The villagers claim they’re being possessed— one by one— by a cannibalistic demon known as the Wendigo. While unraveling the villagers’ strange tales, Mirs and Jo are drawn into a tangle of local politics, mysterious disappearances, and impossible contradictions. When the missing begin to reappear, the boundaries between fact and folklore become dangerously thin. As tensions rise and trust fractures, Mirs and Jo must confront the possibility that the madness around them may not be entirely imagined— or may not be the villagers’ alone. A psychological mystery laced with absurd humor, St. Ulphia’ s Dead explores how trauma warps truth, how isolation breeds belief, and how the most terrifying demons are the ones we conjure for ourselves. About the Author Born and raised in New York, Scott earned a degree in neurobiology from the University of Virginia. He’s toured the Midwest with a progressive rock band, founded an indie press and performance series, earned an MFA from San Francisco State University, tended a 40-acre olive farm, and read a book from every country of the world. He wrote St. Ulphia’s Dead during his daughter’s naps during a year in France, and finally settled with his wife and child in Bellingham, Washington, “the city of subdued excitement.”

events.title: The Book of Luke — Lovell Holder
events.location: Fabulosa Books, 489 Castro St, San Francisco, CA 94114
events.description: Following the car accident that ended his football career and left his body scarred, twenty-two-year-old Luke Griffin joins the cast of Endeavor , a new competition-based reality show that pits the tabloids' darlings against one another in tasks of endurance and problem solving. At first, he thrives, effortlessly forming friendships and even a romantic relationship that he thinks will last a lifetime. But Luke has aspirations far bigger than the show's million-dollar prize, and soon a series of betrayals leads to irreversible tragedy, changing the course of his and his fellow contestants' lives forever. Ten years later, Luke's world looks very different: He is now a father of two and the stay-at-home husband to America's only openly gay senator. When his husband's serial cheating is exposed, Luke impulsively joins the cast of Endeavor 's latest season in a desperate bid to earn some fast cash. Back on set, he is confronted with everything he tried to leave in the past: bitter rivalries, shattered friendships, and crushing guilt, all of which threaten to tear down the walls he's spent a decade building. As Season 20 of Endeavor kicks off, Luke must give everything to the game, even as he finally learns what it means--and what it costs--to face the truth. ​Combining the fabulous rivalries of The Traitors with the epic physical stunts of The Challenge , The Book of Luke offers a grounded portrait of what it means to reinvent yourself when no one will let you forget your past--especially if it's immortalized on streaming services.

events.description: FREE, $10–15 suggested donation Co-presented with City Lights Bookstore Jennifer Croft may be best known as one of our foremost literary translators, bringing such acclaimed international authors as Olga Tokarczuk and Urszula Honek to English-speaking audiences. She’s also gained acclaim for her own writing, including her novel The Extinction of Irina Rey and her hybrid coming-of-age memoir Homesick, called “stunning and surprising” by the New York Times. Notes on Postcards utilizes an innovative format to delve into universal topics: love, loss, parenthood, communication, and connection. events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Delve into the fascinating world of five American women in different states across the country who are among the 80% of voters who rarely, if ever, engage in online rants or raves. We know that their votes count just as much. Experience their compelling stories, as they reveal intimate details of their lives and the experiences that shape their political beliefs. This captivating performance offers a rare glimpse into the moderate heart of America, often overshadowed by the radical fringes. Be prepared to laugh, reflect and question, as our writer and talented performer Erin-Kate Whitcomb impeccably brings these diverse characters to life. This riveting show offers a refreshing perspective on the political landscape, promising an evening of entertainment, humor and thought-provoking dialogue. Erin-Kate Whitcomb (AEA/AGVA/SAG-AFTRA) : Erin-Kate has been acting professionally for 30 years and has won Bay Area Critics Circle, Dean Goodman Choice and other awards for acting and playwriting. As a playwright, she was commissioned by Theatre Rhinoceros to write and perform her play “Route 80: Cars, Cows and Caffeine”, which won critical acclaim for her as a writer and multi-character actor. She has performed with 42 nd Street Moon, Berkeley Rep, TheatreWorks, Theatre Rhinoceros, Oasis SF and other Bay Area theatres. Erin-Kate performed in the US/Canadian tour with Dame Edna in “Dame Edna: My First, Last Tour” as Dame Edna’s disappointing daughter Valmai, and in the star-studded San Francisco revival of “Ruthless: The Musical”. Erin-Kate has supplied her voice for hundreds of radio and industrial jobs, and has appeared in TV and film for the past 35 years. Erin-Kate is a proud member and former Board Member of Northern California’s SAG-AFTRA, where she continues to serve both as an advisor, and on various committees. She is also a member of AEA (Actors Equity Association) and AGVA (American Guild of Variety Artists). EK is a fourth generation San Franciscan, and raised her sons, the fifth generation, in San Francisco with her wife, Michele. Francine Torres (Director) is a recent transplant from New York, where she served as Head of Acting at New Studio on Broadway. She holds an M.F.A. in Acting from UC San Diego/La Jolla Playhouse Professional Training Program, and a B.A. in Theatre from San Francisco State University. Presently, she serves on faculty at Foothill College. Francine began her career under the tutelage of Luis Valdez, founder of the iconic El Teatro Campesino. Steeped in the Teatro lifestyle of performing and touring, she began work with El Teatro de la Esperanza, and played the protagonist, Ana, in the inaugural production of Real Women Have Curves . Since then, she has been committed to educating, performing, and directing theatre exploring the Chicanx experience. She has mentored and taught underrepresented students of color at historically classical theatres such as the American Conservatory Theatre, the American Repertory Theatre, and the La Jolla Playhouse. Her work also includes nearly twenty years at the American Conservatory Theatre, teaching acting, improvisation, and clown work and transitions seamlessly between street and classical theatre. As a professional actor, she has created many indelible characters during her time at El Teatro Campesino and the American Repertory Theatre, has performed in repertory houses including Berkeley Rep, ACT, Dallas Theatre Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Theatresports, Killing My Lobster, and has toured the country and overseas. Francine’s most passionate interest is the intersection of diversity in theatre – gender, sexuality, color, neurodiversity and physical differences, and her experiences are published in the anthology Gravity Pulls You In . She plays the titular role in BITTEN (Bad Dog Productions), currently winning independent film festival awards across the country. events.title: Marcus Thompson, II - Game Changers
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Acclaimed sports journalist Marcus Thompson II presents Game Changers , a fast-paced, stat-filled tribute to the unique players who changed basketball forever and spark endless GOAT debates among fans. Joining the fierce debates every obsessive fan loves to have, acclaimed sports journalist Marcus Thompson II presents a series of bold cases for who he thinks are the unique players who changed basketball forever. Michael Jordan. Dirk Nowitzki. Candace Parker. Steph Curry. These players from the modern era are among a handful of basketball's elite who have earned the rare title of Game Changer. Their contributions go beyond statistics and accolades, beyond wins and records. What they and others like them have achieved is nothing short of revolutionary when it comes to the trajectory of the game. In this utterly unique basketball history, Marcus Thompson II highlights a rare selection of players from the NBA and WNBA, building a thoroughly convincing case for each athlete that points to their irrefutable and lasting impact. Fast-paced with plenty of inarguable stats and well-reasoned takes sure to create endless debate among fans, Game Changers is a glowing tribute celebrating the players we love to crown as GOATS. Marcus Thompson II is a lead columnist at The Athletic. With more than twenty years’ experience, he has developed a respected voice in the industry through his storytelling, ability to connect with athletes, and unique perspective. He is the author of the national bestseller Golden: The Miraculous Rise of Steph Curry , KD: Kevin Durant’s Relentless Pursuit to Be the Greatest , and Dynasties: The 10 G.O.A.T. Teams That Changed the NBA Forever. He lives with his wife, Dawn, and daughter, Sharon, in Oakland, California.
