events.title: Santiago Lastra Author Talk • Mexican Soul: A New Style of Cooking
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Santiago Lastra- Born in Mexico City and raised in Cuernavaca, Santiago Lastra has worked in Michelin-starred establishments around the globe, including the legendary Mugaritz in San Sebastián, Spain and noma in Copenhagen. In October 2020, he opened the doors of KOL in Marylebone, immediately capturing the attention and acclaim of the world’s media. Within three years, KOL secured its first Michelin star, a place on The World’s 50 Best and La Liste, and is regarded as the best Mexican restaurant outside of Mexico. Santiago was also awarded Best Chef at the GQ Food and Drink Awards, and Three Knives by The Best Chef Awards. In 2024, Santiago opened Fonda, a family-style restaurant serving vibrant interpretations of the food found in Mexican markets and homes. Santiago’s ethos is to develop food that celebrates his homeland’s rich cultural tastes, aromas and textures with meticulously sourced seasonal local produce. Mexican Soul is his first book. Mexican Soul - D id you know you can make the best guacamole you’ve ever tasted without using avocado? Or that tortillas and tamales can be made with potato? Through years of research, exploration and cooking in restaurants around the globe, chef Santiago Lastra has discovered a secret: you can make incredible Mexican food without having to hunt down specific ingredients or buy traditional produce that has lost its freshness by the time it lands in your kitchen. Mexican flavor can be unlocked anywhere in the world, with almost any ingredient, and this book is the key to finding it. By breaking down the basics of Mexican flavour profiles then exploring how you can find a wide variety of these elements in your home kitchen, Santiago shows a new way of understanding one of the richest cuisines on the planet so that anything from a Salsa Macha and Tomato and Cherry Aguachile to Tinga Tostadas and Chocolate Tamales with Chocolate and Mezcal Cream can be on the table in minutes, regardless of what you have to hand. Get ready to discover Mexican Soul: A New Style of Cooking .

events.title: Relatefulness with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other

Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli.

Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment.

This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. 

We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance!

What We’ll Explore

Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice:
Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group.
Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society.
Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly.
Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of.

Why Come?

You may be looking to:
Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected.
Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context.
Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns

This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun!

What Not to Expect

This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur.

It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. 

Here’s what NOT to expect:
A space free of conflict or triggers.
When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others.
No enforced hierarchy of emotions.
Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important.
Expression without attunement.
We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence.

Other logistics and notes

Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time!

We hope to see you at a future event! 

Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you.

More about the facilitators

Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring.

When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws.

In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance.

Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

events.title: Psychedelic Breathwork with Matt Barkin
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
By increasing the flow of oxygen or Prana in our bodies, we can begin to move and release tension.

In this class we shift our focus from the realm of thoughts to the intricate web of electrical signals within our bodies. Regardless of whether you've faced significant stress or trauma, this approach offers profound benefits to the nervous system. The accumulation of daily stressors can strain our bodies and without releasing this tension through expression, it can manifest as depression, anxiety, or disease over time.

In this class we

- Lay down for a guided short meditation.

- Practice the breathwork sequence together for around 30 minutes.

- Relax and recover.

- Optional sharing and snacks afterwards.


We have 26 trillion cells in our bodies and they all need oxygen. Come breathe with us and calibrate your nervous system!


NOTE: Doors close 10 minutes after the start of class. This event is in-person only.

Matt Barkin has been studying breathwork and meditation for over 15 years. His training is rooted in the ancient practices of Buddhist Vipassana and Kriya Yoga. His goal as a guide is to help students awaken their self-healing potential with the breath! Learn more about Matt here https://mattbarkin.com/breathwork/

events.title: Andy Richter - Elf Unwrapped
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Step into the magical world of ELF with this captivating oral history, written by beloved comedian and actor Andy Richter, who watched the on-set shenanigans unfold before his very eyes, and featuring a foreword by Will Ferrell!! Ever since Elf hit theaters, audiences around the world have fallen in love with the story of Buddy, the charming (and oversized) "elf" with a heart of gold. But what most people don’t know is that when the screenplay first hit Hollywood, no studio was willing to touch it. How, then, did such a risky gamble turn into one of the most beloved Christmas classics of all time? In this laugh-out-loud oral history, comedian and co-star Andy Richter goes on a mission to find out by reconnecting with the very people who brought this festive vision to life. Through exclusive interviews, hilarious anecdotes, and heartfelt reflections with key players like Will Ferrell, Zooey Deschanel, director Jon Favreau, and many others, Andy ultimately unwraps the story of how a quirky holiday film about a human raised by elves became such an enduring cultural phenomenon. Packed with never-before-seen photos, behind-the-scenes secrets, a foreword by Buddy himself (aka Will Ferrell), and a sprinkle of festive fun, this book is the perfect gift for anyone who believes in the magic of Christmas—and knows that the best way to spread holiday cheer is by singing loud for all to hear. Andy Richter is a comedian, actor, writer, and host. He's best known for his many years as Conan O’Brien’s collaborator and sidekick. He has appeared in numerous television shows and films, some of them quite good. He is also the host of the Three Questions podcast and The Andy Richter Call-In Show , and enjoyed a longer-than-expected run on Dancing with the Stars . He's based in Los Angeles. Aaron Karo (not appearing) is a comedian, screenwriter, author, and podcaster. His books include Ruminations on College Life , Ruminations on Twentysomething Life , I’m Having More Fun Than You , Lexapros and Cons , Galgorithm , and the #1 New York Times bestseller The Hidden Power of F*cking Up . He has developed television series for many studios and networks, and starred in his own one-hour Comedy Central stand-up special. He is based in Los Angeles. events.title: HERLIN RILEY
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of today’s premier jazz drummers · "The Groove Master", Herlin Riley is widely considered one of the best drummers in any genre of music performing today. The longtime drummer for the legendary Ahmad Jamal and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra now leads two groups, his quintet and the New Orleans Groove Masters featuring himself, Jason Marsalis, and Shannon Powell. Herlin’s most recent album, Perpetual Optimism, reunites the quintet of rising stars that Riley assembled for his Mack Avenue Records debut, New Direction. Since the release of that acclaimed album, all four of Riley’s bandmates – trumpeter Bruce Harris, saxophonist Godwin Louis, pianist Emmet Cohen, and bassist Russell Hall – have been making major waves across the modern jazz scene, attesting to the master drummer’s Art Blakey-like ear for talent and sage musical guidance. Herlin Riley's source of strength comes from his faith in God, his wife of four decades, and his family of five children and 10 grandchildren; his lifelong home in New Orleans, the creative community that surrounds it, and his positive approach to life and music. His roots in the church are also vital, shining through in the congregational claps that help establish the celebratory spirit that is showcased in the album opener “Rush Hour.” He also relies on his musical family, including his long-established ties with Wynton Marsalis and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra. Riley’s connection to the Marsalis dynasty traces back a generation earlier, to family patriarch and fellow lifelong New Orleanian Ellis Marsalis. It was while performing with Ellis at the annual New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival in a trio with bassist Reginald Veal that Riley first caught the ear of Wynton, who invited both members of his father’s rhythm section to join him, launching a vital relationship that’s now lasted more than three decades. Riley pays homage to his mentor on the closing track of Perpetual Optimism, the funky arrangement of Ellis Marsalis’ composition “Twelve’s It.” In the quintet’s lively rendition, the tune is not just a cover but a tribute, as Riley intones a short ode to passing the torch that refers to the elder Marsalis as “a great musician who taught a whole lot of fellows.” Another Crescent City icon, the late singer, pianist, songwriter, and producer Allen Toussaint, was the motivator behind Riley’s other vocal turn on the album, a gritty take on Willie Dixon’s blues classic “Wang Dang Doodle.” Toussaint stopped in to hear Riley play at a New Orleans club and heard the drummer’s 5/4 arrangement of the familiar standard. “He was really impressed,” Riley recalls. “He said, ‘Wow, man, I’ve heard ‘Wang Dang Doodle’ a thousand times, but I’ve never heard it performed in 5 before. You should record that.’ A few months later, he passed away, so I recorded the tune to pay homage to the wishes of the great Allen Toussaint.” Though he conveys vivid emotion in his voice, Riley stops short of calling himself a singer. His willingness to step to the mic comes from advice he was given by New Orleans vocal great Germaine Bazzle. “She’s a very elegant and regal lady, but when she’s performing, she scats, rolls her shoulders, dances, and really engages in the music with honesty and passion,” says Riley. When he asked her how she reconciled those two extremes, Bazzle told him, “’ You have to allow yourself to become emotionally naked when you’re on the bandstand.’ When she said that, a light bulb went off in my head. I’m not a singer, but I just do what I do, and I have the audacity to be uninhibited.” The same can be said for Riley’s work behind the kit, where he leads his stellar band with infectious enthusiasm and bristling swing. His “Be There When I Get There” captures the anticipation and excitement of rushing to an eagerly awaited appointment, whether a romantic rendezvous, a gathering of friends, or a night of music. The brisk “Borders Without Lines” comes from the pen of Riley’s Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra bandmate Victor Goines, while the classic “You Don’t Know What Love Is” becomes a sultry simmer, highlighted by Harris’ mournful, muted trumpet. The title track is the rare Riley original composed in a major key, and its sunny disposition perfectly communicates his unflagging hopefulness. The lovely “Touched,” featuring Louis’ achingly lyrical alto, recalls a tender moment with the drummer’s mother before she passed away. “I was in her room in her last days, and she rubbed my head. I’m a grown man, but I felt like an innocent child. There’s a special love wrapped in the touch of a mother of every living creature. That special euphoria only comes from her.” The bittersweet “Wings and Roots” looks to the next generation, referring to Riley’s philosophy of raising children: “You have to root them in good values and fundamental characteristics, but once they get to be a certain age, you have to give them the wings to be free, to go out and be themselves.” Finally, “Stella By Starlight” is another nod to the American Songbook, taken at a graceful midtempo pace with Cohen’s deft touch over Riley’s sensitive brushwork. In the end, Riley hopes that the music of Perpetual Optimism helps spread the upbeat manifesto that he’s chosen to live by. “I always look forward, no matter what happens in life. If you’re grieving or faced with an emotional challenge, keep in mind: If you’re still breathing, there’s a chance that you can overcome and thrive. Commit yourself to PERPETUAL OPTIMISM!”

events.title: Embodiment Practice: Mindful Movement + Stillness with Suzanne (Zan) Beahrs
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest.

Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. 

Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. 

Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. 

Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space.

Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like.

About Suzanne (Zan):
With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. events.title: Somatic Healing 101: The Missing Link to Lasting Change
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
A somatic workshop to understand your nervous system, reconnect with your body, and learn practical tools for real transformation...
Have you ever known exactly what you "should" do, but still found yourself stuck in the same patterns?
Maybe you've read the books, listened to the podcasts, journaled, reflected, and tried to think your way into change. Yet anxiety, overwhelm, self-sabotage, emotional reactivity, procrastination, or feeling disconnected from yourself keep showing up.
That's because lasting transformation doesn't happen through the mind alone. It happens through the body.
In this immersive workshop, you'll learn the foundations of somatic healing and nervous system regulation, and why working with your body is often the missing piece when it comes to creating meaningful, sustainable change.
We'll explore how stress, emotions, beliefs, and protective patterns are stored in the body, and why healing becomes more effective when we include the nervous system in the process.
You'll learn:
What somatics actually is (and why it's becoming more popular)
Why mindset work alone isn't enough to create real, lasting change
How your nervous system influences your emotions, behaviors, and daily experiences
Simple somatic tools you can use to feel more grounded, present, and connected
How to work with your body instead of constantly trying to push through or override it
This workshop isn't just educational — you'll also experience somatics firsthand through guided practices, including breathwork, body awareness, grounding exercises, mindful movement, and embodiment practices designed to help you reconnect with yourself and your body's wisdom.
You'll leave with:
A clear understanding of what somatic healing is and how it works
Practical tools you can immediately integrate into daily life to finally feel more calm and present
Greater awareness of your nervous system and stress responses
Simple ways to deepen your connection to your body, emotions, and intuition
A new approach to personal growth that feels supportive, sustainable, and effective

Whether you're completely new to somatics or looking to deepen your understanding of holistic healing, this workshop will give you a strong foundation and simple practices you can return to anytime!
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.

Podcast: RADIANT YOU (available on all podcast platforms)
Website: www.annabolender.com

events.title: Illah Nourbakhsh - Crunch Time
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: As workers and as parents, we all care deeply about how we must prepare ourselves and our children for fulfilling careers at a time when the changing nature of labor is opaque. In this interactive book talk, co-author Illah Nourbakhsh will share brief remarks regarding our voyage in researching and writing a book about careers, AI and the future of education. We will be joined by two special pioneers who will make brief remarks from the audience: Alan Eustace and Professor Michael Genesereth. Alan Eustace served as senior vice president at Google and has witnessed the digital and AI technology revolutions firsthand. Michael Genesereth is faculty at Stanford University and charted the course of artificial intelligence research as one of its founding scholars. Both Alan and Michael care deeply about the next generation, and the ways in which careers will evolve as AI changes the shape of work. We look forward to a dynamic conversation with the audience. Featuring curated essays from leaders in tech and education, Crunch Time empowers parents, educators, students, and professionals to get informed and access their agency in the AI age. The AI revolution is underway, and none of us are fully prepared. In Crunch Time , education and AI experts Illah Nourbakhsh and Michael Druckman confront one of the central questions of our time: How will artificial intelligence reshape careers, education, and opportunity, and what should we do about it now? Rather than predicting a single future, Crunch Time presents AI as a dynamic, uncertain force that demands informed participation. Originally conceived for educators and parents, the book expands its lens to include students, alumni, mid-career professionals, employers, policymakers, and anyone navigating work and learning in the age of AI. Crunch Time weaves together perspectives from AI inventors, business leaders, educators, technologists, and community leaders, featuring more than forty contributors including AI experts Daniela Rus, Hoda Heidari, Michael Genesereth, Sanjay Sarma, university presidents Nancy Cantor, Lisa Ryerson, Laura Walker, Juan Salgado; business leaders David Siegel, Steve Malony, Dan Draper; visionaries Dame Diane Coyle, William Haseltine, Paul LeBlanc; and leading K to 12 educators. Readers will encounter competing viewpoints, practical guidance, and concrete steps for action. Crunch Time is an invitation to understand, to prepare, and to actively shape a more equitable and human-centered AI future. This timely and empowering book is essential reading for students, parents, educators and leaders who wish to shape an AI future that expands opportunity and strengthens our shared humanity. — Farnam Jahanian, President, Carnegie Mellon University For a book about artificial intelligence, this is brimming with human intelligence. You'll find thoughtful, nuanced, and provocative strategies for growing up and thriving in the age of AI. This book challenges us to redesign the connection between education and employment with intention and courage. This is a powerful call to ensure the AI age expands opportunity and strengthens pathways to meaningful work for all. — Lisa Marsh Ryerson, President, Southern New Hampshire University Our youth are growing up in the middle of a massive transition into the age of AI. Smart guides are critical to navigating this rough terrain, and this book is one of those guides. It elevates the power of human intellect and creativity, providing much-needed guidance on how to harness new technologies for the good of society and humanity. — Lisa Guernsey, Senior Director of Birth-12th Grade Policy, New America Illah R. Nourbakhsh is Kavcic-Moura Professor of Robotics at Carnegie Mellon University, inaugural Executive Director of the Center for Shared Prosperity, and co-director of the Community Robotics, Education and Technology Empowerment Lab. He was the Inaugural K&L Gates Professor of Ethics and Computational Technologies. He obtained his PhD in Computer Science from Stanford University. In 2009 the National Academy of Sciences named him a Kavli Fellow. In 2013 he was inducted into the June Harless West Virginia Hall of Fame. He was previously Robotics Group Lead for NASA/Ames. In 2019 he was named a Hastings Fellow. He has co-authored textbooks and popular literature, including Turn Left , AI and Humanity , Robot Futures , and Parenting for Technology Futures . He has authored articles for The New Yorker and Foreign Affairs, in addition to academic journals and book chapters. He is a trustee of the Claude Worthington Benedum Foundation, Winchester Thurston School and the Southwestern Pennsylvania Environmental Health Project. Michael Druckman (not appearing) is the Executive Chairman and architect of Schools That Can, a national not-for-profit network of urban K to12 schools since 2006 that prepares historically marginalized youth for post-secondary success. He currently is a Fellow of the Leadership and Society Initiative at the University of Chicago. Michael established the “Senator Robert F. Kennedy Education Awards” in partnership with Robert and Ethel Kennedy Human Rights in 2014 to recognize K to 12 school leaders, teachers and students for moral courage and the “Schools That Can Leaders That Can Awards” in 2017 to recognize leaders giving back to our society’s well-being in service of our youth. Both recognitions remain active. Michael chaired the Trey Whitfield School board in East New York, Brooklyn for many years, served on the Portal Learning board in Los Angeles, acted as an advisor to many K-12 schools over the last twenty years and was recognized as Founding Chairman Emeritus of the NYU Center for Global Affairs where he served as Co-Chairman for fourteen years. events.title: Kate Doerge with Myra Sack - Reimagining Grief
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: An inspiring guide that reimagines the stages of grief into five healing actions, Reimagining Grief offers light and a new way forward in the midst of darkness. This is the book Kate wishes she'd had, and she wrote it for you. Kate will be joined in conversation by Myra Sacks, the author of award-winning memoir, " Fifty-Seven Fridays: Losing Our Daughter Finding Our Way ," and founder of E-Motion, Inc. There is no way to spin grief. It's hard. It's messy. It's destabilizing. And every single one of us has to go through it. Author and grief coach Kate Doerge knows this too well. Over six years, she lost her father to heart failure and her mother in a car accident five days before Christmas. She also faced the hardest challenge for any parent, losing her sixteen-year-old daughter, Penny, to complications from a rare genetic condition. After Penny's death, Kate knew she had a choice, she could lose herself to a grief so powerful she might not come back from it—or she could find another way through. Reimagining Grief is the result of that search. Drawing from her own experience, the latest research, and conversations with others who have faced devastating loss, Kate offers five actions that can help ground you when you feel out of control, lift you when you're depleted, and help you process the pain of loss. In this book, you'll learn: Why There Isn’t One Right Way to Grieve — and How to Find Your Own Path An Approach to Saying Goodbye That Honors Both You and Your Loved One The 5 Actions Through Grief — and How to Use Them to Heal What Post-Traumatic Growth Really Looks Like How to Find Joy Again Turning Pain into Purpose These actions won’t make grief vanish or disappear; everyone has to go through the difficult path that you are put on after losing someone you loved deeply. However, Reimagining Grief offers some light and healing in the midst of darkness and a different way forward. This is the book Kate wishes she'd had. She wrote it for you. Kate Doerge is a USA TODAY bestselling author, motivational speaker, certified grief coach, and founder of Penny’s Flight Foundation. Through heartfelt storytelling, research-backed insights, and practical strategies, Kate inspires audiences to navigate change, embrace resilience, and lead lives filled with greater purpose and connection. Myra Sack is the author of award-winning memoir, " Fifty-Seven Fridays: Losing Our Daughter Finding Our Way ," and founder of E-Motion, Inc. a nonprofit organization created to support community, movement and ritual to enhance coping and resilience. Myra's life changed when her older daughter, Havi, died in January 2021. Blending Myra's lived experience and knowledge as a certified Compassionate Bereavement Care provider with her lifelong identity as an athlete and career in social impact, E-Motion evolved out of a new way of living with the most difficult reality. Myra holds an MBA in Social Impact from Boston University, and graduated with a B.A. cum laude from Dartmouth College, where she captained the women's soccer team and earned All-America honors. Myra serves on the Board of the Courageous Parents Network. events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

Johnson’s All Boys Aren’t Blue, their bestselling, critically acclaimed YA “memoir-manifesto” about growing up Black and queer, has been, since its 2020 publication, a source of solace and support for young people. It’s also consistently been at or near the top of the ALA and PEN America’s lists of the most challenged and banned books. events.title: Matt O'Hara's "THE FLYING DEATH"
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Matt shares his dramatic tale of gentlemen-explorers of the 1930s racing to find and harvest a poisonous Amazon vine. Join us at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore on Thursday, November 12 at 7:00 PM when Matt O'Hara comes to the store to present his new book The Flying Death: Poison, Plunder, and the Quest for a Miracle Medicine in the Amazon . Matt will be joined by Rebecca Herman for the conversation and will sign copies of his book after the presentation. In the fall of 1938, a young, frail American explorer set off down a river in the western Amazon in search of curare, a poison he thought might save his life. Richard Gill had learned that local tribes used curare-laced blow darts to kill animals, but it was also potentially a cure for many ailments, including his own. He also thought he could make a fortune by connecting the knowledge of two worlds. Obsessed with curare, he raced to make deals with Indigenous poison masters in the Amazon and pharmaceutical companies back home, even as his Russian-born rival Boris Krukoff sought to do the same. In The Flying Death , the historian Matt O'Hara asks who and what we are willing to sacrifice in the name of discovery and profit. O'Hara brings to life Gill's epic quest, a stranger-than-fiction true story that moves from unexplored territory in the Amazon to rogue medical trials and cutthroat corporate boardrooms in the United States. Navigating treacherous terrain and politics, Gill and Krukoff successfully created a veritable curare–industrial complex, as the plant became a key element in shock therapy, transformed surgery in the United States and across the globe, and eventually led to a Nobel Prize. The Flying Death offers a thrilling ride across Indigenous knowledge, scientific exploration, and exploitation, unearthing a story of discovery that poses searching questions about the price of progress, who pays it, and who gets credit. MATT O'HARA is a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Cruz. He is the award-winning author of many journal articles and two books, The History of the Future in Colonial Mexico and A Flock Divided: Race, Religion, and Politics in Mexico, 1749–1857. REBECCA HERMAN is Associate Professor of History at UC Berkeley, where she teaches about environmental politics, US-Latin American relations, and modern Latin America. She is the author of Cooperating with the Colossus: A Social and Political History of US Military Bases in World War II Latin America and is currently at work on a book about anti-extractivism in Antarctica. events.title: JACKIEM JOYNER
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Contemporary saxophonist, author, and music producer Jackiem Joyner is set to release his 7th album, Touch, worldwide this fall, 2019. After more than 12 years as a recording artist, Jackiem continues to stand out with electrifying live performances and brilliant music productions. As a performer, he has toured over 30 countries and performed with the likes of the late George Duke, Marcus Miller, Keiko Matsui, Donnie McClurkin, Angela Bofill, Najee, Kirk Whalum, Peter White, and many, many more. Joyner’s radio success is widely known within the industry. Joyner has two number-one hit songs, five top 10 Billboard singles, and a number-one debut album under his belt. In addition, he published the highly acclaimed science fiction novel Zarya , which received high praise and a five-star rating on Amazon. “This album is about romance,” Joyner explains of Touch . “I wanted to give everyone something hip, smooth, and sexy at the same time.” The record has an urban feel, laced with the hottest downtempo vibes. The album shares similar textures to the music of artists Tank and Trey Songz. Joyner’s soprano sax leads the charge through most of the album. “My approach to performing on this record was to be melodic and dynamic with my horn”. Peter White joins Jackiem on the first single, “Last Dance”. The combination of soprano sax and nylon guitar pulls you in with its romantic and catchy melody. Najee serves up the flute on a dreamy urban song called “Fairytales”. The unique mix of flute and soprano sax on this vibey tune forms one of Joyner’s best performances and productions. The song was written together with Tim Bailey, aka Twizzboy. Born to a Vietnam War veteran father and a dedicated mother in Norfolk, VA, growing up wasn’t easy for Jackiem. He set his sights high from a young age; he always dreamed of being a performing artist, as unlikely as it was, given his humble upbringing. Even as a child, he loved the attention he received from his family when he danced to Michael Jackson songs. Now, Jackiem is proud to stand front and center on the main stage most weekends around the country. A quick glance at Joyner’s track record makes it clear that he continues to beat the odds in a tough and competitive music industry. “I love what I do, and I have passion”, Jackiem says. “I don’t care how hard things get, it’ll never stop me from doing what I love: playing the sax, writing music and stories, and performing live.” His love of writing novels came as a surprise to many of his fans. “I’m very excited to release my second novel soon after my album release,” Joyner says. “Writing stories is now a big part of my creative journey.” The first single from Joyner’s last album, Main Street Beat (2017), was named for his daughter, Trinity. Joyner’s adoration for his little girl is clearly expressed through the live, pop-influenced song, driven by Steve Oliver’s guitar. The song was an instant hit. Reaching no. 2 on the Billboard. We’re all dying to see if she follows in dad’s footsteps with her own stage career someday! With the creation of his company, JOYNER MEDIA COMPANY L.L.C., Joyner hopes to inspire other creators to follow their dreams and realize their true potential in art and multimedia. When Jackiem is not touring the world, he spends time giving lectures to students across the country. He also enjoys talking to band classes, helping them with practice, and offering insight on how to pursue a career in the performing arts. Currently, Joyner is on a US tour in support of his new album, Touch . He will be touring Los Angeles, CA – Washington, DC – Hampton, VA – Melbourne, FL – Detroit, MI – Chicago, IL – Charleston, SC – Houston, TX – Rehoboth Beach, DE – Mazlatan, Mexico – Syracuse, NY – Tampa, FL – Atlanta, GA, and many more cities.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: School Fair, goldenstar, Poor Image (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: School Fair School Fair (Findlay Buchanan, Semisi Ma’ia’i, Hamish Morgan, De Stevens and Rose Pickernell) make music embedded in the human experience. It’s a product of the band’s native New Zealand, a place that remains intimate and remote, where emotion is magnified over both distance and familiarity. The five band members began the project renting out a factory-sized, sub-zero degree Celsius room normally operated by construction workers in the industrial area of Ōtepoti, Dunedin, New Zealand in 2021, recording music on the 4-track tape recorder that would become debut Gorse on a Hill . The album remained the only trace of the band online for a few years, an artifact for those who know where to look. School Fair’s music has this sense of self-discovery when you find it, a sound that feels both recognizable and like the vacant expanse of a country whirring by on a train. Still with little to no self-promotion, the appearance of sophomore effort Bird the Kid online in early 2025 was a new portal to their world of melodic and intricate indie music that retains a kind of atmospheric beauty. Unexpected Violence (Mutual, 2026) is the first record made between geographical places, with the band now split in between London and New Zealand. You can hear this fragmented approach in the patchwork quality and inherent connective tissue of the album. Recorded initially in a studio in East London, it was the first time the band brought in an outside engineer (Syd Kemp?), as opposed to the band’s prior live recordings, where the tendency was to “feed back off each other in quite a messy abstract and complicated way that works for us but isn’t typically structured.” The band then took these recordings and evolved them back home in Dunedin, with the addition of vocals on some tracks by Pickernell adding to the cohesive energy and collective, dialed-in synergy of the quintet. School Fair is built upon the many eclectic mediums from which the band members individually create: time spent repairing old machines, making short films, metalworking and jewelry-making, writing and engineering. All these counterparts bring a kind of industrial electricity to the music where each part feels necessary and agile, as well as perfectly in conjunction. It’s these points beneath the surface where the songs really bloom. The moody transference of guitar lick to guttural vocal and back again, where melody conjoins with surprising inflection and sharp-hued ambiance, littered with both poetic spoken-word and a self-referentiality of clues and repetition that rewards close listening yet remains accessible and immediate. Transportive lyrics shine with the lore and mythology of a world that is both deeply specific and transcendent in its curiosity toward the surrounding environment. Unexpected Violence is filled with resounding descriptors: from “cat runs blind in the smoke / birds slap their wings away / trees thrash and crash / each lonely in their chosen way” (the meandering “Angelika”) or the consequently spellbinding phrasing of “come out to your dead animal river gushing hard / come out to your heart split open and lit up with stars” of “In Boredom You Shoot Your Gun”. It’s a starkly poetic snapshot into the band’s own universe and a showcase in the thoroughfare of language, where the specificity of one person’s memory counteracts with a landscape that blurs and unravels with the passage of time. Unexpected Violence a record that could only be made in a place like New Zealand, yet its vantage point expands far beyond to the vast unwieldiness of human sentiment. “There’s a sense of remoteness to the record, both emotionally but also in the sense of place, broken farms, cast iron beaches, blank midday fires, lost friends.” Or as the band recites in the austere glimmer of “Spirally Staircase Memory”: “memories are just stories that can’t be found.” But School Fair reaches some sort of access point, a way for them to live on. The name Unexpected Violence was born out of Buchanan and Ma’ia’i coming across the genre title in a bookstore in Berlin, and is a fitting discernment of the heartbreak that often comes with the realities of existence. In album highlight “Gussied Up,” the band intones: “I never never never ever / wanna hear you / see you, feel you or touch you.” It’s a harsh statement that feels swept up in the parallel admission that these are relationships you may never fully escape; they have left their mark. We still pass the places they inhabit, and feel the uncanny emptiness even after moving on. It’s fitting that the record ends on a similar contradiction. Just discernable above spirals of drummed up, ambient noise: “I miss you now you’re gone.” For all things can be true at once. Bandcamp | IG goldenstar Montreal’s goldenstar operate within a distinctly fraught strain of the North American musical canon, dancing in (and emerging from) the shadow of beloved forebears like Duster, Sonic Youth, and Sparklehorse. Their self-released 2025 debut EP alongside a sophomore release on OST have established the band as an essential voice on the contemporary slowcore-noise rock continuum. Bandcamp | IG Poor Image Poor Image is a 7 piece emo/americana tinged slowcore band based in the Bay Area. The project came to fruition when members Reid Devereaux, Nick Ferguson, Keenan Lewis, Declan Lewis, Patrick Madden, Tammer Bagdasarian and Nick Ross, who spent their formative years between Silicon Valley, San Francisco, and San Jose participating in the broader bay area music scene, decided to join forces. Poor Image’s recent debut self titled album out on American Death Records is about coming of age strife and trying to “make it” in the age of supersaturation. As written by Nina Protocol, Poor Image’s debut album “...refers back to a micro-glory age of low-stakes indie music in a way that could only come from a band a few generations removed from the source material. It finds a perfect balance between slowcore and Americana; it incorporates a variety of roots-leaning instrumental flourishes when it needs to; it rocks when it needs to”. Featured on Perfectly Imperfect as ones to watch, Poor Image has recently come off national tours opening for Horse Vision & Dutch Interior and are currently recording their second album. events.title: Wisdom Healing Qigong with Hiromi Vardy
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Experience the deep benefits of Zhineng (Wisdom Healing) Qigong. This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Through simple, time-honored movements, the nervous system unwinds, the mind becomes more spacious, and the heart opens. Over time, practitioners often feel more resilient, centered, and connected — both inwardly and outwardly.

Tickets are sliding scale $10-$25 - Please arrive at least 5-10 minutes early.

 Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back 

Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts.

While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga.

After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today.

Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

events.title: Henry J. Evans - Bombs, Bacon, and Bankruptcy
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Crisis leadership can be the toughest type of leadership—and the most crucial to master. Whether the stakes are literally life-and-death or just feel that way, this is the essential guide to keeping your team at their best when things are at their worst. Successfully navigating a crisis doesn’t require an innate talent for high-pressure situations. It requires understanding why we act the way we do when business as usual is disrupted—and how to stay calm, think clearly, and execute on the right priorities. Henry J. Evans has spent decades studying, practicing, and coaching other leaders through crises. He’s seen firsthand that whether a crisis is as deadly as roadside bombs during counterterrorism operations, as frustrating as bacon shortages during a pandemic, or as stressful as a family business on the edge of bankruptcy, the strategic, interpersonal, and emotional challenges are the same. Drawing on psychology, brain science, vivid true stories, and proven tools and tactics, Evans shows readers how to: Juggle the demands of today’s crisis without dropping the ball on tomorrow’s priorities. Decide when to trust data and AI and when to trust their gut instincts. Hold people accountable without destroying their sense of Emotional Safety.® Take care of the team’s needs without sacrificing the leader’s well-being. This is an invaluable guide for entrepreneurs, corporate leaders, and anyone trying to guide a team through tough times. It includes practical tools for honing your resilience, reaction times, listening and communication skills, threat assessment, emotional regulation, and more. Henry J. Evans is the founder and CEO of Dynamic Results, a strategy and culture transformation firm. While building a global leadership firm, Evans concurrently spent more than 20 years in counterterrorism and national security under four U.S. presidential administrations, holding a Top Secret security clearance. He has logged more than 16,000 hours of executive coaching and 6,000 hours of strategic planning facilitation with leaders across more than 80 countries. A sought-after keynote speaker and international MBA instructor, Evans is the bestselling author of Winning with Accountability and co-author of Step Up . He lives in San Francisco. Henry J. Evans - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Ferry Building store. events.title: Devon Halliday with Daniel Gumbiner - To Stay, To Stay, To Stay
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “ To Stay, To Stay, To Stay is about the great contradiction of love, that it brings both great bafflement and great clarity, and somehow, ultimately, isn’t a contradiction. So much hard-earned daily wisdom here. I needed this book. You probably do too.”—Peter Orner, author of The Gossip Columnist’s Daughter Devon will be joined in conversation by Daniel Gumbiner, the author of Fire in the Canyon. An ensemble cast collides and crosses paths in their small corner of the Midwest where no one is a stranger: the baker, the realtor, the poet, the gardener, the frustrated artist. In Devon Halliday’s transcendent debut novel, secrets turn contagious, impulses transform into resolutions, and no one is certain whether they will remain in the confines of their Appalachian college town or step out into the unknown. Surrounded by hills, buried in green, Eden is a forgotten town full of ordinary lives. But over the course of a humid summer week, seven of these ordinary lives reach their boiling point, as the existential questions of each begin to urgently entwine. Underneath the threat of marital infidelity, financial ruin, and life-changing illness is always the same question: To stay, or to go? If you choose to stay, is it ever a permanent choice? Can you be sure you’ll choose it again tomorrow? A mosaic portrait of love and its close substitutes, the novel suggests, fearfully, that even our best decisions might be fragile, arbitrary, and impermanent. “This brims with insights into the human condition.”— Publishers Weekly “A heartfelt debut … Halliday offers varied, honest looks at the intimate struggles that accompany life’s unexpected turning points.”— Booklist “Devon Halliday has such a mastery of language and storytelling artistry that it’s hard to believe To Stay, To Stay, To Stay is her debut. This novel, a wry and incisive exploration of how people behave (and misbehave) at the critical inflection points in their lives, is a marvel.”—Marisa Silver, author of At Last “In this enchanting tale of small-town love, artisanal bread, and sketchy real estate, Devon Halliday explores the webs that connect us and the mysterious forces that break those webs apart. Everything and everyone in this wonderful novel is rendered with precision, wit, and uncompromising humanity.”—David Haynes, author of Martha’s Daughter “With rare emotional precision and a fierce, glowing heart, Devon Halliday investigates the stories people tell themselves about love and the combustible, constant anxieties that sustain those stories. This marvelous debut novel wisely asks an urgent, contemporary question: What’s braver? Blowing up your life? Or simply living it, however it unfolds?”—Dean Bakopoulos, author of Summerlong “What a delightful debut novel by Devon Halliday—its pages full of sun and shadow, love and gravity. To Stay, To Stay, To Stay handles its cast of characters with deftness and grace, showing us the many facets of people in a small town as they connect and disconnect from one another.”—Alix Ohlin, author of Dual Citizens “A preternaturally wise and wickedly ambitious debut. Halliday’s small town and big cast of characters cast a spell under which I would happily have stayed, stayed, stayed. Alas, the ending is perfection, too.”—Anna Solomon, author of The Book of V Devon Halliday is a Pushcart Prize winner and a Rona Jaffe Foundation Graduate Fellow. Her writing appears in Ploughshares , One Story , the Los Angeles Review of Books , and Lit Hub , among other journals. Her debut novel To Stay, To Stay, To Stay has been longlisted for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize. Daniel Gumbiner’s first novel, The Boatbuilder (2018), was a nominee for the National Book Award and a finalist for the California Book Award. His second book, Fire in the Canyon (2023), was a finalist for the California Book Award and a New Yorker Best Book of the Year. He is the Editor of The Believer and lives in San Francisco. As a high schooler, he worked as a barista at the Book Passage Cafe in Corte Madera. events.title: Janet Thornburg's COGNITIVE DIVINE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) You think it’s hard to herd cats? Try getting seven sub-personalities to agree on anything! Wild Child, Rosie, and Mauve love living in San Francisco, but Raisin and Hannah want to go back to Colorado. When Cora soothes Raisin with cinnamon rolls, Hannah complains that sugar is bad for us. Hannah and Wild Child lock horns over Wild Child’s party behavior. Rosie wants to go shopping for clothes and skin-care products, but Mauve wants to spend the money on writers’ conferences and research for her novel. The conflicts never end, and the arguments create quite a din. All seven of Janet’s sub-personalities are delighted to have this opportunity to give their opinions of Janet’s life choices! Janet Thornburg (writer/performer) is a soloist whose solo show Cognitive Divine won the Best Full-Length Comedy award in the In Front of Your Eyes Festival 2026 at the Marsh. She has written and performed eight solo shows in San Francisco at venues including The Marsh, StageWerx Theatre, Theatre Rhinoceros, Theatre of Yugen, Venue Nine, Next Stage Theatre,Young Performers’ Theatre, and the Solo Mio Festival. Her multi-character play Dinner Roles was presented at the San Francisco Repertory Theatre, and her play Antony and Cleopatra Meet Godzilla enjoyed two runs at the Intersection Theatre. She holds an MFA in playwriting from San Francisco State University and an MFA in fiction from Warren Wilson College. events.title: KRS-ONE
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Rapper, social activist, and hip-hop pioneer from the Bronx, known as "The Teacha" · Appearing on the rap scene in 1986 as Boogie Down Productions, releasing his first hit single “South Bronx” with his late DJ Scott La Rock, KRS “the one” made it clear that Hip Hop was going to have to take itself a lot more seriously than simply being a music genre. KRS, an acronym for “Knowledge Reigning Supreme”, has been called the “conscience of Hip Hop” (Rolling Stone), “the greatest live emcee ever” (The Source), the “spokesperson for Hip Hop” (Wall Street Journal), “master teacher” (Zulu Nation) and the “son of Hip Hop” (Kool DJ Herc). With 20 published albums to his credit and his numerous appearances with other artists, KRS-One is believed to have written the most rhymes in Hip Hop’s history. In the 1990s, as “hip-hop” grew more and more commercialized and corporate, it was KRS-One that openly rejected such cultural exploitation and materialism, grounding Hip Hop in its original principles of peace, love, unity, and safely having fun. Teaching everything from self-creation to stopping violence; from vegetarianism to transcendental meditation, from the establishment of Hip Hop Appreciation Week (every third week in May), to establishing Hip Hop as an international culture at the United Nations (2001), KRS-One has single-handedly held the history and original arts of Hip Hop together now for over two decades. In addition to lecturing at over 500 universities in the United States and publishing three ground-breaking books; “The Science of Rap” (1995), “Ruminations” (2003), and the Gospel of Hip Hop” (2009), KRS-One has also established the Stop The Violence Movement (1989), influenced the creation of the “West-Coast All-Stars’ anti-gang anthem “We’re All In The Same Gang” (1990), warned the Hip Hop community against giving up their humanity for technological advancement (H. E. A. L.—Human Education Against Lies-1991), and has established the Temple of Hip Hop for the spiritual exploration of Hip Hop’s culture (1996). It was KRS-One who first argued that “rap is something we do; Hip Hop is something we live” and introduced the “I am Hip Hop” philosophy in 1994, which Black Entertainment Television uses as the title of their Hip Hop Lifetime Achievement Award today. Without question, KRS-One has been the loudest voice for the actual preservation and expansion of original Hip Hop worldwide. When he is not touring or lecturing, on his so-called “down-time”, KRS-One continues to share his unique knowledge of Hip Hop to younger audiences eager to hear the ‘teacha’ speak. Operating as a kind of “pop-up” school, KRS-One’s Temple of Hip Hop has appeared in various cities in the USA and also in the UK and Europe, offering the more serious student of Hip Hop an effective way to live and understand the culture of Hip Hop more deeply.

events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.title: Writing Picture Books: The Rules (and How to Break Them) with Monica Wesolowska
events.location: Online via Zoom
events.description: How hard can it be to write for children? As it turns out, children’s picture book writing has rules that can be challenging. Fortunately, constraint can actually foster creativity. (Look at what Dr. Seuss did. When asked to write a book using 100 simple words, he found “cat” and “hat” and wrote The Cat in the Hat . And with that subversive book, he transformed reading for generations of children!) In this class, you will learn some of the rules for writing a picture book for publication today. You will also be encouraged to play around with those rules, unleashing your own unique creativity. The class will cover: A brief history of picture book writing The expectations of the publishing world today Craft elements including characterization, point of view, and plot Writing exercises to practice what you learn A chance to share what you are working on This class can be followed by Monica’s four-week class, Writing Picture Books: Drafting and Deepening. Details coming soon. * Note that for all classes held on Zoom, registration closes one day before the class begins. Same-day registrations are not available, so please plan ahead. Meet Your Instructor Monica Wesolowska writes for both adults and children. Her most recent picture book Elbert in the Air (illustrated by Jerome Pumphrey) was named a “Best Children’s Book of the Year” by the Bank Street College of Education. Her debut picture book Leo + Lea (illustrated by Kenard Pak) won an SCBWI Crystal Kite Award. She’s published widely for adults, including the memoir Holding Silvan: A Brief Life which was named a “Best Book of the Year” by The Boston Globe and Library Journal. For over two decades, Monica has taught creative writing around the Bay Area and she works one-on-one with clients as an independent editor.

events.title: You Aren't Alone Creative Relief Mini-Retreat
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Join the You Aren't Alone Project for a one day Creative Relief Retreat designed for people of all backgrounds to engage in creative expression exercises and discussions as a tool for mental health, self-care, support and solace in a safe and collaborative environment.
Spend the afternoon with us exploring how creativity and mental health intersect to support your overall wellbeing. We'll start with a meditation and movement exercise, then hear from guest artists and mental health and wellness practitioners, and wrap up with a creative mental health workshop for tangible tools you can take with you and use in your daily life.
You do not have to be a practicing artist to attend. We just ask that you come with a creative mindset and an openness to the healing power of art and connection.
The You Aren’t Alone Project is a nonprofit organization dedicated to facilitating & changing conversations around mental health so that no one ever has to feel alone.
We offer community programming, events, and resources that bring people together over shared creative journeys to foster holistic connections and we aim to do it all at a very low to no cost.
By tapping into the power of art and storytelling, we create safe, supportive, and inclusive spaces that encourage positive mental health & wellbeing.
From the founder: While healing is a continuous journey and I am far from done, I have spent the last 10 years building spaces and collecting the tools that I wish I had when I was younger. Through that process, I obtained my Masters in Mental Health Counseling and have used that training to grow YAAP. The project started in Louisiana and I am excited to bring our programs to San Francisco and beyond. I hope you'll join for the first in what we hope to be regularly scheduled gatherings.

events.title: The Wisdom of the Odyssey with Phil Cousineau
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “As you set out for Ithaka, / hope your road is a long one, /full of adventure, full of discovery.” —Constantine Cavafy, “Ithaka” Spurred by the summer release of Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster film version of The Odyssey , Homer has never been “hotter,” and The Odyssey has never been more relevant. How can a 3,000-year-old story still matter so much to people around the globe, and at the same time be culturally combustible? Where is the wisdom in this endlessly protean tale? Join us to explore the soulful thread of themes in Phil Cousineau's new book, The Wisdom of the Odyssey . The class will explore: the meaning of home the role of mentors and muses in our lives the loss of soul at war, the need to heal from trauma the redemptive power of love The daylong class and journey into ancient Greece will include film clips, mythic images, vibrant discussions, and a Greek-inspired lunch included in the cost of the class. Recommended reading: The Wisdom of the Odyssey by Phil Cousineau Richard Lattimore’s glorious translation of Homer’s epic , or the translation of your choice Recommended viewing: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Meet Your Instructor Phil Cousineau is a freelance writer, filmmaker, independent scholar, and writing consultant, who has led mythological tours to Greece for over thirty years. He has published over forty books, including the international best-seller The Hero’s Journey: Joseph Campbell on His Life and Work, The Art of Pilgrimage, Once and Future Myths, The Blue Museum, The Lost Notebooks of Sisyphus, Who Stole the Arms of the Venus de Milo? and most recently The Wisdom of the Odyssey. Cousineau also has over forty film and television credits, and has been a commentator on “Myth in the Movies” for myriad movie studios, including Warner Brothers, Pixar, Lucas Films, Twentieth-Century Fox, and the Smithsonian and Discovery Channels. What students are saying about Phil: "Loved it! Phil is fun, informative and entertaining. He clearly loved his topic and that is infectious. And the food was excellent!" Lesley H. "(I enjoyed) Phil's depth and breadth of knowledge, compassion and patience. (His) interest and HIGH and DEEP scholarship level kept (my) attention and curiosity...FABULOUS job with the food!" Grace R. "We loved Phil, his personality, his delivery, his vast knowledge, and his immense excitement about the topic...There was a vibrant discussion. Phil's use of classical paintings of the Odyssey was lovely. Phil's points were resonant, profound, sometimes funny - always entertaining. " Ben L. "Phil Cousineau is a unique mind with vast experience and enthusiasms. (The class was) above and beyond with food, scale and quality of presentation and engagement." John C.

events.title: Devendra Banhart - Four Nose Jobs a Day
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Join us at the Ferry Building for a meet-and-greet celebration of Venezuelan-American singer-songwriter and visual artist Devendra Banhart. Like his music and visual art, Banhart’s poetry converges at the intersection of humor and sorrow. In his second collection, Four Nose Jobs A Day , he explores the heart and soul through a lens that is both slyly absurdist and deeply compassionate. "Banhart approaches somber themes with whimsy... his work expounds on a crucial tenet of queerness: liberation in lightness and in unabashed optimism. Funny and enduringly weird. " — PITCHFORK Like Devendra Banhart’s music and visual art, his poetry appears at the convergence of humor and sorrow, tragedy and joy. With Four Nose Jobs A Day , Banhart’s second collection, the poet explores matters of the heart and soul through an absurdist lens both sly and compassionate. As the opening lines of the collection alert us, Banhart loves “a Love Poem/One that reads/Like Blackberries/On a wooden cup”. With iconoclastic verve, Banhart builds small, often silly paths of poetic language that lead to meaningful conclusions: “Poetry is when/the dead end/Starts to go somewhere” Like professional musicians constantly on tour, Banhart reminds us that we, the readers, have countless places to visit both in the world around us, and inside ourselves—whether these places resonate and register is up to us, not the places. The poems of Four Nose Jobs A Day break the surface of reality, small bubbles of insight. Sometimes there is laughter in the face of absurdity; consolation for grief or despair; and sometimes there is simply gratitude. “What an Honor,” the poet reminds us, “To have emotions/Any of them.” **** Devendra Banhart is a Venezuelan-American singer-songwriter and visual artist. His drawings have been exhibited, among others, at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, the Centre for Fine Arts in Brussels, and Los Angeles’ Museum of Contemporary Art. He has released over ten albums and has performed at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Bonnaroo, and Coachella. This is one of many books he has published. He lives in Los Angeles. events.title: Isabel Allende - Perla and the Princess/Perla y la Princesa
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: In the third children's book written by critically acclaimed, New York Times- bestselling superstar Isabel Allende, Perla, the mighty dog, saves her human brother, Nico Rico, after he and his friend, a little girl dressed as a princess, get lost during a Cinco de Mayo party. Perla is a mighty dog who has two superpowers—making people love her and roaring like a lion. When her human brother, Nico Rico, gets into trouble with a girl he refers to as “the princess” while the neighborhood is out celebrating Cinco de Mayo, Perla knows it’s up to her to save them both. But how will she do it? In this charming and poignant story, Isabel Allende continues her series about the bond between a child and a beloved pet. En la edición en español del tercer libro infantil de Isabel Allende, autora aclamada por la crítica mundialmente y bestseller del New York Times , Perla, la súper perrita, salva a su hermano humano, Nico Rico, y a su amiga, la Princesa, cuando los dos se meten en problemas. Perla es una súper perrita que tiene dos súper poderes: hacer que todos la amen y rugir como un león. Cuando su hermano humano, Nico Rico, se mete en problemas junto a una niña a la que él llama la Princesa, mientras el vecindario celebra el Cinco de Mayo, Perla sabe que le toca a ella salvarlos a los dos. Pero ¿cómo lo logrará? En esta historia encantadora y emocionante, Isabel Allende continúa su serie sobre el vínculo entre un niño y su querida mascota. "Allende has created an appealingly wry, confiding, and easygoing storyteller in Perla. Rodríguez’s watercolor and ink illustrations . . . doesn’t lack for festive colors or community spirit. Good dog—and good book." — Kirkus Reviews "Allende’s English and Spanish versions individually sparkle with wit, charm, and an engaging tone, and . . . Rodríguez’s use of ink and watercolor imbues the cartoonish characters with warmth and expressiveness, and the distinct personalities of the humans and the little pup make the world feel full, rich with possibilities." — The Bulletin of the Center for Children's Books Isabel Allende , born in Peru and raised in Chile, is a novelist, feminist, and philanthropist, and one of the most widely read authors in the world, having sold more than eighty million copies of her books across forty-two languages. In addition to her work as a writer, Isabel devotes much of her time to human rights causes. She has received fifteen honorary doctorates, was inducted into the California Hall of Fame, and received the PEN Center Lifetime Achievement Award and the Anisfield-Wolf Lifetime Achievement Award. In 2014, President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation’s highest civilian honor, and in 2018 she received the Medal for Distinguished Contribution to American Letters from the National Book Foundation. She lives in California with her husband and dogs, one of whom is named Perla. You can visit Isabel Allende at IsabelAllende.com or follow her on Instagram @AllendeIsabel, on Facebook at Facebook.com/IsabelAllende, and on X @IsabelAllende.
