events.title: BRIAN CULBERTSON
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Funk. Jazz. Fusion. Culbertson. · Over the course of crafting a 29-album catalog and architecting 40 Billboard #1 singles as a keyboardist, songwriter, and producer, Brian Culbertson has charted his own unique course in music. Label him jazz, and he makes a funk record. Call him an R&B artist, and he drops an acoustic jazz trio collection. Brand him pop, and he creates a 32-minute New Age opus. And you’d be hard pressed to name another instrumentalist of his ilk who can mount an elaborately designed concert production that will keep him on the road for three consecutive months. Culbertson burst onto the scene in 1994 with a chart-topping album that he recorded in his college apartment, featuring keyboard-led contemporary jazz tracks. “Long Night Out” landed him a lengthy record deal and signaled that a star was born. Flash forward to the present day, Culbertson has been going back and listening more and more to music that inspired him as a young musician, such as David Sanborn, The Brecker Bros, Chick Corea, Al Jarreau, Pat Metheny, and others in the jazz fusion world. "It instantly brought me back to the days of ‘no rules’ and the pure joy of music, something that I think a lot of albums today are lacking. With that said, I set out to write and produce a new album that would try to capture a little bit of that late 70’s and early 80’s spirit of music exploration, along with using only live musicians and real instruments. Similar in style to “Another Long Night Out”, “Day Trip” is the daytime version!” said Culbertson. Possessing style, panache, and a savvy business mind capable of moving the needle in music and beyond, Culbertson founded and curates the annual Napa Valley, New Orleans, Hawaii, and Chicago Jazz Getaways, which have attracted guests from all over the globe to experience his premier events. Whether you’re listening to music from “Day Trip” on record or live in concert, you’re hearing an eclectic, entertaining and engaging set from an artist at the peak of his power.

Their 4th EP No Genre (May 2025) followed suit, becoming their second consecutive million-seller in its first week. After a standout performance at Lollapalooza Chicago, The Action (October 2025) became their third consecutive million-seller, further cementing their global rise. Now, with their 1st studio album HOME (June 2026), BOYNEXTDOOR invite listeners into an emotional sanctuary shaped by the memories and experiences that define their journey. This narrative continues on a global stage as the group embarks on their first world tour, ‘KNOCK ON Vol. 2.’

events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Calling all cat lovers, travelers, and anyone who’s ever felt just a little guilty about befriending a new pet far from home. Join Lonely Planet and authors Diana Helmuth and Eliza Washington for a delightfully mischievous evening celebrating Where to Cheat on Your Cat, an adorable guide on where to find cats on vacation—and how to win them over without your cat back home ever finding out. Diana and Eliza will chat about the making of the book and the particular joys of feline friendships abroad. Guests can unburden themselves at our Cat Confessional, enjoy a cat-themed treat, and take home a special goodie bag—including a little something for the feline friend you left behind. Whether you love small cats, big cats, and everything in between, there is something for everyone. Come for the travel stories. Stay for the cats. Your secret is safe with us. The definitive guide to the top spots around the world where you can see, pet and photograph one of the planet's most beloved animals: cats! Meet warm-bellied felines snoozing in bookstores, gape at lions and tigers roaming through sanctuaries of palm trees, or sip your coffee with a newly-rescued kitten in your lap. From city cats in Paris, to stray cats that strut through Peru, and a wildlife refuge for big cats in Arkansas, this is the ultimate celebration of our beloved house pet–on a global scale. Inside Where to Cheat on Your Cat: Fun and engaging giftable hardback book for people who love cats and travel–and love to travel to see cats Packed with full-colour photography and practical information about worldly cats and their habitats Meet city cats, rural cats and big cats at sanctuaries and public parks Written by Diana Helmuth, an award winning author of many philosophical, nature and travel trend books including Lonely Planet's Hidden Libraries: The World’s Most Unusual Book Depositories Covers cat-tastic destinations including: Paris, Venice, Pittsburgh, Istanbul, Tokyo, Taipei, Beijing, Athens, New York, Cairo, San Francisco Bay Area, and many more This is the purrfect bookish gift for the cat and travel lover in your life! events.location: Books Inc. Alameda, 1344 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501
events.description: Join Books Inc. Alameda in welcoming local authors Carmella Dutra and Michelle Chouinard for an engaging discussion about their latest releases! About the authors: Carmela Dutra is a writer from the Bay Area who loves food trucks, family, and cozy mysteries. Her debut, A Murder Most Fowl, has been praised by Kirkus Reviews for its “serious set of crimes leavened by plenty of amusing moments,” by Criminal Element for the “juicy reasoning behind the sabotage that was almost as shocking as the murder itself,” and described as “the perfect escapist read, brimming with banter and an extra helping of fun” by New York Times bestselling author Ellery Adams. She has also been featured in CrimeReads Magazine. A lover of humor, quirky characters, and all things geeky, Carmela spends her days sketching, sipping far too much coffee, and over-cuddling her allergy-inducing cats and dog. She lives with her husband and two dinosaur-obsessed sons, drawing inspiration from rainy afternoons, bustling farmers’ markets, and the unexpected moments that make life memorable. Michelle Chouinard is the Mary Higgins Clark Award nominated, USA Today, Publishers Weekly, and Amazon Charts bestselling author behind The Serial-Killer Guide to San Francisco mysteries, The Vacation and the Detective Jo Fournier series (featuring The Dancing Girls, Taken to the Grave, Her Daughter’s Cry, and The Other Mothers). In Hot Wings and Homicide Twins Beth and Seth Lloyd are on the chopping block in the follow-up to A Murder Most Fowl, where a perfect recipe for murder is stirred up. Business at Kluckin’ Good is smoking hot. To keep momentum going, Beth and her twin brother, Seth, just scored a prime spot at the Flavors of the Bay Food Festival. For three and a half days, food lovers will flock to the Bay Area’s biggest culinary event to enjoy gourmet food trucks, cook-offs, and live music, but this recipe for success is also the perfect setup for murder. When the infamous food critic Brad Dawson—also Beth’s ex—turns up dead, the only clue at the scene of the crime is a Kluckin’ Good tumbler mug. The timing couldn’t be worse. Beth and Brad were seen in a heated altercation, and days prior, witnesses saw Seth punch Brad. Suspicion naturally falls on the twins. With the cops hot on their trail, Beth will have to avoid the flames to clear their names and save her food truck’s reputation. But the chickens are out of the coop, and as Beth digs into Brad’s final hours, she will uncover rivalries, grudges, and a different side of Brad she never knew. If she doesn’t crack the case soon, she might be the next one to get cooked. Best of cluck! A mouthwatering mystery for fans of Joanne Fluke that will leave you peckish for more. In Michelle Chouinard’s clever mystery The Serial Killer Guide to San Francisco, the granddaughter of a serial killer shows readers another side of the beloved city. Welcome to San Francisco, a city with killer charm. The chill of a San Francisco summer can be deadly. No one knows this better than Capri Sanzio, who makes her living giving serial killer tours of the city. Capri has been interested in the topic since she was a kid, when she discovered she’s the granddaughter of serial killer William ‘Overkill Bill’ Sanzio. She’s always believed in his innocence, though she's never taken the leap to fully dive into the case. But now an Overkill Bill copycat has struck in San Francisco. And Capri’s former mother-in-law, Sylvia, just cut off Capri’s daughter’s tuition payments. Needing cash, Capri wonders if this is the time to exonerate her grandfather. The case is back in the news and the police will be looking to understand the past to catch a present-day killer. Capri could finally uncover the truth about Overkill Bill—documenting the process with a podcast and a book—and hopefully earn some money. Before Capri can get very far, the cops discover the copycat’s latest victim: Sylvia. Capri soon finds herself at the heart of the police’s investigation for an entirely different reason. She and her daughter are prime suspects. Please join us!

events.title: Integration Circle: Imagery & Music with Sophia Wang
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
This is an ongoing monthly group designed to support the integration of mystical, psychedelic, or otherwise transformative experiences. Each session combines guided listening to curated music with expressive arts such as drawing and writing to help you process what a single conversation can't resolve. Come once, or return each month. No musical or art background is required.

During the evening, we will:

Enter a brief guided relaxation
Listen to a short, curated music passage
Express what surfaces through drawing and writing
Share and witness in the group (optional)
Leave with a deeper understanding or perspective

Rooted in the Bonny Method, this circle draws on Guided Imagery and Music (GIM), developed by Helen Bonny from her work with LSD-assisted therapy at the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center in the 1960s and 70s. Bonny found that music paired with deep relaxation could open the same expanded states she observed in psychedelic sessions, and that the imagery work done afterward carried much of the lasting change. GIM's approach to music and imagery now informs how integration is supported across modern psychedelic-assisted therapy.

Please arrive no later than 7pm. Doors lock at 7:10pm.

Sophia Wang is a violinist, board-certified music therapist (MT-BC), integration practitioner, and life coach whose work centers on music, imagery, and non-ordinary states of consciousness. With over a decade of clinical experience across oncology, palliative care, and mental health settings, she draws on Guided Imagery and Music, expressive arts, and depth-oriented inquiry to support emotional healing, insight, and meaningful change.

Sophia works with people across a wide range of inner terrain: those in cancer care or facing the end of life; people moving through grief, depression, or anxiety; and high-performing professionals and seekers drawn to deep self-inquiry and the integration of transformative experiences. Her approach blends clinical training with creative exploration, emphasizing safety, pacing, and integration.

events.title: BRIAN CULBERTSON
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Funk. Jazz. Fusion. Culbertson. · Over the course of crafting a 29-album catalog and architecting 40 Billboard #1 singles as a keyboardist, songwriter, and producer, Brian Culbertson has charted his own unique course in music. Label him jazz, and he makes a funk record. Call him an R&B artist, and he drops an acoustic jazz trio collection. Brand him pop, and he creates a 32-minute New Age opus. And you’d be hard pressed to name another instrumentalist of his ilk who can mount an elaborately designed concert production that will keep him on the road for three consecutive months. Culbertson burst onto the scene in 1994 with a chart-topping album that he recorded in his college apartment, featuring keyboard-led contemporary jazz tracks. “Long Night Out” landed him a lengthy record deal and signaled that a star was born. Flash forward to the present day, Culbertson has been going back and listening more and more to music that inspired him as a young musician, such as David Sanborn, The Brecker Bros, Chick Corea, Al Jarreau, Pat Metheny, and others in the jazz fusion world. "It instantly brought me back to the days of ‘no rules’ and the pure joy of music, something that I think a lot of albums today are lacking. With that said, I set out to write and produce a new album that would try to capture a little bit of that late 70’s and early 80’s spirit of music exploration, along with using only live musicians and real instruments. Similar in style to “Another Long Night Out”, “Day Trip” is the daytime version!” said Culbertson. Possessing style, panache, and a savvy business mind capable of moving the needle in music and beyond, Culbertson founded and curates the annual Napa Valley, New Orleans, Hawaii, and Chicago Jazz Getaways, which have attracted guests from all over the globe to experience his premier events. Whether you’re listening to music from “Day Trip” on record or live in concert, you’re hearing an eclectic, entertaining and engaging set from an artist at the peak of his power.

events.title: Embodiment Practice: Mindful Movement + Stillness with Suzanne (Zan) Beahrs
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest.

Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. 

Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. 

Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. 

Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space.

Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like.

About Suzanne (Zan):
With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley

Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons):

events.title: Deconstructing Yourself with Michael Taft
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. 

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

events.title: JIM EMISON: MURDER ON THE HATCHIE
events.location: Books Inc.
events.description: Books Inc Palo Alto welcomes author Jim Emison November 19 at 7pm, for a discussion of his new narrative nonfiction Murder on the Hatchie. He will be joined in conversation by Matt Gonzalez, Chief Attorney San Francisco Public Defender's Office. About Murder on the Hatchie: Nearly forgotten voting rights history is resurrected. A narrative nonfiction account of the NAACP's 1940 attempt, the first in the 20th Century, to register black voters in majority black western Tennessee's Haywood County; the white terror campaign that followed culminating in the murder of Elbert Williams, the NAACP's first voting rights martyr; the FBI's faux investigation; sabotage by the US Attorney and the FBI; and the DOJ shameful reversal of its decision to prosecute Williams's killers. Murder on the Hatchie resets the timeline and the geography of the beginnings of the Civil Rights Movement and raises the question whether some of the bloodshed in the 1950s and '60s could have been deterred by a vigorous prosecution. Praise for Murder on the Hatchie "At a time of accelerated pushback to hard-won gains of the modern American civil rights movement, this book illuminates the human cost paid to secure voting rights for Black Americans. Expertly researched, it invites us to better comprehend the raw courage of individuals determined to exercise full American citizenship rights in the face of violent white supremacy." --Lecia J. Brooks, Southern Poverty Law Center "A powerful and necessary reminder of the courage and sacrifice that shaped the NAACP's earliest fight for justice. Jim Emison brings to light a painful but pivotal chapter in our history with clarity and care." --Derrick Johnson, president and CEO, National Association for the Advancement of Colored People "Jim Emison brings to light the largely forgotten killing of NAACP organizer Elbert Williams. Through years of research, he reconstructs the violence that followed Black citizens' attempts to register to vote. Murder on the Hatchie restores this story to the history of the civil rights movement." --Gilbert King, Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Devil in the Grove "In a day when just being a member of the NAACP could get you killed in the South, Elbert Williams and five other members stood up against the Jim Crow system and attempted to register to vote. Jim Emison captures the courage of Williams and the others in his insightful book, which reminds us why the right to vote remains critical to the survival of our American democracy." --Jerry Mitchell, investigative reporter "A searing excavation of terror and truth, a thunderous reminder that the right to vote has always been paid for in blood. This is not just buried history; it is a reckoning blazing into the light." --Keith A. Beauchamp, filmmaker, The Untold Story of Emmett Louis Till and Till "This powerful book is no mere cold investigative report of the past, but a warmly inspiring story of a lawyer and a community seeking to find answers for the present and our future. Painstaking research and a poignant story make this book a must-read--and a must-heed." --Rev. Cornell William Brooks, Esq., 18th president and CEO, NAACP, and professor, Harvard Kennedy School "Murder on the Hatchie exposes how racism, fear, and abuse of power shaped both the crime and the community's response to it. More than a true-crime narrative, it serves as a moral reckoning while challenging readers to confront the enduring legacy of racial terror, systemic discrimination, and the importance of historical memory." --India A. Artis, archivist for NAACP, and former business manager of The Crisis magazine "With Murder on the Hatchie, we have it--the right man writing the right book at the right time.... In this invigorating, groundbreaking narrative, Jim Emison recounts the history as can only one who has lived close to it." --Margaret A. Burnham, director, Northeastern University Civil Rights and Restorative Justice Center, and author of By Hands Now Known: Jim Crow's Legal Executioners "Emison importantly confers on Elbert Williams the greater notoriety he deserves for his heroic efforts as an early civil rights pioneer and member of the NAACP. Williams can now take his place in the pantheon of civil rights martyrs." --Matt Gonzalez, chief attorney of the San Francisco Public Defender's Office "This book is a magnificent legacy that shows how a mighty few can expose our worst behaviors of the past, then come together decades later to win redress." --Hank Klibanoff, director of the Georgia Civil Rights Cold Cases Project at Emory University and coauthor of the Pulitzer Prize-winning The Race Beat: The Press, The Civil Rights Struggle, and the Awakening of a Nation BIOS Jim Emison , noted Tennessee courtroom lawyer of 43 years, lives in the adjoining county, only 20 miles from the events he brings to life. He knew many of the actors but the horrific events were a taboo topic he only learned of in retirement in 2012. He has been working and speaking about the murder ever since. Currently he is working to establish an Elbert Williams Interpretive Center in Brownsville Tennessee modelled on the Emmett Till Center in Sumner Mississippi. Matt Gonzalez , Chief Attorney in the San Francisco Public Defender's Office, is a Stanford Law grad, a former President of the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, and was in 2000 the Green Party's candidate for Vice President of the United States.

events.title: Farmers and Climate Change
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Ave., Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: Agriculture, Adaptation, and the Politics of Belonging · An evening with author Margiana Petersen-Rockney in conversation with journalist Anna Sale What happens when the climate is changing faster than the stories we tell about ourselves? Farmers and ranchers are experiencing climate change directly. Drought, wildfire, extreme heat, shifting seasons, water scarcity ~ these are not abstract predictions but realities shaping land, livelihoods, families, and futures. Yet the politics of climate change can make responding to them extraordinarily complicated. In Farmers and Climate Change: Agricultural Adaptation in an Age of Rural Polarization , Margiana Petersen-Rockney takes us beyond the divide between those who “believe” in climate change and those who don't. Drawing on seven years of research in Northern California, she explores how farmers actually adapt ~ and the social, political, economic, and deeply personal forces shaping their choices. Because changing how we farm can mean changing a relationship to land. To family. To neighbors. To identity. To generations of knowledge about what it means to be a farmer. Petersen-Rockney joins award-winning journalist Anna Sale , host of Slate's Death, Sex & Money and People Trying , for a conversation about what happens when climate science meets lived experience, and what becomes possible when we listen to the complicated realities beneath polarization. The evening will begin with a short introduction from anthropologist Cari Borja , whose work sits at the intersection of food, agriculture and education ~ placing the conversation within a larger question: How do we ask people to change without first understanding what we are asking them to risk? Perhaps meaningful climate action begins not only with changing practices ~ but with understanding people, the places they belong to, and what change is asking of them. Margiana Petersen-Rockney is a political ecologist who studies climate change and rural livelihoods. Margiana grew up farming and worked in food justice non-profits before receiving her PhD from University of California, Berkeley where she was a National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellow in the Environmental Science, Policy and Management Department. She’s now an Assistant Professor of Environmental studies in the Franke College of Forestry and Conservation at the University of Montana. Anna Sale is a journalist who hosts the award-winning interview podcast Death, Sex & Money from Slate and the new multimedia interview series People Trying , featuring people who work close to land, water, and nature as we're all adapting to change. She’s also been a contributor to This American Life, Fresh Air, The New York Times, and The Atlantic, and the author of Let’s Talk About Hard Things. She splits time between Berkeley and Cody, Wyoming.

events.title: BRIAN CULBERTSON
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Funk. Jazz. Fusion. Culbertson. · Over the course of crafting a 29-album catalog and architecting 40 Billboard #1 singles as a keyboardist, songwriter, and producer, Brian Culbertson has charted his own unique course in music. Label him jazz, and he makes a funk record. Call him an R&B artist, and he drops an acoustic jazz trio collection. Brand him pop, and he creates a 32-minute New Age opus. And you’d be hard pressed to name another instrumentalist of his ilk who can mount an elaborately designed concert production that will keep him on the road for three consecutive months. Culbertson burst onto the scene in 1994 with a chart-topping album that he recorded in his college apartment, featuring keyboard-led contemporary jazz tracks. “Long Night Out” landed him a lengthy record deal and signaled that a star was born. Flash forward to the present day, Culbertson has been going back and listening more and more to music that inspired him as a young musician, such as David Sanborn, The Brecker Bros, Chick Corea, Al Jarreau, Pat Metheny, and others in the jazz fusion world. "It instantly brought me back to the days of ‘no rules’ and the pure joy of music, something that I think a lot of albums today are lacking. With that said, I set out to write and produce a new album that would try to capture a little bit of that late 70’s and early 80’s spirit of music exploration, along with using only live musicians and real instruments. Similar in style to “Another Long Night Out”, “Day Trip” is the daytime version!” said Culbertson. Possessing style, panache, and a savvy business mind capable of moving the needle in music and beyond, Culbertson founded and curates the annual Napa Valley, New Orleans, Hawaii, and Chicago Jazz Getaways, which have attracted guests from all over the globe to experience his premier events. Whether you’re listening to music from “Day Trip” on record or live in concert, you’re hearing an eclectic, entertaining and engaging set from an artist at the peak of his power.

events.title: Monster Energy Outbreak Tour, Goldenvoice, & CMN Present RØZ: SE ESTÁ HACIENDO TARDE SE ESTÁ HACIENDO TARDE RØZ
events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Artist and producer duo RØZ, comprised of Manolo Cabrera and Hugo Lara, has rapidly emerged as one of the most innovative forces in Mexico’s electronic music renaissance. In less than three years, the project has evolved from digital experimentation to selling out major venues, redefining the expectations of Latin electronic music with a fluid, boundary-breaking sonic identity.

Manolo Cabrera began his artistic journey inspired by the cinematic world of large-scale electronic festivals – specifically, the Tomorrowland films that first awakened his fascination with dance music. Early explorations led him through trap, Tropical House, and Future Bass, releasing early work on SoundCloud as he developed his voice.

Hugo Lara’s path started in classical music. At just four years old, he played violin to the works of Italian composer Antonio Vivaldi. In his adolescence, artists like Skrillex pulled him toward EDM, prompting him to experiment with production through GarageBand – an entry point that eventually enabled his first collaborations with Manolo.

The two met in high school, each maintaining their solo projects while constantly exchanging ideas and feedback. “He created sounds with synths that I didn’t know how to make,” Manolo recalls, while Hugo admired the originality in Manolo’s compositions. Their chemistry crystallized after a joint track with Tom & Collins, and the two officially united under the name RØZ, marking the beginning of the duo.

Their evolution has been intentional and uncompromising. After an early phase shaped by imitation and experimentation, they found their voice when they decided to reject the “rules” of genre altogether. “When our sound truly changed, that’s when we realized there were no rules,” explains Hugo. This breakthrough sparked a distinctive aesthetic that merges drum and bass, trap, reggaeton, UKG, and electronic textures into a singular style. Their transition to Spanish lyrics in mid-2022 became a key turning point, cementing the identity that would propel them into global recognition.

Unlike many Mexican electronic projects that focus on recreating global trends, RØZ is committed to building an identity that is deeply personal – and deeply connected to its audience. “Instead of seeing the people who follow us as fans, we see them as friends,” says Manolo.

In the past year, RØZ’s rise has accelerated to unprecedented heights, marked by major festival debuts at EDC Mexico, Bandidos Festival, Baja Beach Fest, and many more, where their high-energy performances have become a calling card.

Demand reached historic levels in late 2025: their first-ever U.S. tour, “Oye, Estados Unidos,” sold out within minutes in every major market, solidifying RØZ as one of the most sought-after live acts of the year. Just before the tour launch, they delivered their biggest solo concert yet – “Se está haciendo tarde CDMX”– packing Pabellón Oeste del Palacio de los Deportes in Mexico City.

This runaway live momentum paralleled their chart breakthrough, as RØZ secured three entries on the Billboard Hot Dance/Electronic Songs chart with “flashes” featuring Yng Lvcas, their viral anthem “CORA DE HIELO,” and their powerhouse collaboration “Apaga la luz” with Peso Pluma.

Combined with the viral acclaim of their groundbreaking Spotify Sessions, and surpassing 410 million career streams, RØZ’s 2025 run established them as one of the most inventive, globally resonant acts rewriting the future of Latin music.

In December 2025, RØZ released their anticipated debut EP, mañana, temprano– a masterclass in genre fluidity that moves seamlessly through reggaeton, electronic, house, bachata, and techno with cinematic flair. The EP reflects the duo’s boundary-breaking ethos and global reach, featuring collaborations with creative trailblazers Nsqk, DannyLux, El Bogueto, and UK hitmaker Cloonee.

2026 has already been full of milestones for RØZ. They've been on their sold-out tour with stops all over the US and at festivals like Coachella (leaving people out of the tent since it was over capacity both weekends!), EDC Las Vegas, and Sueños Fest. Plus, the guys also joined Peso Pluma on stage at his show in NYC, made it onto Rolling Stone en Español’s Future 25 list, and hit 300M+ all-time global streams.

Showing no signs of slowing down, RØZ recently announced their upcoming debut album SE ESTÁ HACIENDO TARDE, set to release on August 7th with 19 new songs. Their recent single, “HBU” featuring Artemas, offers a glimpse into the duo’s new era as they continue to push their evolving sound to the next level. The duo is building on a remarkable trajectory, establishing themselves as one of the most visionary and influential forces in contemporary Mexican electronic music

events.title: Wisdom Healing Qigong with Hiromi Vardy
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Experience the deep benefits of Zhineng (Wisdom Healing) Qigong. This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Through simple, time-honored movements, the nervous system unwinds, the mind becomes more spacious, and the heart opens. Over time, practitioners often feel more resilient, centered, and connected — both inwardly and outwardly.

Tickets are sliding scale $10-$25 - Please arrive at least 5-10 minutes early.

 Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back 

Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts.

While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga.

After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today.

Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

events.title: The Present Moment Game with Alli Magidsohn
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
When we gather with others, conversation almost automatically drifts toward what has already happened or what might happen next. Stories, plans, reactions, hopes—these patterns are so ingrained that we barely notice how completely we relate to one another through the lens of the past and future.

But when we pause those habits, something surprising occurs.

The room changes.
Attention sharpens.
A different kind of connection begins to emerge.

A small clearing inside awareness opens—a place where no future is rehearsing itself, and no echoes of the past are allowed to enter.

We can touch this space alone in contemplative practices, but it's rare to enter it with others.

The Present Moment Game is a simple social meditation designed to explore that possibility.

Participants speak only from what is happening in the moment, and gently bring each other back when attention drifts. What unfolds is often unexpected, and never the same twice.

Curious? Come play!
___________

What to Expect

6:30 PM — Doors open
Arrive anytime in the next 30 minutes. You’re welcome to enjoy tea as you settle in—just note that drinks won’t be brought into the circle, so come early if you’d like to enjoy an unrushed cup.

7:00 PM — The event begins
This is a “sealed-container” experience. Out of care for the group, we can’t allow late entry, so please be sure to arrive between 6:30 and 7:00. After a brief grace period, doors will close at 7:05.

7:06 PM — Welcome, introductions & game rules
A short orientation covering the simple guidelines.

7:25 PM — The Present Moment Game begins

8:25 PM — The game ends
We’ll then move into group reflections.

~8:45 PM — Event concludes
___________

Is This Event for You?
A few things to consider before you decide:

Phones and watches off
As an invitation to loosen your grip on time, you’ll be asked to remove your watch and fully power down your phone for the full duration of the experience.

This is not an Authentic Relating practice
T-Group, Circling, and other AR forms use present-moment awareness as a vehicle for relational exploration. That’s not what we’re doing here. Our subject isn’t each other, but the moment itself.

Kindness is essential
Please come willing to encounter everyone in the room with openness and warmth. This is a gentle space for contemplation and focused attention, not edge-pushing or confrontation.
___________

One participant’s experience:

"As a person who loves, thinks and talks about language for a living, I am wide-eyed at how speaking solely in the present tense feels rich, alive and vital. It’s the best of meditation and conversation, distilled into an hour of social elixir; a stop-you-in-your-tracks nexus of collective mind. I feel hooked, thirsty for more. Alli creates a magical container. You won’t regret it."  — Sophia
___________

About your host

Alli Magidsohn is the creator of The Present Moment Game, an experimental social meditation that invites a small group to do something surprisingly rare: be fully present together, in real time.

The idea grew out of Alli's experience with T-Group, a practice she found genuinely transformative. But as she went deeper, she became increasingly captivated by something specific: the quality of attention that arises when a group of people focus on what's actually happening, right now.

That observation became a question: What if the present moment wasn’t just the context of a relationally-focused experience, but the primary subject of the inquiry itself?

Drawing in part on the linguistic principles of E-Prime, she designed a set of simple constraints that gently guide conversation away from the past and future, and into the living moment. The result is something playful, quietly profound, and hard to describe until you experience it.

events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. events.title: GERALD ALBRIGHT
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Grammy-nominated saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist · Born and raised in Los Angeles, Albright was already an accomplished saxophonist by the time he enrolled at the University of Redlands, but he switched to bass after he saw Louis Johnson in concert. A few months after graduating from college, he joined jazz pianist/R&B singer Patrice Rushen, who was in the process of forming her own band. Later, when the bassist left in the middle of a tour, Albright replaced him and finished the tour on bass guitar. Playing both sax and bass, he became the consummate session and touring musician in the 80s, working with everyone from Anita Baker, Ray Parker, Jr., Atlantic Starr, The Temptations, and Maurice White to Les McCann, Teena Marie, the Winans, and Whitney Houston. He launched his solo career in the infancy of what became the smooth jazz format, with Just Between Us in 1987, and has been a core part of the genre with chart-topping albums, countless radio hits, and as a member of many all-star tours, including Guitars & Saxes and Groovin’ For Grover. In the late 90s, he fronted a big band and toured with pop star Phil Collins and did a dual recording with vocal great Will Downing called Pleasures of the Night . Between his last two Grammy-nominated solo albums, Pushing The Envelope (2010) and Slam Dunk (2014), he enjoyed hit collaborations with two huge hits – 24/7 with guitarist Norman Brown and Summer Horns by Dave Koz and Friends (including Mindi Abair and Richard Elliot), which were also Grammy-nominated for Best Pop Instrumental Albums. He toured with Brown and Summer Horns, and most recently has been on the road with South African gospel/jazz singer and guitarist Jonathan Butler. Albright’s other albums, whose titles perfectly reflect their flow, include Smooth (1994), Groovology (2002), Kickin’ It Up (2004), and Sax for Stax (2008). Because Albright’s musical muse has taken him to so many fascinating locales along the contemporary R&B/urban jazz spectrum, he’s joyfully defied easy categorizations. “Top to bottom,” Albright says, “Whether in concert, listening to my music over the radio or CD player, I always want my listeners to be taken on a musical journey with different textures, rhythms, chord progressions, and moods. I want people to know where I’ve been and where I’m going, and to let them hear that I’m in a really good place in my life.”

Set to two of the most iconic works in the classical music canon, Copland’s Suite from Appalachian Spring and Debussy’s Prélude à l’après-midi d’un faune ( Afternoon of a Faun ) , the program offers the unparalleled experience of live symphonic music performed on stage alongside LINES’ extraordinary dancers, for an immersive dialogue between movement and sound. Conductor James Gaffigan will lead the San Francisco Symphony in this collaborative program, which will also include Prokofiev’s Sinfonia concertante, featuring SF Symphony Principal Cellist Rainer Eudeikis. Join LINES Ballet and the SF Symphony as we celebrate movement and sound breathing together in real time. To learn more, visit our Fall Season webpage . events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.description: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan . It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Babehoven, Pileup (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Babehoven Babehoven is the Hudson, NY based project of singer-songwriter Maya Bon and collaborator Ryan Albert. Since 2017, the band has carved out a sound that blends melodic indie and folk rock with an occasional nod towards country. Bon serves as the project’s principal songwriter and lyricist, while Albert, a multi-instrumentalist and producer, further shapes the sonic world around her songs. Together, they’ve built a body of work that feels both intimate and expansive. "Blue Around You," Babehoven's new single, is a country-flecked stomper. The song finds Bon singing with hard-won resilience: "Yesterday a stranger told me they can see / That I feel levels of pain that could've broken me / And I thought, mmm but I survived it." Recorded at The Chicken Shack and 12 Lb Genius in Upstate NY, Maya and Ryan gathered an excellent crew of musicians with producer Phil Weinrobe at the helm—Oliver Hill, Zosha Warpeha, Dylan Nowik, Jared Samuel, Ellington Peet, and Nick Kinsey. The core of the song was recorded live with no playback or headphones with the feel of the room being as much an instrument as the hardanger fiddle and harmonies that soar overhead. events.title: Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan - Market Memories Cookbook (Foodwise)
events.location: Ferry Building Foodwise Classroom San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Meet & Greet Book Signing Only • SF Ferry Plaza Market 11:00 AM PT Food Demo // 11:30 AM PT Book Signing Please join us for a special meet-and-greet signing event with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan, following their Foodwise demo at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market. Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan's beautiful new work, Market Memories Cookbook , celebrates 50 years of the Davis Farmers Market with 92 all-new seasonal recipes illustrated by the authors. Guest essays about the market’s origins, the battle for farmers market certification and the sense of optimism and change of the 1970s add yet another dimension to this celebratory book. Throughout the pages, heartfelt anecdotes from the farmers, vendors and shoppers illuminate the poignant role the market continues to play in our daily lives. The Davis Farmers Market was voted USA Today’s 10 Best Farmers Market (2015) and America’s Favorite Farmers Market (2009). For more information on awards and the market, go to www.davisfarmersmarket.org . “When the Davis Farmers Market opened, it was extraordinary, and it is astonishing that it is still here fifty years later. It stands as a testament to the simple, radical idea of connecting people directly with local organic farmers and ranchers. I am so impressed.” ALICE WATERS, Chez Panisse Restaurant and Edible Schoolyard Project, Berkeley For more than fifty years, Ann M. Evans , former mayor and Citizen of the Year of Davis, California, has helped to bring healthful eating to an ever-growing audience through both her work with government and non-profit organizations and her writing. Among her many accomplishments is the co-founding of three regional food-system mainstays: Davis Farm to School, one of the first farm-to-school programs in the country; the 51-year-old Davis Food Co-op; and the award-winning Davis Farmers Market. She was also at the table for the creation of the Certified Farmers Market regulations, representing the Department of Consumer Affairs. Ann is the author of several cookbooks and texts to improve school lunch, as well as a botanical artist drawing inspiration from her garden, the creeks and wildlands of Yolo County, and the market. Her food influences stem from a lifetime of international travel, childhood summers in Chapel Hill and Durham, North Carolina, summers in Provence, France, her northern England family heritage, and a lifetime amidst the agricultural landscape of Northern California. She lives in Davis with her husband, surrounded by a small edible garden where she keeps bees and chickens. At age eight, Georgeanne Brennan wrote her first cookbook. The recipes were written on lined foolscap paper stapled together with a bright yellow cover, titled My Recipes. Since then, she's written more than thirty cookbooks, won a Julia Child award for one and a James Beard award for another. She has lived in Provence, where she raised goats and made and sold cheese, taught high school in Arctic Alaska, and cooking classes across the nation. For six years, she hosted her own Culinary Vacation program, bringing people to share a week for shopping, cooking, and foraging in the interior Provence, where she has had a home for more than forty years. In the early 1980s, Georgeanne co-founded Le Marche' Seeds and was instrumental in importing European heirloom seeds and selling them to farmers across the United States, earning her place in the pantheon of the California Food Revolution. She lives in Winters with her husband, where she gardens, cooks, writes, and paints between welcoming her extended family, including eight grandchildren and their dogs. Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan - photos courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event is a non-seated Meet & Greet signing only. events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. events.title: GERALD ALBRIGHT
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Grammy-nominated saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist · Born and raised in Los Angeles, Albright was already an accomplished saxophonist by the time he enrolled at the University of Redlands, but he switched to bass after he saw Louis Johnson in concert. A few months after graduating from college, he joined jazz pianist/R&B singer Patrice Rushen, who was in the process of forming her own band. Later, when the bassist left in the middle of a tour, Albright replaced him and finished the tour on bass guitar. Playing both sax and bass, he became the consummate session and touring musician in the 80s, working with everyone from Anita Baker, Ray Parker, Jr., Atlantic Starr, The Temptations, and Maurice White to Les McCann, Teena Marie, the Winans, and Whitney Houston. He launched his solo career in the infancy of what became the smooth jazz format, with Just Between Us in 1987, and has been a core part of the genre with chart-topping albums, countless radio hits, and as a member of many all-star tours, including Guitars & Saxes and Groovin’ For Grover. In the late 90s, he fronted a big band and toured with pop star Phil Collins and did a dual recording with vocal great Will Downing called Pleasures of the Night . Between his last two Grammy-nominated solo albums, Pushing The Envelope (2010) and Slam Dunk (2014), he enjoyed hit collaborations with two huge hits – 24/7 with guitarist Norman Brown and Summer Horns by Dave Koz and Friends (including Mindi Abair and Richard Elliot), which were also Grammy-nominated for Best Pop Instrumental Albums. He toured with Brown and Summer Horns, and most recently has been on the road with South African gospel/jazz singer and guitarist Jonathan Butler. Albright’s other albums, whose titles perfectly reflect their flow, include Smooth (1994), Groovology (2002), Kickin’ It Up (2004), and Sax for Stax (2008). Because Albright’s musical muse has taken him to so many fascinating locales along the contemporary R&B/urban jazz spectrum, he’s joyfully defied easy categorizations. “Top to bottom,” Albright says, “Whether in concert, listening to my music over the radio or CD player, I always want my listeners to be taken on a musical journey with different textures, rhythms, chord progressions, and moods. I want people to know where I’ve been and where I’m going, and to let them hear that I’m in a really good place in my life.”

events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . After 26 years with Carlos Santana and a decade with Tower of Power, CT brings a signature blend of deep‑pocket groove, soulful expression, and explosive energy to the stage. His unmistakable sound—anchored by his legendary left‑hand/left‑foot bass—moves effortlessly from smooth and lyrical to thunderous and driving. CT’s career spans iconic contributions to Tower of Power, Grammy‑winning collaborations with Santana, and performances with artists such as Wayne Shorter. Today, he returns to his jazz roots, leading a quartet united by a shared passion for improvisation and groove. events.title: Lynne Kaufman's THE SECRET MUSEUM
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: Opening Reception Sunday, November 8 (Please do not bring infants to the show) Francesca, a contemporary American filmmaker, is shooting a documentary on a newly excavated fresco in Pompeii said to provide startling evidence about sex and the sacred. She has obtained exclusive rights to film the fresco through the good graces of Paolo, the museum’s director and her former college sweetheart. Through three time periods and the lives of three couples, THE SECRET MUSEUM explores the mysteries of eros. Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. Keith has acted in theaters throughout the Bay Area, most recently in 1984 at the Aurora Theatre Company and as the Porter in the California Shakespeare Theater’s production of Macbeth . His film credits include Nomadland , The Last Black Man in San Francisco , Haiku Tunnel , Love and Taxes , Raising Arizona , Fargo , A Serious Man , and The Big Lebowski . As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. He reunited with Ms. Kaufman to direct Who Killed Sylvia Plath and The Smartest Woman in America about the final days of Susan Sontag, both at the Marsh San Francisco. Arwen Anderson ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where she previously collaborated with Lynne Kaufman on a staged reading of her musical Map of Your Mind and performed in Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . Selected regional credits include Testmatch, Men On Boats, Heisenberg , Let There Be Love , A Christmas Carol , and Tales of the City (workshop) at American Conservatory Theater; King Lear , Romeo and Juliet , and The Verona Project at California Shakespeare Theater; August: Osage County , Anne Boleyn , Circle Mirror Transformation , Bellwether , and A Streetcar Named Desire at Marin Theatre ; An Accident , Mrs. Whitney , Expedition 6 , The Rules of Charity , and Mauritius at Magic Theatre; A White Girl’s Guide to International Terrorism, The Fit, and 77% at San Francisco Playhouse; Miss Julie at Stanford Repertory Theater; Lobby Hero and The Shape of Things at Aurora Theatre Company; You Know When the Men Are Gone and 4 Adverbs with Word for Word; and roles with American Stage Festival, San Jose Repertory Theatre, Marin Shakespeare Company, Brava Theater, Encore Theatre Company, and Central Works Theater Company. Her film work includes Hog Island , Ashley 22 , and Dark Retreat . Johnny Moreno ( Performer ) returns to The Marsh, where he previously performed in Lynne Kaufman’s Extreme Acts . He has also appeared at theaters throughout the Bay Area including American Conservatory Theater, Berkeley Repertory Theatre, San Francisco Playhouse, San Jose Stage Company, Marin Shakespeare Company, Center Repertory Company, Marin Theatre , Crowded Fire Theater, and Pacific Repertory Theatre. He has played award winning roles, such as Macheath in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of The Threepenny Opera (Theatre Bay Area Award for Best Actor in a Musical) , and Henry Higgins in San Francisco Playhouse’s production of My Fair Lady (San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Critics Circle Award for Best Actor in a Musical). He has appeared in numerous film and television productions, such as “Betas,” Callback (winner of the Chicago Indie Fest for Best Film), Upside Out (with Olympia Dukakis), Paradise Club, and I’m Still Here (with Joaquin Phoenix). Lyndsy Kail ( Performer ) Marsh Debut. Regional credits include The White Chip at Marin Theatre. California Shakespeare Theater, Center Repertory Theatre, B Street Theatre, Capital Stage, San Francisco Shakespeare Festival, San Jose Stage. FILM/TELEVISION: Trauma, All About Evil, The Optimist . Other: voice and performance capture for Star Wars: Tales from the Galaxy’s Edge, Star Tours, Fortnite, Monster High , many 2K games including BioShock Infinite, NBA2K, and the latest Mafia game. Training: BA in Classics at UC Berkeley and The Groundlings in LA. Joseph O’Malley ( Performer, AEA ) makes his Marsh debut, having performed at the Kennedy Center, La Jolla Playhouse, Berkeley Rep, Marin Theatre, Cal Shakes, Aurora Theatre, Marin Shakespeare and Center Rep. He is thrilled to reunite with director Warren David Keith for The Secret Museum . Up next: The Gift of Nothing and The Crucible at Marin Theatre, as well as Ang Lee’s film Gold Mountain . events.title: Half-Day Silent Unguided Retreat
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice.
This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods.
There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of
meditation, all are welcome.

The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive
between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before
the first bell.

The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation:
9:30 AM – 10:10 AM
10:20 AM – 11:00 AM
11:10 AM – 11:50 AM

A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period.
The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between
sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom.
Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep
voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire
morning.

You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during
a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and
the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice
elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell.

The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website.

Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by
12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely
manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

events.title: Return to Center: Exploring Stability, Mobility & Ease with Vickie Russell Bell
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves..



Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition.

Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.
