events.title: KIMBERLY BEA with THE CURSE OF THE FEATHERS
events.location: Books Inc. Mountain View, 317 Castro St, Mountain View, CA 94041
events.description: Join local author and friend of the store Kimberly Bea at Books Inc. Mountain View for a celebration of her new book The Curse of Feathers! About the book: For fans of Katherine Arden and Kell Woods, an enchanting, feminist fantasy retelling of the Brothers Grimm tale “The Wild Swans”: a young woman’s handiwork and determination is tested to the limits to save her six brothers, cursed to become swans. “Know this; no word of yours shall ever break my spell.” As the only daughter in her noble family, Elisa von Ahlefeldt has always been the untamed outlier. Unlike her six brothers who follow the protocols and duty of the court, she is ellevilde —elf-wild—a child of nature. She spends her days in the woods where she has befriended Nuve, an ash-tree maid who teaches her the ways of forest magic. Elisa finds she has a gift for magic that matches the needlecraft talent she learned from her mother—whose tragic death has torn the family apart. Following the funeral, Elisa’s father reveals he has been spellbound by a Hexe into marriage and sends his young children into hiding. Years pass before stepmother Belinde locates them, transforms the boys into swans, and alters her husband’s perception of his daughter, casting her out of their lives. To break her brothers’ curse, Elisa is guided by Nuve to use her needlecraft to create magical garments from stinging nettles for each of them under a vow of silence. A silence she must keep while impersonating a missing noblewoman. A secret she must hold dear even as she is betrothed to a handsome stranger. A power she must wield to defy the evil Belinde and rescue her family before their bird nature steals their human lives away forever. For Elisa, despite the perils of the Hexen and her own fears, knows deep in her heart that: “Silence has its power, and not all that is wild can be tamed.” A coming-of-age fantasy adventure, Curse of Feathers , is a tale of inner strength at the crossroads of faith and mysticism, rich with historical details in this retelling of the classic Brothers Grimm fairy tale. Kimberly Bea is the author of mythology and fable-inspired fiction, including The Changeling Queen and The Curse of Feathers. A member of the Society for the Promotion of Speculative Fiction, her shorter work has been published in the anthologies Den of Thieves and Spring: Dreams and Nightmares and poetry in the anthology Nothing But Red . She is a social historian and lifelong feminist with undergraduate and graduate degrees in Ancient History with comparative fields in medieval history and the ancient Near East. A native of California, she lived in Minneapolis for 25 years before moving back to her home state. Visit her online at KimberlyBea.com .

This meditation and study group is based in the Insight Meditation tradition and its sources in Thai Forest and Burmese Theravāda Buddhism. To this foundation, we add exploration of Mahāyāna Dharmas particularly from the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñāpāramitā) literature and lineage. The group meets weekly online, and on fourth Tuesdays live at the Alembic.

The focus of the group is on deepening in Buddhist liberation practice, and exploring the links between individual & systemic liberation in the form of social justice and collective healing. I bring a particular focus on working with the nervous system and resolving the symptoms of trauma, supported by devotional practice, study, and ethics as the basis of the path.

All are welcome. Cost is $5, plus Dāna (pay what you can).
Find the online version here: https://momence.com/l/K1hwl2vd

Sean Oakes, PhD (he/him, queer, of Spanish/Puerto Rican and Northern European ancestry living on unceded Pomo land in California), teaches Buddhism, Yoga, and somatic practice. He has studied in Theravāda, Zen, and Vajrāyāna Buddhist lineages since 1993, including training as a monk in Burma, and was authorized to teach Insight Meditation by Jack Kornfield in 2010. His primary Buddhist teachers include Kornfield, Sylvia Boorstein, Gil Fronsdal, Eugene Cash, Kittisaro, Ṭhānissara, Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu, Anam Thubten, and Chammyay Sayadaw (U Janaka), with whom he ordained as a bhikkhu for a Rains Retreat in Burma in 2002.

He studied Haṭha and Vinyāsa Yogas with Alice Joanou, Rachel Shaw, Amanda Moran, and David Moreno, and taught mindfulness-based āsana and prāṇāyāma for 10 years. He performed for many years in music, dance, and performance art, including with Keith Hennessy’s Circo Zero, and was certified in Somatic Experiencing (SE) and Organic Intelligence (OI) with Steven Hoskinson, integrating the complex systems approach from OI in a distinctively Buddhist approach to trauma resolution. He received his PhD in Performance Studies from UC Davis in 2016, writing on extraordinary states of consciousness in Buddhist meditation and experimental dance. He teaches at Spirit Rock Meditation Center, East Bay Meditation Center, Insight Timer, and elsewhere, focusing on the integration of philosophy, somatics, and social justice discourse with the Dharma.

events.title: Relatefulness with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other

Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli.

Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment.

This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. 

We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance!

What We’ll Explore

Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice:
Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group.
Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society.
Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly.
Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of.

Why Come?

You may be looking to:
Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected.
Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context.
Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns

This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun!

What Not to Expect

This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur.

It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. 

Here’s what NOT to expect:
A space free of conflict or triggers.
When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others.
No enforced hierarchy of emotions.
Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important.
Expression without attunement.
We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence.

Other logistics and notes

Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time!

We hope to see you at a future event! 

Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you.

More about the facilitators

Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring.

When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws.

In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance.

Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

events.title: Embodiment Practice: Mindful Movement + Stillness with Suzanne (Zan) Beahrs
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest.

Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. 

Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. 

Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. 

Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space.

Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like.

About Suzanne (Zan):
With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley

Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons): 
IG @suzannebeahrs suzannebeahrs.com

events.title: Wisdom Healing Qigong with Hiromi Vardy
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Experience the deep benefits of Zhineng (Wisdom Healing) Qigong. This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Through simple, time-honored movements, the nervous system unwinds, the mind becomes more spacious, and the heart opens. Over time, practitioners often feel more resilient, centered, and connected — both inwardly and outwardly.

Tickets are sliding scale $10-$25 - Please arrive at least 5-10 minutes early.

 Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back 

Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts.

While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga.

After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today.

Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

events.title: Janet Thornburg's COGNITIVE DIVINE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) You think it’s hard to herd cats? Try getting seven sub-personalities to agree on anything! Wild Child, Rosie, and Mauve love living in San Francisco, but Raisin and Hannah want to go back to Colorado. When Cora soothes Raisin with cinnamon rolls, Hannah complains that sugar is bad for us. Hannah and Wild Child lock horns over Wild Child’s party behavior. Rosie wants to go shopping for clothes and skin-care products, but Mauve wants to spend the money on writers’ conferences and research for her novel. The conflicts never end, and the arguments create quite a din. All seven of Janet’s sub-personalities are delighted to have this opportunity to give their opinions of Janet’s life choices! Janet Thornburg (writer/performer) is a soloist whose solo show Cognitive Divine won the Best Full-Length Comedy award in the In Front of Your Eyes Festival 2026 at the Marsh. She has written and performed eight solo shows in San Francisco at venues including The Marsh, StageWerx Theatre, Theatre Rhinoceros, Theatre of Yugen, Venue Nine, Next Stage Theatre,Young Performers’ Theatre, and the Solo Mio Festival. Her multi-character play Dinner Roles was presented at the San Francisco Repertory Theatre, and her play Antony and Cleopatra Meet Godzilla enjoyed two runs at the Intersection Theatre. She holds an MFA in playwriting from San Francisco State University and an MFA in fiction from Warren Wilson College. Her fiction has been widely published in literary journals, and Rhubarb Pie , a collection of her short stories, was published by Thunderegg Press. For further information about her performances and publications, visit www.janetthornburg.com. events.description: Queen of Percussion · One of life’s constants for Sheila E. comes down to a simple phrase: follow the beat. And her impeccable inner rhythm is the pulse behind a trailblazing career that still knows no bounds. Family, faith and music were guiding forces for Sheila E. growing up in the Bay Area. In addition to percussionist dad Pete, the Oakland, CA native counts former Santana member/Azteca founder Coke Escovedo and The Dragons front man Mario Escovedo as uncles. Fellow Latin star Tito Puente was her godfather. In addition to being weaned on Latin jazz and Motown, Sheila E. was exposed to a diverse array of Bay Area acts. Those influences ranged from the rock of Jefferson Airplane and the Grateful Dead to the R&B/pop of the Pointer Sisters and the funk of Sly & the Family Stone. “I used to sit on the corner outside of the local community center with Twinkies and 7-Up listening to Sly and Larry Graham rehearse,” remembers Sheila E. “The sounds of the Bay Area molded me.” So it’s no surprise that after such a music-immersive childhood, the gifted, world-class drummer and percussionist began amassing an impressive string of credits playing not only with her dad but also with pioneering talents like George Duke, Herbie Hancock, Marvin Gaye, Diana Ross, Lionel Richie, Prince, Ringo Starr, Gloria Estefan, Beyoncé and Jennifer Lopez. Grammy Award-nominated singer/songwriter behind the seminal hits “The Glamorous Life” and “A Love Bizarre.” A fearless multi-instrumentalist, equally proficient on guitar and bass, actress, mentor and philanthropist. Following a Bay Area gig in the late ‘70s, Sheila E. met Prince backstage. Their Purple Rain recording sessions—including her vocals on the 1984 classic “Erotic City”—morphed into launching her solo career that same year. Debut album The Glamorous Life spun off the Grammy Award-nominated top 10 hit of the same name plus a second top 40 single “The Belle of St. Mark.” Between her ‘80s tenure as drummer, songwriter, and musical director for Prince’s backup band, Sheila E. released two more solo albums ( Romance 1600 and Shelia E.) and scored another classic hit with “A Love Bizarre.” Sheila E.’s fierce, dynamic verve onstage has made her a major concert draw since the ‘90s. Along the way, she has acted in the films “Krush Groove”, “The Adventures of Ford Fairlane”, “Chasing Papi” and launched various music projects (E-Train, C.O.E.D., E Family Band). She added to her arsenal of credits performing on the 2012 Academy Awards with pop hitmaker Pharrell Williams and composer Hans Zimmer. Sheila E. was also among the roster of stars chosen to perform at the 2013 Kennedy Center Honors, whose honorees included artists Herbie Hancock, Billy Joel, and Carlos Santana. Sheila E.'s producing, arranging, and performance talents have been showcased throughout the music and film industry with appearances on The Academy Awards, The Latin Grammy Awards, BET Awards, The American Music Awards, The Kennedy Center Honors, The Summer Olympics, WOW Awards, ALMA's, and The Image Awards, just to name a few. In 2010, Sheila was nominated for an Emmy Award for “Outstanding Music Direction” in recognition of her leadership as musical director for President Obama’s Performance at The White House: Fiesta Latina and again more recently in 2020 for “Let’s Go Crazy” Grammy Salute to Prince. Other projects include The E Family

events.title: Andrea Brewster: Draft
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: Andrea Brewster, Draft 1, 2026, giclee print, woven vellum, 10″ x 10″, photo courtesy of the artist Andrea Brewster’s new body of work, Draft, begins with the fundamental structure of weaving: warp and weft, whose interlacing creates both fabric and an underlying grid. She approaches the grid not as a rigid system, but as a living structure capable of variation, interruption, rhythm, and ambiguity. The work draws from weaving drafts, diagrams that function as instructions for generating complex patterns, resembling a form of pre-digital code. The term “draft” also refers to an initial idea or work in progress, connecting structure with imagination and instruction with image.This connection between weaving and digital systems is central to Brewster’s thinking. Although digitally constructed, these pieces retain the appearance of hand-drawn marks, creating a tension between material and virtual, order and improvisation. Through line, color, repetition, and interruption, Brewster explores the relationship between visible patterns and the structures beneath them. Bio: Andrea Brewster is a multidisciplinary artist who investigates the intersection of nature, fiber art, and technology through intricate forms and layered textures. Brewster earned a B.A. in Sculpture from Pomona College and an M.F.A. in New Genres from the San Francisco Art Institute. A 1993 NEA grant recipient, she has exhibited widely in the San Francisco Bay Area, with solo shows at Mercury 20, The Lab, and Southern Exposure, as well as group exhibitions at Metal Haus Gallery, Chandra Cerrito Contemporary, The Oakland Museum, and the Peninsula Museum. Her work has been featured in fiber art exhibitions in Ireland and the U.S. She has participated in the Djerassi Resident Artist Program, and in 2025, her AI work appeared at Load Gallery, Barcelona, and in the book Neo Botanica. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery since 2020. Gallery Hours: Friday and Saturday, 12 – 5 pm (and by appointment) Artists’ Opening Reception: Saturday, October 24, 3 – 5 pm ﻿Oakland Art Murmur / First Friday: November 6, 5 – 9 pm Artist Talks: Saturday, November 7, 3 – 5 pm

events.title: Nicole Nelson - Family Language
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: In this striking debut, an ambitious academic faces difficult choices when confronted with overnight motherhood. Family Language explores the misogyny behind the question of whether women can "have it all" as Mona balances her career with new responsibilities. Dr. Mona Melamed is a happily married, purposefully childfree linguist at a top Southern California university. Her days are spent researching and stressing about finally, finally securing tenure. That is, until her brother-in-law and his wife die, leaving their six-year-old son orphaned. Everyone in Mona's orbit expects her to take the lead in caring for the child, including—to some extent—Mona herself. Motherhood is not something she wanted–it is still not something she wants. And yet, she finds herself negotiating a temporary leave to start looking after the boy. Along the way, as the gender expectations thrust upon Mona intensify, her tenure becomes threatened. Family Language confronts that age old question–Can women really have it all?--and uncovers the misogyny behind it. As Mona tries to balance her new responsibilities as a mother, she has to ask herself how hard is she willing to fight for the career she’s earned, and is it fair that she even has to? "In this post-Roe era, it’s a joy to meet a narrator who is unapologetically feminist! Mona’s story is about ordinary words that have extraordinary complexity and consequences. How does language narrow—or open up—the actual possibilities in our lives? Nicole Nelson writes with compassion and humor about gender, ambition, academia, and the politics of care.” —Leni Zumas, author of Red Clocks "Amidst tragic loss and injustice, Family Language affirms the power, the reparative work of showing up for one another. It asserts, language can heal, alchemize, and hold us. Nelson has created a salve, order among chaos. Tender, heart opening, and life affirming.” —A.M. Sosa, And I'll Take Out Your Eyes Nicole Nelson earned her MFA from Bennington Writing Seminars. Her work has appeared in The Masters Review Blog, Literary Mama, Fiction Writers Review, and elsewhere. For several years, she was a co-host of the podcast "Writers on Writing." She also holds a PhD in linguistics from Rutgers. Nicole Nelson - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.title: A VERY SCRIBE THANKSGIVING with SCRIBE and R50
events.location: The Phoenix Theater, 201 Washington St., Petaluma, CA, Petaluma, CA
events.description: SCRIBE and R50 (Tribute to RUSH) at the Phoenix! · Scribe (All Original Alternative Progressive Rock Power Trio) Scribe is bringing emotionally charged rock, that blends intricate musicianship with accessible songwriting, into an adventurous power trio! Like a fine dish you can't find at any restaurant, Scribe makes the exact music they want to hear. Dynamic bass-driven arrangements, expressive guitar textures, empathetic vocals, and nuanced power drumming move between intimate passages and explosive climaxes. Influences range from rock to musicals, jam bands, R&B, jazz, folk, and classical music. The result is a sophisticated yet approachable sound, balancing technical precision with raw emotion and memorable hooks. R50 (A Tribute to the music of Rush) R50 wants the incomparable music of Rush to live on. In the spirit of R30 and R40, landmark anniversaries of Rush, R50 is committed to keeping this great music alive to the 50th anniversary of the band and beyond. In that spirit, R50 does the heavy lifting as a trio. R50's number one priority is to recreate and perform the music of Rush with astounding accuracy. The music is at its most powerful when delivered with the most imitated drum fills, incredible bass lines, layered keyboards, signature guitar solos, and natural lead vocals. The result is a fabulous, powerful, high energy show that is guaranteed to have the entire venue air drumming, and singing every song all night long. All eras of Rush's journey are represented in R50's live performances- from the hard rock and prog of the 70s, to the synth era of the 80s, to the rock return of the 90s and 2000s. R50 will bring all the best Rush has to offer to their live shows, from the hits to deep tracks. The show appeals to the die hard Rush fans and new listeners

events.title: LABA's NAME GAME
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) What’s in a Jewish name? Two old friends seek to find out in NAME GAME . A playful and profound exploration of naming, identity, sexuality, and reinvention told through monologues, circus, and dance with a vaudeville flair. Come discover how veteran performers Sara Felder and Yehuda Hyman found their names—and themselves. ACTOR : Sara Felder is an Oakland-based theatre artist She has created and toured solo theatre shows that use humor and circus shtick to activate grass-roots discussion on significant topics. The popular June Bride was about a Jewish lesbian lesbian wedding, while her current show, Class Act, shatters the silence around money. ACTOR : Yehuda Hyman is a multi-disciplinary theater artist. His plays have been produced at McCarter Theatre, Mark Taper Forum, and many other venues. His essays have been published in Seeing Israeli and Jewish Dance; Dance in America, a Reader’s Anthology; Mahol Akshav/Dance Today; The Oxford Handbook of Jewishness in Dance. PRODUCER : Elissa Strauss is a writer, curator and cultural producer based in the Bay Area. She is the author of the book “When You Care” and an artistic director at LABA: A Laboratory for Jewish Culture. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: SHEILA E.
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Queen of Percussion · One of life’s constants for Sheila E. comes down to a simple phrase: follow the beat. And her impeccable inner rhythm is the pulse behind a trailblazing career that still knows no bounds. Family, faith and music were guiding forces for Sheila E. growing up in the Bay Area. In addition to percussionist dad Pete, the Oakland, CA native counts former Santana member/Azteca founder Coke Escovedo and The Dragons front man Mario Escovedo as uncles. Fellow Latin star Tito Puente was her godfather. In addition to being weaned on Latin jazz and Motown, Sheila E. was exposed to a diverse array of Bay Area acts. Those influences ranged from the rock of Jefferson Airplane and the Grateful Dead to the R&B/pop of the Pointer Sisters and the funk of Sly & the Family Stone. “I used to sit on the corner outside of the local community center with Twinkies and 7-Up listening to Sly and Larry Graham rehearse,” remembers Sheila E. “The sounds of the Bay Area molded me.” So it’s no surprise that after such a music-immersive childhood, the gifted, world-class drummer and percussionist began amassing an impressive string of credits playing not only with her dad but also with pioneering talents like George Duke, Herbie Hancock, Marvin Gaye, Diana Ross, Lionel Richie, Prince, Ringo Starr, Gloria Estefan, Beyoncé and Jennifer Lopez. Grammy Award-nominated singer/songwriter behind the seminal hits “The Glamorous Life” and “A Love Bizarre.” A fearless multi-instrumentalist, equally proficient on guitar and bass, actress, mentor and philanthropist. Following a Bay Area gig in the late ‘70s, Sheila E. met Prince backstage. Their Purple Rain recording sessions—including her vocals on the 1984 classic “Erotic City”—morphed into launching her solo career that same year. Debut album The Glamorous Life spun off the Grammy Award-nominated top 10 hit of the same name plus a second top 40 single “The Belle of St. Mark.” Between her ‘80s tenure as drummer, songwriter, and musical director for Prince’s backup band, Sheila E. released two more solo albums ( Romance 1600 and Shelia E.) and scored another classic hit with “A Love Bizarre.” Sheila E.’s fierce, dynamic verve onstage has made her a major concert draw since the ‘90s. Along the way, she has acted in the films “Krush Groove”, “The Adventures of Ford Fairlane”, “Chasing Papi” and launched various music projects (E-Train, C.O.E.D., E Family Band). She added to her arsenal of credits performing on the 2012 Academy Awards with pop hitmaker Pharrell Williams and composer Hans Zimmer. Sheila E. was also among the roster of stars chosen to perform at the 2013 Kennedy Center Honors, whose honorees included artists Herbie Hancock, Billy Joel, and Carlos Santana. Sheila E.'s producing, arranging, and performance talents have been showcased throughout the music and film industry with appearances on The Academy Awards, The Latin Grammy Awards, BET Awards, The American Music Awards, The Kennedy Center Honors, The Summer Olympics, WOW Awards, ALMA's, and The Image Awards, just to name a few. In 2010, Sheila was nominated for an Emmy Award for “Outstanding Music Direction” in recognition of her leadership as musical director for President Obama’s Performance at The White House: Fiesta Latina and again more recently in 2020 for “Let’s Go Crazy” Grammy Salute to Prince. Other projects include The E Family

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.title: Amy Oppenheimer's LOOKING FOR JUSTICE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence. Artist Biography Amy Oppenheimer , a lesbian feminist lawyer and retired judge, has spent her 45-year legal career advocating for women and people of color and speaking truth to power. events.title: LABA's NAME GAME
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) What’s in a Jewish name? Two old friends seek to find out in NAME GAME . A playful and profound exploration of naming, identity, sexuality, and reinvention told through monologues, circus, and dance with a vaudeville flair. Come discover how veteran performers Sara Felder and Yehuda Hyman found their names—and themselves. ACTOR : Sara Felder is an Oakland-based theatre artist She has created and toured solo theatre shows that use humor and circus shtick to activate grass-roots discussion on significant topics. The popular June Bride was about a Jewish lesbian lesbian wedding, while her current show, Class Act, shatters the silence around money. ACTOR : Yehuda Hyman is a multi-disciplinary theater artist. His plays have been produced at McCarter Theatre, Mark Taper Forum, and many other venues. His essays have been published in Seeing Israeli and Jewish Dance; Dance in America, a Reader’s Anthology; Mahol Akshav/Dance Today; The Oxford Handbook of Jewishness in Dance. PRODUCER : Elissa Strauss is a writer, curator and cultural producer based in the Bay Area. events.title: PAUL TAYLOR
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Smooth jazz alto and soprano saxophonist · Paul Taylor grew up in Denver, where he took up the saxophone at the age of seven. He played in school bands and in high school joined a Top 40 band called Mixed Company. Jazz keyboardist Keiko Matsui and her husband, producer Kazu Matsui, discovered him playing at the Catalina Island Jazz Festival and hired him to play in their band. He spent two years with them, and then Kazu Matsui produced his 1995 debut album, On the Horn, which reached the jazz charts and spawned a radio hit in “Til We Meet Again.” Pleasure Seeker, his second album, followed in 1997 and was equally successful. Taylor released his third album, Undercover, on Peak/N-Coded Music in February 2000. Also in 2000, he toured as a special guest artist with the Rippingtons. Subsequent albums Hypnotic (2001), Steppin’ Out (2003), Nightlife (2005), and Ladies’ Choice (2007), all issued by Peak Records, figured high in the contemporary jazz charts, with Ladies’ Choice going all the way to number one. Peak released Taylor’s eighth album, Burnin’, in 2009. Two years later, Taylor returned with the album Prime Time. In 2014, Taylor released Tenacity, which featured guest appearances from Jeff Lorber and Jonathan Fritzen. The album was produced by Dino Esposito, who was also at the controls for Taylor’s 2016 release Countdown, which cracked the Top Ten of the jazz album charts. The number thirteen is cloaked in mysticism, regarded by some cultures as unlucky and revered by others as a sacred good omen or the birth of a new beginning. Saxophonist Paul Taylor’s anticipated new recording and Shanachie debut, It’s A Brand New Day, is his thirteenth recording as a leader. The charming and down-to-earth saxman reveals, “This album in some ways signifies a new cycle for me, as this is my first new recording in three years. The title speaks to my desire to give my fans an optimistic outlook as we approach every brand new day.” The chart-topping saxophonist has enjoyed an enviable career with a string of Billboard #1 hits and collaborations with a genre-crossing list of musicians including Regina Belle, Maxi Priest, Peabo Bryson, and Keiko Matsui. The Rippingtons, Peter White, Euge Groove, Michael Lington, Jamie Jones and Marion Meadows. Taylor confesses, “I simply love creating and making my own music. I am the happiest when I am doing just this. It never gets old.” Danny Weiss, VP of Shanchie’s Jazz A&R, states, “I’ve been an admirer of Paul’s brilliant work dating back to his very first recordings. His superb tone and phrasing are second to none. Paul Taylor is a true icon whose status is well deserved.” “I am an optimist in every way. Each new year, I just keep trying to do my best, which means playing my horn, staying in shape, touring, and continuing to create,” shares Paul Taylor, who is an avid golfer. He scores an ace on It’s A Brand New Day, showcasing ten tracks of nine originals and one Billie Eilish cover, inspired by a character from one of her favorite movies, Spirited Away. Taylor’s saxophones conjure a mesmerizing recreation of Eilish’s ethereal vocals. He shares, “I heard this single over the speakers in a store and was like, ‘Wow, this is pretty cool.” When I heard it again, I knew I had to record my own version on soprano. When I got together with Dino, we put our own spin on it, and I think we paid a beautiful homage to the song. Who knows, maybe Billie will hear it and like it!” The feel-good track “Makin’ Moves” (another Esposito collaboration) features Paul’s fluid and melodic sax juxtaposed against the swinging and driving rhythm section. The hypnotic melody lingers long after the track fades away. The R&B-infused and sultry “Where I Want To Be” shines a spotlight on Paul Taylor’s gorgeous tone, which is amplified by layered effects. The rhythmic breakdown and soulful groove create the perfect place to be. The buoyant “Inner Circle” is a head-nodding jam while “What You Do For Me” is a funky dance groove with Paul Taylor’s sax out front set against a funky and gritty rhythm section. It’s A Brand New Day comes to a fitting finale with the sweet, reflective, and tender “Downtime.” Taylor reflects, “Music is like the wallpaper of our lives. There are songs from certain periods of our lives that stay with us. I hope my fans can grab onto some songs on the album that will stay with them and remind them of good times.

events.title: Mona Chalabi - Ten Lives
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A visually striking exploration of money—and the lack of it—in America told through the lives of ten individuals, from a Pulitzer Prize–winning data journalist and artist “Astonishing . . . Chalabi’s taboo-busting transparency about peoples’ financial lives is revolutionary enough. But it’s the pellucid clarity of her data visualizations that will really change how you understand capitalism.”—Alison Bechdel, bestselling author of Fun Home: A Family Tragicomic Anna has a comfortable life in a mansion in Maine thanks to her husband (well, his parents, really) until he suddenly asks for a divorce. In Arizona, Hunter is a U.S. veteran, feeling ashamed about claiming disability benefits. Then there’s Levi, who is trying to pay off his debts from a gambling addiction, one social media video at a time. And Christian, stifled by his job at an Amazon warehouse before a union-organizing effort offers a way out for his comrades and his young kids. Ten people, ten different incomes, all of them afraid for their futures. For five years, data journalist Mona Chalabi followed them all, documenting how wealth shaped their feelings, their choices, their identities, and their insecurities. She researched the data behind their taxes, groceries, inheritances, and so much more to understand the systems that keep people stuck. But then, she too found herself facing the same fears, when her mother’s sudden illness and subsequent medical bills threatened her own financial safety and made the questions she had been writing about all too real. How much money is enough? To live a “good” life? To protect the people you love in an emergency? Interweaving her own story with those of her interviewees and illustrated throughout with the data visualizations for which Chalabi is renowned, Ten Lives asks how much wealth it takes to be safe in the United States. It explores how difficult it is for us to be honest and open about what we have and argues that until we get better at it, we will never be able to address the underlying problems that drive inequality and insecurity for us all. “We live in an insanely unequal world. Does the concentration of wealth and resources into fewer and fewer hands make a difference? This book explores how deeply relevant inequality is—how it molds our minds and bends our moralities. It’s the most vivid and readable exploration of the wealth gap I’ve ever read. Anyone who cares about a better future should read this.” —Brian Eno, producer and songwriter “Mona Chalabi writes with frank, engaging precision about what we’re all really wondering about: Money, and all the big, sinister financial machinery that makes each of our lives ‘just happen to be’ what they are. Ten Lives is Jane Austen without all the boring romance stuff, and with a sweeping lens that feels like finally looking up from your own narrow little corner. Or like eating something utterly satisfying you weren’t expecting. And the diagrams—both informative and funny. I️ recommend this book enthusiastically to everyone. I️ can't wait to reread it.” —Liana Finck, author of Let There Be Light “ Ten Lives is a brilliant melding of rage, empathy, and tactical rigor that maps the emotional intimacy of income inequality. Chalabi has a rare ability to bring statistics to life, teasing out the human stories buried within data to illuminate uncomfortable societal truths. Ten Lives cuts cleanly through the numbers, sharpening how we see the world.” —Tessa Hulls, Pulitzer Prize–winning author of Feeding Ghosts Mona Chalabi is an award-winning writer and illustrator. Her work has earned her a Pulitzer Prize, an honorary fellowship at the British Science Association, an Emmy nomination, a fellowship from New America, and recognition from the Royal Statistical Society. In recent years, her art has been exhibited at the Tate, the Smithsonian Design Museum, and the Brooklyn Museum. Her writing and illustrations have been featured in The New Yorker , The New York Review of Books, and The Guardian . events.description: Susan Spungen is a cook, food stylist, recipe developer, and cookbook author. She was the Founding Food Editor at Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia from its inception until 2003, where she built one of the most influential visual food brands in publishing history. She served as Culinary Consultant and Food Stylist on the feature films Julie & Julia , It’s Complicated , and Eat, Pray, Love . She is the author of Recipes: A Collection for the Modern Cook , What’s a Hostess to Do? , and Strawberries (A Short Stack Edition) and co-author of the bestselling Martha Stewart’s Hors d’Oeuvres Handbook . Each year during the holiday season, she releases coveted cookie content through her Susanality newsletter, highlighting favorites and debuting new recipes. She lives in New York City and East Hampton, NY. Kristina Cho is an award-winning cookbook author, recipe developer, home cook, baker, food stylist, and food photographer. Her groundbreaking debut cookbook, Mooncakes and Milk Bread, won two James Beard awards and was described as an instant classic by The New York Times. Her latest cookbook, Chinese Enough, is a tribute to Chinese American home cooking, inspired by her family, growing up in the Midwest, and life in California. Cookie Queen: 80+ Irresistible, Doable, Giftable Recipes- Making cookies is both an art and a craft. With Cookie Queen , you have an exciting and invaluable resource whether for a single good cookie recipe or for embarking on a cookie box project, a holiday activity that in recent years has risen to the level of competitive sport. Want to bake but not sure which cookies would go well together? This book takes a modular approach, so whether you want to make three different cookies or thirteen, picking from the different sections will give your boxes and platters variety. No need to spend a lot of time planning to figure out what will taste good and look good together. This mix and match approach is baked into the concept. Try recipes such as: Tiger-Striped Sables Earl Grey Shortbread with Blood Orange Glaze Striped Black and Whites Chewy Ginger Crinkles Strawberry Iced Oatmeal Cookies Pecan Linzers There is no one more qualified to take you on this baking journey of joy than Susan Spungen. As food editor at Martha Stewart Living for twelve years from its founding in 1991, Susan is unmatched in her wealth of knowledge in the food world. Each year during the holiday season, Susan releases her coveted cookie content on her Susanality newsletter, highlighting her favorites as well as debuting new recipes. Cookies are connection. Whether making them together or sharing the delicious results with others, no other food has the power to bring people together and spread as much joy as cookies can.

events.title: Coming of Age in Macholand
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: The hidden costs of becoming men. · In 2019, Sandeep Brar, a twenty-seven-year-old Punjabi man from an elite household, gunned down five members of his family before taking his own life after a date was set for his wedding. In his suicide note, he described feeling trapped by society’s expectations and condemned to a marriage - and a life - he had not chosen. His final act was horrific. But the question he left behind was harder to dismiss: What happens when patriarchy tells men they are powerful while giving them almost no freedom to decide who they will become? In Coming of Age in Macholand , anthropologist Harjant Gill explores how young men respond to a rigid patriarchy - submitting to it, rebelling against it, trying to escape it, and sometimes coming undone by it. Drawing on four years of research, conducted over a decade, Gill brings readers into the intimate worlds of Punjabi boys as they learn what it means to become men. In this deeply personal blend of memoir, ethnography, and social investigation, he makes a compelling case against a system that brutalizes women and queer people while also constricting the emotional, sexual, and intimate lives of the men it claims to serve. Gill will be in conversation with anthropologist David Vine to discuss what men must relinquish – and what they might reclaim – to become truly free. Harjant Gill is an anthropologist, filmmaker, and writer whose work explores masculinity, migration, sexuality, and the intimate effects of patriarchy in South Asia and its diasporas. He is the director of several award-winning documentaries which have been broadcast on the BBC, PBS, and Doordarshan (Indian National TV). Gill’s work has been supported by the Fulbright Program, the Whiting Foundation, the Wenner-Gren Foundation, the Point Foundation, the Institute for Citizens and Scholars, and the American Institute of Indian Studies. Born in Chandigarh (India) and raised in Northern California, he now lives in Washington, DC, and teaches anthropology at Towson University. Gill’s website is www.HarjantGill.com David Vine is the author of a trilogy of books about war and peace including The United States of War: A Global History of America’s Endless Conflicts, from Columbus to the Islamic State , which was a finalist for the LA Times Book Award in History. David has written about militarized masculinity in the US military and its role in the sexual violence epidemic in the armed forces, as well as how gender and masculinity shape US foreign policy and war making. David, a Clio's neighbor, was a professor of anthropology at American University in Washington, DC, for 18 years, before resigning with the rank of full professor in 2024.

events.title: Return to Center: Exploring Stability, Mobility & Ease with Vickie Russell Bell
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves..



Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition.

Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.

events.title: Half-Day Silent Unguided Retreat
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice.
This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods.
There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of
meditation, all are welcome.

The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive
between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before
the first bell.

The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation:
9:30 AM – 10:10 AM
10:20 AM – 11:00 AM
11:10 AM – 11:50 AM

A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period.
The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between
sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom.
Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep
voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire
morning.

You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during
a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and
the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice
elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell.

The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website.

Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by
12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely
manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

events.title: Yirah: A Jewish Psychedelic Integration Circle with Dr. Lyssa Menard
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Psychedelics can surface anything, including awe, insight, grief, trauma, even ancestral or collective pain. Without support, it can be hard to make sense of what happened, let alone carry it forward in a meaningful way.

Yirah—often translated as awe, reverence, or a kind of holy trembling—is the feeling of standing at the edge of something vast, meaningful, and not entirely knowable. Psychedelic experiences often bring us right to that edge. This Jewish psychedelic integration circle offers a space to meet those moments together, within the safety of Jewish community and the container of Jewish teachings. Together, we make meaning of what we’ve seen and felt, and begin the slow, human work of weaving those insights into our lives.

Each monthly, drop-in circle includes grounding and intention-setting, a brief orientation, an experiential practice (meditation, movement, somatic work, or parts work), and small- and large-group sharing. This is a supported peer group rather than psychotherapy, designed to foster connection, reflection, and practical integration.

Note: This is an affinity space exclusively for people who identify as Jewish—by heritage or conversion—including those who are part-Jewish. Those who do not meet these criteria will not be admitted. To support safety and connection in a time of deep division, we also hold a clear and intentional container: we do not engage in political discussion here. The focus is on integration, presence, and community.

Whether you’re new to Jewish practice or finding your way back in, whether your journeys have been expansive, messy, or disorienting—you’re welcome here.

Facilitator Bio: 
Lyssa Menard, PhD, is a clinical psychologist, psychedelic therapist, and professor at Northwestern University Medical School who specializes in trauma, integrative medicine, and what it actually takes to change. She’s been featured in places like CNN and The New York Times, but her real work happens in circles like this one—where people show up as they are and do the brave, uncomfortable, life-changing work of integration.

Jewish by birth and in a more recent, intentional deep dive into Jewish life, Lyssa brings a deep respect for tradition alongside a willingness to question, wrestle, and reinterpret—in the long Jewish tradition of meaning-making. After all, Israel can be translated as “one who wrestles with God.” Her relationship to psychedelics is both professional and personal. She’s experienced their power, their limitations, and everything in between—which makes her equal parts skeptic and believer.

events.title: Walter Stahr - William Howard Taft
events.location: Book Passage Ferry Building 1 Ferry Building San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: From an acclaimed New York Times bestselling biographer comes a remarkable new look at the only man to serve as both president and chief justice of the United States. The conventional wisdom is that William Howard Taft was a mediocre president, a man almost without political skills. Yet Taft’s modest, judicial approach to the presidency—he served as a state and then federal judge before entering the White House—looks quite extraordinary in retrospect. Admired by those on either side of the aisle for his genial personality and hearty chuckle, Taft spent his four years in office reducing tariffs, eliminating federal deficits, pursuing government efficiency, avoiding foreign wars, and honoring the Constitution. Yet even Taft’s presidency would serve as merely a prelude to one of the greatest second acts in American history. More than any chief justice since John Marshall, Taft transformed the judicial branch, particularly as the principal proponent of the legislation that allowed the Supreme Court to begin choosing its cases—and thus to devote its energy entirely to deciding key constitutional and statutory issues. A rigorously researched and elegant account of five decades of public service, William Howard Taft offers a bold reassessment of a forgotten great American. Walter Stahr is the New York Times bestselling author of Seward: Lincoln’s Indispensable Man , Stanton: Lincoln’s War Secretary , and John Jay: Founding Father . A two-time winner of the Seward Award for Excellence in Civil War Biography, Stahr practiced law in Washington and Asia for more than two decades. An honors graduate of Stanford University and Harvard Law School, he now lives in Newport Beach, California. events.title: Rebecca Handler with Daniel Handler - In the Round
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Rebecca Handler the award-winning author of Edie Richter is Not Alone presents her profoundly moving new novel, In the Round . "Only Rebecca Handler can write a play within a novel within an identity crisis that comes with cat jokes, an extraordinary act of kindness, betrayal, and disdain for musical theater . In The Round is profound and pithy and not like any other book you will ever read in just one sitting. Wow." —Marcy Dermansky Rebecca will be joined in conversation by Daniel Handler. A woman is consumed by the belief that her life has become a play. Lively, moving, and at moments astonishing, Rebecca Handler’s Kafkaesque literary mystery is either a reflection on middle-aged malaise or the cover-up for a murderous plot. Or maybe it’s a theatrical production. We meet In the Round’s unnamed protagonist a few minutes after she’s become convinced she’s a victim of a home invasion. Nothing is missing from her family’s San Francisco home, but everything feels wrong. Certain a burglar was there recently, the woman lurks about her own house during a sleepless night of questioning. Have you ever been sure that someone is watching you? Does a lifetime of putting others first lead to permanent paranoia? Have we all built versions of ourselves we’re performing for an unseen audience? In the depths of one strange night in her living room, she seeks answers from her teenage son and her troubled neighbor. She dances to ’90s music and buys herself underwear online. And she wonders: Will she be able to solve the mystery of her own purpose so she can save herself? “I read the opening pages of this remarkable book with a thrill of finding myself in the hands of a gifted conjuror, and finished in a state of total enchantment, profoundly moved.” —Michael Chabon "In this delicately immersive novel, quiet shifts of scale, reminiscent of the great Paula Fox, evoke a whole sense of our time. Here, the dynamics of witnessing and surveillance are the constant texture of consciousness. Mapping the movements of the mind of an ordinary woman at home in the night, Rebecca Handler shows us what makes a life worth watching: access to the everyday endurance of suffering and the reality of joy." —Lucy Corin "What a beguiling storyteller Rebecca Handler is! In the Round gives the readers an enthralling pleasure of being inside a character and watching the character from outside, which is perhaps akin to the most important experience of living with attention and reflection." —Yiyun Li "I wandered into this literary labyrinth late at night, thinking I'll just take a quick peek at what's inside. Instead, I found myself forgoing sleep to follow its twists and turns, surprised and delighted, reluctant to return to the real world." —Soma Mei-Sheng Frazier " In the Round is the most exciting, original novel I've read in years. I couldn't put it down and couldn't stop thinking about it long after I'd read the breathtaking final words. Fans of Katie Kitamura, Jenny Offill, and Rachel Cusk: Here is your new favorite writer." —Joanna Rakoff "I read the spectacular IN THE ROUND in a single delighted sitting, entranced by the possibilities opened up, the life made urgent and real. Bravissima!" —R. O. Kwon Rebecca Handler’s debut novel, Edie Richter is Not Alone , received a Kirkus Starred Review and was longlisted for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize. Her short stories have been published and awarded in several anthologies. A MacDowell fellow, Rebecca lives in San Francisco with her husband and, when they’re not off pursuing their own adventures, their two daughters. Daniel Handler is the author of seven novels, including Why We Broke Up , All The Dirty Parts and Bottle Grove, and most recently a memoir, And Then? And Then? What Else? As Lemony Snicket, he is the author of far too many books for children, including Poison for Breakfast, the four-volume All The Wrong Questions and the thirteen-volume A Series of Unfortunate Events , which has been adapted for screen and television. He lives in San Francisco with the illustrator Lisa Brown, to whom he is married. events.title: Marie's Tree
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: Implosions and Injustice in San Francisco · Marie Harrison (1948-2019), an environmental activist of San Francisco’s Bayview Hunters Point, spent her life fighting for basic services such as housing, energy, and employment that had become money makers for a few but a dream deferred for her community. What she endured, from the brown water that ran out of her taps at Geneva Towers, the blood that ran from her grandson’s nose while living next door to the PG&E smokestacks, and the fear of radiation poisoning from one of the country’s worst superfund cleanup sites, are environmental injustices that citizens of the United States suffer every day. Freelance journalist Tom Molanphy will be in conversation with Arieann Harrison , ennvironmental activist and Marie's daughter, about Marie's life, legacy, and the continued fight for environmental justice. Half of the book proceeds will go to the Marie Harrison Community Foundation . Tom Molanphy ’s journalism has appeared in 48 Hills, USA Today Travel.com, Earth Island Journal, and The San Francisco Chronicle , among other publications. His work as a 2022 USC Annenberg Center for Health Journalism Data Fellow led to a 2023 1st Place Award in Environmental Reporting from the California News Publishers Association. His essay “The Road Less: John Huston, Blue-Footed Boobies and Me” earned a 2017 Bay Area Travel Writers award, and his short story “Of Subareas and Public Bathrooms” was included in the California Prose Directory. His last book was a memoir, Loud Memories Of A Quiet Life . He is a member of the Society of Environmental Journalists and teaches journalism, composition, creative writing and art/design appreciation classes at the Academy of Art University in San Francisco. Arieann Harrison is the Founder and Executive Director of the Marie Harrison Community Foundation . Arieann Harrison is a resident of San Francisco District 10 and has lived and worked in the Bayview Community for 30+ years. Her work includes providing social services, employment opportunities, community resources, and engaging in environmental advocacy with local D10 residents, taking an all-inclusive, solutions-based approach to providing good information for the best outcome that will lead to preservation of life. #CanWeLive has become the rallying cry of a community that has gone long overlooked when it comes to social, environmental, and economic justice.

events.title: ISAIAH SHARKEY
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Confluence of modern soul, jazz, R&B, and Black American guitar tradition · Isaiah Sharkey stands at the confluence of modern soul, jazz, R&B, and Black American guitar tradition, carrying forward a lineage that links George Benson, Curtis Mayfield, Wes Montgomery, and Jimi Hendrix while forging a vocabulary entirely his own. A Grammy Award–winning guitarist, vocalist, composer, and producer, Sharkey has become one of the most respected musicians of his generation—celebrated for his sophisticated harmonic sensibility, unmistakable tone, and ability to shape-shift effortlessly between musical worlds. Born and raised on Chicago’s North Side in a deeply musical family, Sharkey was immersed from childhood in gospel, jazz, and classic R&B. His father, a working musician, recognized early his son’s extraordinary ear and feel, guiding him through professional-level repertoire before most children his age would form basic chords. By the time he was 14, Sharkey was touring nationally; by his late teens, he had already become a first-call session player in Chicago’s tight-knit recording community. Sharkey’s breakthrough into the international spotlight came through his long-standing creative relationship with D’Angelo. His guitar work on D’Angelo’s landmark album Black Messiah earned him a Grammy Award and positioned him among the most innovative guitarists shaping contemporary Black music. From that point forward, Sharkey’s trajectory accelerated: he became a go-to collaborator for a wide range of artists including John Mayer, H.E.R., Robert Glasper, Cory Henry, Lettuce, Chris Dave & The Drumhedz, Lalah Hathaway, Common, Paul Simon, Brian McKnight , Greg Phillinganes, among many others. As a solo artist, Sharkey has developed a distinctive, emotionally resonant sound that blends deep-pocket groove, virtuosic improvisation, and songwriter-driven storytelling. His current album, RED , introduced audiences to his modern fusion of soul, R&B, jazz, and guitar-based narrative. His follow-up projects—each expanding his sonic palette—solidify his standing as an artist capable of speaking fluently to instrumental purists and mainstream audiences alike. Sharkey is equally at home on global festival stages, intimate jazz clubs, and stadium tours. His work has spanned from serving as an MD for Raphael Saadiq's NBA All-Stars televised performance to late-night television appearances to the Grammys televised tribute to Quincy Jones and Blue Note residencies. Yet his most defining characteristic remains his musical integrity: a commitment to depth, craft, and authenticity. A multi-instrumentalist, arranger, and producer, Sharkey’s creative range continues to grow. His forthcoming releases explore new integrations of analog and electronic texture, guitar-forward harmonic architecture, and songwriting rooted in personal truth. Whether performing his own music or elevating the work of others, Sharkey brings the same signature qualities—precision, warmth, spirituality, and an unshakeable sense of groove. Today, Isaiah Sharkey is widely regarded as one of the most vital contemporary voices in the continuum of guitar excellence. His artistry honors his lineage while pushing the idiom forward, ensuring that his influence will resonate for decades to come.

events.title: Embodiment Practice: Mindful Movement + Stillness with Suzanne (Zan) Beahrs
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest.

Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. 

Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. 

Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. 

Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space.

Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like.

About Suzanne (Zan):
With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley

Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons):
