events.title: Melissa Clark Author Talk • The Big Book of Dinner: Recipes and Rules (and How to Break Them)
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Melissa Clark is the New York Times bestselling author of Dinner in One , as well as Dinner: Changing the Game , Dinner in an Instant , Comfort in an Instant , Kid in the Kitchen , and Dinner in French . She is a staff writer for The New York Times Food section, where she writes their daily newsletter, and her wildly popular food column, "A Good Appetite." The winner of multiple James Beard and IACP awards, Melissa earned an MFA in writing from Columbia, and her work has been selected for The Best American Food Writing . The Big Book of Dinner- Acclaimed New York Times food writer and James Beard Award–winning author Melissa Clark presents her ultimate guide to cooking just about anything, with 175 any-night recipes—plus 150 tested variations—and lessons to make cooking easy, intuitive, and a total joy. Working with a chef’s creativity for flavor and a home cook’s sensibility for ease, Melissa Clark has been one of America’s favorite recipe creators for decades, helping millions make stunningly great food with flair and no fuss. And now, with The Big Book of Dinner she gives you her ultimate treasure trove: all the recipes you need, the ways to riff off of them, and lessons you learn from them along the way to make you a great cook. She shares the building blocks that make these recipes work, so you’ll know exactly how to follow them to perfection, or how to go off-script if you want and to make it your own. With Melissa’s friendly instructions guiding the way, you can take classic Italian-American Meatballs , and switch them up with aromatic spices reminiscent of Middle Eastern kibbe, or use them in an easy sheet-pan dinner with roasted vegetables. Super-quick Sweet and Spicy Chicken with Cumin and Honey can be transformed with ginger and marmalade for a fresh punch, or honey mustard and lemon for a different spin. Throughout, there are signature Melissa favorites like Creamy Corn Pasta with Tomatoes and Chile Flakes , lessons on cooking the perfect steak or nailing a braise every time, plenty of vegetables and plant-based dishes, a baker’s dozen (and then some) of perfect desserts, and beautiful photographs for every recipe. Whether you’re a novice in the kitchen or a longtime cook, a devotee of Melissa’s or just getting to know her, The Big Book of Dinner will be your cooking companion for a lifetime.

events.title: Deconstructing Yourself with Michael Taft
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. 

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

events.title: Americans Without Borders
events.location: Clio’s Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: The hidden history of American radicals abroad · One night in 1940, a group of Stalinists opened fire on Leon Trotsky’s compound in Mexico City. In the end, the victim was not Trotsky, but his bodyguard: a young American named Sheldon Harte. For investigative journalist Julia Harte, the quest to uncover the truth about Sheldon—her father’s second cousin—was just the beginning of her discovery. Her new book, Americans Without Borders: The Radical Activists Who Fought for US Ideals Abroad While Facing Political Persecution at Home reveals the hidden two-hundred-year history of Americans who traveled abroad to join revolutionary liberation movements—and in return were labeled radicals by the U.S. government. The surprising stories Harte uncovers include those of Black veterans of the Spanish Civil War who helped launch the civil rights movement; the forgotten Native American contingent in Nicaragua’s Sandinista/Contra conflict; Elaine Mokhtefi’s work with the Algerian National Liberation Front; Melinda Paras and her organization of Filipinos against the repressive US-backed Marcos regime; and many more. Through meticulous research and on-the-ground reporting, Harte brings her subjects to life in deeply personal detail, exploring not only their heroic sides but also the tensions between their actions and ideals. Interrogating how and why activists were branded as threats by an expanding security state, Americans Without Borders asks what makes a ‘radical’. Join author Julia Harte for a conversation about the long history of transnational radicalism as an irrepressibly American tradition. She’ll be joined by journalist, writer, and producer Sonia Paul . Julia Harte is an investigative reporter in New York City. For the past decade, she has covered U.S. national affairs and the Justice Department for Reuters. Her writing has also appeared in publications including Harper's Magazine , The Nation , Slate , National Geographic , The Center for Public Integrity , and Lapham's Quarterly . Sonia Paul is an award-winning independent journalist, writer and producer who specializes in investigating how power hierarchies and transnational issues impact state systems and individual and community identities. Her stories have been published widely, in outlets like WIRED , Mother Jones , Harper’s Magazine , NPR, 99% Invisible and BBC World Service. She is also the host of a new podcast from Berkeley Social Sciences and a forthcoming podcast based on her reporting. Sonia is a Bay Area native and lives in Oakland. She is on Instagram @sonipaul.

events.description: Two Voices, One Purpose. A Night of Gospel Brilliance, Soul & Praise · Join us for an unforgettable night of Gospel, Soul, and Praise as we usher in the holiday season with the angelic voice of gospel singer-songwriter Sylvia Anderson and her anointed guest, Grammy Award winner Darrel Walls, gospel legend Derrick Hall, and the music direction and ministry of Carl Wheeler. An inspiring evening of deliverance, celebration, and worship you won’t want to miss. Presented by Sylvia Anderson & Mark Elliott of the A-list Musiq Circle - Your Bay Area Who's Who Entertainment network. With Special Guest Host TBA. A gifted gospel artist with an angelic voice and a heart devoted to ministry, Sylvia Anderson has spent over 40 years using her God-given talent to inspire, uplift, and spread the love of Jesus Christ. Born into a family rich in musical and spiritual heritage, her journey began at the tender age of five when she discovered her ability to sing. Guided by her father, a preacher and singer, and her mother, a vocalist, she was nurtured in a household where music and faith were inseparable. She first sang with the Coleman Sisters, under the influence of her father, Willie Coleman, and continued to grow musically, sharing her voice with groups such as Derrick Hall & Company and the Center of Hope Choir. Her remarkable gift has also led her to sing background for gospel greats, including Tramaine Hawkins and Nona Brown, and appear on BET’s renowned Bobby Jones Gospel Hour. A true musician, she’s sung in concerts, gospel festivals, weddings, homegoing services and private events, further enhancing her ability to minister through music. In addition to her musical journey, she has served faithfully in ministry and is currently a minister at Covenant Worship Center in Berkeley, California. Beyond the stage, she is deeply committed to serving her community. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Theology and is the owner of a care home for children, as well as actively involved in foster care initiatives—demonstrating her passion for nurturing and uplifting the next generation. A woman of many roles, she is a devoted mother of three, a loving wife, grandmother, sister, and friend. For over 30 years, she has also worked as a professional hairstylist, touching lives both inside and outside the church, and retired after 33 years from the medical field. Rooted in Oakland, California, her life’s mission is simple yet powerful: to send God’s love through every song, every act of service, and every life she encounters. Her favorite song, “Because He Lives,” reflects the foundation of her faith and the message she carries wherever she goes. Darrel Walls is the eldest sibling and eldest member of The Walls Group, the acclaimed four-sibling group celebrated for their distinctive harmonies, musicianship, and progressive sound. A gifted vocalist, musician, and creative force, Darrel has long been an integral part of the group’s unmistakable musical identity. Stepping into his own as a solo artist, he recorded his debut solo project, Heart of Mine, with Grammy-winning artist and producer PJ Morton, earning the 2026 Grammy Award for Best Gospel Album. His breakout solo season has continued with three Stellar Award wins, including Artist of the Year and Contemporary Male Artist of the Year, while his single “ABLE” reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Gospel Airplay chart. His solo journey has further established him as one of gospel music’s standout voices. While continuing to bring his unmistakable sound to The Walls Group, Darrel is building an exciting solo legacy of his own.

events.title: Keltie Knight - The F*ck Them Theory
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: We are thrilled to present an evening with three-time Emmy Award-winning TV personality and New York Times bestselling author Keltie Knight, celebrating her new self-help book, The Fck Them Theory —a guide for anyone who is done being the bigger person and shrinking themselves. Joined in conversation by Holly Madison, Keltie will lead a no-rules night featuring a pep talk, celeb conversation, ugly-cry writing session, meet & greet, cool merch, and a signed book. A Special Note For You From the Author: I wrote a whole book telling you to stop shrinking yourself. Now I'm coming to your city to say it to your face. This is a full-body, full-feels night for the ambitious, exhausted, gloriously over-it human who's done apologizing for being "too much" and ready to weaponize it instead. Here's what I'm bringing: I'm inviting my famous friends to grill me during a book talk in each city, I'm bringing my favorite musical artists to play acoustic and make us get in our feels when I can, I'm telling the stories I couldn't keep in the book because they're too juicy, and I'm signing your books and hugging you. About the Book Everyone's favorite TV and podcast host is back ... with a vengeance. After realizing that every win in her life came right after being underestimated, rejected, or told she wasn't enough, Keltie Knight decided to build a theory around it: The F*ck Them Theory. Part memoir, part manifesto, The F*ck Them Theory is your permission slip to stop apologizing and start transforming rejection into power. It's not about bitterness, it's about alchemy. It's about turning humiliation into humor, heartbreak into healing, and rage into reinvention. Keltie goes where most "empowerment" books don't dare. She shares raw, unfiltered stories from behind the curtain--the breakdowns, the pills, the plastic surgery, the feud the tabloids never caught, and the family secrets she's never shared ... until now. The F*ck Them Theory is for anyone who's been underestimated or is tired of being "grateful for the opportunity" when they deserved so much more. If you've ever wanted a best friend who tells the truth, drops the act, and still shows up in sequins, then welcome home. About the Author Keltie Knight is a three-time Emmy Award–winning television personality, New York Times bestselling author, and People’s Choice Award–nominated podcast host. She currently hosts E! Live From The Red Carpet and is widely known for her work on Entertainment Tonight, The Insider, and CBS’s SUPERFAN, which she also created and executive produced. As co-creator and host of the hit podcast LadyGang, with over 300 million downloads and a New York Times bestselling book, Knight has built a pop-culture empire rooted in female friendship, ambition, and unapologetic authenticity. Her fashion and cultural influence have been featured in Vogue, Elle, and The New York Times. Keltie spearheaded and created LADYWORLD, the first-ever podcast festival dedicated to female voices, bringing together over 3,000 attendees and generating more than $1M in brand partnerships. Positioned at the forefront of innovation in the female podcast space, she continues to develop new formats that expand how audiences experience content, community, and live events. A sought-after content creator and brand ambassador, Keltie has developed long-term partnerships with brands such as Marshalls and Fabletics, consistently translating audience trust into high-performing, multi-platform campaigns. Her first full length solo book "The F*CK Them Theory: Self-Help For People Who are Done Being the Bigger Person was released through Blackstone Publishing Nov. 2026. In addition to her on-air work, Knight is an investor and advisor to ALTA, an AI-powered fashion technology platform recently named to Time’s 100 Best Inventions of the Year, recognized by Vogue as a Best Invention, and announced as an official AI fashion partner of the Council of Fashion Designers of America (CFDA). events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) You think it’s hard to herd cats? Try getting seven sub-personalities to agree on anything! Wild Child, Rosie, and Mauve love living in San Francisco, but Raisin and Hannah want to go back to Colorado. When Cora soothes Raisin with cinnamon rolls, Hannah complains that sugar is bad for us. Hannah and Wild Child lock horns over Wild Child’s party behavior. Rosie wants to go shopping for clothes and skin-care products, but Mauve wants to spend the money on writers’ conferences and research for her novel. The conflicts never end, and the arguments create quite a din. All seven of Janet’s sub-personalities are delighted to have this opportunity to give their opinions of Janet’s life choices! Janet Thornburg (writer/performer) is a soloist whose solo show Cognitive Divine won the Best Full-Length Comedy award in the In Front of Your Eyes Festival 2026 at the Marsh. She has written and performed eight solo shows in San Francisco at venues including The Marsh, StageWerx Theatre, Theatre Rhinoceros, Theatre of Yugen, Venue Nine, Next Stage Theatre,Young Performers’ Theatre, and the Solo Mio Festival. Her multi-character play Dinner Roles was presented at the San Francisco Repertory Theatre, and her play Antony and Cleopatra Meet Godzilla enjoyed two runs at the Intersection Theatre. She holds an MFA in playwriting from San Francisco State University and an MFA in fiction from Warren Wilson College. Her fiction has been widely published in literary journals, and Rhubarb Pie , a collection of her short stories, was published by Thunderegg Press. For further information about her performances and publications, visit www.janetthornburg.com. events.title: DEMOLA THE VIOLINIST
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Internationally known award-winning recording artist & multi-instrumentalist · Demola the Violinist returns to Yoshi’s Oakland with a holiday vibe that’s straight-up next level. This is where classical finesse meets street energy , flipping the season with bold beats, symphonic melodies, and that signature Demola swagger. The global phenomenon brings a dope fusion of Afrobeats , R&B , Hip Hop , and Soul —turning winter into a full-on cultural avalanche to kick off the Holiday season. From viral social media star to award-winning showman, Demola delivers a festive, high‑energy experience that never falls short of amazing. This isn’t just a concert. It’s a holiday “ turn-up ”, a sonic joyride , and a seasonal celebration with real Oakland flavor you don’t want to miss. Presented by Kim Pruitt of KP Entertainment Connections, Mark Elliot of the A-List Musiq Circle, with Special Guest Host TBA. DEMOLA the VIOLINIST BIO: Demola, known to fans as “Demola the Violinist,” is an internationally recognized musician, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and award-winning self-taught multi-genre violinist. Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Demola moved to the United States to pursue his solo music career, blending his love for Afrobeat, reggae, R&B, hip-hop, pop, and country into a sound that is distinctly his own. In 2024, Demola’s career reached new heights, fueled by his vibrant social media presence and viral performances. With over 6 million followers and millions of streams across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, his videos regularly attract millions of views, making him one of the most-followed and celebrated violinists worldwide. His performances captivate global audiences, and his fanbase continues to expand with each viral hit. This year, Demola launched his highly successful “One in a Million 2.0” tour, performing in over 20 cities and mesmerizing audiences with original songs like “ONE IN A MILLION,” “MBAPPE,” and “LOVA,” which have collectively amassed millions of streams. He also made waves with his feature on the song “FORGIVE OUR TRESPASSES,” showcasing viral Afrobeat across the US and performing at Coachella. A hometown hero in Houston, Texas, Demola, has performed the national anthem for major sports teams, including the Houston Astros, Rockets, Dynamo, and Texans, before crowds of up to 70,000 people. He has also shared the stage with country music star Jelly Roll, performing for 74,000 fans at the Houston Rodeo. Demola is a fan favorite on television as well, with appearances on Good Morning America Online, FOX 26 Houston, CultureMap Houston, 97.9 KBXX Houston, FOX 31 Denver, WGN-9 Chicago, Black News Channel, and many others. His innovative fusion of genres has made him one of the first artists of his kind, captivating listeners with the melodic beauty of his violin and proving that he is truly one in a million. Demola - Afrobeat & Hip-hop Violinist, Artist, Singer

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.description: Join us for a winter/holiday cardmaking class! Students will make a standing star card--a perfect fold for the holidays. This gorgeous card has plenty of shine to express your heartfelt greetings. Learn to create a glittering star that folds flat to fit in a 5x 7 envelope but pops up to a 3-dimensional standing card when opened. events.title: Willow Older with Erin Gordon - Get Off That Screen!
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: With its humor, candor, delightful illustrations, and (of course) a bit of implied profanity, Get Off That Screen! is a gift book for adults that will resonate with ANYONE trying to raise, educate, or connect with kids in this digital age: from parents, caregivers, and grandparents to teachers, coaches, and therapists—and every adult in between. Willow will be joined in conversation by San Francisco author Erin Gordon. More than just “a balm for our shared exasperation”, Get Off That Screen! includes an Afterword with practical guidelines from author and parenting/technology expert Katherine Martinko and an extensive Resources section with books, events, and organizations to help families enjoy screen-free time, together. Is your kid’s obsession with screens driving you nuts? Do you spend your days begging and bribing your kiddo to “ Get off that screen! ”? This book can’t eliminate screen addiction (including, ahem , your own). But it can help you vent your frustrations about raising kids in the digital age. Willow Older’s lighthearted approach to a serious problem will make you giggle and groan—and you’ll find tips for reducing your family’s screen time, too. “An all-too-relatable tribute to the challenge of prying kids—and ourselves!—off of screens.” —Catherine Price, #1 New York Times bestselling author of How to Break Up With Your Phone “Willow Older injects some much-needed humor and hope into an otherwise overwhelming topic.”— Katherine Martinko, author of Hold the Phone and Childhood Unplugged and creator of The Analog Family newsletter “Just what the doctor ordered for the screen-addicted generation.”— Zibby Owens, host of the “Totally Booked” podcast “This whimsical tale is a balm for our shared exasperation.”— Tiffany Shlain, artist, Emmy-nominated filmmaker, and author of 2 4/6: Giving up Screens One Day a Week to Get More Time, Creativity, and Connection “A Shel Silverstein-esque author for the digital age, Willow Older makes you laugh out loud and feel seen in the best of ways.”— Erin Gordon, author of PEEPS and Look What You Made Me Do Willow Older is an author, illustrator, speaker, and ghostwriter in Mill Valley. She’s the co-founder of Today I Noticed mindfulness and the co-author of Today I Noticed: A Little Book of Mindfulness that Will Change the Way You See the World (Blue Star Press, 2023). For that book, which is now in its third printing and has been translated into multiple languages, Willow and her co-author, Deborah Huber, were thrilled to hold their launch event in front of a large and enthusiastic crowd at Book Passage, where all 40+ books in stock sold out. Erin Gordon is a San Francisco author whose work spans fiction, memoir and contemporary romance. A Stanford-trained journalist, she brings decades of reporting and storytelling experience to her conversation with Willow Older. events.title: Steve Thomas - The Last Navigator
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: This richly illustrated lecture* will take us into a world of ocean navigation largely unknown to the West, a world in which the traditional navigator’s only directional tools are the stars, the ocean swells and the flight paths of birds. In 1983 and 1984 I spent eleven months on Satawal Island and in the Western Carolines as an apprentice to Mau Piailug, then one of the last paliuw, captains fully initiated in the Talk of Navigation, the closely guarded, ancient practices around reading the cosmos and the seas. I chronicled my experiences and the navigational techniques in the book The Last Navigator, first published in 1987, and a documentary film of the same title for PBS in 1988. Now some forty years on I have updated the stories with a new generation of Satawalese islanders and researchers in the revised and fully illustrated edition of The Last Navigator. *Original photographs and film footage, 1983-1987 The classic account of traditional Micronesian navigation and “the last navigator,” Mau Piailug, who fought to preserve it—now available in a revised edition illustrated in full color As a young man piloting a small sailboat across the Pacific, Steve Thomas developed a fascination with ancient methods of navigation. He learned that, for thousands of years, the peoples of Oceania had sailed unerringly across the Pacific without compass or charts, guided only by natural signs—stars, waves, and the flight paths of birds. In search of this secret knowledge, Thomas traveled to the tiny island of Satawal in Micronesia, home to Mau Piailug, one of the few surviving paliuw , or navigators. In The Last Navigator , Thomas tells how he convinced Piailug to accept him as his student and teach him the closely guarded Talk of Navigation. It is a remarkable book, offering at once a clear and precise account of Micronesian wayfinding and the moving story of one man trying to preserve his culture against the tide of modernity. Now, forty years after his original journey to study under Mau Piailug, Thomas has worked with a new generation of researchers, including natives of Satawal, to prepare this revised edition of The Last Navigator . All Satawalese words are rendered in the now-accepted orthography, and the islanders, originally identified by pseudonyms, appear under their true names. And throughout, Thomas has added a generous selection of color photographs from his time on Satawal, documenting the island, its people, and its seafaring culture. This result is a lasting tribute to the spirit of the Satawalese, and to the Talk of Navigation A fascinating exploration of a remoted archipelago and its seagoing people — Peter Matthiessen If you have any interest in the sea and navigation or in the impact of colonialism on indigenous cultures, or if you just enjoy a well-told story of adventure, then read on. — from the foreword by David Barrie [Thomas] is a dual explorer, simultaneously trying to rediscover an ancient system of sailing, using only nature’s navigational signals, and trying to find himself in the myth-made culture of Micronesia. . . . [This] is a travel book with a dream. — Los Angeles Times Book Review This is a story of adventure, and coming of age. It is also an important document, preserving an ancient oral tradition. — San Francisco Chronicle Steve Thomas is familiar to television viewers as the two-time Emmy award-winning host of This Old House, Renovation Nation, and Save Our History. But he is also an experienced home builder and sailor. Beginning in 1977, he sailed a 43-foot wooden sloop from England to San Francisco via the Panama Canal, Galapagos, Marquesas, and Hawaii. In the early 1980’s, he journeyed to the remote Micronesian island of Satawal to learn the ancient technique of star path navigation, an experience that resulted in this book as well as a documentary for the PBS series Adventure. events.title: MARTHA FREEMAN: KITTY VS. CHRISTMAS
events.location: Books Inc. Alameda, 1344 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501
events.description: Join Books Inc. Alameda for our First Saturday Storytime. This month we are thrilled to present author, Martha Freeman, reading and signing copies of her new book, Kitty vs. Christmas. About the book: Kitty is back—but that doesn't mean he's ready for the holidays! The most wonderful time of the year fills this finicky feline with dread. Can Santa help Kitty feel the Christmas spirit? Kitty is a good, nice kitty with a good, nice family who has everything he could ever want. He has his raggedy one-eyed mouse, breakfast at 7:00, supper at 7:00, and a so-cozy life that should never change. But to Kitty’s everlasting surprise and annoyance, things continue to change around him! So when the holiday season arrives, Kitty is not excited. He doesn’t like the itchy sweaters, his family doesn’t appreciate him singing along to Christmas carols, and he’s not even allowed to eat the cookies left right out in the open on Christmas Eve! So Kitty tangles the tinsel, wrecks the wreath, and messes up the mistletoe. Kitty doesn’t feel bad until he sees what a rough night Santa has had. As he and Santa show one another kindness, Kitty realizes that Christmas might not be so bad after all. Martha Freeman was born in Southern California shortly after the Big Bang. As the universe cooled and the Earth formed, Martha grew up and fought injustice, mostly with her pen but sometimes with her feet. Martha has worked as a newspaper reporter, copy editor, substitute teacher, college lecturer, advertising copywriter, and freelance magazine writer. In 1995, she published her first book for children, STINK BOMB MOM (not an autobiography). Subsequently, she has published 30 more books, most recently ZAP! a techno-thriller about a power blackout, and IF YOU'RE GOING TO A MARCH, the perfect how-and-why picturebook for kids on their way to a protest. Besides writing, Martha enjoys running, parallel parking, making pies, hiking and talking on the phone to her far-flung children.

events.title: Kirk Lombard's THE SHADOW STREAM In-Store Meet and Greet and Book Signing
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: Kirk shares his new novel for young readers filled with brilliant storytelling, original writing, humor, and a forest filled with animals. Northern California author Kirk Lombard will be at Mrs. Dalloway's Bookstore chatting with his fans and signing copies of his book The Shadow Stream . He'll be at the store on Saturday, December 5 from 2:00 PM - 3:00 PM so come on down and join the fun! A throwback to family reads of yore, this epic follows a troubled boy and a host of hilariously vexed animals who must save a river before it’s dammed, so they can save themselves. Gabriel (“G” for short) is wasting away in the Abiddon County Juvenile Center when he’s introduced to the Shongunk River by his dying uncle. The river valley—trash-heaped but chock-full of mysteries and fish—wins G over. But, as G has learned, good things can’t last. The Shongunk is scheduled to be dammed by a local developer. In a matter of days, it will cease flowing, and all of the talkative creatures who live there in the river valley will be as homeless as G. Just as G decides it’s no time to accept his fate, so too do the animals. To inspire an uprising, a young trout is nominated to make a fateful journey up the river; a raccoon swears a violent oath against humans; and a newly sober buck leads his skittish flock out of harm’s way. Together with G, they show that good can triumph and that there is power in all of us, even the smallest minnow. KIRK LOMBARD is an author, angler, sustainable fishmonger, and tuba player who once worked inside the juvenile rehabilitation system. His first book, the award-winning Sea Forager’s Guide to the Northern California Coast , was described as “poetry” for fish by NPR. He lives in Half Moon Bay with his family, raising his children on herring and sea shanties.

events.title: Joyful Raven's TACTICAL FRIVOLITY
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. events.title: DEMOLA THE VIOLINIST
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Internationally known award-winning recording artist & multi-instrumentalist · Demola the Violinist returns to Yoshi’s Oakland with a holiday vibe that’s straight-up next level. This is where classical finesse meets street energy , flipping the season with bold beats, symphonic melodies, and that signature Demola swagger. The global phenomenon brings a dope fusion of Afrobeats , R&B , Hip Hop , and Soul —turning winter into a full-on cultural avalanche to kick off the Holiday season. From viral social media star to award-winning showman, Demola delivers a festive, high‑energy experience that never falls short of amazing. This isn’t just a concert. It’s a holiday “ turn-up ”, a sonic joyride , and a seasonal celebration with real Oakland flavor you don’t want to miss. Presented by Kim Pruitt of KP Entertainment Connections, Mark Elliot of the A-List Musiq Circle, with Special Guest Host TBA. DEMOLA the VIOLINIST BIO: Demola, known to fans as “Demola the Violinist,” is an internationally recognized musician, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, record producer, and award-winning self-taught multi-genre violinist. Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Demola moved to the United States to pursue his solo music career, blending his love for Afrobeat, reggae, R&B, hip-hop, pop, and country into a sound that is distinctly his own. In 2024, Demola’s career reached new heights, fueled by his vibrant social media presence and viral performances. With over 6 million followers and millions of streams across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, his videos regularly attract millions of views, making him one of the most-followed and celebrated violinists worldwide. His performances captivate global audiences, and his fanbase continues to expand with each viral hit. This year, Demola launched his highly successful “One in a Million 2.0” tour, performing in over 20 cities and mesmerizing audiences with original songs like “ONE IN A MILLION,” “MBAPPE,” and “LOVA,” which have collectively amassed millions of streams. He also made waves with his feature on the song “FORGIVE OUR TRESPASSES,” showcasing viral Afrobeat across the US and performing at Coachella. A hometown hero in Houston, Texas, Demola, has performed the national anthem for major sports teams, including the Houston Astros, Rockets, Dynamo, and Texans, before crowds of up to 70,000 people. He has also shared the stage with country music star Jelly Roll, performing for 74,000 fans at the Houston Rodeo. Demola is a fan favorite on television as well, with appearances on Good Morning America Online, FOX 26 Houston, CultureMap Houston, 97.9 KBXX Houston, FOX 31 Denver, WGN-9 Chicago, Black News Channel, and many others. His innovative fusion of genres has made him one of the first artists of his kind, captivating listeners with the melodic beauty of his violin and proving that he is truly one in a million. Demola - Afrobeat & Hip-hop Violinist, Artist, Singer

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Dagmar Zuniga (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Dagmar Zuniga Nicaraguan-American artist Dagmar Zuniga makes music that feels both intimate and expansive: songs drift like disrupted signals, carried by harmony, tape hiss, and a strong sense of touch. Her debut solo album in filth your mystery is kingdom / far smile peasant in yellow music — written and recorded in New York, Norway, and Athens, Georgia over a period of five years on her longtime companion, the Tascam 424 — was released by the People’s Coalition of Tandy on Bandcamp & YouTube in January 2025, accompanied by a small tape run that sold out instantly. The project quickly garnered over two hundred thousand views and the attention of artists such as Mount Eerie, who invited her to tour with them that summer. This year, what was once a jewel of tapped-in algorithms and message boards will meet the world at large, with in filth arriving digitally on March 4 , and physically on April 10 , via AD 93 . in filth is an atmospheric, devotional collage where one voice multiplies into a chorus of selves, sometimes delicate, sometimes severe; an effect created by Zuniga’s masterful layering of texture and complex harmonies. Synths glitter out like spears of sunlight from beneath clouds of moody, time-distorted guitars, and songs spin about themselves like tightly-wound music boxes, making use of a kind of hypnotic repetition, before melting apart into their components or slipping into the following track. Zuniga began recording to tape as a teenager, drawn to the physicality of the medium — how a tape recording is fragile, mutable, and alive. Though her ethereal sound may draw easy comparisons to other female pioneers of psychedelic folk, she is influenced just as much by the darker sounds of Syd Barrett and The Fall. Like Barrett, Zuniga is a painter, and she is interested not only in recording music but in creating a full, self-contained artistic universe: she creates her own artwork, merchandise, music videos, and bootleg tapes of new and unfinished music that she exclusively sells at live shows ( “If something is not material, it does not exist,” she insists). Her world has not gone unvisited, garnering her a monthly show on NTS Radio ‘World of Pain’, as well as a forthcoming appearance at Rewire Festival in April 2026. Though Zuniga’s work explores themes of solitude and suffering, the suffering in her songs is not borrowed or displayed; it is held, then opened outward through empathy — an exacting practice of attention that insists on shared ground. Solitude, in her work, is not withdrawal but a starting point for connection. Likewise, over time, her recording process has become increasingly communal, with in filth featuring musicians across the globe. Newer recordings widen the circle even more. For Zuniga, collaboration is a way to “find a place between worlds,” echoing Badiou’s idea of love as a vision refracted through the prism of difference. Meaning emerges there — in the space between voices, between artist and listener. “I hope my music helps people work through difficult experiences,” she says. “The same way it helps me.” Bandcamp | IG Support to be announced DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.description:
On the 1st and 3rd Sundays of every month, Sacred Garden Community gathers at the Alembic for Sunday Service between the hours of 11:00 am - 1:00 pm PST. 

Welcome! (Community) - 11:00 - 11:11
Connect to your sacred community of practice, grow connections. Introduce yourself if you're new or feeling it. 

Opening the way, in a good way -  11:11 - 11:20pm

Plant (Fungus + Molecule) Time! - 11:20 - 11:40
Plants, Molecules and Fungi, Oh my!

Community Satsang - 11:40-12:05
Around the wheel we go, where it stops nobody knows...

Closing, integrating, going forth - 12:05- 12:15pm
 
Community Announcements - (Community) 12:20-12:30 
Member Check-In, Fundraising, Calendar, Q&A, Processes Etc.

We also gather online every week if you are unable to make the Satsang live. The zoom link is the same every week for our online services and can be found at https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82492750630. 

We hope to see you around the garden soon!

Sacred Garden is a living sanctuary for globally identified seekers who yearn for authentic connection, radical inclusion, and collective evolution. We observes a principle of least dogma, which is the minimum belief we need to share to be a cohesive religious community. This is the entirety of our shared faith: We are open to the possibility that respectful practice with the Sacraments of our Church can bring about a direct experience of the Divine, within this lifetime.

events.title: Jennifer Levi with the Live Like Braun Foundation - The Braunicles
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A joyful, mischievous, heartfelt book for children and the grown-ups who love them. Recommended for ages 6–10, parents, grandparents, teachers, and anyone who wants to remember what it feels like to live with curiosity, courage, humor, and heart. The Braunicles invite readers into the wonderfully imperfect world of a spirited little boy named Braun. A world filled with adventure, mischief, big feelings, unexpected lessons, and an irresistible enthusiasm for life. Written by Jennifer Levi, the stories are warm, funny, honest, and deeply human. Jennifer gives a distinctive voice and captures childhood in a way that feels both whimsical and completely real: the bold ideas, the questionable decisions, the enormous emotions, the funny family dynamics, and the little moments that often become the memories we treasure most. At its heart, The Braunicles is about living fully. Braun approaches the world with curiosity. He takes chances. He includes people. He makes mistakes. He loves fiercely. He finds fun where others might not see it. And through each story, young readers discover that some of the qualities that make a child challenging, surprising, loud, adventurous, or different can also become their greatest strengths. For parents and grandparents, there is another layer. These stories are a gentle reminder not to rush through childhood trying to make everything perfect. Sometimes the mess is the memory. Sometimes the mischievous child becomes the unforgettable adult. Sometimes the moments that make us shake our heads today are exactly the stories we will tell for the rest of our lives. Jennifer’s voice brings humor and perspective to parenting without preaching. That makes The Braunicles more than a children’s book. -It is a book children can enjoy for adventure. -It is a book parents can recognize themselves in. -It is a book grandparents can give with meaning. -And it is a book families can read together and talk about long after the final page. Jennifer Levi is the founder of The Live Like Braun Foundation and the force behind The Live Like Braun movement. Since the death of her son in May 2025, Jennifer has become a powerful advocate for DUI awareness and meaningful legislative change, passing a new Bill in CA, testifying at the CA State Capitol and on Capitol Hill. She regularly speaks to audiences at DUI workshops and schools all over Southern CA. She serves on MADD's CA State Legislative Board. Jennifer’s advocacy has been featured across multiple media outlets and television networks including NBC, ABC, Fox, and CBS, along with well-known podcasts hosted by Dr. Phil, Kennedy, Jason Kennedy, Amanda Kloots, Kelly Gores, Meghan Judge, and Kate Casey. Jennifer has spoken openly about the profound transformation of her life following the death of her son. She has become a featured contributor to Maria Shriver’s Sunday Paper, writing about the ways grief has reshaped her life with raw honesty, deep emotion, and a touch of irreverence. She hopes The Braunicles inspires children to embrace exactly who they are and encourages grown-ups to give young people the freedom to let their brightest, silliest, most authentic selves shine. Jennifer is a mother, wife, advocate, writer, and former TV executive. Although she has worn many hats, she has always said she is most proud of her role as mom to her two children, Adelle and Braun. She lives in Pacific Palisades, California, with her family and two very naughty dogs. events.title: Mosaic: A Women’s Psychedelic Integration Circle with Dr. Lyssa Menard
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Many of us work with psychedelics without a guide or with limited support to integrate these experiences. That can feel painful or lonely when we’ve had meaningful journeys (and also when we’ve had disappointing journeys!). Healing – especially from interpersonal injuries – deepens when done in community. The same is true of personal and spiritual growth. Even the most joyful experiences are best metabolized when witnessed. Together, we become a mosaic – a colorful and varied community, greater together than the sum of our parts.

Mosaic is a psychedelic integration circle for self-identified women. Here, you’ll find a supportive space to integrate the lessons, challenges, and wisdom from psychedelic journeys so that you can apply those learnings to everyday life. Together, we’ll seek to understand our psychedelic experiences and make profound insights accessible and actionable.

This is a drop-in, monthly supported peer group rather than a psychotherapy group. We create space for sharing stories and experiences, receiving support, and forging genuine connections. Meditation, mindful movement, somatic practices, Internal Family Systems parts work, and creative tools are all part of the fun.

Whether you’re new to integration or looking to deepen your practice, you’ll find a supportive community here.

Note: You’re invited to bring an object for our community altar that represents some aspect of your journey.

No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please pay at the door.

This event is a closed container. There will be no further entry after 2:15.

Dr. Lyssa Menard is a psychologist, psychedelic therapist, and professor (Northwestern University Medical School) with specialties in Integrative Medicine, trauma treatment, and health psychology. She is the founder of Strategies for Change, a coaching and consulting firm promoting personal, organizational, and leadership change and has been a consultant to a wide range of media outlets, including CNN, New York Times, and WebMD. She brings this varied background to her integration groups, facilitating growth and change through a multi-media concoction of integrative therapeutic approaches (mindful movement, creative arts, somatic healing and embodiment, social connection, and spiritual ritual).

Dr. Menard’s book, "Results May Vary: Hope & Healing through Psychedelic-assisted Psychotherapy" is scheduled for release in 2026. As a beneficiary of excellent (and also, sadly, lackluster) psychedelic treatment, she is a skeptic of the field, a critic when necessary, and a true believer in the healing possibilities offered by these medicines. She serves as an advocate for community and patient education and fights for legal access to psychedelics for health and healing.

As a recent transplant to California's Bay Area, Dr. Menard spends a ridiculous amount of time at The Berkeley Alembic, cavorting in nature, worshipping the sun, and developing community.

Learn more about Lyssa here: https://lyssamenard.com/

Read Lyssa’s musings on Substack: https://lyssamenard.substack.com/

events.title: KAT EDMONSON - HAVE YOUR MERRY CHRISTMAS WITH ME
events.location: Bach Dancing & Dynamite Society (Douglas Beach House), 311 Mirada Rd, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019
events.description:
Vocalist Kat Edmonson brings her sparkling holiday celebration, blending jazz, cabaret, and vintage pop into an afternoon of timeless Christmas favorites and original gems. Known for her warmth, wit, and crystalline vocals, Kat creates a festive experience that’s both sophisticated and joyful. Her latest album, Have Your Merry Christmas With Me drops November 6 and plays like the soundtrack to a classic romantic comedy—lush, witty, soulful, and filled with longing, flirtation, and holiday warmth. Her prior holiday album Holiday Swingin’! A Kat Edmonson Christmas Vol. 1 was named one of the New York Times’ “13 Albums That Revisit (and Redefine!) Holiday Classics.”

Kat Edmonson is an award‑winning songwriter and singer “with an equal foothold in jazz, cabaret and vintage cosmopolitan pop” (The New York Times). Raised on early‑to‑mid‑century music and film, she blends nostalgic charm with a modern sensibility. Beyond her holiday work, Kat’s Billboard‑topping Dreamers Do inspired a 66‑episode livestream during the pandemic. Honored by the Songwriters Hall of Fame, she has written more than 40 songs, including “Lucky,” featured in Coca‑Cola’s 2014 Winter Olympics campaign, and has appeared on Austin City Limits, Tiny Desk Concerts, A Prairie Home Companion, and The Tonight Show.

events.title: Amy Oppenheimer's LOOKING FOR JUSTICE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence.

events.title: Return to Center: Exploring Stability, Mobility & Ease with Vickie Russell Bell
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves..



Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition.

Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.

events.title: Half-Day Silent Unguided Retreat
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice.
This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods.
There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of
meditation, all are welcome.

The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive
between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before
the first bell.

The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation:
9:30 AM – 10:10 AM
10:20 AM – 11:00 AM
11:10 AM – 11:50 AM

A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period.
The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between
sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom.
Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep
voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire
morning.

You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during
a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and
the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice
elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell.

The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website.

Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by
12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely
manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

events.title: Bookagami with Adrienne Biggs
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: What is Bookagami? Book Folding is a global art genre. No glue, no scissors, no stress! Learn how to repurpose discarded (or favorite) books into beautiful, sculptural art with the award-winning Marin artist Adrienne Biggs, the originator behind Bookagami. This hands-on Bookagami workshop guides participants through the meditative and mindful practice of folding books into unique, creative, and sustainable art. Adrienne Biggs’ Bookagami art has captivated Marin . A 30-year Marin resident and former book publishing professional, Adrienne will introduce her unique approach—combining origami, altered books, and circular economy principles—to help every attendee fold up to three books into works of art. Workshop Highlights: Learn Bookagami techniques: Start with simple folds and progress to more complex forms, suitable for all skill levels. Embrace sustainability: Discover how book folding diverts unwanted books from the landfill and gives them renewed purpose. Connect and create: Enjoy a community atmosphere where creativity sparks joy and every fold is intentional yet also spontaneous. Take home your art: Finish the session with your handmade Bookagami sculptures to display at home or give as gifts, and the skills to keep folding. What to bring to the workshop: Newer paperbacks or hardcovers with minimum 1” spine (around 300 pages) work best. Books with words and books with images produce different results/color patterns, so you are encouraged to bring and try both at the workshop (see images below for examples). Book Passage can also supply you with books if needed. Meet Your Instructor Adrienne Biggs is an accomplished artist known for fostering creative inclinations within this community, while rescuing books from landfill (or a dusty bookshelf) by repurposing these common two-dimensional objects into three-dimensional works of art that people of all ages can enjoy, create, and share. Since 2024, she has created more than 600 unique “Bookagami” (as she calls them). Her Atlas, 1963: You Are Here won First Place Blue Ribbon at the 2024 Marin County Fair, and her Bug-a-Gami totem and her Stars, Stripes & Stories piece each won ribbons in 2025 and 2026. Past public art exhibits include two-month shows at Town Books in San Anselmo and at Marelli’s in downtown San Rafael; three month shows at the downtown San Rafael Public Library and at the Friends School in San Francisco; one-month show at ACCI Gallery in Berkeley; and various exhibits at ArtWorks Downtown in San Rafael. Her current solo show, Black White & Read All Over, is at Falkirk Cultural Center in San Rafael November 6 - December 15, 2026. Learn more at @IntoTheFoldBookagami on Instagram. What students are saying about Adrienne "Adrienne was so much fun, and I took home 3 lovely art projects and will make more on my own." Susan F. "Loved it! Adrienne was an excellent teacher. She told fun stories and was very motivating. I had three great examples I created and brought home...I am not crafty and Bookagami was easy to do and fun to learn." Diana S.

events.title: The Politics of Publishing
events.location: Clio's Books, 353 Grand Avenue, Oakland, CA 94610, Oakland, CA
events.description: Who Gets to Tell the Story? · Every book on a shelf is the result of a series of choices. Which ideas are considered urgent? Which voices are given space? Who decides what gets published, how a book is positioned, who is imagined as its reader, and, ultimately, which books find their way into our hands? From the outside, publishing can look like a relatively straightforward journey: an idea becomes a manuscript, a manuscript becomes a book, a book arrives on a shelf. But behind that journey is an ecosystem of editors, publishers, marketers, distributors, booksellers, institutions, economics, relationships, taste, timing, and power. At every stage, someone is deciding what is worth paying attention to. Join us at Clio’s for a conversation about the politics of publishing with Tim McKee , Publisher of North Atlantic Books; Michelle Phan , Marketing Manager at University of California Press; author and advocate Kelechi Ubozoh ; and cultural anthropologist and Clio’s founding member Cari Borja , whose programming explores what can happen when different voices, disciplines, and ways of knowing are deliberately juxtaposed, creating the possibility for unlikely conversations. Together, we’ll follow a book from idea to bookshelf while asking the harder questions beneath that journey: Who gets through the door? What kinds of knowledge are valued? Which stories enter the cultural conversation, and which don’t? What gets changed, or lost along the way? And what roles do authors, publishers, marketers, booksellers, programmers, and readers play in determining which ideas circulate through our culture? Kelechi Ubozoh’s We’ve Been Too Patient: Voices from Radical Mental Health gives us a particularly powerful book through which to examine these questions. Bringing together voices challenging conventional understandings of mental health and healing, the anthology asks what happens when lived experience itself becomes a form of knowledge, and what it takes for voices outside dominant systems to make their way into print and into public conversation. A bookstore is never simply a place where books are sold. It is a place where voices are chosen, ideas are juxtaposed, unlikely conversations begin, and culture is made. Tim McKee, Publisher, North Atlantic Books Tim came to NAB in 2013 and is honored to serve as publisher. Born in New York City, McKee grew up in Los Angeles and received a BA from Princeton University and an MA in journalism from the University of Missouri. He has worked in the nonprofit sector for his entire career, including serving as the long-time managing editor of The Sun magazine, the grants director for a social-justice foundation in San Francisco, and as a writer for several community-based organizations in California. He has also taught college-level writing and journalism. His book No More Strangers Now: Young Voices from a New South Africa (Dorling Kindersley) was an Honor Book for the Jane Addams Book Award and a Los Angeles Times bestseller. He is happiest when bringing necessary stories to the page. Michelle Phan , Marketing Manager, UC Press Michelle launched her publishing career at North Atlantic Books as a publicist before transitioning to marketing at UC Press. With 7+ years of experience in book promotion, she is passionate about uplifting authors and books that share the knowledge necessary for our times. As Vice President of Bay Area Women in Publishing and Co-Chair of the Robin Seaman Award Committee, she also cares deeply about fostering meaningful relationships and building inclusive community within the industry. Kelechi Ubozoh, Author and advocate For over a decade, Kelechi has worked in the California mental health system in the areas of research and advocacy, community engagement, stigma reduction, youth development and peer support. Kelechi has spoken publicly about her experiences on multiple platforms, including CBS This Morning with Gayle King, O The Oprah Magazine, and The S Word documentary. Kelechi began her career as an investigative reporter in New York City, and was the first student-reporter ever published in The New York Times . In 2019, Kelechi published her anthology with L.D. Green, We’ve Been Too Patien t, which features diverse voices who all share their stories of radical healing and consider the recent movement towards reform in the mental health field, including the mad pride/consumer movement, theater as therapy, peer support, combating stigma, and trauma-informed care. Most recently, she co-authored What I Wish My People Had Known: The Psychiatric Green Book: A Guide for Black Folks with Yolo Akili Robinson, a strategic guide helping Black communities protect against racialized violence and institutional harm.

Whether in a concert hall or at an outdoor jazz festival, there is no easing you in as they come at you full force, from start to finish. With an unwavering respect for the music’s storied history, the ensemble’s thirteen world-class musicians and vocalists come together to create an unparalleled musical experience. For over 20 years, SHO has been dedicated to the sounds of the barrio (Spanish Harlem, NYC). Their music is characterized by the raw, organic, and vintage sound defined by the genre. They are on a mission to keep the musical legacy of salsa dura (hard salsa) alive and expand its audience to those who love great music, not just Latin music. Grounded in the past, while focused on the future, they strive to keep the music relevant, creating a unique and fresh approach. “As a leader and producer, my mission and vision are to represent the great history and legacy of this music that I’ve been blessed to be a part of my entire life,” reflects Hernández. “Our passion and commitment to this music is never-ending.” With this unyielding motivation, SHO’s GRAMMY® nominated 2022 release Imágenes Latinas saw the band exploring new dimensions but never deviating from its core belief. “As with all the new SHO recordings, the concept and sound are the same, but the playing of new songs, arrangements, and performances always aim to create a new magic for the listeners,” Hernández adds. SHO released their 9th studio album, Swing Forever , in 2024, further solidifying the group as “the leading light of the salsa reconstruction movement” ( Newsday ). events.title: Matt O'Hara with Rebecca Herman - The Flying Death
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: “Compulsively readable, well structured, historically informative, and entertainingly written. The Flying Death tells the story of how a modern-day miracle drug was born out of an Amazonian blowgun poison thanks to the efforts of a motley crew of fortune-seeking adventurers—a crew that included a handful of unscrupulous medical researchers, an obsessive White Russian émigré, and an American storyteller with big dreams.”—John Lee Anderson, author of Che: A Revolutionary Life Matt will be joined in conversation by Rebecca Herman, Associate Professor of History, U.C. Berkeley. In The Flying Death: Poison, Plunder, and the Quest for a Miracle Medicine in the Amazon (FSG; November 10, 2026), historian Matt O’Hara tells the story of a young, frail American explorer named Richard Gill, who traveled to the Amazon in the 1930s to open a tourist ranch. Instead, he stirred up an international hunt to harvest a local vine known as curare. As Gill and his rivals quickly realized, curare was both a dangerous poison used by local tribes in blow darts and a potential cure for numerous ailments, including multiple sclerosis and other motor diseases. Seeking to treat his own degenerative illness and make a fortune, Gill established connections with tribal leaders and pharmaceutical companies back home—even as his Russian-born rival, Boris Krukoff, sought to do the same. Navigating treacherous terrain and politics, Gill and Krukoff successfully created a veritable curare industrial complex. The plant became a key element in shock therapy treatments and, eventually, in anesthesia back in the United States. Gill and Krukoff’s rivalry and ethical compromises offer a timeless reflection on how personal ambition, competition, and obsession can shape—and sometimes distort—scientific and cultural progress. In this ethnobotanical adventure story, O’Hara deftly explores the intersections of indigenous knowledge, scientific exploration, and exploitation, and poses searching moral ​conundrums about the price of progress. And who pays it. “The Flying Death is as gripping as the exotic poison at its heart. Matt O’Hara is a master researcher who brews a tale at the frontiers of scientific discovery, with healthy doses of ambition and adventure mixed in. This is historical narrative nonfiction at its best.” —Mitchell Zuckoff, author of Lost in Shangri-La “Matt O’Hara has uncovered the thrilling true story of Richard Gill, a sickly American explorer who ventured into the Amazon in 1938—and ended up transforming medicine. Moving from jungle rivers and poison-masters to medical trials and corporate boardrooms, O’Hara offers a gripping, exciting, and deeply researched adventure story about ambition, exploitation, and the true cost of medical breakthroughs.”—Charles Duhigg, author of The Power of Habit “The Flying Death, Matt O’Hara’s brilliant tale of the South American poison curare, is a wild ride driven by courage, mystery, pharmaceutical wrongdoing, and Indigenous wisdom. The story will surprise you, infuriate you—and it will definitely make you smarter.” —Deborah Blum, author of The Poisoner’s Handbook “An unforgettable tale of medicine, ambition, greed, and the natural world, The Flying Death is a true page-turner. Matt O’Hara is a tenacious historian who writes with great skill and with a keen eye for human drama and injustice.”—Hector Tobar, author of Deep Down Dark Matt O’Hara is a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Cruz. He is the award-winning author of many journal articles and two books, The History of the Future in Colonial Mexico and A Flock Divided: Race, Religion, and Politics in Mexico, 1749–1857. Rebecca Herman is Associate Professor of History at UC Berkeley, where she teaches about environmental politics, US-Latin American relations, and modern Latin America. She is the author of Cooperating with the Colossus: A Social and Political History of US Military Bases in World War II Latin America and is currently at work on a book about anti-extractivism in Antarctica. Her first novel, The Outposters, will be published next summer by Cardinal.
