events.title: Relatefulness with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other

Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli.

Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment.

This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. 

We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance!

What We’ll Explore

Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice:
Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group.
Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society.
Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly.
Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of.

Why Come?

You may be looking to:
Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected.
Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context.
Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns

This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun!

What Not to Expect

This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur.

It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. 

Here’s what NOT to expect:
A space free of conflict or triggers.
When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others.
No enforced hierarchy of emotions.
Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important.
Expression without attunement.
We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence.

Other logistics and notes

Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time!

We hope to see you at a future event! 

Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you.

More about the facilitators

Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring.

When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws.

In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance.

Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

events.description: Rebuilding Our Cities — And Our Democracy · Cities like New York, Los Angeles, and San Francisco are in crisis. Chronic housing shortages are driving countless middle-class and working-class households out of high-opportunity areas. Homelessness is skyrocketing. Cars continue to rule city streets, poisoning the climate and putting everyone’s health and safety at risk. And city governments, instead of rising to meet the challenge, are increasingly dysfunctional and unaccountable. Build or Die: How America Is Suffocating Its Cities and What to Do About It traces the history of a disaster a century in the making, detailing how shortsighted and reactionary policy decisions led to the interlocking crisis that threatens America’s great cities.Join Build or Die author Ned Resnikoff, California Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, and Economic Security Project co-founder Natalie Foster for a conversation about what ails America's great cities—and how we can revitalize both urban America and American democracy. Ned Resnikoff is an independent writer and urban policy analyst. His work has appeared in The New York Times , San Francisco Chronicle , The New Republic , The Nation , Dissent , and The Atlantic , among other publications. He writes Public Comment , an online newsletter about cities and democracy. Natalie Foster is author of The Guarantee: Inside the Fight For America’s Next Economy and co-founder and former President of Economic Security Project, an organization dedicated to building economic power for everyday Americans. She's a Senior Fellow at the Aspen Institute Future of Work Initiative.

events.title: SPANISH HARLEM ORCHESTRA
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Three time GRAMMY® winning ensemble · Spanish Harlem Orchestra, the three-time GRAMMY® winning Salsa and Latin Jazz band, sets the gold standard for excellence in authentic, New York-style, hardcore salsa. Whether in a concert hall or at an outdoor jazz festival, there is no easing you in as they come at you full force, from start to finish. Their energy on stage and their rich sound and musical precision leave audiences mesmerized until the last note is played. With an unwavering respect for the music’s storied history, the ensemble’s thirteen world-class musicians and vocalists come together to create an unparalleled musical experience. For over 20 years, SHO has been dedicated to the sounds of the barrio (Spanish Harlem, NYC). Their music is characterized by the raw, organic, and vintage sound defined by the genre. They are on a mission to keep the musical legacy of salsa dura (hard salsa) alive and expand its audience to those who love great music, not just Latin music. Grounded in the past, while focused on the future, they strive to keep the music relevant, creating a unique and fresh approach. “As a leader and producer, my mission and vision are to represent the great history and legacy of this music that I’ve been blessed to be a part of my entire life,” reflects Hernández. “Our passion and commitment to this music is never-ending.” With this unyielding motivation, SHO’s GRAMMY® nominated 2022 release Imágenes Latinas saw the band exploring new dimensions but never deviating from its core belief. “As with all the new SHO recordings, the concept and sound are the same, but the playing of new songs, arrangements, and performances always aim to create a new magic for the listeners,” Hernández adds. SHO released their 9th studio album, Swing Forever , in 2024, further solidifying the group as “the leading light of the salsa reconstruction movement” ( Newsday ). With eight albums and six GRAMMY® nominations, this powerhouse orchestra is aware that it is crucial to continually push itself and raise the bar. Their sixth album, entitled Anniversary, won the 2019 GRAMMY® Award for Best Tropical Album.

events.title: Embodiment Practice: Mindful Movement + Stillness with Suzanne (Zan) Beahrs
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest.

Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. 

Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. 

Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. 

Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space.

Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like.

About Suzanne (Zan):
With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley

Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons):

events.title: Deconstructing Yourself with Michael Taft
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. 

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

events.title: The Present Moment Game with Alli Magidsohn
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
When we gather with others, conversation almost automatically drifts toward what has already happened or what might happen next. Stories, plans, reactions, hopes—these patterns are so ingrained that we barely notice how completely we relate to one another through the lens of the past and future.

But when we pause those habits, something surprising occurs.

The room changes.
Attention sharpens.
A different kind of connection begins to emerge.

A small clearing inside awareness opens—a place where no future is rehearsing itself, and no echoes of the past are allowed to enter.

We can touch this space alone in contemplative practices, but it's rare to enter it with others.

The Present Moment Game is a simple social meditation designed to explore that possibility.

Participants speak only from what is happening in the moment, and gently bring each other back when attention drifts. What unfolds is often unexpected, and never the same twice.

Curious? Come play!
___________

What to Expect

6:30 PM — Doors open
Arrive anytime in the next 30 minutes. You’re welcome to enjoy tea as you settle in—just note that drinks won’t be brought into the circle, so come early if you’d like to enjoy an unrushed cup.

7:00 PM — The event begins
This is a “sealed-container” experience. Out of care for the group, we can’t allow late entry, so please be sure to arrive between 6:30 and 7:00. After a brief grace period, doors will close at 7:05.

7:06 PM — Welcome, introductions & game rules
A short orientation covering the simple guidelines.

7:25 PM — The Present Moment Game begins

8:25 PM — The game ends
We’ll then move into group reflections.

~8:45 PM — Event concludes
___________

Is This Event for You?
A few things to consider before you decide:

Phones and watches off
As an invitation to loosen your grip on time, you’ll be asked to remove your watch and fully power down your phone for the full duration of the experience.

This is not an Authentic Relating practice
T-Group, Circling, and other AR forms use present-moment awareness as a vehicle for relational exploration. That’s not what we’re doing here. Our subject isn’t each other, but the moment itself.

Kindness is essential
Please come willing to encounter everyone in the room with openness and warmth. This is a gentle space for contemplation and focused attention, not edge-pushing or confrontation.
___________

One participant’s experience:

"As a person who loves, thinks and talks about language for a living, I am wide-eyed at how speaking solely in the present tense feels rich, alive and vital. It’s the best of meditation and conversation, distilled into an hour of social elixir; a stop-you-in-your-tracks nexus of collective mind. I feel hooked, thirsty for more. Alli creates a magical container. You won’t regret it."  — Sophia
___________

About your host

Alli Magidsohn is the creator of The Present Moment Game, an experimental social meditation that invites a small group to do something surprisingly rare: be fully present together, in real time.

The idea grew out of Alli's experience with T-Group, a practice she found genuinely transformative. But as she went deeper, she became increasingly captivated by something specific: the quality of attention that arises when a group of people focus on what's actually happening, right now.

That observation became a question: What if the present moment wasn’t just the context of a relationally-focused experience, but the primary subject of the inquiry itself?

Drawing in part on the linguistic principles of E-Prime, she designed a set of simple constraints that gently guide conversation away from the past and future, and into the living moment. The result is something playful, quietly profound, and hard to describe until you experience it.

Instagram: @thepresentmomentgame

events.title: CON FUNK SHUN
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Bay Area’s Legends of Funk & Soul 6th Annual Holiday Concert Rendition · All Aboard the LOVE TRAIN — a Bay Area-beloved holiday rendition of funk, soul, and pure celebration with CONFUNKSHUN . This season, let the groove bring you home as the legendary hitmakers return to Yoshi’s Oakland for their 6th annual Holiday Concert Series . It’s more than a show—it’s a soul-charged reunion , gift-wrapped in rhythm, nostalgia, and that signature Fun, Fun, Fun energy only Confunkshun can deliver. Get ready for a festive ride through: Timeless classics you know by heart Holiday gems from their 2024 album Home for Xmas A special first listen to unreleased tracks from their upcoming 2027 project, Smooth Jukebox Get ready for a night made for dancing , reminiscing , and straight vibing with the band that feels like family. As Confunkshun brings home a high-powered mix of holiday heat and signature funk—it’s a homecoming celebration built to move you, lift you, and light up your holiday spirit. And don’t miss the chance to grab limited-edition merchandise, CFS holiday CD jams —and CONFUNKSHUN’s 2027 Pre-released Smooth Juke Box T-Shirts. Presented by Mark Elliot & The A-List Musiq Circle, Your Bay Area's Who's Who Entertainment Network. Pre-Show VIP Q & A Meet & Greet with special guest host TBA. CONFUNKSHUN The R&B funk icon, Confunkshun, who has been pleasing fans for over 50 years, is at it again! After the success of Love’s Train being rerecorded by Silk Sonic (Bruno Mars and Anderson Paak) and reaching #1 on the charts, the band’s locomotive has once again rolled out with recent singles Text Me Tomorrow and Smooth from their highly anticipated 2024 spring album release, Smooth Jukebox. Initially known as Project Soul, the R&B funk icon group we now know as Confunkshun has been pleasing fans for over 50 years. Originating in Vallejo, CA, founding member Michael Cooper, along with high school classmates Louis McCall, Karl Fuller, Cedric Martin, Danny Thomas, Paul “Zebulan” Harrell, and newfound talent Felton Pilate, started this unprecedented music journey. Eventually, the group found a home in Memphis in the mid-'70s when they booked a performance backing Stax Recording Artist the Soul Children. Soon, they were recruited as the background band for Rufus Thomas for the Golden Globe-nominated Wattstax Benefit Concert/ Documentary. While in pursuit of a recording contract, the group adopted a new name inspired by the group NiteLiters’ song, Confunkshun. The newly renamed act attracted the attention of Mercury Records, and soon set funkateers around the world on fire with their debut album featuring their first single “Sho'Feels Good To Me.” Confunkshun went on to release a total of 11 albums and eight top ten Billboard hits, including the No. 1 hit single “Ffun”, “Chase Me”, “Shake & Dance”, “Baby I’m Hooked”, and more. Ironically, their biggest hit was an album cut that was never released as a single. The fan favorite, Love’s Train, propelled Confunkshun’s “To the Max” album to Gold Status. But it was 40 years later that supergroup Silk Sonic’s remake of the single took it to #1 on the charts, helping the duo (Bruno Mars & Anderson Paak) win a BET Album of the Year Award. In 2022, Michael Cooper and Felton Pilate were presented with Honorary Doctorates of Humane Letters from the Christian Bible Institute, with Confunkshun member Dr. Ron Moton earning his Ph.D. In 2018, Confunkshun can proudly claim to be one of the only R&B Funk bands with three doctoral members! Dr. Cooper and Dr. Pilate were also honored to receive the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Awards for their lifetime of service through music and more. This prestigious award has been awarded to a select few Americans to recognize over 4,000 hours of extraordinary service. Confunkshun’s current lineup includes three original members, Michael Cooper, Felton Pilate, and Karl Fuller, as well as the talents of Kurt “KC” Clayton, Ron Moton, Aaron Green, Rene Escovedo, and Brian LaTour. Additional support includes the service of long-time road manager and travel agent Steve Sullivan & Master of Ceremonies (Conductor), Clarence Isadore. They continue to mesmerize audiences with magnetic performances on their worldwide 2023 Smooth Jukebox Tour. The group is also a frequent favorite on the Soul Train Cruise and Tom Joyner Cruise, and will soon be on the upcoming Keith Sweat’s Sweatfest in the Dominican Republic. Their contribution to R&B music was recognized in 2014 with the National R&B Music Society Lifetime Achievement Award. Confunkshun’s catalog of hits remains on worldwide radio playlists and in the hearts of their dedicated fans. Con Funk Shun has produced several hits throughout their career. Some of their most popular songs include: 1. Ffun: This song topped the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 2. Shake and Dance with Me: This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 3. Chase Me: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1979. 4. Got to Be Enough: This song reached No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1980. 5. Too Tight: This song peaked at No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1981. 6. Baby, I’m Hooked (Right into Your Love): This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1983. 7. Electric Lady: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1985

events.title: Author Storytime: Elsa's Chessboard and Story Power!
events.location: Black Bird Bookstore, 4033 Judah St, San Francisco, CA 94122
events.description: Jenny Andrus Children's Book Author and Librarian Elsa's Chessboard Elsa carries her chessboard everywhere, always ready for a game. When World War II forces her from Europe, can chess help make America home? Growing up in 1900s Vienna, Elsa watches her brothers play chess. “No girls!” they tell her when she first asks to learn; but she’s determined, and soon she’s such a pro that they give Elsa her very own special chessboard. From then on, Elsa plays chess whenever she can. When she grows up, she even meets her husband over games in the park. But when World War II grips Europe, the young Jewish family flees to America, where they find themselves surrounded by unfamiliar languages. Luckily, Elsa knows one language that can always bring people together: chess! Based on the life of author Jenny Andrus’s grandmother, with illustrations by award-winning artist Julie Downing, Elsa’s Chessboard is an inspiring and exciting tale, perfect for any reader who's ever found meaning in a special object. CCBC’s Best-of -the-Year List (Cooperative Children’s Book Center) Tablet’s Best Jewish Children’s Books of the Year CALIBA Golden Poppy Finalist  (California Independent Bookseller’s Alliance) Grinspoon Jewish Story Award, PJ Library Horn Book Starred Review 2025 Stephanie Wildman Stephanie Wildman is the author of six children’s books: Story Power! (2025)(co-author Simon Wildman chung, illustrated by Estefanía Razo; translated into Spanish as !El Poder de los Cuentos! by Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave); Ghost Writer (2024)(co-authored with Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave, illustrated by Estefanía Razo; in Spanish as Escritor Fantasma); Breath by Breath (2024)(illustrated by Estefanía Razo; translated into Spanish as Respiro a Respiro by Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave); Treasure Hunt (2022) (illustrated by Estefanía Razo; translated into Spanish as Búsqueda del Tesoro by Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave); and Brave in the Water (2021) (illustrated by Jenni Feidler-Aguilar; translated into Spanish as Valiente en el Agua by Cecilia Pópulus-Eudave), all from Lawley Publishing, and Miri’s Moving Day (2024)(co-authored with Adam Chang, illustrated by Dream Chen from Kar-Ben Publishing). She became a Professor Emerita after serving as the John A. and Elizabeth H. Sutro Chair at Santa Clara Law . She directed the school’s Center for Social Justice and Public Service. In 2007, the Society of American Law Teachers, the largest national organization of law school faculty, honored her with their Great Teacher Award.

Since 2007, Patchwork Show has been where creativity, community, and small business come together. events.title: Rhys Bowen - To Crown It All
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Multi-award-winning mystery author Rhys Bowen presents her latest work in the acclaimed A Royal Spyness series, To Crown It All . Lady Georgiana Rannoch never expected to be more than a guest at the coronation of King George VI, but murder and some international intrigue make for a change of plans… One of the most daunting things about being related to the royal family but not being royalty myself is finding just the right ensemble for incredibly important events like the coronation. The process has become especially difficult as my maid has fallen ill and I am now relying on Queenie for everything—well almost everything. We do have a lovely new nanny with whom my son James is quite smitten. My concerns about gowns and Queenie-related disasters are put aside when I receive a worrisome letter from my mother. She seems anxious to see me and is missing her grandson-not at all like her! Darcy and I read between the lines only to discover a coded plea for help. We decide the best way to get Mummy away from Hitler and his cronies is to secure her an invitation to the coronation and have her stay at Eynsleigh along with our other guests for the big event. Two complications quickly arise. A stern member of the German government has arrived with Mummy who seems to be watching her-and our-every move. And then I unexpectedly find myself involved in the coronation ceremony at Westminster Abbey. Well, that solves my worry about what I should wear as I will be outfitted by Buckingham Palace for the festivities. But with a house full of visitors for the big event, Darcy receives word that the ceremony itself, and all of the royal attendees are under threat. And to make matters immeasurably worse, one of my esteemed house guests is found quite dead in their bed. Darcy and I must find a killer and prevent a terrible tragedy all while I do my best to avoid any embarrassing mishaps at the coronation, as quite literally, the world will be watching. Rhys Bowen , a New York Times bestselling author, has been nominated for every major award in mystery writing, including the Edgar®, and has won many, including both the Agatha and Anthony awards. She is also the author of the Molly Murphy Mysteries, set in turn-of-the-century New York, and the Constable Evans Mysteries, set in Wales, as well as two international bestselling stand-alone novels. She was born in England and now divides her time between Northern California and Arizona. events.title: LIVE MUSIC: June McDoom, Eliana Glass (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: June McDoom There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own. She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition. She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for. Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive. Mento is the root of all of it: ska, rock steady, reggae, dub and everything after. He is the one who put a guitar in her hands. An inheritance, a gift and a map. Even her name is part of it, though she will tell you she landed on it more by feel than reason. She records as June McDoom, born Alyssa, June being a nickname one of her grandmothers, Joan, went by, a name she thought was cool to carry and simply liked the sound of. An etheric channel that reverberates all the same. A dub all its own. Made slowly and by hand with her longtime partner Evan Wright, Follow the Light lays the harmony of folk over the rhythm of dub, with Dionne Warwick, Minnie Riperton, Pentangle and the washed guitars of Cocteau Twins haunting its outer edges. Voice and guitar seeking each other out first, then everything else stacked across long days in the studio they keep at home, restraint kept on purpose. The lead single "Without You" is the whole method surfacing, split open and sparkling like a geode in a creek bed. Angelic heroics, and nothing less. At the heart is family. Her grandmother Aggie, the light behind "Memory," guiding still. And underneath, the quieter truth the record keeps: none of us are only one person, but a continuum of selves, the ones who shaped us and the ones we have yet to meet. Future you is an ancestor your current self gets to greet. Press play and the same invitation is yours: A few minutes out of time, a place that turns familiar the longer you stay until you surface somewhere new and find it was yours all along. events.description: Bay Area’s Legends of Funk & Soul 6th Annual Holiday Concert Rendition · All Aboard the LOVE TRAIN — a Bay Area-beloved holiday rendition of funk, soul, and pure celebration with CONFUNKSHUN . This season, let the groove bring you home as the legendary hitmakers return to Yoshi’s Oakland for their 6th annual Holiday Concert Series . It’s more than a show—it’s a soul-charged reunion , gift-wrapped in rhythm, nostalgia, and that signature Fun, Fun, Fun energy only Confunkshun can deliver. Get ready for a festive ride through: Timeless classics you know by heart Holiday gems from their 2024 album Home for Xmas A special first listen to unreleased tracks from their upcoming 2027 project, Smooth Jukebox Get ready for a night made for dancing , reminiscing , and straight vibing with the band that feels like family. As Confunkshun brings home a high-powered mix of holiday heat and signature funk—it’s a homecoming celebration built to move you, lift you, and light up your holiday spirit. And don’t miss the chance to grab limited-edition merchandise, CFS holiday CD jams —and CONFUNKSHUN’s 2027 Pre-released Smooth Juke Box T-Shirts. Presented by Mark Elliot & The A-List Musiq Circle, Your Bay Area's Who's Who Entertainment Network. Pre-Show VIP Q & A Meet & Greet with special guest host TBA. CONFUNKSHUN The R&B funk icon, Confunkshun, who has been pleasing fans for over 50 years, is at it again! After the success of Love’s Train being rerecorded by Silk Sonic (Bruno Mars and Anderson Paak) and reaching #1 on the charts, the band’s locomotive has once again rolled out with recent singles Text Me Tomorrow and Smooth from their highly anticipated 2024 spring album release, Smooth Jukebox. Initially known as Project Soul, the R&B funk icon group we now know as Confunkshun has been pleasing fans for over 50 years. Originating in Vallejo, CA, founding member Michael Cooper, along with high school classmates Louis McCall, Karl Fuller, Cedric Martin, Danny Thomas, Paul “Zebulan” Harrell, and newfound talent Felton Pilate, started this unprecedented music journey. Eventually, the group found a home in Memphis in the mid-'70s when they booked a performance backing Stax Recording Artist the Soul Children. Soon, they were recruited as the background band for Rufus Thomas for the Golden Globe-nominated Wattstax Benefit Concert/ Documentary. While in pursuit of a recording contract, the group adopted a new name inspired by the group NiteLiters’ song, Confunkshun. The newly renamed act attracted the attention of Mercury Records, and soon set funkateers around the world on fire with their debut album featuring their first single “Sho'Feels Good To Me.” Confunkshun went on to release a total of 11 albums and eight top ten Billboard hits, including the No. 1 hit single “Ffun”, “Chase Me”, “Shake & Dance”, “Baby I’m Hooked”, and more. Ironically, their biggest hit was an album cut that was never released as a single. The fan favorite, Love’s Train, propelled Confunkshun’s “To the Max” album to Gold Status. But it was 40 years later that supergroup Silk Sonic’s remake of the single took it to #1 on the charts, helping the duo (Bruno Mars & Anderson Paak) win a BET Album of the Year Award. In 2022, Michael Cooper and Felton Pilate were presented with Honorary Doctorates of Humane Letters from the Christian Bible Institute, with Confunkshun member Dr. Ron Moton earning his Ph.D. In 2018, Confunkshun can proudly claim to be one of the only R&B Funk bands with three doctoral members! Dr. Cooper and Dr. Pilate were also honored to receive the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Awards for their lifetime of service through music and more. This prestigious award has been awarded to a select few Americans to recognize over 4,000 hours of extraordinary service. Confunkshun’s current lineup includes three original members, Michael Cooper, Felton Pilate, and Karl Fuller, as well as the talents of Kurt “KC” Clayton, Ron Moton, Aaron Green, Rene Escovedo, and Brian LaTour. Additional support includes the service of long-time road manager and travel agent Steve Sullivan & Master of Ceremonies (Conductor), Clarence Isadore. They continue to mesmerize audiences with magnetic performances on their worldwide 2023 Smooth Jukebox Tour. The group is also a frequent favorite on the Soul Train Cruise and Tom Joyner Cruise, and will soon be on the upcoming Keith Sweat’s Sweatfest in the Dominican Republic. Their contribution to R&B music was recognized in 2014 with the National R&B Music Society Lifetime Achievement Award. Confunkshun’s catalog of hits remains on worldwide radio playlists and in the hearts of their dedicated fans. Con Funk Shun has produced several hits throughout their career. Some of their most popular songs include: 1. Ffun: This song topped the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 2. Shake and Dance with Me: This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 3. Chase Me: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1979. 4. Got to Be Enough: This song reached No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1980. 5. Too Tight: This song peaked at No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1981. 6. Baby, I’m Hooked (Right into Your Love): This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1983. 7. Electric Lady: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1985

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: Amy Oppenheimer's LOOKING FOR JUSTICE
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence.

events.title: Ella Dair Ensemble
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Ella Dair is a NYC-based jazz vocalist. Originally from San Francisco, she started singing at a young age, performing with many Bay Area legends in her aunt’s swing band “Lavay Smith & Her Red Hot Skillet Lickers.” Ella continued her education in music and performance with SFArtsEd, falling in love with the songs of Harold Arlen and Kander & Ebb, among other classics of the Great American Songbook. As a teenager she was a vocal soloist with the youth choir at Glide Memorial, the renowned non-denominational church presided over by civil rights leader Cecil Williams. Ella earned her bachelor’s degree from Bard College, studying anthropology and Latin American studies with a particular interest in ethnomusicology. Her studies broadened her musical tastes and sent her to Mexico City, where she lived post-grad. Ella then moved to New York City, joining the staff at Dizzy’s Club at Jazz At Lincoln Center, where she has been exposed to many of the greatest jazz musicians in the world. On her regular trips to the West Coast Ella performs at The Royal Cuckoo Organ Lounge in San Francisco, an iconic institution that has received rave reviews from the New York Times and the San Francisco Chronicle. At the Royal Cuckoo, Ella has sung with Etta James’ trumpet player Mike Olmos, Lyle Lovett’s alto player Brad Leali, and tenor saxophonist Howard Wiley, a resident Artistic Director at the SFJAZZ Center. Ella covers a range of material, including jazz standards, soul, country and folk tunes. She has a keen eye for unique and beautiful songs, and she continues to work tirelessly on expanding her repertoire, always on the lookout for obscure gems in addition to timeless classics.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: MIKE STERN BAND
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: FEAT. DENNIS CHAMBERS, DENNIS GWIZDALA, BOB FRANCESCHINI & LENI STERN · Legendary Guitarist Mike Stern On Tour! Mike Stern’s Debut Release With Mack Avenue Music Group/Artistry Music Features Collaborations With Christian McBride, Chris Potter, Antonio Sanchez, Dennis Chambers and Richard Bona Produced By The Late Jim Beard, Stern’s Longtime Collaborator and Friend Mike Stern's new album Echoes, And Other Songs marks his debut release on Mack Avenue Music Group/Artistry Music. Echoes delivers all the elements that longtime Stern fans want, and then some: the hook-filled rapid-fire bebop writing; the gorgeous melodic sensibility culled from African music, gospel and other influences; the breakneck improvisations that pepper hornlike bop virtuosity with rock fire. Along with the announcement, Stern has shared the lead single “Stuff Happens,” which features the 9-time Grammy Award winner Christian McBride . “It’s definitely got a Blues vibe, and it opens with a short but really wonderful solo from Christian McBride,” Stern says of the track. “He is definitely not only one of the greatest upright bass players ever, but he plays amazing electric bass. Of course, I knew that going into this project, so I asked him to play a lot of electric bass and he did that so beautifully on this tune. He played great on everything.” Stern has been celebrated for his versatile playing style since he first hit the scene in the 1970s, transcending genres by performing with Blood, Sweat & Tears, Miles Davis, Jaco Pastorius, The Brecker Brothers, David Sanborn, Béla Fleck, Yellowjackets and more. With Echoes and Other Songs, Stern brings together an all-star group of musicians, including Christian McBride, Chris Potter, Antonio Sanchez, Richard Bona & Dennis Chambers, for 11 brand-new originals that will captivate and unite guitar and jazz fans of all generations. This is Stern’s first release since the loss of longtime producer and keyboardist Jim Beard (who played on and produced the album), the closure of Stern’s beloved 55 Bar, and his 2016 injury, from which he continues to face physical hurdles. Echoes and Other Songs is a powerhouse document from one of the finest guitarists in jazz history, at a time in his career when he overcame immense physical struggles and experienced profound loss. In the sheer might of these performances, Echoes is a defiant record — not so much a victory lap as a call to arms. Echoes and Other Songs could be considered a loving farewell to Jim Beard, who passed away in March 2024. Beard acted as Stern’s go-to producer for over three decades, and as a favorite keyboardist for even longer. “I’m not exaggerating when I call Jim Beard a genius,” Stern says. “People would say, ‘You should change up your producer — you know, just mix it up.’ And I would say, ‘Why?’ Everybody loved Jim. He was just great at what he did — how he used technology, how he produced, how he mixed.” Stern goes on to describe Beard’s touch as a player. “Incredible.” He pauses. “Ridiculous… Everything he did was perfect. The records he came out with were amazing, but I think he could have done even more as a piano player.” In the end, though, Stern was most affected by Beard’s devotion as a friend. “When I had the blues,” he recalls, “when I felt low and wanted to talk to somebody, he’s one of the people I would reach out to. It would be short, but he would know exactly what I was talking about. It’s a heartbreaker.” Echoes also marks the first album Stern has released as a leader since the West Village jazz haunt 55 Bar closed its doors in 2022, a casualty of the pandemic. Stern’s regular gig there was legendary, enduring and advantageous; it was at 55 where Michael Brecker became interested in hiring the guitarist. His 55 residency also provided a physical-therapy regimen of sorts after Stern broke both of his humerus bones in 2016. He stumbled over construction materials on the street in New York and fell, and the aftermath included potentially career-ending nerve damage that threatened his picking hand. The road to recovery has been long, hard, and ongoing. Stern has had the abiding support of his wife, Leni, to help him, as well as godsends like Dr. Alton Barron, an orthopedic hand specialist recommended by a friend, fellow guitar master Wayne Krantz. Advised by another pal, the drummer Ray Levier, Stern came up with an efficient system for holding his pick, using wig glue and tape. “It was a challenge and a half,” Stern says, “and it still is, sometimes, just to accept it. It gets me really upset and frustrated because I used to play stuff with my fingers. I had to change certain things about my technique.” But Stern pushes on and rises above, as he has throughout his career — like when he rejoined Miles Davis’ band in 1985, having found sobriety. Throughout Echoes, you’d be hard-pressed to find a second in which Stern’s chops are less than sublime. In terms of expressivity, his flatpicking has no limitations. “I’m gonna keep trying with whatever I got,” Stern says. “You know I got to. Because I love it, and love means that some days you hate it; those two sides are on the same coin. But the love is definitely winning out.” Consider Mike Stern’s Echoes and Other Songs his love letter to jazz, to the guitar, to bandstand camaraderie, and to his own undefeated will. Echoes And Other Songs tracklist: 1. Connections 2. Echoes 3. Stuff Happens 4. Space Bar 5. I Hope So 6. Where’s Leo 7. Gospel Song 8. Crumbles 9. Curtis 10. Climate 11. events.title: Half-Day Silent Unguided Retreat
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice.
This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods.
There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of
meditation, all are welcome.

The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive
between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before
the first bell.

The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation:
9:30 AM – 10:10 AM
10:20 AM – 11:00 AM
11:10 AM – 11:50 AM

A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period.
The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between
sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom.
Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep
voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire
morning.

You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during
a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and
the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice
elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell.

The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website.

Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by
12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely
manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

events.title: Return to Center: Exploring Stability, Mobility & Ease with Vickie Russell Bell
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves..



Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition.

Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.

events.description: The West Coast Blues Revue Experience world-class blues, dinner, and drinks — all in one intimate setting. NONSTOP MUSIC · 6:30 PM TO 9:30 PM · DOORS 5:15 PM Admission: $15 Led by the incomparable Hal Petcher, The West Coast Blues Revue brings together a rotating lineup of top-tier Bay Area talent. Each show delivers a fresh mix of powerhouse players, from Chris Burns to Tim Wagar plus surprise guests, all locking in for raw, soulful, high-energy blues that hits you right in the chest. With musicians who play like they've got something to prove, it is one of the most electric, authentic blues experiences in San Francisco. This is the Tuesday night house revue that regulars build their week around, and at fifteen dollars in a room this small, the good seats go early.   about The West Coast Blues Revue The Revue has become a Biscuits and Blues Tuesday night institution, running weekly since 2025 and drawing on the deep bench of players who keep San Francisco a blues town. events.title: Rent
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: In New York’s East Village, a group of young artists struggles to build lives, make art, and hold onto each other in the face of uncertainty. Over the course of a single year, friendships are tested, love is complicated, and every moment feels urgent. With an iconic score featuring “Seasons of Love,” “La Vie Bohème,” “Take Me or Leave Me,” and more, Jonathan Larson’s groundbreaking musical captures a generation living under the shadow of HIV/AIDS, where joy and loss exist side by side, and the question is not how long you have, but how you choose to spend it. Winner of the Tony Award for Best Musical and the Pulitzer Prize for Drama, Rent is an electrifying, deeply human story about connection, resilience, and living fully in the present.

events.title: Charm School with Lara Starr
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Learn to Make Resin Charms! Join us for this popular workshop where participants learn to make wearable charm keepsakes. What are resin charms? Little metal frames that you can fill with glitter, tiny gems, bits of paper ephemera, beads, leaves, or anything itty bitty! Perfect for capturing special memories from 2026 or making as gifts for loved ones. Instructor Lara Starr will provide all of the tools, supplies, and inspiration to make as many charms as you like during the three-hour workshop. You’re also welcome to bring little bits and bobs that are meaningful to you, such as an earring that has lost its mate, petals or tiny flowers, a ticket stub, a stamp from a special letter, or photo of a loved one. You'll graduate charm school with 5-7 unique mini-collage keepsakes! For ages 12 to adults. Meet Your Instructor Lara Starr is a publicist, cookbook author, former radio producer, Substacker, and semi-pro thrift shopper. A 25-year Marin resident, she’s mentored aspiring authors at Book Passage’s Path to Publishing Program. After making her first resin charm at Maker Faire, she couldn't wait to make more, and has been teaching Charm School workshops at private parties as well as at the Indie Alley, San Anselmo Recreation, and College of Marin Community Education. What students are saying about Lara: "(Lara) was very nice and explained things very well. She had an abundance of items for us to use and take with us. I got to take away quite a few gifts for people and myself. It was taught very coherently and it was an extremely creative outlet." Stephanie H. "(Lara) was warm, helpful and encouraging!" Anon. "This is a fun workshop to take with friends & family. My sister, niece, and I all enjoyed turning summer memories into charms we could keep and also give as gifts." Jen S.

events.title: Should Huckleberry Finn Be Banned from Our Schools — For Its Own Good?
events.location: The Commonwealth Club of California, San Francisco
events.description: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn has been in trouble almost from the moment Mark Twain published it, first in Britain in 1884 and then in the United States in 1885. The original objections included Huck’s bad behavior and socially subversive thinking, but also the book’s bad grammar and unconventional language.

events.title: Sufi Whirling Workshop with Anna Whirling and Dervish Aziz
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Learn the practice of Sufi whirling, using body movements and chanting to open the heart.

In this workshop we will be doing movement exercises and begin learning the practice of Sufi whirling.

This is a physical practice that uses body movements and chanting to open the heart, and experience the Unity of Love in the human body.

This workshop is open to all levels of experience. Come with an open heart, comfortable clothing, and socks

Aziz Abbatiello was raised in an American Mevlevi family. He has walked the path of the mystics following in the tradition of the Sufi. He was initiated as Semazen in 1996, and has made Sema with several Sufi groups in America and abroad.

Anna Whirling is from Ukraine. In the beginning of the war, she moved to Turkey and then to the United States. Anna has practiced whirling since her childhood. She has performed on stage for 20 years.

events.title: MELBA'S KITCHEN
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Winter Holiday Jazz Celebration · MELBA’S KITCHEN - the all-women big band spotlighting Black women musical geniuses Melba Liston and Mary Lou Williams, and their friends - delivers the holiday swing and soul to YOSHI’S. The “…Crackling!…unit” ( Downbeat ) lights up the pre-Solstice with Strayhorn/Ellington “Nutcracker” selections and legendary Liston and Williams compositions. The band will wrap up Melba Liston’s Centennial year with new pieces developed from Liston’s catalog, in-house compositions, and some seasonal surprises. MELBA’S KITCHEN is a “talent-packed ensemble” (Andy Gilbert), “so astonishing - so swinging” (Dr. Dee Spencer), that delivers “a marvelous night and good vibes all around.” (Rebeca Mauleon) MELBA’S KITCHEN honors the under-recognized jazz great MELBA LISTON and her formidable contributions to jazz. Liston toured with and wrote for Dizzy Gillespie, Quincy Jones, Gerald Wilson, and collaborated for decades - in the Ellington/ Strayhorn mode - with piano titan Randy Weston. Liston had a great big beautiful sound on the trombone, and was a pioneer as a woman in jazz. She arranged for many, including Abbey Lincoln, Betty Carter, Marvin Gaye, Clark Terry, and Ruth Brown. Liston also arranged for her dear friend and inspiration, MARY LOU WILLIAMS, who was an activist for jazz, a virtuosic and inspired pianist, composer, and arranger. MELBA’S KITCHEN intends to bring Liston’s and Williams’ names into your musical household. (Photo by Stu Brinin) (Headshot Photo by Irene Young)

events.title: Embodiment Practice: Mindful Movement + Stillness with Suzanne (Zan) Beahrs
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest.

Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. 

Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. 

Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. 

Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space.

Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like.

About Suzanne (Zan):
With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley

Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons): 
IG @suzannebeahrs suzannebeahrs.com

events.title: Deconstructing Yourself with Michael Taft
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. 

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

events.title: ROBERT GLASPER
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

events.title: Florencia Ramirez - The Kitchen Activist
events.location: Ferry Building Foodwise Classroom San Francisco, CA 94111
events.description: Meet & Greet Book Signing Only • SF Ferry Plaza Market 11:00 AM PT Food Demo // 11:30 AM PT Book Signing Please join us for a special meet and greet signing event with Florencia Ramirez, following her Foodwise demo at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market. The Kitchen Activist empowers readers to transform everyday meals into joyful, practical actions that reduce waste, restore the planet, and, with a 30-day meal planner and 17 approachable recipes, make the home kitchen a catalyst for meaningful environmental change. The Kitchen Activist is a spirited guide to transforming daily food choices into meaningful environmental action. With warmth, humor, and grounded research, Florencia Ramirez invites readers to reimagine the kitchen as a catalyst for change--after all, the global food system accounts for over 30% of greenhouse gas emissions, and the home kitchen is responsible for 42% of all food waste. From smart meal planning to low-waste shopping and regenerative food sourcing, this book offers practical strategies rooted in environmental science, cultural wisdom, and personal storytelling. Whether you're a seasoned cook or just starting out, The Kitchen Activist meets you where you are, with no judgment, only encouragement to begin making a difference. A follow-up to her award-winning Eat Less Water , this book serves as both a toolkit and a manifesto for anyone ready to connect their plate to the planet. "With its accessible action plans, this will encourage readers to build purposeful action into their everyday routines." —Publisher's Weekly " The Kitchen Activist shows us that food is about more than what’s on your plate. It tells the story of why what we eat matters—and, most of all, how it connects us to nature. Ramirez reminds us that farmers and everyone who works with food are part of that story. Eating, after all, is an act of nature." —Mas Masumoto, third-generation organic farmer and Julia Child Cookbook Award–Winning Author "Like music, food and the art of cooking cross political, environmental, artistic, and cultural barriers. The Kitchen Activist shows how we can be catalysts for positive environmental and social change, beginning right in our own kitchens." —Joan Baez Florencia Ramirez is the author of Eat Less Water: The Solution to Water Shortages Is in the Kitchen. A storyteller at heart and researcher by training, she holds a masters degree in public policy from the University of Chicago. Through writing, research, and lived experience, she explores how the everyday choices we make in our kitchens can become acts of environmental and social change. Her work has been featured on NPR, PBS, KTLA, CBS, KCRW's Good Food, and in the Los Angeles Times.She is the founder and Executive Director of the Pesticide Free Soil Project and the recipient of the Environmental Hero Award and the Gift of Freedom Award in Creative Nonfiction. Married and the mother of three Kitchen Activists, she splits her time between Oxnard, California, and Santa Fe, New Mexico. Florencia Ramirez - photo courtesy of Foodwise Event details: This event is a non-seated Meet & Greet signing only. This event will be hosted by Foodwise with Book Passage at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market (Foodwise Classroom tent) at the SF Ferry Building. Free Admission For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .
