events.title: Alligator Lizards in the Air: Integration Through Creative Expression with Krisztina Lazar
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Mercury), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression.

Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making.

Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore.

No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start.

Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity.

Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement.

Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

events.description: In New York’s East Village, a group of young artists struggles to build lives, make art, and hold onto each other in the face of uncertainty. events.title: Norman Fischer - The Great Road
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: From beloved Zen teacher and poet Norman Fischer, a new collection of wise and surprising essays that explores what it means to dive fully into spiritual practice and to embody our deepest aspirations in every waking moment. In The Great Road , acclaimed Zen teacher and writer Norman Fischer explores what it means to make everyday life itself a spiritual practice. Inspired by the teachings of legendary Japanese Zen master Eihei Dogen, this wide-ranging collection of essays examines the philosophy of “continuous practice”—the idea that awakening is not separate from ordinary living, but discovered within it. Weaving Buddhist thought with literature, Western philosophy, and deeply personal reflection, Fischer brings Dogen’s teachings into conversation with figures such as Simone Weil and William Wordsworth, while drawing on his own decades among America’s most influential Zen practitioners. The result is a work that moves fluidly between the spiritual, philosophical, and literary, inviting readers into a richer understanding of attention, compassion, and human experience. At once intellectually expansive and deeply intimate, The Great Road offers a timely meditation on how to live with greater presence and meaning in a distracted world— revealing the extraordinary possibilities contained within ordinary life. “A true delight! Norman Fischer has long been one of the best interpreters of Zen Buddhism for the modern world. By illuminating the everyday relevance of Zen's most far-reaching teachings, Fischer gives us a book that is simultaneously thought-provoking, inspiring, and deeply hopeful.” —Adam Frank, author of Light of the Stars: Aliens Worlds and the Fate of the Earth “Repetition is central in Zen practice, offering us an opportunity to see with fresh eyes. That’s the relationship you will want with this book, returning to it again and again for new insights. Norman has given us a deep and accessible book. He invites us into continuous practice and the miracle of presence in everyday life.” —Frank Ostaseski, author of The Five Invitations: Discovering What Death Can Teach Us About Living Fully “The Great Road winds around a single question: what is our human life, really, and what are we supposed to do about it? ... Continuous practice is not particular to Dogen or to Zen. It is the form of any serious human life. As Fischer teaches us, continuous practice means closing the gap between one's deepest aspirations and one's ordinary speaking, thinking, and acting.” —Bonnie Nadzam, author of The Magpie Spoke to Me: How the Stories We Tell Shape Our World NORMAN FISCHER is a Zen teacher, poet, translator, and director of the Everyday Zen Foundation. A beloved figure in the Buddhist world, he is also well-known for his efforts at interreligious dialogue. His numerous books include The World Could Be Otherwise: Imagination and the Bodhisattva Path, What Is Zen?: Plain Talk for a Beginner’s Mind, and Training in Compassion: Zen Teachings on the Practice of Lojong. Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

events.title: ROBERT GLASPER
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

events.description:
On the 1st and 3rd Sundays of every month, Sacred Garden Community gathers at the Alembic for Sunday Service between the hours of 11:00 am - 1:00 pm PST. 

Welcome! (Community) - 11:00 - 11:11
Connect to your sacred community of practice, grow connections. Introduce yourself if you're new or feeling it. 

Opening the way, in a good way -  11:11 - 11:20pm

Plant (Fungus + Molecule) Time! - 11:20 - 11:40
Plants, Molecules and Fungi, Oh my!

Community Satsang - 11:40-12:05
Around the wheel we go, where it stops nobody knows...

Closing, integrating, going forth - 12:05- 12:15pm
 
Community Announcements - (Community) 12:20-12:30 
Member Check-In, Fundraising, Calendar, Q&A, Processes Etc.

We also gather online every week if you are unable to make the Satsang live. The zoom link is the same every week for our online services and can be found at https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82492750630. 

We hope to see you around the garden soon!

Sacred Garden is a living sanctuary for globally identified seekers who yearn for authentic connection, radical inclusion, and collective evolution. We observes a principle of least dogma, which is the minimum belief we need to share to be a cohesive religious community. This is the entirety of our shared faith: We are open to the possibility that respectful practice with the Sacraments of our Church can bring about a direct experience of the Divine, within this lifetime.

events.title: Discovering Vividness: Meditation and Movement with Evolving Ground
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
The Bay Area Evolving Ground local group meets regularly at The Alembic to meditate together and explore contemporary Vajrayana. We meet and greet, then start with a short introduction to opening awareness meditation. We sit for 20 minutes, take a break, practice some slow standing meditations together, take a break, and then sit for another 20 minutes. We end with questions and discussion.

Opening awareness is a seated meditation leading to vividness and spacious clarity. It is Evolving Ground’s foundational meditation and is a contemporary version of the Dzogchen practice of shi-ne (shamatha in Sanskrit).

The movements come from the Sky Realm Series (Nam'khor in Tibetan). These are Dzogchen long-de practices unique to Evolving Ground. They look and feel quite similar to Qi Gong, though they operate on a different principle: discovery of the nonduality of clarity and bliss, through the experience of “tsal”—embodied awareness as non-ordinary sensation.

Attendees need no prior experience. There will be plenty of space for questions, reflections, and group exploration of the practices.

This meetup is free to attend.



Evolving Ground is a global community exploring a transformational path of passionate involvement with the world. Our life-affirming approach empowers creative, effective individuals: people who live with courage, kindness, and grace.

events.title: Butoh-Inspired Movement Meditation with Maya Kaufman
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Butoh is a slow, surreal movement practice rooted in deep listening, imagination, and transformation. In these guided movement meditations, we explore the body as landscape, myth, and memory, softening habitual patterns and awakening new ways of being. No dance experience is needed, only a curiosity and openness to move, feel, and enter the unknown.
Each class begins with a gentle opening circle to arrive, ground, and set intention together. We move into a somatic warm-up, awakening sensation, breath, and subtle awareness in the body. From there, you’ll be guided through a butoh-fu score; poetic, image and/or narrative based originally written long-form prompts that invite transformation from the inside out, allowing the body to become something other than itself. We’ll also explore simple butoh exercises that deepen presence, perception, connection, and imaginative embodiment.

We close with a soft landing: time to integrate, reflect, and share (if desired), leaving you resourced, expanded, and a little more in touch with the mysterious wisdom built of your body. Arrive however you are, and leave having touched something vast, intimate, and unknowably alive within you.

In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

events.title: Half-Day Silent Unguided Retreat
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic, 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice.
This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods.
There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of
meditation, all are welcome.

The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive
between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before
the first bell.

The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation:
9:30 AM – 10:10 AM
10:20 AM – 11:00 AM
11:10 AM – 11:50 AM

A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period.
The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between
sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom.
Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep
voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire
morning.

You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during
a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible.

This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and
the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice
elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell.

The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website.

Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by
12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely
manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

events.title: Return to Center: Exploring Stability, Mobility & Ease with Vickie Russell Bell
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves..



Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition.

Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.

events.title: MINDI ABAIR CHRISTMAS SHOW
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Be swept up in the joy of the season · PRE-SHOW WINE TASTING + MUSIC EXPERIENCE AVAILABLE HERE (SHOW TICKETS NOT INCLUDED) JOIN MINDI ABAIR AND FRIENDS FOR A MAGICAL NIGHT OF CHRISTMAS CLASSICS AND SMOOTH JAZZ HITS Mindi Abair’s I Can’t Wait For Christmas Tour is bringing the spirit of the holidays to audiences across the U.S. for an exciting, heartfelt season of music—now in its third year hosted by Mindi Abair. Joined by five exciting solo artists, expect Christmas classics you love, fresh original songs, and of course those moments that will make you laugh, tear up, and leave with your heart full of the Christmas spirit. Come early for the pre-show Wine and Jazz Tasting experience hosted by Mindi Abair and her husband Eric Guerra. Pouring their company’s www.WINEandJAZZ.com fine wines, Eric will walk the group through an informative wine-by-wine “taste like a sommelier” master class, while Mindi then pairs each wine style with a live performance song. During her remarkable 26-year recording career, Mindi Abair has garnered 2 GRAMMY nominations, recorded with some of the biggest names in music, and built a devoted following among jazz and blues audiences with her soaring melodies and powerhouse style. As co-founder of WineandJazz.com, she brings people around the world on intimate Wine & Jazz Adventures and hosts her annual Wine & Jazz New Year’s Eve in San Diego, CA. Rebecca Jade will move you. Named Smooth Jazz Network’s “Breakout Artist of the Year” and JazzTrax “Debut Artist of the Year” in 2022, she brings that rare mix of polish and raw emotion. She has toured extensively with Sheila E, shared the stage with Sir Elton John at the Academy Awards, and has been a regular featured artist on Dave Koz & Friends at Sea. She’s performed at Mindi Abair’s Wine & Jazz New Year’s Eve and Wine & Jazz Adventure in Sonoma, so the musical chemistry is already baked in. Andréa Lisa , the South African-born, New Zealand-raised singer, guitarist, composer, and producer, is a musical powerhouse – think the heart of Alicia Keys with the guitar sensibility of John Mayer. Her collaborations include Jonathan Butler, Kirk Whalum, and Kool & The Gang. She’s the artist who can melt a room with one lyric… then light it up with one solo. Xavier Gordon arrives as an exciting new voice on the jazz scene — pianist, songwriter, producer, and performer with a feel-good sound that hits hard live. He earned a GRAMMY nomination in 2018 for his production work and has toured extensively with Marcus Miller. Arthur Thompson , Mindi’s long-time drummer, is the heartbeat behind the music — a visionary artist with purpose as a drummer, vocalist, producer, author, and educator. He was voted 2023 “Breakout Artist of the Year” by the Smooth Jazz Network. And Darryl Williams brings smooth-jazz firepower. His debut album That Was Then earned praise from JazzTimes and national airplay on SiriusXM. He’s shared stages with heavy hitters like Dave Koz, Peter White, Gerald Albright, Jonathan Butler, and of course, Mindi Abair. This isn’t just another holiday show — it’s a night that will leave you energized, moved, and truly in tune with the joy of the season. Whether you come for the songs, the shared moments, or just to be swept up in the joy of the season, this night promises to stay with you long after the last note. For more info, visit mindiabair.com.

events.title: Insight Meditation Satsang with Sean Oakes
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
This meditation and study group is based in the Insight Meditation tradition and its sources in Thai Forest and Burmese Theravāda Buddhism. To this foundation, we add exploration of Mahāyāna Dharmas particularly from the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñāpāramitā) literature and lineage. The group meets weekly online, and on fourth Tuesdays live at the Alembic.

The focus of the group is on deepening in Buddhist liberation practice, and exploring the links between individual & systemic liberation in the form of social justice and collective healing. I bring a particular focus on working with the nervous system and resolving the symptoms of trauma, supported by devotional practice, study, and ethics as the basis of the path.

All are welcome. Cost is $5, plus Dāna (pay what you can). This is the online version of the event: https://momence.com/l/GBhB5e6w

Sean Oakes, PhD (he/him, queer, of Spanish/Puerto Rican and Northern European ancestry living on unceded Pomo land in California), teaches Buddhism, Yoga, and somatic practice. He has studied in Theravāda, Zen, and Vajrāyāna Buddhist lineages since 1993, including training as a monk in Burma, and was authorized to teach Insight Meditation by Jack Kornfield in 2010. His primary Buddhist teachers include Kornfield, Sylvia Boorstein, Gil Fronsdal, Eugene Cash, Kittisaro, Ṭhānissara, Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu, Anam Thubten, and Chammyay Sayadaw (U Janaka), with whom he ordained as a bhikkhu for a Rains Retreat in Burma in 2002.

He studied Haṭha and Vinyāsa Yogas with Alice Joanou, Rachel Shaw, Amanda Moran, and David Moreno, and taught mindfulness-based āsana and prāṇāyāma for 10 years. He performed for many years in music, dance, and performance art, including with Keith Hennessy’s Circo Zero, and was certified in Somatic Experiencing (SE) and Organic Intelligence (OI) with Steven Hoskinson, integrating the complex systems approach from OI in a distinctively Buddhist approach to trauma resolution. He received his PhD in Performance Studies from UC Davis in 2016, writing on extraordinary states of consciousness in Buddhist meditation and experimental dance. He teaches at Spirit Rock Meditation Center, East Bay Meditation Center, Insight Timer, and elsewhere, focusing on the integration of philosophy, somatics, and social justice discourse with the Dharma.

Website: SeanFeitOakes.com

events.description: Step into the Spirit—Where Christmas Meets God's Promise · Back by overwhelming demand, Nzuri Soul returns to Yoshi's Oakland with the fourth installment of her beloved holiday tradition, Christmas in Egypt IV – The Gift. After selling out year after year, this unforgettable production has become one of the Bay Area's most anticipated Christmas concerts. More than a concert, The Gift is an extraordinary musical experience that reimagines the Christmas story through the beauty, mystery, and majesty of Egypt—the place where the Holy Family found refuge. Through breathtaking vocals, powerful storytelling, and soul-stirring music, Nzuri Soul invites audiences on a journey of faith, hope, and celebration. Blending the timeless sounds of Gospel, R&B, Soul, Jazz, and inspirational music, this spectacular production features Nzuri Soul's award-winning live band, dynamic vocalists, and an atmosphere filled with joy, reverence, and celebration. Every song is thoughtfully woven together to honor the true meaning of Christmas while embracing the rich cultural beauty and spiritual significance of Egypt. From soaring worship moments to uplifting holiday classics and original music, The Gift reminds us that the greatest gift ever given was one of love, hope, peace, and salvation. It is a celebration for families, friends, and music lovers of every generation. Whether you're experiencing Christmas in Egypt for the first time or returning to continue the tradition, prepare for an evening that will inspire your heart, lift your spirit, and leave you filled with the joy of the season. This show sells out every single year. Don't wait. Secure your tickets early and experience one of the Bay Area's most unforgettable holiday traditions. Presented by Nzuri Soul About Nzuri Soul Award-winning vocalist, songwriter, producer, and entertainer Nzuri Soul has become one of the Bay Area's premier live performers, captivating audiences with her powerful voice, heartfelt storytelling, and unforgettable stage presence. Born in Texas and raised in Oakland, California, Nzuri Soul effortlessly blends R&B, Soul, Gospel, Jazz, and Funk into a signature sound that is both timeless and refreshingly original. Her music transcends genres, connecting deeply with audiences through messages of love, resilience, faith, and hope. A multiple-time Entertainer of the Year and Live Performer of the Year, Nzuri Soul continues to raise the standard for live entertainment. She has released five original studio albums, including her critically acclaimed Love Language, along with her beloved holiday project Christmas in Egypt, which has become a seasonal favorite for listeners year after year. Whether performing with her acclaimed band, leading inspirational productions, or creating unforgettable theatrical experiences, Nzuri Soul delivers every performance with authenticity, excellence, and soul. Her annual Christmas in Egypt concert series has grown into a cherished holiday tradition, drawing sold-out audiences who return each year to celebrate the music, the message, and the magic of Christmas through her unique artistic vision.

events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic.

As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest.

Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. 

Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. 

Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. 

Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space.

Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like.

About Suzanne (Zan):
With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley

Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons):

events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A Bay Area favorite family holiday tradition! Physical comedy maestro Unique Derique, the Clown Prince of Fools, is back at The Marsh Berkeley with his all-new show, Fool La La: Whimsical . This high-energy annual holiday extravaganza is packed with jaw-dropping circus feats, chest-thumping Hambone body percussion, and state-of-the-art multimedia special effects. It is custom-built to delight and inspire the whole family! Unique Derique is a longtime San Francisco Bay Area favorite whose dual careers merge the performing arts and healing with the belief that the world can be a brighter place, one laugh—and one breath—at a time. The “Clown Prince” comes out to play with classic physical comedy in performances that have spanned the globe in South Africa, Scotland, Taipei, London, Paris, and Tokyo, with TV appearances including PBS-KQED, Univision, and the Disney Channel. His clowny past includes the famed Pickle Family Circus , Children’s Fairyland, Prescott Circus Theatre, and Bread and Roses Presents and sharing the stage with entertainers such as Bobby McFerrin, The Temptations, Laura Nyro, Tuck and Patti, and Lou Rawls. Fool La La plays annually at The Marsh with a delightfully different twist each season. Described as “exhilarating,” the San Francisco Examiner has said of Derique, “he leaves them laughing coast to coast.” Hailed by The New York Times for his Hambone skill, he has also been lauded by the San Francisco Chronicle, who declared, “Derique will be back… remember the name.” When not bringing joy to all ages as a clown, alter-ego Lance McGee is a Trauma-Informed Wellness Consultant, Drama Therapist, and Mindfulness Coach providing support to school educators, administrators, staff, and students. He also leads workshops on trauma-informed care practices and mindfulness for non-profit organizations, health clinics, colleges and educational systems. events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A Bay Area favorite family holiday tradition! Physical comedy maestro Unique Derique, the Clown Prince of Fools, is back at The Marsh Berkeley with his all-new show, Fool La La: Whimsical . This high-energy annual holiday extravaganza is packed with jaw-dropping circus feats, chest-thumping Hambone body percussion, and state-of-the-art multimedia special effects. It is custom-built to delight and inspire the whole family! Unique Derique is a longtime San Francisco Bay Area favorite whose dual careers merge the performing arts and healing with the belief that the world can be a brighter place, one laugh—and one breath—at a time. The “Clown Prince” comes out to play with classic physical comedy in performances that have spanned the globe in South Africa, Scotland, Taipei, London, Paris, and Tokyo, with TV appearances including PBS-KQED, Univision, and the Disney Channel. His clowny past includes the famed Pickle Family Circus , Children’s Fairyland, Prescott Circus Theatre, and Bread and Roses Presents and sharing the stage with entertainers such as Bobby McFerrin, The Temptations, Laura Nyro, Tuck and Patti, and Lou Rawls. Fool La La plays annually at The Marsh with a delightfully different twist each season. Described as “exhilarating,” the San Francisco Examiner has said of Derique, “he leaves them laughing coast to coast.” Hailed by The New York Times for his Hambone skill, he has also been lauded by the San Francisco Chronicle, who declared, “Derique will be back… remember the name.” When not bringing joy to all ages as a clown, alter-ego Lance McGee is a Trauma-Informed Wellness Consultant, Drama Therapist, and Mindfulness Coach providing support to school educators, administrators, staff, and students. He also leads workshops on trauma-informed care practices and mindfulness for non-profit organizations, health clinics, colleges and educational systems. events.title: Avotcja & Modúpue: afro-latin jazz and poetry
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: AVOTCJA’s poetry is music and Avotcja’s music is poetry. Both are as hot as fire and as soothing as snow flakes. And in both she brings the best of her talent in Spanish and English. Listen to her. Read her. Enjoy her. Celebrate her.” • Camincha – Peruvian Poet/Novelist; & Pacifica Poet Laureate, 2017-2021. Poet / Playwright / Essayist / Fiction Writer / Multi-Percussionist / Photographer / Teacher, Avotcja is a Bay Area icon and is renowned for her group Modúpue. At Bird & Beckett tonight, Modúpue will be a quintet with Avotcja joined by violinist Sandi Poindexter , saxophonist Francis Wong , bassist Heshima Mark Williams and talking drum master Baba Ken Okolulo . Modúpue was named best jazz group of the year twice, in 2005 and again in 2010, by the Bay Area Blues Hall of Fame. Avotcja herself was named a “Jazz Hero” by the Jazz Journalists Association. Her radio shows on KPFA – Bebop, Cubop & the Musical Truth (Tuesdays, 8-10pm), and KPOO – La Verdad Musical (Fridays, noon-3pm), have been soul satisfying for decades, expressing the boundless joy she always finds in the music. As for her poetry, no one taps deeper wells of humanity than Avotcja! We love her more than we can express. Read here what Linda Tillery, Chuy Varela, Camincha, Greg Landau, Leslie Simon, Ishmael Reed, Lady Bianca, Elaine Cohen, Julian Carroll and Melanie Berzon have had to say in praise of Avotcja! The cover charge for the quintet tonight is $25 cash or venmo, payable at the door. College and high school students – $10. Grade school and younger, free. No one turned away for lack of funds. Wheelchair accessible. Bring your own beverages, but please eat out or at home before or after the show. Lots of good restaurants in the neighborhood, cafes, and grocers!

events.title: The Best Journey in the World: An Antarctic Story with Kim Stanley Robinson
events.location: Grace Cathedral, 1100 California St, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation, $49 with signed book Co-presented with Grace Cathedral’s The Forum Interweaving memoir and good old fashioned ice adventure, Kim Stanley Robinson’s latest takes readers along on the journeys that have happened before and those that may never happen again. In May of 1911, Robert Scott and his men said goodbye to the sun and settled in for the long Antarctic winter. When the sun returned in September, they would try to become the first people to reach the South Pole. However, a week past the winter solstice, Scott’s second-in-command decided to take an impromptu sled trip. Chronicled by zoological assistant Apsley Cherry-Garrard, this side trip became The Worst Journey in the World, one of the best adventure books ever written. Robinson first read Cherry-Garrard’s book in his twenties and re-read it again in 1995, as preparation for a research trip to Antarctica for his Mars novels. It was a dream excursion: he traveled around the continent, by snowmobile and helicopter and airplane, and followed in their ill-fated footsteps. Doors at 7:00 PM.

events.title: STEVE TURRE QUARTET
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the world’s preeminent jazz innovators, trombonist and seashellist Steve Turre, has consistently won both the Readers’ and Critics’ polls in JazzTimes, Downbeat, and Jazziz for Best Trombone and for Best Miscellaneous Instrumentalist (shells). Turre was born to Mexican-American parents and grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area, where he absorbed daily doses of mariachi, blues, and jazz. While attending Sacramento State University, he joined the Escovedo Brothers salsa band, which began his career-long involvement with that genre. In 1972, Steve Turre’s career picked up momentum when Ray Charles hired him to go on tour. A year later, Turre’s mentor Woody Shaw brought him into Art Blakey’s Jazz Messengers. After his tenure with Blakey, Turre went on to work with a diverse list of musicians from the jazz, Latin, and pop worlds, including Dizzy Gillespie, McCoy Tyner, J.J. Johnson, Herbie Hancock, Lester Bowie, Tito Puente, Mongo Santamaria, Van Morrison, Pharoah Sanders, Horace Silver, Max Roach, and Rahsaan Roland Kirk. The latter introduced a hum to the seashell as an instrument. Soon after that, while touring in Mexico City with Woody Shaw, Turre’s relatives informed him that his ancestors similarly played the shells. Since then, Turre has incorporated seashells into his diverse musical style. In addition to performing as a member of the Saturday Night Live Band since 1984, Turre leads several different ensembles. Sanctified Shells utilizes the seashell in a larger context, transforming his horn section into a “shell choir”. Turre’s Spring 1999 Verve release, Lotus Flower, showcases his Sextet With Strings. The recording explores many great standards and original compositions arranged by Turre for a unique instrumentation of trombone and shells, violin, cello, piano, bass, and drums. Turre’s quartet and quintet provide a setting based in tradition and stretching the limits conceptually and stylistically. In the Summer of 2000, Telarc released In the Spur of the Moment. This recording features Steve with three different quartets, each with a different and distinct master pianist: Ray Charles, Chucho Valdes, and Stephen Scott. Turre’s self-titled Verve release pioneers a unique artistic vision, drawing upon jazz, Afro-Cuban, and Brazilian sources. This innovative recording also features Cassandra Wilson, Randy Brecker, Graciela, Mongo Santamaria, and J.J. Johnson. Previously, Turre recorded Right There and Rhythm Within, featuring Herbie Hancock, Jon Faddis, Pharoah Sanders, and Sanctified Shells, on Verve’s subsidiary label, Antilles. Steve Turre continually evolves as a musician and arranger. He has a strong command of all musical genres, and when it comes to his distinct brand of jazz, he always keeps one foot in the past and one in the future.

events.title: Deconstructing Yourself with Michael Taft
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. 

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours prior to the event start.

events.title: COCO MONTOYA
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Award-winning guitar virtuoso and blues singer · " One of the most prodigious and gifted electric bluesmen on the planet...a deeply soulful singer and incendiary guitarist [with] a seemingly endless penchant for invention." –AllMusic "Smoking songs and heavy-hitting guitar full of fire and passion...Montoya’s rough-edged voice is filled with feeling. Bluesy, powerful and unpredictable...[It]really gets the blood flowing." –Blues Music Magazine "Montoya is a show-stopper...heartfelt singing and merciless guitar with a wicked icy burn. He is one of the truly gifted blues artists of his generation." –Living Blues “’Just play what you feel, be real about it, and enjoy yourself.’ That’s what Albert Collins taught me,” says the award-winning guitar virtuoso and soul-deep singer Coco Montoya. The self-taught, left-handed Montoya mastered his craft under Collins’ tutelage. Incorporating lessons learned from his mentors, the iconic Collins (for whom he originally drummed), and UK legend John Mayall, Montoya puts his own stamp on every song he performs. Since his first solo album in 1995 (which won him the Blues Music Award for Best New Artist), Montoya’s endlessly inventive guitar work and passionate, hard-hitting vocals have kept him at the top of the blues world. With his new Alligator Records album, Writing On The Wall (his sixth for the label), Montoya delivers what he is already calling one of the best records he’s ever made. For the very first time on Alligator, he decided to bring his road-tested band—noted keyboardist and songwriter Jeff Paris (Keb’ Mo’, Bill Withers), bassist Nathan Brown, and drummer Rena Beavers—into the studio with him. Between the camaraderie of the long-time bandmates and the sheer talent of all involved, the results have left Coco, in his words, “over the moon.” Produced by Grammy Award-winner Tony Braunagel (Bonnie Raitt, Taj Mahal) and co-produced by Jeff Paris, Writing On The Wall is a tour-de-force of memorable, hook-filled songs, sung with passion and fueled by equally memorable, top-shelf musicianship. The 13 tracks include five written or co-written by Montoya. The set opens with a signature, career-defining performance of the soul-baring I Was Wrong , written for Coco by songwriter Dave Steen. From the blistering Save It For The Next Fool to the enjoy now/pay later philosophy of Jeff Paris’ (I’d Rather Feel) Bad About Doin’ It to the riveting reinvention of Lonnie Mack’s Stop , Montoya delivers each song with heart-pounding emotion. Special guest Lee Roy Parnell adds his well-seasoned slide guitar to the smoldering A Chip And A Chair . And Coco’s friend, guitarist Ronnie Baker Brooks (son of late Alligator star Lonnie Brooks), joins in for some good-natured fun on the droll Baby, You’re A Drag and adds his blistering playing to the searing cover of Bobby Bland’s You Got Me. “I am so proud of this one,” Montoya says of Writing On The Wall . “We recorded in Jeff Paris’ studio, and everything just gelled together. And the band inspired me; they all gave extra effort at every turn. Jeff, Nathan and Rena played so great, they ended up making me play even harder. They made me sound better than I am!” Henry “Coco” Montoya was born in Santa Monica, California, on October 2, 1951, and raised in a working-class family. Growing up, Coco immersed himself in his parents’ record collection. He listened to big band jazz, salsa, doo-wop and rock ‘n’ roll. His first love was drums; he acquired a kit at age 11. He got a guitar two years later. “I’m sure the Beatles had something to do with this,” Montoya recalls. “I wanted to make notes as well as beats.” But guitar was his secondary instrument. Montoya turned his love of drumming into his profession, playing in a number of area rock bands while still in his teens and becoming an in-demand drummer. In 1969, Montoya saw Albert King opening a Creedence Clearwater Revival/Iron Butterfly concert at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles. He was transformed. “After King got done playing,” says Montoya, “my life was changed. When he played, the music went right into my soul. It grabbed me so emotionally that I had tears welling up in my eyes. Nothing had ever affected me to this level. He showed me what music and playing the blues were all about. I knew that was what I wanted to do.” The next chapter of Montoya’s story was kick-started by a chance meeting in the mid-1970s with legendary bluesman Albert Collins. Montoya says, “Albert was coming through Los Angeles and needed to borrow my drum set, which I left at the club where he was going to be playing. I went down to see his show that night, and it just tore my head off. The thing that I had seen and felt with Albert King came pouring back on me when I saw Albert Collins.” A short time later, Collins hired Montoya as his band’s drummer. With Albert mentoring Coco on the guitar during the band’s downtime, Coco soon became Collins’ second guitarist. “We’d sit in hotel rooms for hours and play guitar,” remembers Montoya. “He’d play that beautiful rhythm of his and just have me play along. He was always saying, ‘Don’t think about it, just feel it.’ He was like a father to me,” says Coco, who often slept at Collins’ home. When Collins declared Montoya his “son,” it was the highest praise and affection he could offer. In return, Montoya learned everything he could from the legendary Master of the Telecaster. Needing a more regular paycheck, Montoya left Collins’ band after two years and took a job tending bar, jamming on weekends at Los Angeles clubs. One day, legendary British musician John Mayall heard Coco playing Otis Rush’s All Your Love (I Miss Loving) onstage. Soon after, Mayall called on Montoya to join his famous Bluesbreakers. Filling the shoes of previous Bluesbreakers guitarists Eric Clapton, Peter Green and Mick Taylor would not be easy, but Montoya knew he could not pass up the opportunity to play with another legend. For the next ten years he toured the world and recorded with Mayall on seven albums, soaking up the experience of life on the road and in the recording studio. Montoya’s recorded debut as a bandleader came with 1995’s Gotta Mind To Travel (originally on Silvertone Records in England and later issued in the USA on Blind Pig Records). The album became an instant fan favorite. Blues enthusiasts, radio programmers, and critics sent praise from all corners. The album immediately made it clear that Montoya ranked among the best players on the contemporary scene. Two more Blind Pig albums followed, and Coco was well on his way. In 2000, Montoya’s Alligator debut, Suspicion , quickly became the best-selling album of his career, earning regular radio airplay on over 120 stations nationwide. Montoya’s fan base exploded. After two more highly successful and massively popular Alligator releases—2002’s Can’t Look Back and 2007’s Dirty Deal —Montoya signed with Ruf Records, cutting both a live and a studio album. Returning to Alligator with 2017’s Hard Truth and 2019’s Coming In Hot , the guitar master continued to blaze his trail. “Montoya unleashes one career-topping performance after another,” declared the UK’s Blues Matters . Still an indefatigable road warrior, Montoya continues to tour virtually nonstop, bringing audiences to their feet from New York to New Orleans to Chicago to San Francisco. Across the globe, he’s performed in countries including Australia, Belgium, Switzerland, Germany, Norway, England, Brazil, Argentina, Spain, Mexico, Ecuador, Italy, Poland, Russia, the Czech Republic and Canada. Now, with the dynamic Writing On The Wall and a tour calendar busting at the seams, Coco Montoya is as excited as he’s ever been to perform the new songs live with his burning-hot band. Montoya’s well-earned reputation as an eye-popping live performer precedes him. Vintage Guitar states, “Coco keeps getting better and better. He plays with fire and passion rarely seen in this day and age.” Billboard declares, “In a world of blues guitar pretenders, Coco Montoya is the real McCoy. He exudes power and authenticity. Be prepared to get scorched by the real thing.”

events.description: Dancers ages 14–25* are invited to come dance with us for a full weekend during our LINES Winter Weekend. During this 2-day workshop, students will get a sneak peek into the experience and process that makes Alonzo King LINES Ballet’s education programs so transformative. Dancers will be placed in appropriate groups for the classes according to age and/or level. Classes include ballet, LINES repertory, contemporary, floorwork, GYROKINESIS® , investigative improvisation, guided movement generation, & more. Dancers may join us for the full workshop or choose to participate for just 1 day. Students applying for our renowned 2027 Summer Program may also use LINES Winter Weekend as their audition. It is included in their experience! REGISTER Limited scholarships are available! Learn more and apply for a scholarship to attend here . Curriculum Ballet, LINES Ballet Repertoire, Movement Exploration, Contemporary, and GYROKINESIS® Dress Code There is no dress code, nor are there restrictions of color or style. However, one must wear tasteful, form-fitting dance or athletic wear, and appropriate footwear (socks, ballet slippers) should be used for classes accordingly. events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: ANA POPOVIC
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the most dynamic forces in contemporary blues · Grace. Power. Drive. Meet the Queen of the Pack Some guitar players play the blues. Ana Popovic sets it on fire. An award-winning guitarist, singer, songwriter, and bandleader, Ana Popovic is a force of nature onstage. Blending smoking electric funk, fiery slide guitar, soulful vocals, jazz-infused instrumentals, and deep blues grooves, she has created a sound that is unmistakably her own. For more than 25 years, Popovic has relentlessly toured the world, continually pushing the boundaries of contemporary blues. Her music never stands still. She bends genres, challenges expectations, and reinvents herself with every record, while remaining deeply connected to the power, emotion, and freedom of the guitar. A ten-time Blues Music Award nominee, Popovic was the only female guitarist selected for the 2014-2018 Experience Hendrix all-star lineup, sharing the stage with legendary artists including Buddy Guy, Eric Johnson, and Kenny Wayne Shepherd. She has appeared on the covers of Vintage Guitar and Guitar Player and has shared headlining stages with B.B. King, Joe Bonamassa, Gary Clark Jr., Robben Ford, Keb' Mo', and many other major artists. Bruce Springsteen summed up her musicianship simply: "One helluva guitar player." Popovic's recordings have earned widespread critical and commercial recognition. Can You Stand the Heat and Unconditional were named Pick of the Week by USA Today and featured by NPR Music. Her album POWER reached #1 on the Billboard Blues Albums chart, marking another major milestone in her career. Albums including Like It On Top, Trilogy, Can You Stand the Heat, Unconditional, and Dance to the Rhythm have all appeared among Billboard's best-selling blues albums. Her international profile has also been reflected in numerous magazine covers, including Vintage Guitar (US), Guitar Player Gear Guide (US), Blues Music Magazine (US), Blues Magazine (France), American Blues Scene (US), and Blues Matters! (UK), among many others. POWER & FANTASTAFUNK POWER is a record about unity, friendship, resilience, and the strength we find in one another. Its striking cover-two hands, one black and one white, holding on to each other-captures the album's central message: connection and collective strength have the power to move the world forward. Recorded during one of the most challenging periods of Ana's life, POWER became a deeply personal expression of survival and a renewed faith in the transformative power of music. That same spirit inspired Popovic's FANTASTAFUNK, an explosive 11-piece big band launched in 2023. Bringing together funk, gospel, soul, and blues, FANTASTAFUNK expands her guitar-driven sound into a full-scale, high-energy live experience designed for major festival stages. DANCE TO THE RHYTHM In 2025, Popovic released DANCE TO THE RHYTHM, a vibrant celebration of perseverance, joy, gratitude, and a renewed love of life. Created with longtime collaborator Buthel, the ten-track album blends funk, soul, blues, and gospel into what Popovic calls her "ever-evolving gumbo of sound." Tracks such as "Dance to the Rhythm" and "Sho Nuff" push the electric guitar into infectious, dance-driven grooves, while songs including "Dwell on the Feeling" and "Sisters and Brothers" explore inclusiveness, resilience, faith, love, and the powerful connection between artist and audience. As Popovic puts it: "POWER was about survival. DANCE is about celebrating life-a second chance." Popovic writes for the stage-and that is where her music truly comes alive. Whether leading her powerful band or the FANTASTAFUNK big band, she delivers performances that are soulful, fearless, dynamic, and impossible to sit still through. Ana Popovic isn't just playing the blues. She's pushing it forward. She remains one of the most dynamic forces in the contemporary blues and beyond. Endlessly curious, fiercely committed, and always evolving, Ana Popovic is not simply carrying the blues into the future-she is helping redefine what the genre can become. When she's not on the road, Popovic divides her time between Los Angeles, California, and Detroit, Michigan. She is endorsed by Fender, D'Addario, Jim Dunlop, and DR Strings. 'Plainly and simply - the album is damn good. Selections such as "Worked Up.* "California Chase.* "Hurt So Good," and "Dwell On the Feeling" shine as a medium between the artist's Blues. Funk. and Soul meeting place, where her skills as a guitar virtuoso and her soul-nature converge naturally and brilliantly. "Highly recommended* is an understatement. GOLDMINE MAG (USA) ' Dance To The Rhythm' sees Ana Popovic at the top of her game; all the songs are fabulous, yet diverse. A lot of thought and passion has gone into this. An album that you will be going back to again and again. POWERPLAY MAG (UK)

events.location: San Francisco
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Barbara has to clean out her oddball uncle’s house. He’s dead. Does she find his porn stash? Of course. Is that the strangest thing in there? Not by a long shot. Barbara explores family secrets from an unusual perspective. It’s about what happens when someone becomes the in-case-of-emergency person for the elephant in the family room. My Dead Uncle’s Porn Collection is about confronting the damage done by a dysfunctional family and coming through it with grace and humor. Yes, humor! So many aspects of the story are just ludicrous. You can’t make this stuff up! Following a career in business communication, Barbara discovered solo performance (like so many others) in David Ford’s class. What started as an attempt to blow off steam turned into two solo shows, (so far). She is a frequent performer at The Marsh and other Bay Area performance venue and has performed at The Marsh’s In Front of Your Eyes Festival, The PlayGround Free-Play Festival, The Binge Fringe Festival at Santa Monica Playhouse, Orlando International Theater Festival, Cincinnati Fringe, Tampa Fringe, Ooley Theater Women’s Wit & Wisdom Festival, Rogue Festival, Soaring Solos Stars Series and elsewhere, to laudatory reviews. events.title: Deconstructing Yourself with Michael Taft
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Sol), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation.  We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108

Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. 

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours prior to the event start.

events.title: Phoebe Thompson - Girls Our Age
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: Join us at Book Passage for an author event in celebration of Phoebe Thompson and her debut novel, Girls Our Age. Three women navigate their late twenties together in a bittersweet novel about female friendship, identity, and growing up—from the hope and promise of college to the realities that lie beyond. Lily, Ana, and Margot have been best friends ever since Hawthorne Res Life assigned them as roommates during their first year of college. Ten years later and Lily is planning her wedding to the endlessly supportive and entirely symmetrical Jack. Ana is a fourth-grade teacher at the prestigious Horizon Academy, alma mater of her long-term boyfriend, who’s finally asked her to move in. Margot is about to land a life-changing promotion at ad agency McQueen O’Doul. It all looks good from here. But when the three friends converge on Maine for the wedding, the real challenges they’ve been able to keep from each other begin to surface. It’s finally time to open up about the very private struggles they’ve hidden for too long and the risks they’ve taken to protect themselves, and those they love, from the truth. “Nostalgic, aching, and sharply observed, Girls Our Age is a story about the friendships that shape us, the lives we think everyone else is living, and the quiet heartbreak of realizing we only ever see the polished version. With tender precision, Phoebe Thompson reminds us that girlhood never really leaves us and that the people who knew us then often know us best now.” —Alissa DeRogatis, author of Call It What You Want “Girls Our Age is full of heart, tenderness, and characters who are so lifelike they might as well be my own friend group, with all the struggles, doubts, and aches of twentysomething adulthood. Thompson’s empathetic and riveting debut pulls on the heartstrings, will make you text your friends just to tell them how much you love them, and announces an exciting new voice in fiction.” —Isabel Banta, author of Honey “I see myself and my closest friends in the characters of Girls Our Age, an honest and gripping coming-of-age story about the ways that friendships bend and waver in your twenties, only to grow back stronger. I devoured this book, and I didn’t want to say goodbye to Lily, Margot, and Ana!” —Morgan Pager, author of The Art of Vanishing “Visceral and emotional, Girls our Age is a monument to the metamorphosis from girlhood to adulthood. In her unflinching debut, Phoebe Thompson renders all the intimate, hilarious, painful nuances that make friendship among girls of any age some of life’s most compelling subject matter.” —Courtney Preiss, author of Welcome Home, Caroline Kline Phoebe Thompson writes about female friendship, mothers and daughters, and money. She studied English literature at Bowdoin College, got her MFA in fiction at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, and runs a marketing agency in Brooklyn, New York. She grew up in Mill Valley, California. GIRLS OUR AGE is her debut. You can follow her on Instagram and TikTok: @phoebethompsonwrites Phoebe Thompson - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Free Admission / Open Seating Following the presentation, there will be a signing line or a meet-and-greet. For any questions regarding our events, please contact us at books@bookpassage.com .

Stanford GSB alumnus. Forged on a Stanford × U.S. Army mission in 2016, applied at Home Depot Supply’s $1.3B eCommerce P&L and across 20+ years in Product. Thought Leader at Forbes. events.title: RISING - Irma Herrera's The ICEmen Cometh
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: (Please do not bring infants to the show) The ICEmen Cometh critiques the Trump Regime’s full-frontal attack on immigrants, and how the brutality and cruelty of ICE agents as they catch, detain, disappear, and deport people, is eroding the civil rights of everyone in the United States. Stories about earlier waves of anti-immigrant hysteria explain how white supremacy has shaped our nation’s immigration laws. Irma Herrera’s new play, The ICEmen Cometh, uses current events to examine the history of immigration and the racial attitudes that have controlled who is allowed entry into the United States. Her first solo show, Why Would I Mispronounce My Own Name? is a personal narrative with laugh-out-loud humor and a substantial dose of American history. Her characters show who is valued and seen as “Real Americans.” The play had a five-month run at The Marsh Theaters (both SF and Berkeley) and has been performed nationally. Before becoming a playwright and solo performer, Irma was a San Francisco-based civil rights lawyer and journalist for three-plus decades. Through her powerful plays, Irma urges audiences to confront the enduring power of xenophobia, racism, sexism, and other forms of prejudice, and to speak up for fairness and equality.
