events.title: ANDY MCKEE
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: One of the world’s finest acoustic guitarists · Andy McKee is one of the world’s finest acoustic guitarists, and it’s evident from the accolades he’s received throughout his career. It’s his youthful energy, attention to song structure and melodic content that elevates him above the rest. After nearly a decade without releasing new studio recordings, McKee returns with his six-track EP, Symbol, out Friday, September 17 on Mythmaker Records in conjunction with Cruzen Street Records. “These are my interpretations of tunes that really inspired me,” says McKee. “I wanted to give listeners a chance to hear what I hear when I listen to this music. I also wanted to branch out a bit and include music that isn’t originally for acoustic guitar.” While Symbol is a collection of inspired renditions, they are important song choices; artists that deeply influence McKee and songs that connect to his musical past. He pulls from the catalogues of greats like Michael Hedges, Preston Reed, Billy McLaughlin, and Prince. There’s “Ragamuffin,” the EP’s lead single, which is a nod to one of McKee’s biggest influences, Michael Hedges. McKee notes that “Michael was not only a revolutionary guitarist on the technical side, his ability to compose for solo guitar was also genius. Most importantly though, he was able to search inside of himself and consistently pull up very human and evocative themes that made him a true artist. I’ll always be grateful for his music.” One track that might catch fans by surprise on Symbol is McKee’s gorgeous rendition of Prince’s “Purple Rain.” In 2012, McKee played alongside Prince in his band on the “Welcome 2 Australia” tour, with the song being one of the setlist highlights. “I had originally come up with the ‘Purple Rain’ arrangement to open the shows with while I was on tour with Prince in Australia,” recalls McKee. “I have played it occasionally since then while touring and figured I should finally get a recording of it down. One thing that I learned from Prince while we were on the road is that we both really admire Joni Mitchell. I used that as a reference when trying to describe what I do. Although some of what I do on the guitar is technically demanding, I don’t ever really want that to overshadow the music.” Another standout from Symbol is McKee’s take on “Chattanooga” by acclaimed guitarist Preston Reed. “In my opinion, ‘Chattanooga’ by Preston Reed is one of the finest fingerstyle guitar pieces ever written,” saysMcKee. “It’s just loaded with texture, harmony, percussion, and melody. I love the key changes and chromaticism between some of the chords. This tune really inspired me a lot.” McKee, like many, was infatuated with the Rocky IV soundtrack, specifically the Vince DiCola compositions “War” and “Training Montage.” For Symbol, McKee and DiCola joined forces to craft “Rocky IV Medley.” “That was about as surreal as it gets for me,” says McKee. “I became a fan of Vince’s work when I was six years old, and I bought the soundtrack to the film on cassette. I used to listen to it all the time on my Sony Walkman, and I really found that my favorite tunes were the instrumental tracks, which were “War” and “Training Montage” from Vince. Those tunes awakened my mind to the possibility of being moved by music with no words. To be able to recreate those tunes with the electric guitar and play with Vince is really something I could never have dreamed of.” Andy McKee entertains both the eye and the ear as he magically transforms the steel string guitar into a full orchestra via his use of altered tunings, tapping, partial capos, percussive hits and a signature two-handed technique. McKee’s crossover success has helped him to achieve millions upon millions of YouTube viewers, underscoring his emergence as one of today’s most unique and influential artists. His song “Drifting” became one of the first YouTube viral videos with almost 60 million views. He has been featured as a cover story in both Acoustic Guitar Magazine in the U.S. and Acoustic Magazine in the UK. He also curates his own annual guitar retreat called Musicarium. McKee’s tour dates have taken him through Europe, Asia, Australia and North America, including tours with legendary acts from Dream Theater to Tommy Emmanuel.

events.title: Christy Scott Cashman - What Happened in Beulah
events.location: Book Passage Corte Madera 51 Tamal Vista Blvd. Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: A teenage girl uncovers the dark secrets of her Smoky Mountain town while searching for a missing classmate in this gripping coming-of-age mystery perfect for fans of Where the Crawdads Sing . Nestled in the foothills of the Smoky Mountains, Beulah has always seemed steady—rooted in tradition, shaped by generations, and slow to change. But in 1986, the ground has shifted, and no one feels that more than fifteen-year-old Barrett Childress Owens. Between her parents’ unraveling marriage and a school full of kids she can’t connect with, she feels invisible in her own hometown. When Lacy Gunderson, the captivating new girl everyone is curious about, suddenly vanishes, the town’s calm surface fractures. Search parties comb the woods. A police investigation begins. Rumors multiply. Families close ranks. And Barrett begins to sense how much the adults around her choose not to say. As Beulah clings to its usual rituals—including the annual Miss Kudzu pageant, which has shaped local girlhood for decades—Barrett is forced to navigate a community where loss lingers in the air and secrets are carefully kept. Her journey through the uncertainty reshapes her understanding of friendships, family, and the complex place she calls home. A rich coming-of-age story with a pulse of mystery and a budding romance, What Happened in Beulah explores the fault lines of a small town and the courage it takes to face the truths people would rather bury. Christy Scott Cashman is a mother, author, and active member of the literary and arts communities. She serves on the boards of directors of the Associates of the Boston Public Library and the American Film Institute and is the founder of YouthINK, a nonprofit mentorship program for young artists in the United States and Ireland. events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: NPR’s Emily Feng on How China’s Repression Fueled a Militant Movement…In Syria
events.location: Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California, San Francisco
events.description: What drove a few thousand men and women from the deserts and cities of western China to the front lines of Syria’s war? In her new book, Our Hearts Burned for Home, journalist Emily Feng unearths the untold story of Uyghur exiles who fled China’s expanding police state—only to become a pivotal force behind the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime. At the heart of this narrative is a startling paradox: Beijing’s repression, meant to crush dissent, instead scattered and radicalized a generation.

events.title: INVENTION OF SOLITUDE BOOK CLUB: TAIWAN TRAVELOGUE
events.location: Books Inc. Alameda, 1344 Park St, Alameda, CA 94501
events.description: Join us for the Invention of Solitude Fiction Book Club. This month we will be discussing the novel, Taiwan Travelogue by Yang Shuang-Zi. About the book: WINNER OF THE 2024 NATIONAL BOOK AWARD FOR TRANSLATED LITERATURE WINNER OF THE 2026 INTERNATIONAL BOOKER PRIZE A bittersweet story of love between two women, nested in an artful exploration of language, history, and power May 1938. The young novelist Aoyama Chizuko has sailed from her home in Nagasaki, Japan, and arrived in Taiwan. She's been invited there by the Japanese government ruling the island, though she has no interest in their official banquets or imperialist agenda. Instead, Chizuko longs to experience real island life and to taste as much of its authentic cuisine as her famously monstrous appetite can bear. Soon a Taiwanese woman-who is younger even than she is, and who shares the characters of her name-is hired as her interpreter and makes her dreams come true. The charming, erudite, meticulous Chizuru arranges Chizuko's travels all over the Land of the South and also proves to be an exceptional cook. Over scenic train rides and braised pork rice, lively banter and winter melon tea, Chizuko grows infatuated with her companion and intent on drawing her closer. But something causes Chizuru to keep her distance. It's only after a heartbreaking separation that Chizuko begins to grasp what the "something" is. Disguised as a translation of a rediscovered text by a Japanese writer, this novel was a sensation on its first publication in Mandarin Chinese in 2020 and won Taiwan's highest literary honor, the Golden Tripod Award. Taiwan Travelogue unburies lost colonial histories and deftly reveals how power dynamics inflect our most intimate relationships.

events.description:

Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Grace Hwang Lynch Author Talk • How to Cook Rice: On the Care and Feeding of an Immigrant Family
events.location: Omnivore Books on Food, 3885a Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Grace Hwang Lynch is a San Francisco Bay Area writer specializing in Asian American food and culture. Her writing has been published by outlets such as NPR, Eating Well, KQED, San Francisco Chronicle, and San Jose Mercury News and was a finalist for an IACP Food Writing award. Follow her on Instagram @gracehwanglynch. Linda Shiue, MD, Chef , is a Taiwanese American physician, professionally trained chef, and author of the award-winning cookbook, Spicebox Kitchen. She is the Director of Culinary Medicine and Lifestyle Medicine at Kaiser Permanente San Francisco, where she founded Thrive Kitchen, a teaching kitchen. You can connect with Dr. Shiue @spiceboxtravels. In How to Cook Rice: On the Care and Feeding of an Immigrant Family , Grace Hwang Lynch takes readers on a bittersweet journey as the firstborn daughter of Taiwanese immigrants learning to navigate the California suburbs, Asian American identity, and motherhood while exploring what love, food, and family mean in light of her generational roots. Through Grace’s stories and included recipes, these meals express what words cannot, prompting an examination of what love—and food—mean in an immigrant family.

Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young.

He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True.

From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: @ (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: @ Songwriters Victoria Rose and Stone Filipczak are the creative force behind @, a singular duo whose inventive collaboration has reimagined psychedelic folk for a new generation. On Autosmile, their first album for 4AD, the pair expand on the acclaimed promise of their debut Mind Palace Music, blending timeless songwriting with adventurous arrangements, dense harmonies, and a playful spirit that constantly pushes beyond genre boundaries. Though now based in Philadelphia, Victoria and Stone continue their distinctive songwriting process: working independently before completing each other’s compositions. Recorded largely at home with a humble collection of equipment and enriched by contributions from close friends on cello, violin, and drums, Autosmile transforms lo-fi methods into something remarkably lush, immersive, and emotionally resonant. Across eleven songs, @ balance darkness and wonder with striking confidence. The album moves effortlessly between haunting folk textures, progressive flourishes, indie-pop hooks, and moments of cinematic beauty. Highlights include the expansive title track “Autosmile,” the nostalgic earworm “I Know You Are (But What Am I Thinking),” and the intricately arranged “Punish My Mind,” each exploring themes of change, self-reflection, loss, and acceptance through lyrics that remain deliberately open-ended and deeply relatable. Equal parts mysterious, virtuosic, and playful, Autosmile showcases @ at their most fully realized—an adventurous partnership capable of looking backward and forward at once. It is an album of contrasts: beauty and pain, humor and gravity, intimacy and ambition. In the face of uncertainty, @ offer curiosity, connection, and the possibility of transformation. Bandcamp | IG Support to be announced. DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.description: A father sets out to build the perfect daughter. events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.description: Students ages 11–25 are invited to audition for our 2027 Summer Program hosted in San Francisco! We are searching for aspiring dance artists to train with our exceptional faculty this summer at LINES Dance Center. Class will be led by former LINES Ballet artist and faculty member Brett Conway and LINES faculty member Sandra Chinn . Our Summer Program offers a unified approach to dance training. Rooted in the philosophy of Alonzo King , our programs guide students on a collaborative journey that values risk-taking, independent thinking, problem solving through exploration, and a tenacious work ethic, expanding students’ understanding of what is possible with dance . San Francisco Summer Program 2027 Dates Pre-Professional (ages 18–25) | June 7–26 Junior Week 1* (ages 11–14) | June 28–July 2 Junior Week 2* (ages 11–14) | July 5–9 Advanced (ages 14–17) | July 12–31 *Those accepted to the Junior Program may attend one or both weeks of the program AUDITION DETAILS Summer Program Audition | Ages 11–25 Sunday, March 7, 2027 2–4pm PST Check-in starts at 1:30pm PST REGISTER Format and Attire Details The audition consists of a ballet class, LINES repertoire, and movement exploration. Wear form-fitting dancewear and style hair neatly away from your face. Most students wear a leotard and tights or shorts, but there is no restriction on color or style. Pointe work is optional at the audition. Required Materials for LINES Summer Program Auditioners Please upload these items to your audition registration account in ACTIVE. Registration | via ACTIVE System Headshot | Think smiling passport or ID picture Video Clip Link for ages 14–25* | 1–2 minutes of contemporary or improvisational movement highlighting your movement quality and artistic choices (optional) *Make sure all videos are set to public so we can view them. Registration and Refund Policies —Fees paid by credit card only —No refunds. Dancers may transfer to another audition session —Online registration only Photography: Alonzo King LINES Ballet | Summer Program | © Steve Disenhof

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Writing Into The Next Chapter: Exploring Your Creative Potential in Midlife and Beyond
events.location: Book Passage, Corte Madera Store 51 Tamal Vista Blvd Corte Madera, CA 94925
events.description: By midlife and beyond, the societal messages for women and non-binary people are clear: disappear or accept whatever life has wrought in their personal and creative lives. Two authors who span generations, Kate Farrell (Silent Generation) and Jordan Rosenfeld (Gen X), reject this notion completely. This workshop offers revised attitudes and innovative approaches to our writing and lives in midlife and beyond. Come prepared to discuss, write, and reframe how we think about creativity, feminine archetypes, and aging. Drawing on mythology, literary examples, personal stories, psychological research, and an exploration of the enduring power of feminine creativity (widely defined), Kate and Jordan crack open old ideas and lead participants in exercises to awaken our essential forces through challenging midlife transitions. You don’t have to be a writer, but come prepared to respond to thoughtful, playful prompts that ignite the power of your life's next chapter. Meet Your Instructors Jordan Rosenfeld is author of Writing Through the Pause: Mining Midlife for Powerful W riting , seven other books on the craft and process of writing including Make a Scene, How to Write a Page Turner , and The Sound of Story: Developing Voice and Tone in Writing , and three novels, with a fourth, Seeking Solace , publishing in ’28. Learn more at Jordanrosenfeld.net and jordanwritelife.substack.com. Kate Farrell is the author of Fairy Tale Heroine: Live and Write Her Journey, Story Power: Secrets to Creating, Crafting, and Telling Memorable Stories , and she founded Woven, an ongoing workshop platform using the framework of the heroine's journey for creative projects. Read more at woventales.net and katefarrell.net .

events.title: 40 FINGERS
events.location: Yoshi's, 510 Embarcadero West, Oakland, CA 94607
events.description: Phenomenal quartet of guitarists · They are called 40 FINGERS, they are Italian and they are the phenomenal quartet of guitarists who, to the tune of millions of views, are conquering social networks all over the world (over 100 million views: https://www.youtube.com/@40Fingers) with their masterful reinterpretations and rearrangements of fa-mous rock and pop hits, film and TV series soundtracks, and an official endorsement such as that of Queen, who applauded and published on their website the “40 Fingers” version of Bohemian Rhapsody (official Queen website). They have also been acclaimed by numerous Italian and international music stars who have chosen them to duet together: from Andrea Bocelli to US singer Tory Kelly, and Andy Summers of The Police to revisit the band’s famous song “Bring on the Night”(https://bit.ly/40fingerspolice). Each with a strong musical history and a different background, the four musicians together explore new sonic universes in the name of fingerpicking, proposing a vast repertoire that starts with a reinterpretation for four guitars of rock and pop songs and ends with their own original compositions. The shared passion that the four of them have for the world of film and TV series and for their scores has also led them to try their hand at a series of original arrangements of famous soundtracks, including their “40 finger” version of the two main themes of John Williams' work on George Lucas' Star Wars saga, The Last of the Mohicans, a sensational Disney medley and the medley from Harry Potter, also including some of the themes written by the great John Williams. The stage is the natural home of 40 FINGERS. Accompanied by a highly spectacular visual production created by some of Europe's best light designers, they take the audience on a musical journey with no linguistic or geographical boundaries through their versions of Sultans of Swing, Africa, Sound of Silence, Bohemian Rhapsody, The Last of the Mohicans, Libertango and other tracks that span genres in a comprehensive way, uniting and thrilling all music lovers.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: Flamenco Vivo Carlota Santana
events.location: Presidio Theatre, 99 Moraga Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: Popular and innovative Flamenco Vivo Carlota Santana returns with Quinto Elemento (Fifth Element), an evening-length work by acclaimed choreographer Patricia Guerrero, winner of Spain’s National Dance Award, with an original score by Francis Gómez performed live. Featuring Flamenco Vivo’s world-renowned international cast of dancers and musicians, the work explores the invisible essence that connects all things. Guerrero is hailed by The New Yorker as “a master of tradition who dares to deconstruct the art form.”

events.description: If you are unable to audition with us in-person, we welcome you to submit a video audition! We are searching for aspiring dance artists to train with our exceptional faculty this summer at LINES Dance Center in San Francisco. Our Summer Program offers a unified approach to dance training. Rooted in the philosophy of Alonzo King , our programs guide students on a collaborative journey that values risk-taking, independent thinking, problem solving through exploration, and a tenacious work ethic, expanding students’ understanding of what is possible with dance . Video Requirements Audition footage should be no longer than 8 minutes in length. The intention is to show technical clarity, placement and understanding. Please include: Barre work | 1 side only Center adagio Pirouettes Petite & Grande Allegro Solo | 1–2 minutes of contemporary or improvisational movement highlighting your movement quality and artistic choices. *Make sure all videos are set to public so we can view them. Registration Opens January 1 Accepting submissions January 1–March 31, 2027. Additional Required Materials Please upload these items to your audition registration account in ACTIVE. Registration | via ACTIVE portal Headshot | Think smiling passport or ID picture Video link | Please remember to set your video to “public” so we can view it. San Francisco Summer Program 2027 Dates Pre-Professional (ages 18–25) | June 7–26 Junior Week 1* (ages 11–14) | June 28–July 2 Junior Week 2* (ages 11–14) | July 5–9 Advanced (ages 14–17) | July 12–31 *Those accepted to the Junior Program may attend one or both weeks of the program Registration and Refund Policies —Fees paid by credit card only —No refunds. Dancers may transfer to another audition session —Online registration only Photography: Alonzo King LINES Ballet | Summer Program | © Steve Disenhof

events.title: Lizard Boy
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Trevor has spent years hiding from the world. Ever since a childhood encounter left him with green, scaly skin, he’s become something of a local legend in Seattle, more myth than man. But on the night of Monster Fest, he decides to take a risk. A first date with his crush, Cary, pulls him out of isolation and into a city alive with possibility. When an unexpected encounter hints that the past may not be finished with him, Trevor is forced to confront the part of himself he’s tried to keep hidden. With an electrifying indie-rock score, Lizard Boy has become a cult favorite, celebrated for its originality, heart, and genre-bending storytelling. This bold, offbeat musical is a celebration of identity, connection, and the courage it takes to be seen.

Based on the beloved 1976 Paramount Pictures film written by Bill Lancaster , this new musical follows a washed-up baseball player who takes a job coaching a ragtag team of Little League misfits, including his ex-stepdaughter. Through practice, persistence, and some good luck, they just may find victory in surprising places. Remember: they're not losers. events.title: Perfect Daughter
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: A father sets out to build the perfect daughter. With the help of a scientist, he creates an AI version of Claudia, adjusting her life again and again in pursuit of something just right. But each new iteration brings unexpected results. The more he tries to control who she becomes, the more complicated she gets. By turns hilarious and deeply revealing, Chloé Hung’s Perfect Daughter explores the gap between expectation and reality, and the quiet heartbreak of trying to be seen, understood, and loved on your own terms.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: Gilles Vonsattel Piano Recital
events.location: Presidio Theatre, 99 Moraga Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: The extraordinary pianist Gilles Vonsattel offers a captivating look inside Beethoven becoming Beethoven as we know him, part of a series of special engagements in the Bay Area that see the stunningly original performer take on the composer’s complete piano sonata cycle. With this rare performance of four landmark piano sonatas presented in a single evening, Gilles Vonsattel hands us the keys to unlocking the psyche of a genius. Works to be performed – Sonata no. 1 in F Minor, Op. 2; Sonata No. 21 in C Major, Op. 53 “Waldstein”; Sonata No. 27 in E Minor, Op. 90; Sonata No. 28 in A Major, Op. 101. Presented in partnership with Music@Menlo and Stanford Live.

events.title: Life of Pi
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Sixteen-year-old Pi Patel sets out on a journey across the ocean with his family, only to find himself alone after a catastrophic shipwreck. Adrift on a lifeboat in the vast Pacific, he must learn to survive alongside a group of unlikely companions, including a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a Bengal tiger. As the days stretch into weeks, reality and imagination begin to blur. Pi is pushed to his limits, confronting fear, faith, and the stories we tell ourselves to endure the unimaginable. Winner of five Olivier Awards including Best New Play, and hailed by The Guardian as “extraordinary and unmissable,” this breathtaking stage adaptation brings Yann Martel’s beloved novel to life through stunning visuals and groundbreaking puppetry. Life of Pi is a theatrical event about survival, belief, and the power of storytelling.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: The Comeuppance
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: When a group of millennial classmates meet to pregame for their twentieth high school reunion, everyone is nervous for the night ahead. As alcohol and weed help the self-declared “Multi-Ethnic Reject Group” let their guards down, they begin to reminisce and reveal how their lives have unfolded since graduation. Did their friendships stand the test of time? Why do they remember certain moments from their past differently? From Pulitzer Prize–winning and two-time Tony Award–winning playwright Branden Jacob-Jenkins ( Gloria ) comes a new profound tragicomedy about the reunion that awaits us all.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: Song Circle with Amateur Music Network
events.location: Berkeley
events.description: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! 


Teacher Bio: 

Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life.

For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches.

For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives.

In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach.

Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

events.title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Benjamin Barker returns to London a changed man. Now known as Sweeney Todd, the barber comes back to a city that took everything from him, driven by a single, consuming desire for revenge. Above Mrs. Lovett’s struggling pie shop, he sets up a new practice, and together they form a darkly ingenious partnership. As business begins to thrive, the line between justice and obsession starts to blur, with chilling consequences for all who cross their path. Winner of eight Tony Awards including Best Musical, Stephen Sondheim’s Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is a thrilling and unforgettable tale of vengeance, morality, and the cost of losing one’s humanity.

events.title: 5Rhythms® Sweat Your Prayers
events.location: The Berkeley Alembic (Luna), 2820 Seventh Street, Berkeley, CA
events.description:
5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic.

In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing.

5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you.

The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. 

We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. 

This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week!
